items.statement: Q3 TCV was $10.2 billion with double-digit YoY growth and no mega deals
items.quote: The highlight of the quarter was our exceptionally strong and broad -based TCV at US$10.2 billion.

items.statement: North America TCV was $5.9 billion and BFSI TCV was $3.2 billion in Q3
items.quote: North America TCV was at US$5.9 billion. BFSI TCV was at US$3.2 billion and consumer business accounted for US$1.3 billion .

items.statement: Operating margin improved 40 bps sequentially to 24.5% despite furloughs and seasonality
items.quote: Our Q3 operating margin was 24.5%, a sequential improvement of 40 basis points, despite headwinds on account of furloughs and Q3 seasonality, which was offset by operating efficiency through improvement in productivity, utilization and pyramid.

items.statement: Margin aspiration remains 26-28%; happy to exit Q4 at 26% but not committed
items.quote: So, Sandeep, margin aspiration remains 26% to 28%. I had not committed that we will reach 26% by Q4, wha t I said is we will be happy if we can exit Q4 at

items.statement: Early signs of discretionary spend revival in BFSI and Retail; Manufacturing and Life Sciences to recover in medium term
items.quote: We are seeing early signs of revival in discretionary spend in BFSI and Retail. Manufacturing and Life Sciences and Healthcare should also start seeing growth in the medium term as near-term challenges have bottomed out in this quarter.

items.statement: Client IT budgets expected to remain similar in CY25 with positive bias
items.quote: We expect client IT budgets to remain similar in CY '25 with a positive bias.

items.statement: Manufacturing expected to bottom out in Q4 with growth reviving subsequently; Life Sciences awaiting US policy clarity
items.quote: From a manufacturing perspective, I feel we'll bottom out in Q4, and growth should revive subsequently. In Life Sciences and Healthcare, that's one industry waiting for more policy clarity in the US . So once clarity emerges, discretionary spend could return there.

items.statement: Campus hiring on track; preparing to onboard increased number of campus hires next year
items.quote: Our campus hiring program is progressing as planned and we are gearing up to onboard an increased number of campus hires next year.

items.statement: Over 25,000 promotions awarded in Q3; total promotions for fiscal year exceed 110,000
items.quote: This quarter, we are proud to have recognized the exceptional contributions of our associates by awarding over 25,000 well-deserved promotions across levels, taking the total promotions for the fiscal year to more than 110,000.

items.statement: DSO at 74 days in dollar terms; net cash from operations $1.54B (105.3% of net income); free cash flow $1.45B
items.quote: Our accounts receivable was at 74 days DSO in dollar terms. Net cash from operations was $1.54 billion, which is 105.3% of net income Free cash flows were at $1.45 billion

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of ₹76 per share including ₹10 interim and ₹66 special dividend
items.quote: Consistent with our capital allocation policy of returning substantial free cash flow back to our shareholders, the Board has recommended a dividend of ₹76 per share, which includes an interim dividend of ₹10 and a special dividend of ₹66 per share.

items.statement: Revenue grew 4.5% YoY in constant currency; dollar revenue $7,539M up 3.6% YoY
items.quote: In dollar terms, the revenue was $7,539 million and a year -on-year growth of 3.6%. That translates to a constant currency growth of our revenues to 4.5%.

items.statement: Deal cycles shortened by few weeks for deals >$20M; decision-making improving
items.quote: for the first time, there is a good decrease in the deal cycle, by few weeks. We looked at deals that are more than $20 million and above, there is a deal cycle reduction also, which also shows that the decision -making is also improving largely.

items.statement: Not guiding to double-digit growth but expecting stronger growth in CY25 vs CY24; core markets to do heavy lifting
items.quote: No, we are not guiding to a double-digit growth, but we are expecting a stronger growth. And we are also hoping that we'll be able to compensate the BSNL revenue in multiple other ways both internationally as well as domestically.

items.statement: Invested funds at $7.28 billion at end of period
items.quote: invested funds at the end of the period stood at $7.28 billion.

items.statement: Capital allocation policy considers tax/regulation changes; both buyback and dividend options available
items.quote: Both the alternatives are still available. The point you mentioned is also right, but the Board considers various preferences from various classes of shareholders and arrives at the decision. Regulation changes or tax changes will also be factored in when that decision is taken.

items.statement: Furloughs similar to last year; some spillover into first weeks of January but small proportion
items.quote: Yes. Like the reason I said that is I see in some geographies, furloughs do spill over into until first couple of weeks of January, but it's a small proportion of overall furlough

items.statement: Europe had one of best deal wins; all-round better deal wins across geographies and industries
items.quote: From a geography perspective, Europe has one of the best deal wins. So, it has been all-round better deal win from a geography as well as industry perspective.

items.statement: Agentic AI enabling orchestration of transactions in business value chains using LLM planning and reasoning capabilities
items.quote: Agentic AI represents the next step of maturity in the exponentially evolving space of AI. It allows us to orchestrate actual transactions inside business value chains using the rapidly improving planning and reasoning capabilities of large language models .

items.statement: Net income margin 19.4%; EPS grew 6.4% YoY
items.quote: Net income margin in Q3 was 19.4%, and our EPS grew 6.4% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Digital cable TV subscriber base at 9.6 million with 8.9 million paying subscribers; broadband active subscribers at 1.042 million, home pass at 5.95 million (75% FTTX-ready)
items.quote: stood at 9.6 million. Among the total subscriber base, paying subscribers stood at 8.9 million. On a Y- o-Y basis, the increase in both active and paying subscriber is 200K respectively. Home pass stood at 5.95 mil

items.statement: Broadband ARPU increased by INR5 YoY to INR465; average data consumption per month at 365 GB, up 6% YoY

items.statement: Consolidated reported EBITDA INR1,138M at 13% margin; operating EBITDA INR1,021M at 22% margin; standalone operating EBITDA margin 22%
items.quote: Consolidated reported EBITDA stood at INR1,138 million at an EBITDA margin of 13%. Operating EBITDA for the quarter was INR1,021 million with a margin of 22%.

items.statement: Annual capex guidance INR350 crore; INR265 crore spent in 9M FY25 (INR160 crore cable TV, INR95 crore broadband); HITS project ~80% complete on capex side
items.value: INR350 crore annual, INR265 crore spent 9M
items.quote: Yes so total cap ex as we have given th at for the annual capex we are going to do the INR350 crores. Out of that we did INR265 crores right now. TV side we did cable TV side we did INR160 crores and broadband side we did the INR95 crores till 9 months 31st December, 2024.

items.statement: HITS (Headend-in-the-Sky) project ~80% complete on capex side, targeting launch in FY26; will enable nationwide signal coverage and cost savings
items.quote: We are spending it. Already you can say that the project is around 80% completed on the capex side. And we are just looking forward that by next quarter the whole project will be completed and we will be ready to launch.

items.statement: Broadband ARPU increase driven by customer demand for higher packages; cable TV facing broadcaster price hikes of 10-18% effective Feb 2025, pass-through assessment ongoing
items.quote: ARPU on the broadband side, yes t his quarter, if you see, it has gone up and this is now at INR465. That is mainly due to the demand from the customers for higher packages which is going on. We are launching some of the higher packages at higher ARPU.

items.statement: Wireline broadband underpenetrated with demand for reliable high-speed data; B2B broadband inquiries strong, B2C muted in Gujarat; wireless-to-wired shift seen after telecom price hikes but muted recently
items.quote: Wire line broadband continues to be under penetrated in our country with demand driven by need for reliable high -speed data at affordable prices.

items.statement: Broadband net additions: ~60% from B2B (22-23K YoY), 40% B2C; B2B subscriber base >100K, expanding pan-India; B2C focused on Gujarat and select cities
items.quote: Yes, it is on 37,000 on a Y-o-Y basis. We can say that B2B is around 22k to 23k and rest is B2C. So more is coming from; ~ 60% is coming from B2B right now on that basis.

items.quote: Same in the broadband, when we are fighting their lower is at 30 Mbps at our price. We are providing on those at 50 Mbps and 60 Mbps or 100 Mbps which we manage in that way. So, there the room is there to fight with them on the pricing side, on our own products.

items.statement: Net debt ~INR15 crore; increase due to HITS project term loans and higher OD utilization; expect net debt negative by Sep-Dec 2026; term loans repaid via EMI over ~12 months
items.quote: Right now if we talk about the net debt basis hardly it is around you can say the debt is on the net debt side. The debt is hardly around INR15 crores more in the whole scenario in the bank. That is why we have not stated this quarter that we have net debt zero or net debt negative right now, but yes this company will again become net debt negative by you can say somewhere September or December 26

items.statement: BharatNet Phase III participation pending judicial matter resolution; previously executed Gujarat BharatNet (17,000 km fiber, 4,000 gram panchayats); exploring other government projects
items.quote: BharatNet project, as you know that BSNL and BBNL have launched that. And recently they have launched for 16 states. And the tender has been filled and given and the results have been announced also, b ut it is under judicial matter right now. We are also waiting that once the judicial matter will be over, then it will be pursued.

items.statement: Launched GTPL Buzz consumer app (live TV, DistroTV, Blacknut gaming, AI chatbot GIVA); TV Key Cloud with NAGRA; app downloads >1.3M (150K new in 3-4 months), 6K gaming subscribers
items.quote: Yes. So, the responses are very good. Actually, we have - when we launched GTPL Buzz it is with the live TV p lus we have introduced the Distro TV and the gaming Blacknut t he gaming, all are together there plus the general app for the complaints and maintenance and services and all.

items.statement: Acquired remaining 49% stake in subsidiary (100K subscribers) for INR11-12 crore via conversion of pre-tariff outstanding; cash outflow negligible; part of consolidation to reduce 26 subsidiaries
items.quote: Here, what we are doing, that there are outstanding which is like pre-tariff outstanding and all and through that, we are converting it into 51%. items.statement: Cable TV broadcaster price hikes (10-18%) may cause consumer churn if not fully passed through; assessment ongoing at company, industry, and consumer levels
items.quote: Seeing in the situation of the industry right now, we have to assess that whether any price hike the consumer or at the ground level, the price hike can be observed or not. So, that assessment has to come. And we have to see because once you go for the price hike, the likely situation is that churn will happen on the consumer base.

items.statement: No specific subscriber count guidance for FY25/FY26; will disclose HITS project details, targets, and subscriber growth plans in Q4 FY25; expect broadband B2B acceleration from FY26
items.quote: That is what we are going to give you in quarter 4. We are trying to launch that in FY26 this headend in the sky and it is going to be very positive for the company.

items.statement: FY25 top-line growth guided at 25% YoY
items.quote: So if you compare us with the previous year, FY '24, our incremental growth on the top line would be by 25%.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR500 million as of call date
items.quote: Order book as on today would be INR500 million.

items.quote: During this period, we have achieved revenue of INR44.83 crores, which is an increase by 19% as compared to first half of FY '24

items.quote: In this first half of FY '25, we have achieved EBITDA of INR10.36 crores, which is 23.1% of our total revenue early in first FY '25.

items.quote: The current existing capacity utilization, I would say, on the ballpark figure would be 80%. And the new plant in Kaman, which is 20 kilometers from the existing plant is already integrated and would be ramped up in the next 2 or 3 months period maximum.

items.quote: The same ratio as we are currently using. It is in domestic we are using 40%, export 60%.

items.statement: Target INR275 crore revenue by 2028; service/O&M share 35-40% (INR80-85 cr) in 5 years
items.quote: I can give you a consolidated figure for, say, 5 years, our aim is to take the company to at least INR275 crores by 2028.

items.statement: FY27 service/O&M revenue expected INR15 crore; FY28 adds INR10-15 crore incrementally
items.quote: In FY '27, we expect a revenue of INR15 crores on end user business.

items.quote: In FY '25, we expect the revenue of almost INR8 crores from Russia alone, which is profitable and which is a growing business for us in Russia.

items.quote: In FY '24, we have done almost 175 mechanical seals which went for projects. And this year, we are planning more than 250 seals for projects.

items.quote: No, not put our -- to an extent that we have felt a pinch or kind of a push when the system is seamless and in fact, sort out the components have reduced to the price of the previous year, because the volume also increased over here at Sealmatic.

items.quote: The withdrawal of preferential issue will have no bearing on the cash flow or the liquidity of our company. We are well and sufficiently financed.

items.statement: Pricing ~15% below global MNC peers; service repairs at 75% of new seal cost

items.quote: Most of the machines are -- imported from various countries, namely Europe. And I think if I would make a ballpark figure, 80% of the machines are all imported over here.

items.quote: Saudi Arabia is much bigger market and, of course, a difficult market as we all know because of stringent conditions from the end users.

items.quote: We also established 5 sales and service centers in India, which are manned by Sealmatic employees, there is some are expenditures.

items.quote: Of course, they need to be approved by ADNOC, which is a good news that we are approved by ADNOC.

items.statement: Global mechanical seal market $4.25B; focus on oil & gas, refinery, petrochemical, power, nuclear, urban, defense (Indian Navy/Air Force)
items.quote: Current market size, as we see globally on mechanical seals is $4.25 million. Our current focus, of course, is India. The Middle East and Russia. items.statement: FY25 expected to be a soft year; difficult to exceed FY24 growth rate
items.quote: I think FY '25 will definitely be a soft year. We were hoping that these headwinds that we're seeing in automotive industry, we will still be able to find a way to recover. items.statement: Normalized tax rate expected upwards of 25% for FY25 and beyond
items.quote: On a normalized basis, I believe that our tax rate would be upwards of 25%, probably 26%, but we may exit the full year at an effective tax rate of something between 24.5% to 25%.

items.statement: Management aims to return to 25-26% EBIT margin band in short to mid-term
items.quote: Yes, I think that is a fair understanding, and that is our plan to get back to those margins. I think Manoj also mentioned during the previous question that the priority for us is to improve our billability and utilization, and that will come from improving our top line.

items.statement: Europe automotive market recovery expected to take a quarter or two; US steady; APAC/India accelerating
items.quote: Europe will be a little slow. APAC, India will definitely accelerate. U.S. will be steady. So that's the outlook for the automotive industry.

items.statement: Healthcare and Media verticals showing green shoots; growth pickup expected from Q4/Q1
items.quote: We are hoping that in both these verticals, the pickup of business should start from the next quarter onwards, in some cases from Q1. W e have won some large deals and those ramp -ups will happen next quarter and the subsequent quarters

items.quote: During the quarter, EBITDA margins stood at 26.3% and PBT margin was reported at 26.1%. This was the first quarter in which the full impact of salary increases for all our employees was seen. Margins in the quarter was also impacted by adverse currency movements in GBP, Euro and JPY.

items.statement: Currency impact ~140 bps; wage hike impact ~100 bps largely mitigated; third-party contractor +60 bps; COGS/depreciation benefit ~45 bps
items.quote: So, in all total, there's an impact of about 150 basis points when you compare 25% EBIT last quarter to 23.5% this quarter.

items.statement: Large multi-year deal won with US-headquartered operator in Media; large deals in pipeline across verticals
items.quote: We won a large multi-year deal with a U.S. headquartered-operator to develop and manage their portfolio of applications and expect to ramp this up over the next few quarters. items.statement: OEM revenue share increased from 67% to 72% in auto; Tier-1 outsourcing declining
items.quote: Revenues from OEMs has increased I think from 67% to 72% this quarter.

items.statement: JLR remains significant but dependence reduced over time; comfortable with current concentration
items.quote: JLR is definitely one of our significant customers, no doubt about it. But there are a number of other OEMs as well that we work with. items.statement: Chinese OEMs' rapid growth pressuring Western OEMs' China revenues, leading to budget cuts and shift to ICE/hybrid

And China market used to be pretty big for many of these custom

items.quote: And of course, there's also a push towards ICE and hybrid because in some sense, they believe that moving towards the EV is only going to strengthen the China ecosystem because most of the batteries and components, the motors, inverters, everything comes from China, even for the global OEMs, right? So, there's a little bit of competition, there is politics, there is everything intertwined there.

items.statement: No additional capex incurred during the year; SEZ units moved from 100% to 50% tax benefit
items.quote: One, due to the differential in the deferred tax asset because of reduction in the depreciation and we didn't incur any additional capex during the year.

items.statement: Selective M&A focus on small-sized companies in adjacencies; no big bang acquisitions
items.quote: Regarding M&A and acquisition, yes, we continue to look out and scan for opportunities, especially in adjacencies and new areas that we want to invest in. Typically, we are looking for small-sized companies, we don't believe in big ban g acquisition

items.quote: During the quarter, our revenues from India has grown by 21.9% year-on-year, while Japan and emerging markets grew at 66.8% year-on-year.

items.statement: Pricing not a major issue in Japan; pricing pressure in India; competition intensity higher in Western markets
items.quote: Especially in Japan and so on, we don't see that much of an issue with respect to pricing. Of course, in the Indian market we definitely see pricing will be an issue. items.statement: Third-party contractor costs increased 60 bps due to skill gaps; travel/visa costs up for on-site roles

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty, currency volatility, and industry-specific challenges in Europe and US persist

items.quote: Our system integration business witnessed decision delays in some large projects that had a significant impact on revenues in the quarter. items.statement: Aerospace, Avionics & Defence targeted as significant revenue contributor in 4-5 years; partnerships with NAL, HAL for UAV/eVTOL
items.quote: So definitely, we see Aerospace, Avionics and D efence going to be a big opportunity area for us, not just in India, but also overseas. items.statement: Full bouquet across active/passive, equity/fixed income/money market, ETFs/index/smart beta; best-in-class product suite; focus on fair share in each category
items.quote: we have now best -in-class product bouquet across active and passive, across equity, fixed income, money market. Within passive, we have products across ETFs and index funds, both mark et cap-based indices as well as smart beta.

items.statement: HDFC AMC added 40 lakh new customers in last 12 months; focus on increasing allocation from existing investors via 'Mutual Funds Sahi Hai' campaign
items.quote: As an AMC, we have added 40 lakh new customers in last 12 months or so. These are like phenomenal numbers. I a lso keep thinking that one investor addition, but the two, a big opportunity for us is also to ensure we get more allocation from the existing investors.

items.statement: Client base growing at 40-45% year-on-year, with 2.1 million clients added in Q3 FY25, 88% from Tier 2/3+ cities.
items.quote: The good part is that customer inflow in this market remains very healthy. So we are growing at 40-45%, and that trend continues.

items.statement: Aggregate orders declined 13.8% sequentially to nearly 422 million, partly due to 4.7% fewer trading days.
items.quote: Our aggregate orders for the quarter were lower by 13.8% to nearly 422 million, which also includes the impact of 4.7% lower number of trading days.

items.statement: Reported consolidated EBDAT margin was 42%, down 787 bps QoQ; adjusted for ancillary income loss, compression was 257 bps.
items.quote: Our Q3 FY 2025 reported consolidated EBDAT margin stood at 42%, while this was lower by 787 basis points quarter-on-quarter as compared to our reported Q2 margins. However, this compression was lower by 257 basis points when adjusted for the impact of the ancillary transaction income.

items.statement: Margins likely to remain in current range until new regulations fully implemented and client behaviour normalizes.
items.quote: Our margins are likely to remain in this range till the time the new regulations are fully implemented and client behavio ur normalizes

items.statement: Average client funding book (MTF) grew 4.2% QoQ to ₹40.5 billion; end-of-quarter book at ₹43.3 billion.
items.quote: Our average client funding book grew by 4.2% sequentially to ₹ 40.5 billion for the quarter, which at the end of the quarter was higher at ₹ 43.3 billion.

items.statement: Cumulative personal loan disbursements on platform reached ₹600 crores; live with 3 lenders, integrating 3 more.
items.quote: So far, we have cumulatively disbursed ₹ 600 crores in personal loans on the platform. We are also integrating with 3 more lenders in the final stages and will scale in a measured manner.

items.statement: Mutual fund distribution hit nearly 9 lakh unique SIP registrations in Dec 2024, highest ever; over 2 million SIPs for two consecutive quarters.
items.quote: In the mutual fund distribution business, we achieved a major milestone in December 2024 with nearly 9 lakh unique SIP registrations, our highest ever. For the past two consecutive quarters, we have recorded over 2 million SIPs.

items.statement: Introduced flat fee brokerage for cash delivery (₹20 or 0.1% with min ₹2) and interest charges on non-cash collateral >₹50,000 from mid-November 2024.
items.quote: To adapt, we took proactive steps introducing flat fee brokerage for cash delivery orders and implementing interest charges on disproportionate non-cash collateral exceeding ₹ 50,000 from mid-November 2024.

items.statement: Launched insurance journey (motor) in beta on SuperApp; received regulatory approvals for Mutual Fund (AMC) and PMS; launched wealth brand 'Ionic Wealth'.
items.quote: I am happy to share, Q3 FY '25 saw significant milestones, including the beta launch of insurance journey within the SuperApp. The regulatory approvals for launching our Mutual Fund under the aegis of Angel One Asset Management Limited and Portfolio Management Services under Angel One Wealth Limited. I am also delighted to announce the launch of wealth management brand 'Ionic Wealth' by Angel One.

items.statement: AMC will focus on passive-only products (ETFs and index funds); Wealth management offers passives, quant, PIPE, secondaries, high yield, and global themes.
items.quote: Our product offerings will focus on 5 themes; passives, quant, PIPE, secondaries and high yield. And of course, also Global is one of it that we are quite excited about to ensure we cater to diverse customer needs.

items.statement: Demat market share expanded 26 bps sequentially to 15.9%; retail equity turnover share up 41 bps to 19.7% in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: Our consistent focus on growing market share is evident with 26 basis points sequential expansion in our share across India's total demat account to 15.9% as of December 2024. Furthermore, our overall -- the retail equity turnover market share expanded by 41 basis points to 19.7% in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Direct business share of net broking revenue steady at 76%; assisted business contributes balance.
items.quote: Share of direct business in our net broking revenues remained consistent at 76%, and the balance being contributed by clients under our assisted business.

items.statement: Monthly expiry grouping (2 exchanges to 1 day/week) to cause additional 3-4% revenue decline.
items.quote: Additional regulatory update on grouping monthly expiry for each of the exchange, 2 exchanges to 1 day of the week, would bring an additional 3% to 4% decline.

items.statement: Depreciation and amortization increased 4.2% QoQ to ₹267 million due to capitalization of infra assets.
items.quote: Depreciation and amortization costs increased by 4.2% sequentially to ₹ 267 million in Q3 as we capitalized infra assets.

items.statement: Margin monies from clients lower, borrowings higher vs March 2024; net worth increased to ₹56.3 billion as of Dec 31, 2024.
items.quote: As of December 31st, 2024, the margin monies from clients were lower, while borrowings were higher when compared to March 2024. The consolidated net worth of the company increased to ₹ 56.3 billion as of 31st December.

items.statement: Finance cost rose 10.8% QoQ to ₹835 million due to 4.6% higher borrowings for MTF growth and margin requirements, plus 35-40 bps higher cost of funds.
items.quote: Finance cost increased by 10.8% quarter-on-quarter to ₹ 835 million on account of 4.6% higher borrowing to fund the growth in the client funding book and for margin requirements at the exchanges, coupled with a 35 to 40 basis points increase in average cost of funds.

items.statement: Board approved reinstatement of dividend distribution at 35% of quarterly consolidated profit after tax.
items.quote: I am pleased to announce that the Board has approved reinstatement of dividend distribution of 35% of quarterly consolidated profit after tax.

items.statement: Employee benefit expenses grew 3.1% QoQ to ₹2.4 billion due to headcount additions in tech, product, data analytics, legal, and wealth business.
items.quote: Employee benefit expenses, including cost of granting stock options, grew 3.1% sequentially to nearly ₹ 2.4 billion on account of headcount increase in tech, product, data analytics, legal and the wealth business.

items.statement: 9M FY25 gross revenue ₹41.9 billion (+43.4% YoY), PAT ~₹10 billion (+27% YoY); 9M PAT is 88.6% of full FY24 PAT.
items.quote: Our 9-month FY2025 reported gross total revenues and profit after tax stood at ₹ 41.9 billion and nearly ₹ 10 billion, representing a growth of 43.4% and 27%, respectively, over the corresponding year last year. Our 9-month FY2025 profit after tax is 88.6% of our entire FY '24 profit.

items.statement: 9M FY25 annualized ROE at 33.3%; expected to trend back to historical levels as business normalizes.
items.quote: Our 9-month FY 2025 annualized return on average equity remains healthy at 33.3%. As the business normalizes, we strongly believe that our ROE should trend back to our historical levels.

items.statement: Regulatory changes may cause temporary disruption; management expects client behaviour to normalize over 1-2 quarters.
items.quote: While regulatory changes often lead to temporary disruption and volume corrections. History shows that client adapt quickly, as seen during the peak margin regulation between 2020 and 2021, which ultimately fuelled growth through an expanded client base.

items.statement: Credit distribution faces industry headwinds (KYC fraud, over-leverage, delinquencies); lenders adopting cautious approach causing short-term growth pause.
items.quote: Over the last two to three years, the personal loan space has grown rapidly but not without challenges. In the industry, there has been higher KYC frauds, over-leverage and delinquencies exceeding expectations. As a result, lenders are now adopting a more cautious, measured approach. While this has led to some short-term growth headwinds, this pause is crucial for building a stronger and more sust

items.statement: Management will wait 1-2 quarters to assess permanent revenue impact before considering F&O price hikes; pricing levers available if needed.
items.quote: See, Prayesh, what we will wait for 1 or 2 quarters to see a permanent impact. And if needed, definitely, we have levers to play on our prices. So prices, we would like to see all patterns stabilize in terms of what's an hit because of market conditions, because of global environment. And then we'll take a very informed call on how much hike we have to incorporate.

items.statement: Management targets sustained EBITDA margin (OPM) of 50% long-term; price hikes considered if trajectory at risk
items.quote: So what we look at that we are focusing on business model, which can give an OPM of 50% on a very sustained and long-term basis.

items.statement: Regulatory impact on net revenue estimated at 18-20%; expected to recover in 2-3 quarters via 40-45% customer growth
items.quote: Hit of revenue in terms of 20%, market normalizing and growth rate of customer to the tune of 40%, in 2-3 quarters, we'll be back to these numbers.

items.statement: Long-term cost recovery target of 75-80% of regulatory cost impact once behavior normalizes
items.quote: in the long term once things settle down and the behaviour normalizes, we should be able to ideally recover almost 75%, 80% of this cost that we've been talking about in the past also.

items.statement: Customer acquisition growth rate remains 40-45% despite regulatory changes
items.quote: customers that are coming to the market are coming at the same numbers. And not only they are coming at the same numbers, in fact, their spending in second year, third year is increasing.

items.statement: Focus on wallet share across broking, mutual funds, insurance, lending, wealth; not segment-specific revenue
items.quote: Focus is on wallet share. We want customers to come on our platform, retain with us, buy all the services, whatever is needed in terms of mix of services, that person should be satisfied with us.

items.statement: Mutual fund distribution: #2 in incremental SIPs; AUM crossed Rs 10,000 cr; B2C free to retain customers, B2B charged
items.quote: When we started 6 quarters back, we had clear cut view that we want to become a leader in this segment. So today, as we speak, we are number 2 in terms of incremental SIP.

items.statement: Credit disbursed ~Rs 600 cr; insurance beta testing done; wealth licenses and team in place; all verticals contributing to top line
items.quote: In terms of credit, we have disbursed around ₹ 600 crores. Insurance journey, we have just did a beta testing. Wealth, we just got licenses and team is in place.

items.statement: AMC will take time to build sustained retail-focused business; not immediate bottom-line contributor
items.quote: AMC, because we want to build a very sustained, a very large business will take its own time because we want to sell just right product which is for retail.

items.statement: Churn rate ballpark same as industry; active NSE client additions trending superior to competition over 12-month rolling period
items.quote: We do not share data on churn rate, but it will be ballpark in the same way as the industry rate. There's not much difference.

items.statement: Equity-first customer base creates higher stickiness vs payment platforms; cross-sell receptivity higher due to adjacency
items.quote: Our consumers who have come in so far have come in from an equity-first use case. Now, when an adjacency like a mutual fund or an adjacency like an insurance or an adjacency which could be in the form of a wealth product is pitched to that consumer, the receptivity of that consumer is far higher.

items.statement: Trade payables fell QoQ from Rs 9,400 cr to Rs 6,500 cr due to weaker market sentiment; expected to improve with sentiment
items.quote: this is in trend with the weaker sentiments in the market. And when people trade more, they bring more money when people trade less, they keep lesser money.

items.statement: Majority of fixed costs for new verticals already taken; CEO joining next financial year; IPL spend decision based on season response
items.quote: almost we have taken a majority of expenses, except for our CEO would be joining maybe in our next start of the financial year.

items.statement: AI investment focused on personalization and developer productivity (Copilot); not primarily headcount reduction
items.quote: we are working closely with Microsoft on figuring out how Copilot can improve, developer productivity and how we can automate certain tasks which were previously done manually.

items.statement: Major regulatory changes implemented; no further major changes foreseen; customers need time to adapt
items.quote: I think whatever like major kind of like regulatory changes, which they had in mind, have already been implemented. I don't see any major kind of this thing coming now.

items.statement: Revenue impact 18-20% on net revenue (ex-AP payouts); recovery depends on market normalization and customer growth
items.quote: Right. It's the net impact on our revenue.

items.statement: Incremental SIP market share: #2 position achieved in 6 quarters
items.quote: today, as we speak, we are number 2 in terms of incremental SIP.

items.statement: CEO joining start of next financial year; senior build-up largely complete
items.quote: except for our CEO would be joining maybe in our next start of the financial year. So otherwise, I don't see any major kind of changes in terms of fixed expenses because we were in that build-up at almost like whatever was needed in terms of senior resources.

items.statement: Platform vision: fully connected ecosystem with AI-driven personalization across personal finance in 3-5 years
items.quote: We'll be using lots of AI tools to understand personalized every cohort, every person's requirement and be fully connected with ecosystem.

items.statement: VAW added to OFAC SDN list by U.S. Treasury, blocking U.S. property and dollar transactions
items.quote: As per the U.S. Department of S tate's press release dated 10 th January 2025, the set of Russian companies in the manufacturing sector which includes VAW, were added to the U.S. Department of Treasuries, Office of Foreign Assets Control, (OFAC), Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Person List (SDN list) for operating or having operated in the manufacturing sector of the Russian Federation

items.statement: VAW has no U.S. business operations or sales; assessing impact of designation
items.quote: As such, VAW has no business operation or sales in the U.S. VAW is assessing the impact of its designation. Material update, if any, will be informed post the completion of such assessment.

items.statement: ~12% of VAW business is U.S. dollar denominated; working with customers to switch currencies
items.quote: We think around 12 percentage of our business is U.S. dollar denominated and this we would be talking to each customer to understand their willingness to switch to other currencies.

items.statement: 60% of VAW sales within Russia, 40% exported; USD sales occur outside Europe and U.S.
items.quote: So it is typically no Europe, no U.S. sales, as I said in my opening remarks, and it typically happens outside of the Europe, this 12%.

items.statement: Miniscule outstanding USD receivables; no collection risk seen currently
items.quote: So we have very, very miniscule outstanding receivable, and these will have to be collected. We understand these are known customers who have been working with us for quite some time and there are individual customers that we need to start working with them to collect. We don't see at this point in time a risk.

items.statement: Further update expected in February earnings call; currency shift timeline unclear
items.quote: I think probably we'll have more update when we meet in the month of February after our earnings call or during the earnings call.

items.statement: No growth aspirations for Russia business until geopolitical clarity emerges
items.quote: We don't have any kind of aspiration of growth, and we have been communicating this as well until clarity emerges in this manner. So I would say that's the stand we that continues even now.

items.statement: Dividend repatriation from VAW via banking channels expected to continue; ~30% of profit typically paid out
items.quote: So typically, the dividend is paid and that is how the repatriation of dividend happens using the banking channels. And we think that, that should continue to happen.

items.statement: No other restrictions or sanctions on VAW beyond OFAC designation
items.quote: No other restriction to our knowledge exists. This is the first time we have faced and that's what we are sharing with you.

items.statement: High-purity SiC pilot plant in India unaffected by VAW situation
items.quote: We don't see any impact of that, that's happening in India and it will continue to progress in that direction.

items.statement: VAW has not sold to U.S. previously; no expected material change in global SiC prices
items.quote: So silicon carbide is a very large market. And as I said, that VAW has not been selling to U.S. in the past as well.

items.statement: Impact limited to VAW; no effect on other CUMI U.S. businesses
items.quote: This, as we understand as per our discussion with multiple people involved, this is highly focused on VAW and its business and that is how we understand and we have communicated the same thing also to the investors.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY25 is INR 980 crores; PAT guidance is INR 295 crores.
items.value: Revenue INR 980 crores; PAT INR 295 crores
items.quote: We have achieved 75% of our revised revenue guidance as well of INR 980 crores on the revenue side and 77% of our revised PA T guidance of INR 295 crores in the first 9M FY25

items.statement: Equity MF net flows grew 51% YoY to INR 5,831 crores; equity MF share of AUM rose to 55% from 52%.
items.value: Equity MF net flows INR 5,831 crores; Share 55%
items.quote: Equity Mutual Fund's net flows achieved year-on-year growth of about 51% to INR 5,831 crores. Share of Equity Mutual Funds in AUM increased to 55% as of December 2024 as compared to 52% last December 2023.

items.statement: Added 1,515 net new client families in 9M FY25, total 11,426; client AUM attrition 0.28%.
items.quote: In our flagship private wealth business, the first 9 M FY25, we added 1,515 new client families on net basis, bringing our total number of client families to 11,426. Client attrition rate in terms of AUM lost for the 9M period was as little as 0.28

items.statement: Added 61 net new RMs in past 12 months, total 383; near-zero regret RM attrition (1 in last 6 quarters).
items.value: 61 net new RMs; Total 383; Regret attrition 1 in 6 quarters
items.quote: We have added 61 new relationship managers on net basis over the past 12 months, bringing our total RM count to 383. In the last quarter, we have achieved near zero regret RM attrition. We have lost one RM who had an AUM greater than INR 40 crores, which we call regret attrition.

items.statement: Digital wealth AUM grew 23% YoY to INR 1,827 crores; clients up 24% to 5,772. OFA platform has 6,273 subscribers with INR 1.4 lakh crores platform assets.
items.value: Digital AUM INR 1,827 crores; Clients 5,772; OFA subscribers 6,273; Platform assets INR 1.4 lakh crores
items.quote: Digital wealth business, which is a B2B2C platform, registered an AUM growth of 23% year-on-year to Rs 1,827 crores. The number of clients increased 24% to 5,772. The OFA business, Omni Financial Advisor business, which is abbreviated as OFA, which is a SaaS platform, has 6,273 subscribers with platform assets of INR1.4 lakh crores at the end of 9M FY25.

items.statement: Aspiration to grow net mobilization 30-40% YoY; targeting INR 4,500-5,000 crores net flows next year same quarter vs INR 3,500 crores this quarter.
items.quote: We see this trend; we are putting in effort for a 30% - 40% growth in net mobilization rate. So if we have collected INR 3,500 crores this quarter, I am just simply rounding it off. I would like to see INR 4,500 crores - INR 5,000 crores for the same quarter next year at least.

items.statement: Structured product primary mobilization Q3 FY25 INR 1,347 crores vs INR 1,231 crores YoY; secondary INR 589 crores vs INR 427 crores. 9M primary INR 4,630 crores vs INR 3,994 crores; secondary INR 1,546 crores vs INR 960 crores.
items.value: Q3 Primary INR 1,347 crores; Secondary INR 589 crores; 9M Primary INR 4,630 crores; Secondary INR 1,546 crores

items.quote: In alignment with our policy of rewarding shareholders, the company has declared a bonus share in the ratio of 1:1.

items.statement: No new product launches; same 14-scheme model portfolio and structured products sold repeatedly; portfolio approach drives stickiness.
items.quote: No new product launch, okay? We have not launched a new product. Like we've done the same old product, 1,000 times, 1,500 times, the same structure product. So no newness and business continuity is something unique. Generally, even if somebody is manufacturing cars, he launches a new car and then the revenues go up. Maintain, same products, trying to put the business on autopilot stands unique.

Just because I want him in the 14-scheme basket, I will not book his taxes. I would want to wait till it gets into long term sometimes.

items.quote: Return on equity on an annualized basis stood at 44.8% for 9M FY25.

items.statement: Acquiring closed DAP/NPK unit in Dahej, relocating to Nardana, Maharashtra for Rs. 535 crore, operational by September 2026
items.quote: we entered into a definitive agreement to acquire a closed unit of DAP/NPK based in Dahej, Gujarat. The strategy is to diversify the marketing coverage geographically to Maharashtra and below. We estimate this plant to be operation

items.statement: Phosphoric acid capacity expansion at Sagar by 33,000 tons for Rs. 70 crore, targeted for Q2 FY26
items.quote: Further, in Sagar, MP, at our existing manufacturing location, we plan to increase our phosphoric acid capacity in stages by 33,000 tons with a minor CapEx of Rs. 70 crore. This brownfield expansion is targeted to be captively consumed. With this, our phosphoric acid capacity at Sagar will increase from 49,500 tons to 82,500 tons in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Financial closure of Rs. 248 crore for Dhule project with SBI, Axis Bank and Federal Bank completed during the quarter
items.quote: We already have done the financial closure of Rs. 248 crore for Dhule project during the quarter with SBI, Axis Bank and Federal Bank. The closure showcases the confidence of banks on us with the project.

items.statement: DAP/NPK plant ran at 85% utilization in Q3 FY25, which is optimum
items.quote: Our DAP/NPK plant ran at 85% utilization, which is optimum. We could clock thereby recording quarterly sales of 45,676 tons, which was up from 43.8% YoY due to the increased NPK sales.

items.statement: Industry NPK demand grew 50% YoY in Q3 FY25; NPK sales up 43.8% YoY to 45,676 tons, SSP sales up 5.4% YoY to 39,331 tons
items.quote: On the current business environment, we have witnessed a very robust market for NPK for the beginning of the rabi season. The industry demand for the quarter is estimated to have grown 50% YoY. Our DAP/NPK plant ran at 85% utilization, which is optimum. We could clock thereby recording quarterly sales of 45,676 tons, which was up from 43.8% YoY due to the increased NPK sales.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton ~Rs. 5,000 in Q3 FY25, highest for the year; expect similar range for FY26; Maharashtra plant EBITDA per ton likely exceeding ~Rs. 6,000
items.quote: Our product mix has improved and we have been able to record EBITDA per ton of ~ Rs. 5,000 per ton for the quarter, which is highest for the year. We foresee that EBITDA per ton from the upcoming Maharashtra plant will be much higher as it will only be manufacturing DAP/NPK, which is a high-margin product as compared to SSP.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton clocked ~Rs. 4,800 for Q3 FY25, expect similar range for full year FY26; Maharashtra project EBITDA per ton likely exceeding ~Rs. 6,000
items.quote: See, currently, if you see our EBITDA per ton has clocked ~Rs. 4,800 for this quarter, and we expect this to be in a similar range for the full year in FY26. Regarding Maharashtra project, we expect the EBITDA per ton from the Maharashtra project will be much higher, likely exceeding ~Rs. 6,000 per ton.

items.statement: Shift towards NPK driving EBITDA per ton increase; NPK volumes up 43.8% YoY, product mix improved
items.quote: The shift in the product mix towards NPK is one of the key reasons for the increase. Additionally, there was an increase in subsidy on a YoY basis, which further contributed to the rise in EBITDA per ton.

items.statement: Sulphur prices increased recently; expect minor upward revision in subsidy next cycle to offset; pass through raw material cost changes to fertilizer prices
items.quote: On the subsidy scenario, we have observed largely stable raw material prices, except for sulphur, which increased recently during the quarter. We foresee minor upward investment in the subsidy during the next subsidy cycle to offset that subsidy rise.

items.statement: As raw material costs rise, will adjust fertilizer prices accordingly; if prices drop, will reduce prices; target reasonable price for farmers
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier, there has been an increase in raw material prices, and manufacturers have already started raising prices. We have also increased prices in the market. As the cost of raw materials rises, we will adjust fertilizer prices accordingly, and if the prices drop, we will reduce the prices. items.statement: Ad yield Y-o-Y unchanged; pre-COVID comparison not readily available

items.statement: Gaining market share everywhere; competition losing more copies; distribution manpower challenges in smaller markets
items.quote: I can't say I'm happy but at least I should inform yo u that we are gaining market share everywhere, which means the competition is losing much more than whatever we have lost.

items.quote: The problem what we are facing since you mentioned, I must inform you is that in these smaller markets, we are finding difficult now for the distribution boys.

items.statement: Digital monetization experiments underway in pockets; positive results seen; blanket rollout after numbers firm up
items.quote: Yes, we are experimenting, sir, in certain pockets in digital and we have seen some positive results over there. So, we'll continue experimenting on that. An d once we believe that numbers are firm and steady, then certainly, we could do a blanket rollout

items.statement: GDP growth at 6.4% a downer; hopeful for improvement per government outlook; lower GDP would hurt all sectors
items.quote: So, GDP for what happened in this quarter was 6.4%. That was certainly a downer. We are hoping that this should improve going forward. As the government of India is saying that the numbers will improve in this quarter and going forward.

items.statement: Forward contracts for newsprint being discussed with suppliers; mixed response so far
items.quote: We are certainly trying that, discussing with the suppliers. Some of them are okay, some of them are not. So, it's a mixed basket, sir.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin firm at 29%; 9M FY25 EBITDA grew 4% to INR 5,252 million
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter was INR 1,902 million as against INR 2,031 million in the last year. EBITDA margin remained firm at impressive 29%.

items.statement: Radio advertising revenue grew 6% Y-o-Y to INR 492 million in Q3; EBITDA grew 2% to INR 187 million
items.quote: In the Radio segment, we registered growth with advertis ing revenue, up 6% Y-o-Y to INR 492 million compared to INR 464 million. EBITDA in this segment grew by 2% Y -o-Y to INR187 million from INR 183 million.

items.statement: 9M FY25 Radio revenue grew 9% to INR 1,287 million; EBITDA grew 11% to INR 451 million
items.quote: Radio business led radio industry growth with 9% Y-o-Y growth to INR 1,287 million against INR 1,181 million in the last year and EBITDA growth of 11% Y-o-Y to INR 451 million.

items.statement: ~1,000 people deployed for door-to-door circulation survey across country
items.quote: Almost 1,000 people are deployed on a door-to-door survey across country. Those who are going and convincing people, mee ting them about the circulation.

items.statement: Total readership across print, digital, WhatsApp, social media reached 14 crore (~10% of Indian population)
items.quote: Dainik Bhaskar Group has now re ached a remarkable milestone of 14 crores readers spanning print, digital, WhatsApp channel, social media platforms, and we are celebrating this in a big way.

items.statement: New initiatives spend guidance revised to INR 50-55 crore for FY25 from earlier INR 60-65 crore
items.quote: I mean, our aim is to be probably in the range of about INR. 50 odd crores, between INR 50 crores and INR 55 crores. And we are confident.

items.statement: Debt reduced to INR 331 crore as of December 2024 from INR 338 crore in September 2024
items.quote: So, debt for December is INR 331 crores.

items.statement: Committed to reduce debt by INR 100 crore over next two years, targeting end of FY26
items.quote: And I mean, our effort to reduce it by INR 100 crores over the next two years is definitely fully on, and we are committed to reduce that.

items.quote: For Q3 FY '25, the revenue from operations stood at INR 164 crores, which was a growth of 5.4% on a Y -o-Y basis. EBITDA loss for the quarter was INR 42 crore and net loss reported at INR 37 crores.

items.quote: This quarter, we experienced a subdued festive season advertising trend, marking one of the lowest levels in recent years due to sluggish consumer demand.

items.statement: Traditional B2B syndication deals deferred due to industry transitional shifts; expected to materialize in coming months
items.quote: Our traditional B2B syndication business also remained under pressure due to deferred deal closures, which was a consequence of the ongoing transitional shifts in the media industry 's various players over the past few quarters.

items.quote: Digital media revenues for the 3rd Quarter stood at around INR 71 crores, up by approximately 25% Y-o-Y, while for nine months ended for the current financial year, it was INR 195 crores, which grew approximately by 14%.

The last reported balance sheet, which was a September six -month number, we were at INR 618 crores. And as of December, we stand at INR 589 crores.

items.statement: Accelerated inventory charge-offs planned to continue through FY26 on same lines
items.quote: We had mentioned that this additional write-off or the extended write-off that we are planning is planned till FY '26. So it would be on the same lines.

items.statement: Nine months operating cash flow positive INR 7 crore including new initiatives investment; excluding content investment would be ~INR 50 crore positive
items.quote: For the nine months ended, there is a net positive cash flow of INR 7 crores, because of which the debt has come down compared to March levels,

items.statement: Employee cost jump of 23% in Q3 due to one-time annual PLI/bonusing at Diwali; expected to normalize to ~INR 30 crore per quarter
items.quote: It is a one-time expense on account of the annual PLI or bonusing which happens generally at the Diwali time, around that time.

items.statement: Digital syndication business driving growth; advertising demand stress continues on both TV and digital platforms
items.quote: So, Yash, the growth in digital segment has been largely driven by our digital syndication business. The demand stress on advertising continues to be there, both on TV and on digital.

items.statement: ShemarooMe released 14 new titles in Q3 including Gujarati blockbuster Jhamkudi; YouTube channel Shemaroo FilmiGaane crossed 70 million subscribers
items.quote: This quarter, we released 14 new titles, including movies, w eb series, and plays, expanding our content portfolio. Noteworthy premieres include the blockbuster movie, Jhamkudi, which was the highest -grossing Gujarati film of 2024.

items.statement: Launched new DTH service Deiveegam, a Tamil Devotional service on Tata Play
items.quote: During the quarter, we launched a new DTH service called Deiveegam, a Tamil Devotional service available on Tata Play.

items.statement: General entertainment channels achieved 7.6% viewership share in overall Hindi GEC genre
items.quote: Our general entertainment channels continue to perform well, achieving a viewership share of around 7.6% in the overall Hindi GEC genre.

items.statement: Received GST show cause notice; company has firmly replied denying claims and awaiting further action
items.quote: However, the update is that we have got the show cause notice, and the company has firmly replied with the relevant authorities denying such claims. We are waiting for further course of action with the department.

items.statement: Temporary borrowing for content acquisition during quarter caused higher interest cost; subsequently repaid within 2-3 months
items.quote: We have taken temporary borrowing for acquisition of content during the quarter. And o n account of debt, there is an incremental interest cost which has been incurred.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance near 10% growth including Intelliswift, organic near 8%
items.quote: For FY25, including Intelliswift our revenue guidance is for near 10% growth while organically we'll be near 8%.

items.statement: FY25 EBIT margin aspiration near 16% organically
items.quote: And we continue to aspire for near 16% EBIT margin levels for FY25 organically.

items.quote: For Q4 FY25, at consolidated level, we aspire for EBIT margin to be near 15% levels and will improve to mid 16% levels between Q4 FY27 and Q1 FY28.

items.quote: I want to reaffirm our ambition of building 3x $1 Bn segments and getting to a revenue of $2 Bn with 17-18% EBIT margin in the medium term.

items.statement: Robust large deal pipeline across segments, bulkier and better than same time last year and last quarter
items.quote: Also, the pipeline as we stand today is bulkier and better than it was same time last year, last quarter, and we continue to operate.

items.quote: In addition to that, within Tech segment we've seen our Medical segment to be relatively higher which has resulted in what you see almost about 300 bps of incremental margin sequentially in Q3 over Q2.

items.quote: Therefore, we declined by 5.2% in constant currency in Q3 , with some parts of the portfolio doing well while others got impacted.

items.statement: Sustainability grew 4.0% in Q3 with strong Process and Industrial; large deal pipeline increasing
items.quote: We had another strong quarter with 4 .0% growth in both Process and Industrial firing well.

items.quote: We had a strong rebound with 11.1% growth led by C ommunications, ISV, Media and MedTech sub-segments.

items.statement: All three segments expected to grow in Q4 FY25 and beyond
items.quote: We expect all 3 segments to grow in Q4 FY25 and beyond.

items.quote: Some of the aggression on pricing perhaps was, if I may say so, funded by surrender charges on non -par and with that, r educing quite significantly, we expect to se e some sense prevailing on the pr icing of term, annuities and credit life
