items.statement: Two monitored accounts: one court-related not classified as NPA but fully provided, one standard restructured Rs.15-16 crore fully provided
items.quote: Of course , two accounts which are already declared to the notes , that one is a court -related account which is not classified as NPA but can be NPA anytime, depending on the court . We are adequately provided for in that account. Another standard restructured account of around Rs.15 crore to Rs. 16 crore that account has also been fully provided for.

items.statement: QIP driven by SEBI requirement to reduce government holding to 75%; Rs.2,000 crore QIP would reduce holding by ~8%
items.quote: Yeah, it's primarily of course the SEBI requirement , because we know that we five banks are in that category which are required to bring it down. So, of course, Rs.2,000 crore will bring that percentage to around 8%.

items.statement: Churning AAA corporate book due to inadequate pricing; repaid low-yielding AAA assets
items.quote: It is not due to the downgrade, but it is due to the repayment that has happened in a big AAA rated account as the pricing was not adequate for our bank.

items.statement: Corporate pipeline focused on infrastructure, hospitality, renewable energy, real estate
items.quote: The major industries which will come is, of course, the infrastructure, hospitality sector, renewable energies , some real estate also. So, these are some of the areas which we are looking at.

items.statement: Expect substantial recovery from Rs.435 crore insolvency account in Q4
items.quote: Yes, we expect substantial recovery in that segment. Yes, we expect in Q4.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 sales volume target 3.1-3.2 million tons; absolute EBITDA slightly better than FY24 (INR1,192 cr)
items.quote: So based on these factors, we are confident that we shall achieve 3.1 million to 3.2 million tons of sales volume for full year. And absolute EBITDA slightly better than last year because there was a lot of mix on the earnings front in the second quarter.

items.statement: FY26 sales volume target 4 million tons; FY27 target 5 million tons
items.value: 4 million tons by FY26, 5 million tons by FY27
items.quote: Now that we are ready with 4.5 million ton s capacity going to 5 million tons over the next 12 months, so we do maintain our sales volume target of 4 million tons by FY '26 and 5 million tons by FY '27

items.statement: Residual capex ~INR6 billion over next 3-4 quarters to reach 5 million tons capacity, funded from internal cash flows
items.quote: The residual capex for these new plants and to reach 5 million tons is around INR6 billion, which will be funded from internal cash flows over the next three to four quarters.

items.statement: Operating leverage benefit INR400-500 per ton over 1-2 years as utilization nears 100%; value-added mix improvement INR400-500 per ton; discounting pullback when demand recovers
items.quote: So, there is INR400 to INR500 per ton operating leverage benefit, what we see over the next 1 to 2 years as we utilize near 100% levels. Then value-added product mix improvement coming from our Raipur and Dubai plants. Again, it gives us visibility for INR400 to INR500 per ton expansion in our EBITDA spreads.

items.statement: Expect retail demand recovery in H2 CY2025 as monetary easing and government spending resume
items.quote: And as the monetary situation eases out, the retail demand should also recover in the second half of the ongoing calendar year.

items.statement: Rustproof pipes at INR6,000/ton spread; rustproof sheets lower margin; blended rustproof ~INR5,000/ton
items.quote: In pipes, we are still making INR6,000 per ton spread. In sheet, we are making lower margin. That's why on blended basis, it looks at INR5,000 per ton.

items.statement: Solar opportunity: three products - alu zinc coils for ground-mounted structures, specialized tubes for trackers (slow approvals), standard pipes for residential rooftop; small proportion now, growth expected in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Right now, the proportion is small, but over the next two, three quarters we see good volume coming from solar segment.

items.statement: Discounting INR300-350/ton currently; INR100-200/ton pullback in first 20 days of Q4
items.quote: So, Sneha till now whatever trends we see in the first 20 days of the quarter, ongoing quarter we see INR100 to INR200 per ton discounting pull off has been done by our sales team

items.statement: Balance sheet near debt-zero; residual capex funded from internal cash flows
items.quote: If you look at our balance sheet, it remains near debt zero, which is obviously backed by efficient working capital management, now that has been proven over many quarters.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on secondary steel; primary steel capacity additions (JSPL, JSW, AM/NS) will keep primary-secondary price gap ~INR10,000/ton long-term
items.quote: And when this capacity will build up the cost of production from secondary material it is almost 10,000 per ton it is less, short term maybe there is a future, bu t in long term if we see it will be sold in less rate and it will be

items.statement: 9M FY25 ROE/ROCE depressed due to Q2 profitability; will improve as earnings normalize and capacities ramp
items.quote: The nine-month ROE/ROCE looked slightly depressed because of, again, poor profitability in second quarter, but same shall improve over the coming quarters as our earn ings expand to normalized level and we ramp up our capacities

items.statement: Government infrastructure spending below budget for 9M FY25 due to new government formation and delayed fund release; recovery expected post-budget
items.quote: But we a lso read a newspaper, etcetera, what everyone is, or everyone must be reading that the government spending on infrastructure for the first 9 months has been below budget, right. That is one. And second, of course, because of new government formation and th e delayed budgets and delay in release of funds, that is impacting some overall demand for the construction sector

items.statement: New product launches: 1000mm square in Q3, Galvalume in Q4, quarterly innovation pipeline
items.period: Q3 FY25, Q4 FY25, Q1 FY26
items.quote: We have a new product of 1000 mm squa re in this quarter. In next quarter, we will have a new product of Galvalume. In Q1, Galvalume – quarter-on-quarter we will keep bringing a product for innovation

items.statement: Un-executed order book stands at 3.4 GW peak as of 9M FY25
items.quote: We are pleased to report that our un-executed order book stood at 3.4 gigawatt peak in the first nine months of financial year 2025.

items.statement: Expect 500-600 MW execution in Q4 FY25
items.quote: We expect next quarter, I mean this quarter to be of January to March, we should be doing 500 to 600 megawatt of execution, that's what we expect.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin at 19.96%; 9M FY25 at 16.5%; medium-term target maintained at 15%
items.quote: We have already guided in since 3 -odd quarters, we have been guiding that our margins must be in the range of 15%. However, we are pleased that they have turned out to be 19.96% this quarter. And for nine months ended, they are nearer to our internal calculations, which we keep saying that we should be under 15%. So 16.50% is for nine months.

items.statement: Annual execution capacity of 3-3.5 GW under current manpower
items.quote: In the current circumstances, we should be able to deliver between 3 to 3.5 gigawatt of business annually.

items.statement: 2 GW balance-of-system order from Jindal Renewables received in November; execution timeline 8-9 months
items.quote: About roughly about 8 or 9 months.

items.statement: Board approved amending object clause to enter data center EPC business; will build capabilities before bidding
items.quote: Right now, the Board has approved amending the object clause because we do want to foray into data center business.

items.statement: Cash position INR200-220 cr; only INR28 cr term loan outstanding; no funded debt raise planned; non-fund limits INR1,400 cr at 75-80% usage plus INR300 cr insurance limits
items.quote: So, our cash position is quite comfortable. We are around INR200 crores - INR220 crores of cash. Our debt position is currently only one loan that is running is around INR28 crores outstanding right now for us. We are not looking to raise any funded debt, but we are always scouting for non-fund-based limits because we need to give bank guarantees, et c, to our customers.

items.statement: Order book and pipeline skewed toward utility-scale private IPP players; government share ~30-35%
items.quote: Historically, if you witness Waaree Renewables book, it is more finding favor with utility scale IPP players, which are on the private side. And even the current order book is geared towards that. Our pipeline is also geared towards more towards larger private players as of now.

items.statement: Do not undertake unprofitable projects; per-MW realization blended at INR1-1.1 cr; BOS orders can range INR70 lakh-4 cr/MW depending on scope
items.quote: We don't undertake projects which are not profitable to us.

items.statement: India added 24.5 GW solar in 2024 (18.5 GW utility); total solar installed 97.86 GW; targeting 500 GW renewable
items.quote: The country added 24.5 gigawatts of new solar capacity in 2024, a significant surge led by utility scale solar projects, which contributed 18.5 gigawatts, almost 3 times the capacity added in 2023.

items.statement: O&M portfolio at 587 MW; expect 2-3x increase from April as projects go live
items.quote: As regards to O&M, we are sitting on right now 587 megawatts of O&M. And we have certain projects going live in March, which will get converted into O&M for us about 2x to 3x size of our current base from April onwards.

items.statement: Two subsidiaries set up for potential solar park opportunities; no land bank currently
items.quote: In fact, we have two subsidiaries we have set up for same opportunity. Tomorrow, if you have an opportunity, we'll use those subsidiaries to obtain connectivity and land for the same.

items.statement: Focus on domestic market; Middle East and US export opportunities exist but not prioritized
items.quote: See, the market is quite big in Middle East and U.S. , but we are right now focused because the domestic opportunity is also equally big.

items.statement: Competitive intensity rising with market growth; maintain margin discipline and avoid unprofitable bids
items.quote: As market grows, competition keeps growing, which I said in my previous communication also, sometimes it is good for the industry because you get the best productivity out. But as Waaree, we are very cautious on our margins and our profitability. We don't get into unnecessary competitive intensity to just bring business on board.

items.statement: No formal revenue guidance; 9M FY25 revenue INR1,121 cr; Q4 FY25 revenue implied INR500-600 cr based on 500-600 MW execution
items.quote: As a policy, we don't give guidance, but we have already delivered about INR1,120 crores of -- INR1,121 crores of revenues.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 execution 319 MW; Q2 FY25 execution 488 MW; 9M FY25 execution ~1 GW
items.quote: I have already completed 1 gigawatt in first 9 months itself. So I can't extrapolate my 319 megawatts that I have delivered in this quarter. If you look at my past quarter, we have delivered 500 megawatts of business in the last quarter, a little less than 500 megawatts maybe, but that's what we delivered. 488 megawatts was the precise number that we delivered in our previous quarter.

items.statement: No significant client-side execution delays experienced; macro demand strong with government commitment
items.quote: On the client side, projection delays, I can't comment something specific because we are always on time, and we have been delivering whatever is our commitment with customers. But from a customer side, we have not experienced any significant delays as such.

items.statement: Employee costs fixed regardless of quarterly revenue recognition; platform model provides operating leverage
items.quote: When you are putting people on site, whether you complete a project or not, you have to pay for the people's cost out there. That's what the platform business is and that leverage of people's cost in platform works both ways.

items.statement: Pipeline at 24 GW; total addressable solar market ~40 GW/year plus battery storage
items.quote: We have already said that we are now sitting on 24 gigawatt pipeline. So that's the opportunity we are sitting as of today. But the entire market of 40 gigawatts that in the solar side that comes up along with battery and these our opportunity right now.

items.statement: Green hydrogen EPC opportunity emerging; Waaree Group has 350 MW electrolyzer award; will bid for EPC portion of large-scale hydrogen projects
items.quote: Waaree Group already has a presence in hydrogen. They have been awarded 350 megawatt of electrolyzer. But as and when huge case opportunity comes up, which is likely to come up, we will definitely be bidding for EPC part of the hydrogen play as well.

items.statement: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana driving rooftop solar growth (53% increase, 4.59 GW added in 2024)
items.quote: Additionally, rooftop solar saw 53% increase with 4. 59 gigawatt added, WAAREE/RTL Execution with Pace & supported by initiatives like PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli

name: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd

items.statement: Management expects full-year ROE to be within 16-18% range and Combined Ratio to be influenced by industry outcomes and market response in Q4
items.quote: we should definitely end the year within that range of about 16% to 18%.

items.statement: Motor loss ratio target range maintained at 65-67% for medium to long term across the portfolio
items.quote: the range that we are comfortable with to operate with will be between 65% to 67% for Motor as a category.

items.statement: Retail Health loss ratio target range maintained at 65-70% for the indemnity book
items.quote: the range that we are comfortable on running the book is a loss ratio of around that range between 65% to 70%.

items.statement: IRDAI mandated 1/n premium recognition for long-term products effective October 1, 2024, impacting health and other lines reporting in Q3 FY2025
items.quote: general insurers are mandated to recognize premium for long-term products on a 1/n basis, effective October 1, 2024.

items.statement: Solvency norms changed to disallow receivables on gross basis instead of net, reducing solvency ratio by ~30 bps to 2.36x as at Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: Due to this, there is a reduction of ~30 basis points in our solvency ratio as at December 31, 2024. Consequently, our solvency ratio was 2.36x as at December 31, 2024.

items.statement: Commercial lines de-grew 8.4% industry-wide due to sluggish government capex spending impacting infrastructure and construction sectors
items.quote: The Commercial Line segment de-grew at 8.4%. Within this, the Fire segment continued to de-grow, registering a de-growth of 22.0% on account of pricing pressure.

items.statement: Retail Health grew 44.3% (19.1% on 1/n basis) vs industry 6.6%, gaining market share to 3.2% in Q3 FY2025
items.quote: Within Health, our Retail Health segment registered a growth at 44.3%. With 1/n accounting norm, the growth was at 19.1% as against industry growth of 6.6% during the same period. Resultantly, we gained market share in Retail Health, reaching 3.2% in Q3 FY2025.

items.statement: Combined ratio improved to 102.7% in Q3 FY2025 from 103.6% in Q3 FY2024; 9M FY2025 at 102.9% vs 103.7% prior year
items.quote: The Combined ratio was 102.7% in Q3 FY2025 as against 103.6% in Q3 FY2024.

items.statement: Motor combined ratio target 65-67% loss ratio range maintained; current outcome below range due to favorable loss development and mix
items.quote: the range that we have spoken about running overall motor in that range of 65% to 67%, I think that's broadly the range that we believe we should continue to see as an outcome in terms of the portfolio experience.

items.statement: Health loss ratios: Corporate Health 97.2% in Q3 FY2025 (93.1% prior year), Retail Indemnity 65% in Q3 FY2025 (66% prior year)
items.quote: for Corporate Health, Q3 FY2024, that number was 93.1%, that number for Q3 FY2025 is at 97.2%. And Retail Indemnity numbers last year was 66%, which is down to about 65%.

items.statement: Fire segment pricing expected to improve in coming months after 22% de-growth due to pricing pressure
items.quote: We expect the pricing to improve in the Fire segment in the coming months.

items.statement: Motor TP tariff hike expected after 3-4 years, possibly for next financial year, though timing depends on regulator and MoRTH
items.quote: we do believe, yes, it's been 3 to 4 years and there might be possibly a hike at least which we'll get for next financial year.

items.statement: Health Retail Indemnity price hikes not ruled out if portfolio warrants; previous hikes of 8% and 20-22% implemented in past years
items.quote: if the portfolio warrants any price revision, we will not shy away from taking one.

items.statement: Motor advance premium at ₹36.44 billion as at Dec 31, 2024, up from ₹35.13 billion at Sep 30, 2024
items.quote: The advance premium numbers for the Motor segment was ₹ 36.44 billion as at December 31, 2024, as against ₹ 35.13 billion as at September 30, 2024.

items.statement: Agent count including POS increased to 140,077 as at Dec 31, 2024 from 133,683 at Sep 30, 2024
items.quote: Our agents, which included the point-of-sale distribution count was 1,40,077 as at December 31, 2024, up from 1,33,683 as at September 30, 2024.

items.statement: Motor portfolio mix in Q3 FY2025: Private Car 52.9%, Two-wheeler 26.7%, CV 20.4%
items.quote: During the quarter, we sustained a balanced portfolio with a mix of private car, two-wheeler and CV at 52.9%, 26.7% and 20.4% respectively.

items.statement: Motor new and old vehicle growth similar at 9.5% and 9.3% respectively in Q3 FY2025
items.quote: new was again, 9.5% which is what I just mentioned in response to one of the calls, largely the numbers were similar. 9.5% growth for new and almost a similar number of 9.3% for the old.

items.statement: IL TakeCare App surpassed 13.2 million downloads, generating ₹664.2 million premium in Q3 FY2025
items.quote: During the quarter, our IL TakeCare App has surpassed 13.2 million user downloads registering a premium of ₹ 664.2 million for Q3 FY2025.

items.statement: Preferred Partner Network serviced 73.6% of Non-OEM claims in Q3 FY2025 vs 67.3% in Q3 FY2024
items.quote: Our Preferred Partner Network (PPN) serviced 73.6% of our Non-OEM claims in Q3 FY2025 as against 67.3% in Q3 FY2024.

items.statement: Average claim settlement improved: Motor OD from 6 days (FY2024) to 5 days (9M FY2025); Health from 5 days to 3 days
items.quote: Our average claim settlement period on Retail line of business has seen improvement. It has improved from 6 days in FY2024 to 5 days in 9M FY2025 for Motor OD, and from 5 days in FY2024 to 3 days in 9M FY2025 for Health.

items.statement: NPS healthy at 69 for Health and 65 for Motor claims in H1 FY2025
items.quote: Our NPS continues to be healthy at 69 and 65 for H1 FY2025 for Health and Motor claims respectively, supported by customer trust.

items.statement: Investment leverage (net of borrowings) at 3.76x as at Dec 31, 2024 vs 3.91x at Sep 30, 2024
items.quote: Our investment leverage (net of borrowings) was 3.76x as at December 31, 2024 as against 3.91x as at September 30, 2024.

items.statement: ROAE at 20.8% for 9M FY2025 vs 17.1% prior year; Q3 FY2025 at 21.5% vs 15.3%
items.quote: Return on Average Equity (ROAE) was 20.8% in 9M FY2025 as against 17.1% in 9M FY2025. The ROAE for Q3 FY2025 was 21.5% as against 15.3% in Q3 FY2024.

items.statement: Investment income grew to ₹33.73 billion in 9M FY2025 from ₹26.57 billion; Q3 FY2025 at ₹11.21 billion vs ₹8.57 billion
items.quote: Investment income was at ₹ 33.73 billion in 9M FY2025 as against ₹ 26.57 billion in 9M FY2024. On a quarterly basis, investment income was ₹ 11.21 billion in Q3 FY2025 as against ₹ 8.57 billion in Q3 FY2024.

items.statement: Capital gains (net of impairment) at ₹7.96 billion in 9M FY2025 vs ₹3.95 billion; Q3 FY2025 at ₹2.76 billion vs ₹1.08 billion
items.quote: Our capital gains (net of impairment in investment assets) stood at ₹ 7.96 billion in 9M FY2025 as compared to ₹ 3.95 billion in 9 FY2024. Capital gains (net of impairment) on investment assets stood at ₹ 2.76 billion in Q3 FY2025 as compared to ₹ 1.08 billion in Q3 FY2024

items.statement: Management will withdraw from business lines like GHI and Fire if pricing goes below commercial viability threshold rather than violate EoM guidelines
items.quote: If you see business lines like GHI and some others, further going low, we would abstain rather than participate. So we have absolute clarity as a team to let go what is not making commercial sense for us.

items.statement: 1/n accounting impact on profits varies by business mix, reinsurance structures and acquisition costs; Q3 outcome showed higher profit due to deferral of acquisition costs on long-term retail business
items.quote: In a quarter, if you do see businesses where you already had an element of a reinsurance arrangement, and if that business gets subdued, and therefore, the relative impact in outcome will not necessarily be the same as compared to a line of business, for example, in Quarter 3, we also have contracts of other lines of businesses, where we don't have a reinsurance arrangement, but there's a cost of

items.statement: Management reiterated full-year outlook of 18-20% APE growth and VNB growth upwards of 15%.
items.quote: we basically said that we will try and get to 18% -20% APE growth and try and deliver a VNB growth of upwards of 15%.

items.statement: Individual WRP grew 22% YoY in 9MFY25, outpacing private industry (19%) and overall sector (14%).
items.quote: We have registered a healthy growth of 22%, based on individual WRP for 9MFY25, outpacing private industry and overall sector growth of 19% and 14% respectively.

items.statement: Individual APE mix in 9MFY25: ULIPs 37%, non-par savings 35%, participating 18%, term 6%, annuities 5%.
items.quote: Individual APE in 9M was composed of ULIPs: 37%, non -par savings: 35%, participating policies: 18%, term: 6%, and annuities: 5%.

items.statement: VNB margin for 9MFY25 was 25.1%, down from 26.5% YoY, mainly due to product mix shift to ULIPs and 10 bps surrender regulation impact.
items.quote: Value of new business for the 9M period was Rs. 2,586 crores, reflecting a 14% YoY growth. New business margin for the 9-month period was 25.1%, with the compression mainly attributable to changes in product mix in line with macro trends.

items.statement: Q3 VNB margin was 26%, up ~60-70 bps sequentially on normalized basis, driven by better ULIP margins from higher persistency and protection attachment, offset by 30 bps surrender regulation impact.
items.quote: the margins are expanded by about 60 bps if we were to look at it from that perspective. And that is largely on account of inherent product margins being a lot better now, especially on the Unit Linked segment because of two reasons; o ne is our persistency has improved significantly and second is our level of protection that we are able to attach on Unit Linked products is a lot higher than what

items.statement: Surrender value regulations implemented Oct 1; gross margin impact 100 bps, net impact 30 bps in Q3 and 10 bps for 9M after commission clawbacks, deferrals, and reductions.
items.quote: We're basically talking about on a nine-month basis, a 10-basis points impact, and on a quarter basis, about 30 basis points impact of the surrender value regulation implementation.

items.statement: Management expects annualized surrender regulation impact to be 20-30 bps going forward, with no further benefit in Q4 from distribution arrangements.
items.quote: our endeavor will be to try and keep it as close to 20 -30 bps on an annualized basis going forward as well because that's basically more in terms of sharing this burden with our distributors and leaving our customer proposition intact.

items.statement: Non-par savings APE grew 55% YoY in 9MFY25; retail protection APE grew 28%; credit protect growth tepid due to slower MFI disbursements.
items.quote: Non-par savings products sustained their strong growth, growing by 55% YoY. Retail protection continues to grow well, with APE for nine months clocking a growth of 28%. Credit protect growth has been tepid due to slower disbursements amongst specific part ners and the MFI sector, in particular

items.statement: Over 70% of customers acquired in 9MFY25 are new to HDFC Life; lives insured crossed 36 million.
items.quote: Over 70% of the customers acquired during this period are new to HDFC Life, demonstrating progress towards our objective to expand our customer base. Retail sum assured has grown by 22% YoY for this p eriod. We continue to clock secular growth across tier 1, 2 and 3 cities with number of lives insured crossing 36 million during 9M FY25.

items.statement: All channels registered double-digit growth; HDFC Bank counter share stable at ~65% in 9MFY25; agency growth 19% YoY in 9MFY25.
items.quote: All channels registered healthy double-digit growth. Our counter share at HDFC Bank has remained stable at close to 65% in 9M FY25. We are focused on building a profitable, high -quality Agency franchise and are happy to report that protection business sourced by this channel grew more than 2x when compared to our overall growth in protection of 28%.

items.statement: HDFC Bank channel grew 20% YoY for 9M and ~10% in Q3; bancassurance is 35% of new business premium (received premium basis), HDFC Bank ~1/4th.
items.quote: for the year, we have seen HDFC Bank growing at 20%. And for the quarter, it's around 10%, where we have seen the base impact of last year also coming in.

items.statement: Added ~65 new branches in 9MFY25; branch expansion to continue.
items.quote: We also added a lot of agents in this year. We've also expanded by adding nearly 65* branches this year, that expansion of branches will also continue.

items.statement: 13th month persistency 87% (+110 bps YoY), 61st month persistency 61% (+780 bps YoY) in 9MFY25.
items.quote: 13th and 61st month persistency stood at 87% and 61%, an increase of 110 and 780 bps respectively.

items.statement: Profit after tax grew 15% YoY to Rs 1,326 crore; renewal collections grew 12% YoY.
items.quote: Profit after tax grew 15% YoY to Rs. 1,326 crores, driven by an 18% increase in profit emergence from our back book. Renewal collections grew by 12% YoY.

items.statement: HDFC Pension AUM Rs 1.06 lakh crore, market share 43.2%; HDFC International maintains S&P BBB and AM Best B++ ratings.
items.quote: HDFC Pension continues to be one of the fastest growing pension fund management company in the industry, enjoying a market share of 43.2% and an AUM of Rs 1.06 lakh crore.

items.statement: Peers have revised non-par IRRs down, annuity prices down, term prices up; HDFC Life has not changed pricing. Market share expanded 70 bps to 10.8% overall, 15.3% private.
items.quote: We have seen non -par pricing, non -par IRRs come down. We've seen annuity prices being revised downwards. We've also seen term prices increase. So, we've seen a combination of all these measures across the sector.

items.statement: No changes to pricing on protection, non-par savings, or annuities despite peer revisions; disciplined pricing approach maintained.
items.quote: we have not made any changes to our pricing, whether it's on protection or non-par savings or annuities, but we definitely have seen some downward revision in pricing from some of our peers.

items.statement: New business strain grew 13% for 9M, in line with new business growth; EB surplus grew 18%. Non-par savings growth (55%) outpaced back book surplus generation, causing negative segment surplus.
items.quote: So, if you look at the growth in the New Business Strain , it's only 13% for the nine months, which is in line with the new business growth. And the EB surplus has grown by 18%, which is in the range that we have always explained.

items.statement: No communication from regulator on bancassurance limits; only media reports. Management focused on diversification, open architecture, and reducing concentration risk.
items.quote: We've only heard it from media sources. We haven't heard anything at all from our regulator. At the same time, if misselling is the purpose then misselling complaints is something that we anyway work on.

items.statement: Agency channel added many agents; growth recovered to 19% in 9MFY25 after tax change impact last year; term contribution highest in agency.
items.quote: the agency growth this year has been 19%, which is quite in line with what we have grown as an organization. Last year we had seen a lower growth and that largely came in from the impact that we have on greater than Rs 5 lakh regulation which changed there the tax benefit was changed.

items.statement: Exploring inorganic solutions for distribution diversification beyond organic channel expansion.
items.quote: And there are many other things also up our sleeve in terms of not only organic but also inorganic solutions.

items.statement: Project Inspire first phase (group business module) partially deployed; enables automated onboarding, straight-through claims, real-time communication.
items.quote: We are excited to announce the partial deployment of the first phase of Project Inspire, which includes the group business module. We expect our partners and members covered to avail of benefits such as automated member onboarding, issuance of Certificates of Insurance, straight through claims processing, payouts and real -time communication.

items.statement: Expects to maintain healthy above 20% growth for a long period and reach net margin around 20% and operating margin around 23% this year if top line momentum continues
items.quote: We don't see any broad reduction on our growth prospects. We think that we can continue maintaining a healthy above 20% growth for a long period of time.

items.statement: 90% of deals signed in nine months FY25 expected to flow into revenue in FY26
items.quote: Yes. I think we should assume that 90% will flow in FY '26.

items.statement: Targets $500 million revenue in next three to four years with mature markets as primary strategy
items.quote: And we do think that our next three, four years are the timeframes where we think should be able to do things, so that we can be closer to that goal.

items.statement: India banking deposit growth weakness causing slowdown in digital lending projects but new generation NBFCs investing to gain market share
items.quote: So while we see there is a bit of slowdown in the overall momentum of digital lending projects, but on the other hand, the new generation NBFCs, they are right now in the position to go and invest in the market to gain market share.

items.statement: U.S. banking space picking up; hopeful to start winning banking deals this quarter and next quarter
items.quote: As for the U.S., we do see -- we are hopeful that the U.S. banking space is picking up, and I think the larger players have a very different business than ours. But we are hopeful that this quarter and next quarter, we should start winning some banking deals in U.S.

items.statement: Added 15 new logos in Q3 FY25 and 36 new logos in nine months FY25
items.quote: In total, we have added 15 new logos in Q3. Over the nine months period, we have added 36 new logos.

items.statement: Won RBI order for Regulatory Application Management System worth INR32 crores; Aye Finance loan origination INR24 crores; Saudi power company $2.3M; Singapore records management SGD1.7M; U.S. banking digital account opening $1.8M; India rem
items.value: INR32 crores, INR24 crores, $2.3M, SGD1.7M, $1.8M, INR20.8 crores, $2M, $1.6M
items.quote: We have won an order from RBI for implementation and maintenance of the Regulatory Application Management System with an aggregate contract value of INR32 crores. Our expertise in data science and AI embedded in our core products have contributed to our success in the RBI bid, and we plan to work with other financial institutions as well. In India, we also entered into an agreement with Aye Financ

items.statement: Q3 PAT INR89 crores, up 30% YoY; nine-month PAT INR207 crores, up 41% YoY; margins expanding due to revenue growth above budgeted 18-20%
items.quote: Profit after tax was at INR89 crores for the quarter, witnessing a growth of 30% Y-o-Y. For the nine months period, our revenues were INR1,057 crores, witnessing a growth of 22%. Profit after tax was INR207 crores, witnessing a growth of 41%.

items.statement: Expects Q4 margins slightly better and full-year net margin near 20%, operating margin near 23% if top line momentum holds
items.quote: So I personally feel that this will still expand maybe 0.5 basis points or 1% more by the year. So we will reach there close to 20% and 23% what we had initially planned, if we continue to maintain our top line moment.

items.statement: R&D expenses 9% of revenue; sales and marketing expenses 22% of revenue in nine months FY25
items.quote: Our investment in building capabilities across the organization for the next level is reflected in our R&D and sales and marketing expenses. R&D expenses were 9% of revenues and sales and marketing expenses were at 22%.

items.statement: Annuity revenues INR208 crores in Q3; license growth broad-based across all regions; implementation cycles lengthening beyond one year for large projects delaying downstream ATS/support revenue
items.quote: Annuity revenues were at INR208 crores. While deal velocity has been very good, our projects now have longer execution cycle due to the level of complexity we are handling. This has led to the implementation cycle moving beyond one year for some of our larger projects.

items.statement: ~80-85% revenue from existing clients; new license deals often from mining existing accounts
items.quote: If you look at it, around 80%, 85% comes from existing clients. Because even a lot of new license deals are from existing clients, because they're about mining of those records.

items.statement: AI (Marvin, Harper, Number Theory) now central to sales; AI-enabled digital lending and RBI deal are AI-centered; bundling AI with NewgenONE/ECM platform
items.quote: Most of our sales today, AI is very central to that sale. So most of the use cases have to be either complemented or they have been centered around AI. So some of the recent deals, whether they are in the part of AI-enabled digital lending or what we got from the Central Bank, the RBI, they are completely AI-centered deals.

items.statement: ~50 person dedicated AI team; will expand organically over next 2-3 years; not a services model so headcount not scaling linearly
items.period: Q3 FY25, next two, three years
items.quote: We have a team of roughly around 50 people right now dedicated for AI, who are creating our products and helping our customers on that. I think this team will expand organically over a period of time, and we are continuously looking at augmenting good talent out there.

items.statement: Net trade receivables INR463 crores as of Dec 31; net DSO 118 days
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, our net trade receivables were at INR463 crores as of 31st December, which resulted in net DSO of 118 days.

items.statement: Large public sector/Tier 1 projects in India started parallelly causing implementation delays; learning curve not captured across projects; now able to deliver new projects in 8-9 months
items.quote: Last two years, I think we would have started more than 20, 25 digital lending projects all parallelly together. So some of the learnings from one another has not been caught on so actively. But I think now if we are going to take a project today, I think we can easily deliver it in eight, nine months with the whole comprehensive things.

items.statement: Implementation delays hurt both client and Newgen but transformative value justifies delay; delay of 1-2 quarters not affecting business model broadly
items.quote: See, it is joined. So finally, there is no project plan which is not in sync with the client. And I think whatever you are selling to the clients are extremely critical for their business. So they want to go live as soon. So any delay does hurt them and does hurt us, both of us. But I think we are in sync with the client. But the -- see, one of the things is the value we deliver at the end of the

items.statement: Expect 25-30% revenue growth to continue sustainably
items.quote: And the existing growth rate will continue, means every year around we hope 25% to 30% growth it will continue.

items.statement: Expect PLI income of INR9-10 crores this fiscal, recognized upon approval in Q1 or Q2 next year
items.quote: Yes, yes. Every quarter. I think this year, we hope we'll expect around INR9 crores to INR10 crores of PLI income. Once approval is received, then we'll recognize. Maybe in next year first quarter or second quarter it may be.

items.statement: Payback period for recent investments is around 3 years
items.quote: Yes, yes. The payback period, it would be around 3 years.

items.statement: Old MCC capacity running at 90-98% utilization
items.quote: Old capacity is already hovering around 90%, 95%, 98%.

items.statement: CCS plant environmental clearance expected in 4 weeks, then civil works to commence
items.quote: So I'm expecting the environmental clearance in the next 4 weeks. So there has been a file movement in the last 2 weeks. And I believe once the environmental clearance comes in, we will commence our civil works for the CCS project.

items.statement: Margins declined in Q2/Q3 due to price reductions to penetrate market with new capacity; expected to improve as utilization rises and prices increase gradually
items.quote: Because we expanded capacities comes into operational, then we are -- to penetrate into the market, some price reductions we've done. And then once that is settled down, slowly, gradually, we'll increase, and then our margins will also go up.

items.statement: API margins currently low domestically; will improve upon CEP approvals and entry into regulated markets
items.quote: Once we get the CEP filings and once we enter into a regulatory market, then the margins are higher side, and then we'll scale up the operations also, then we hope our profits also will increase in API business also.

items.statement: Middle East subsidiary (Sigachi Arabia) expected to turn profitable in next 2 quarters as volumes ramp up
items.quote: Going forward, maybe in another 2 quarters, we hope we'll see a positive margin, positive figures there.

items.statement: 9-month MCC volume of 12,682 MT nearly matches full-year FY24 volume of 13,469 MT
items.quote: Now during 9 months, we achieved 12,682 metric tons, which is combined. In 9 months itself, almost we'll be reaching 13,649 metric tons, last year's full turnover.

items.statement: API revenue share expected to exceed 15% by FY27, potentially 25-30%
items.quote: Can we expect about 15% coming in from APIs? O.Subbarami Reddy: Yes, yes. We hope -- more than that actually. It is more than. Far, far more than that we are expecting

items.statement: Sultanpur facility audited and approved by Intertek on behalf of GAIN, enabling global supply of vitamin/mineral premixes
items.quote: I'm also proud to share that our Sultanpur facility has been audited and approved by Intertek on behalf of Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition, that is GAIN. This recognition reaffirms our dedication to the highest quality standards, enabling us to supply our premium base blend brand of vitamins and minerals premixes to clients worldwide.

items.statement: DSO at ~107 days, target to reduce to 90 days; inventory built up anticipating wood pulp price rise, now stopping further stock build
items.quote: Receivables, now we have given little leverage to the customers. Recently, we have given instructions to our sales team to bring it down to 90 days. Now it is there around 107 days is there, the DSO days. And now we have advised to reduce it to 90 days.

items.statement: Export collection issues due to customer currency/regulatory constraints; >50% of stuck receivables recovered, balance coming; now requiring LCs or advances
items.quote: Initially, there was a problem in certain countries that even though the customers are rich and then they wanted to pay it, but their local regulations and the foreign currency issues, they couldn't pay. Now we are getting it. And also, we are taking corrective action also. Going forward, if any such kind of issues are there, we are asking for LCs or advances.

items.statement: Preferential allotment: INR286.45 crores raised, INR122 crores received by quarter end, INR16 crores more since; INR100 crores used for Trimax API unit acquisition (80%), balance 20% over 3 years
items.quote: In preferential, INR286.45 crores we have raised. So far, we have received -- till quarter ending, 31st, we have received INR122 crores. And in that, we have spent towards the acquisition of our Trimax API unit. That total API unit cost is INR125 crores, and 80%, it is already acquired for INR100 crores, and the balance 20% we'll be going to acquire within a period of 3 years.

items.statement: CARE Ratings reaffirmed CARE A- (long-term) and CARE A2 (long/short-term) with stable outlook
items.quote: CARE Ratings Limited has reaffirmed Sigachi Industries Limited's credit rating for its bank facilities, maintaining a stable outlook with a rating of CARE A- for long-term facilities and CARE A2 for long-term/short-term facilities.

items.statement: Q3 FY25: Operating income INR139.41 crores (+25.7% YoY), EBITDA INR33.2 crores (+46.9% YoY, 23.81% margin), PAT INR20.51 crores (+26.5% YoY, 14.7% margin)
items.quote: Operating income increased by 25.7% year-on-year, reaching INR139.41 crores. EBITDA witnessed a significant growth, rising 46.9% year-on-year to INR33.2 crores with an EBITDA margin of 23.81%. Net profit surged by 26.54% year-on-year to INR20.51 crores, translating into a PAT margin of 14.7%.

items.statement: MCC segment revenue +56.7% YoY to INR115.24 crores; O&M +12.9% to INR9.88 crores; API INR8.85 crores
items.quote: Revenue from the MCC segment rose by 56.72% year-on-year, increasing from INR73.53 crores in Q3 FY '24 to INR115.24 crores in Q3 FY '25. Revenue from the O&M segment grew by 12.91% year-on-year to INR9.88 crores, while the API segment continued INR8.85 crores during Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Raw material prices not a constraint; sourcing competitively; any increases can be passed to customers
items.quote: Raw material prices is never a constraint, but we are getting at most competitive prices, and we are sourcing at the right time, and it's not an issue. Even whatever the increase is there further that can be passed on to the customers.

items.statement: Finance costs doubled QoQ due to higher working capital needs from increased DSO and inventory buildup
items.quote: The major reason is the company is growing and a lot of amount towards working capital, it is there, because the DSOs also -- there is an increase in DSOs and now we are trying to reduce the DSO, debtors outstanding. And also the inventory also, it is in the higher side is there, because with an anticipation to increase the prices of wood pulp, we have kept it, huge inventory.

items.statement: Trimax API unit acquisition: USFDA-approved facility for advanced intermediates, purchased for INR125 crores (80% paid, 20% over 3 years with call option)
items.quote: That total API unit cost is INR125 crores, and 80%, it is already acquired for INR100 crores, and the balance 20% we'll be going to acquire within a period of 3 years, and there is a purchaser's call option, we can exercise it.

items.statement: No management changes discussed; focus on R&D and quality as core pillars
items.quote: I would like to emphasize that Sigachi's unwavering commitment to R&D has been instrumental in broadening our product portfolio. The company delivers exceptional products across pharma API intermediates, pharma excipients, film coating, and food and nutrition segments.

items.statement: FY25 presales guidance of INR7,000-8,000 crores remains intact with Q4 launches and sustenance sales
items.quote: Harsh, so apart from the launches, there are also sustenance sales. So, with a combination of both that we are pretty reasonably confident that we will be able to achieve this promised target.

items.statement: No presales guidance given for FY26; will assess after Q4 performance
items.quote: So, we'll refrain from giving any guidance at this point of time. Let's see about the quarter 4.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 booking value up 257% YoY to INR675 crores; collections up 175% YoY to INR501 crores
items.quote: Q3 FY'25, the real estate business performed very well with booking value increasing by 257%. Year-on-year to INR675 crores at our already launched projects and collection increased by 175% year-on-year to INR501 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 launches of ~INR8,000 crores GDV across 6 projects including Birla Trimaya, Sangamwadi, Sector 31 Gurgaon, Barmalt, Sarjapur, Navya Phase 2
items.quote: So together, we expect to launch about INR8,000 crores of new projects worth of inventory.

items.statement: Birla Niyaara Tower 1: 400/414 units sold; Tower 2: 86/148 units sold; Tower 3 planned for FY26
items.quote: Yes, so in the first tower, about 400 units are sold out of 414. Second tower, about 86 units are sold out of 148.

items.statement: FY25 construction spend ~INR1,800 crores; positive operating cash flow of INR500+ crores from ongoing projects
items.quote: Around INR1,800 crores is our construction spend going to be this year, roughly.

items.statement: Real estate project margins 25-35% for ongoing and upcoming; Worli projects ~45% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Ongoing, it roughly takes 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Pulp & Paper Q3 FY25 EBITDA down 79% YoY; NSR down 6% YoY, 3% QoQ; volumes down 15-16% YoY
items.quote: Average net sales realization for the quarter were down by 6% year -on-year and 3% vis-à-vis previous quarter. While production volume fell by around 15% year -on-year, sales volume decreased by 16% year -on-year. That resulted in EBITDA declining by 79% year-on-year.

items.statement: Imported pulp cost up ~17% YoY; domestic wood cost up ~6.5% YoY; cost pressures to continue near-term
items.quote: The wood prices have gone up by close to around 6.5% from last year and imported pulp has gone up close to almost 17-odd percent up. So that pressure will continue.

items.statement: Paper & board Q4 FY25: writing & printing prices recovered end of Q3, expected higher in Q4; tissue segment challenging due to new entrants and adverse demand-supply
items.quote: On the market outlook prices have recovered in writing and printing paper segment at the end of Q3 and Q4, realizations are expected to be higher, while the operating environment in the tissue segment is expected to be challenging in Q4.

items.statement: No capacity additions planned in pulp & paper; focus on cost reduction via bagasse pulp trial, bamboo usage increased to 31% in Fiberline, chipper capacity for wood chip storage
items.quote: The company continued to implement various cost reduction initiative to counter these market conditions, like trial of using bagasse pulp in middle layer of board without compromising on quality. Bamboo usage in Fiberline was increased from 14% in Q1 to 31% in Q3 to reduce cost of captive

items.statement: Net debt near 1.1x equity comfort level; Q4 collections of INR1,000-1,200 crores expected to reduce net debt; INR5,000 crores receivable over 2-3 years from launched projects
items.quote: So yes, the comfortable level for us will be somewhere around 1.1 of the equity. And I know we are very close to it. But then the thing you have to understand is we have these launches. So a lot of cash is expected to come roughly to -- even if you take 20 % of what we are going to launch, that would be about INR1,000 -odd crores at least that will come. That will help in reducing the net debt to

items.statement: Supreme Court order on Worli West 6.5-acre lease land: ~INR5,000 crores GDV impact, ~6.8 lakh sq ft FSI; no impact on Birla Niyaara; rehabilitation liabilities transfer to BMC if land lost
items.quote: The lease land, which is under Supreme Court order measuring to 25,544 square meters or equivalent to 6.31 acres under the development potential of approximately 5 lakhs square feet to INR5,000 crores booking potential. This has no impact on Birla Niyaara project, as land parcel are different.

items.statement: Acquired 70-acre land parcel in Boisar for plotted development (~INR500 crores GDV); launch expected FY26 H1; BD pipeline robust with INR23,000 crores added this year
items.quote: We acquired a 70 acres land parcel in Boisar for our first ever plotted development project.

items.statement: Real estate: FY25 collections INR1,600+ crores YTD; expect additional INR1,000-1,200 crores in Q4; net operating cash flow INR500+ crores
items.quote: So collections, of course, we have collected INR1,600-plus crores last quarter, which is already higher than what we collected the whole of last year. And through all these launches and further handovers, etcetera, we are reasonably confident of adding ano ther INR1,000 to INR1,200 crores in that range

items.statement: Revenue mix shifting toward real estate; pulp & paper turnover to marginally improve via capacity utilization and NSR; no capacity additions planned
items.quote: So yes. I mean our focus in terms of revenue growth is going to be in the real estate sector, because we have no plans to add any capacities in our pulp and paper business. So gradually, you will see the turnover amount increasing in favor of the real estate business.

items.statement: Pulp & paper: 5-6% cost disadvantage vs peers due to older plant, locational logistics, lack of captive mechanical pulp, imported pulp pricing; antidumping case not strong
items.quote: Usually, we have a little bit of a cost disadvantage of close to about 5% to 6% vis-a-vis our premier competitors.

items.statement: Luxury segment (Walkeshwar, Silas) seeing strong footfalls and traction; Q4 typically high-action period for >INR10 crore units
items.quote: But I can be confident in saying that we are getting a lot of traction in both these projects, a lot of interest is being shown, people are coming and going.

items.statement: Domestic wood prices expected to sustain, not decline; imported pulp pressure continues due to rupee depreciation; no wood imports
items.quote: Mostly, we expect them to be at least sustained. But we don't expect it to considerably go down.

items.statement: Paperboard import pressure slowing due to rupee depreciation; domestic capacity additions (ITC, JK) maintaining competitive intensity
items.quote: Well, I think it would probably always be there. And now with particularly rupee depreciating also would probably slow it down a bit in my opinion. So, the pressure may be there, but it won't be as intense it was in this financial year.

items.statement: Noida project pending conditions precedent from land JV partner; no timeline; Mathura Road Delhi approvals pending post-elections; Century Bhavan ~INR4,000 crores potential, strategy under review
items.quote: Yes. So, Noida is still work in progress. As I mentioned last time, there are a few conditions precedent, which still is being handled by the land JV partner, the landowner. So, unless that is complied with, we are in no position to declare or talk about it.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 volume target of ~350,000 tonnes, implying ~8% growth over FY24's 325,000 tonnes
items.quote: the last year, we sold total volumes of 325,000 tonnes. And we maintain that we should have a volume growth of around 8% for the full financial year. We should be doing around 350,000 tonnes this year

items.statement: Q4 FY25 volume expected at ~96,000 tonnes, similar to Q4 FY24
items.quote: More or less, we should

items.statement: Mass ABS Phase 1 (70,000 tpa) mechanical completion by end March 2025, commissioning in Q1 FY26
items.quote: the implementation of our first phase of Mass ABS Project, with capacity of 70,000 tonnes per annum is progressing well, and the mechanical completion is expected by end March of 2025, with commissioning scheduled for Q1 FY'26.

items.statement: Haryana plant pre-project activities started; site implementation expected to begin Q3 FY26 with ~INR 800 crore capex
items.quote: We are working on the Haryana plant,. The pre-project activities have started. We expect that towards the third quarter of FY '26, we should be starting the project implementation at the site.

items.statement: Mass ABS Phase 2 hoped to start in FY26
items.quote: Phase-2 of ABS, also, we hope to start in the coming financial year

items.statement: Haryana plant planned capacities: Polystyrene 100,000 tpa, EPS 50,000 tpa, XPS 100,000 cubic meters, 3D panels 1 million sqm, sheeting 1 million sqm
items.value: 100,000 tpa PS, 50,000 tpa EPS, 100,000 cubic meters XPS
items.quote: Polystyrene would be 100,000 tonnes, EPS would be 50,000 tonnes, and the 100,000;NZ meters for XPS. And for the 3D panels, it will be, again, 1 million square meters and similarly for the sheeting business

items.statement: Mass ABS expected to lift EBITDA from high single-digit to double-digit over time
items.quote: With the Mass ABS coming in, and their volumes going up, and with the second line of Mass ABS coming up, we expect that, we should from high single-digit EBITDA, cross to double digits then.

items.statement: Value-added grades (specialty PS, flame-retardant EPS, SPC compounds, XPS) constitute 38-40% of business
items.quote: They are around 38% to 40% of our business' lt is the business where we have better margins than the normal grades

items.statement: XPS ramp-up to full utilization (current 50k + expanded 100k) expected in 2-3 years via marketing, roadshows, architecture college outreach
items.quote: we hope that now in the near future, in the next 2 to 3 years, we should be able to load not only the current capacity, but also the expanded capacity.

items.statement: Mass ABS customer discussions ongoing with Versalis collaboration; confident of selling full volume post-commissioning
items.quote: our discussions with some of our customers are already on, with the help from our collaborators. So once the product is out, we are confident that we should be able to sell the product comfortably.

items.statement: Mass ABS working capital cycle expected similar to current business
items.quote: Yes, we expect the same.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with INR 680 crore investible surplus as of Dec 2024
items.quote: The Company remains debt-free with an investible surplus of INR 680 crore at the end of December 2024, and is continuing to invest in all its capital programs through internal accruals and reserves,

items.statement: Exports ~45,000 tonnes, mainly polystyrene to OEMs and XPS manufacturers in Italy, Greece, Turkey, Egypt, Bangladesh; freight rates 3x pre-pandemic hurting export margins
items.quote: We export to the OEMS, we export to the XPS manufacturers. ln ltaly and in Greece, we export to some customer who uses it for XPS' Customers in Turkey or Egypt or Bangladesh are OEMs

items.statement: Hedging policy: 50-65% of forex exposure hedged depending on USD-INR dynamics; export revenue provides natural hedge
items.quote: we hedge, Generally, we are always hedged to the extent of 50% to 65%, depending upon the dynamics of the dollar-rupee. But in any case, the depreciation impacting our cost is also built in our selling prices.

items.statement: Solar power installations at maximum permissible limit; saving 25% of power cost; will add solar for ABS incremental power needs
items.quote: based on our installed solar power and our consumption, we have been able to save 25% ol our power cost.

items.statement: XPS lacks ISA certification, limiting government/PWD approvals; CPWD and some state PWDs have approved; working with Bureau of Energy Efficiency for insulation mandates
items.quote: However, on the government side, since we don't have ISA certification in our XPS, so that seems to be a barrier and PWD does not grant approval.

items.statement: No EBITDA/spread guidance for FY26/FY27 due to dependence on global deltas in NE/SE Asia
items.quote: I can't give you any guidance on those, Aditya, because the base spreads are all determined by the global deltas, prevailing the Northeast Asian countries and Southeast Asian countries. So it is very difficult to predict that.

items.statement: SPC compounds business expected to double in 2 years driven by ABS compounding
items.quote: The SPC business, with our ABS coming online, we should be able to grow it very fast. And I expect that in the next 2 years, we should be able to double the compound business.

items.statement: Company maintains 15-16% volume growth guidance for Plastic Piping System in FY25 but cites uncertainty due to PVC prices
items.quote: We said we are talking 3 % to 4% more than the country growth, but specifically number on Plastic Piping System, we maintain still 15% to 16%, but in uncertain time we are scared to give any number, but definitely we are confident we will grow more than the country.

items.statement: Company expects overall operating margin of 13.5-14% for FY25
items.quote: We anticipate this year the margin may be between 13.5% to 14% overall.

items.statement: Highest ever planned capex of Rs 1500 crore for FY25 including carry-forward commitments
items.quote: Looking at the business outlook and opportunities, the Company has planned and committed the highest capex (including carry forward commitments) of around Rs. 1500 Crs.

items.statement: Cash outflow of Rs 718 crore in first nine months, likely to reach Rs 1000 crore for full year
items.quote: Total cash outflow towards capex has been Rs. 718 crores during first nine months and is likely to reach around Rs. 1000 crores for the year.

items.statement: Plastic Piping capacity reached 820,000 MT as of Dec 2024, will reach 900,000 MT by end of FY25
items.quote: The company has reached to annual capacity of 8,20,000 M.T. as on 31st December 2024 and with completion of all the expansion plans undertaken in hand, total installed capacities of the Piping System Business Vertical shall reach 9,00,000 M.T. per annum by the end of FY 24-25.

items.statement: Three new greenfield plants for Plastic Piping at Jammu, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh to be executed in FY26
items.quote: Three new greenfield plants for Plastic piping division at Jammu, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh shall be taken up for execution in the coming financial year.

items.statement: Window manufacturing facility at Kanpur Dehat with 5,000 tons annual capacity to launch in H1 FY26
items.quote: First, I must clarify that we are not going to sell profile. We are going to supply completely customized window and our annual capacity is 5,000 tons per annum.

items.statement: Agri demand wiped out in Q3 due to extended rains, housing demand low but present, infra demand non-existent
items.quote: In third quarter, demand was very weak. In third quarter, In Agri the demand was wiped out. And housing demand was also not so robust but the demand was there. And infra demand has not picked up.

items.statement: Good demand expected in Q4 from Agri and Housing segments as distribution pipeline has de-stocked
items.quote: The Company expects good demand from Agri and Housing segments for the last quarter. The entire distribution pipeline has de-stocked seeing the continued fall in prices.

items.statement: CPVC volume grew over 20% in nine months FY25
items.quote: CPVC market definitely has grown better. Our company has grown also in excess of 20% of CPVC.

items.statement: Inventory loss exceeded Rs 100 crore in first nine months on PVC and polyethylene
items.quote: as on first nine months, because the inventory loss was not only in PVC, it was on polyethylene also, and which was in excess of INR100 crores in first nine months

items.statement: Open market PVC prices lower than domestic producer prices, local makers adjusting close to import parity
items.quote: The plastic piping business was affected in the third quarter as PVC prices in open market were quite low compared to domestic producer prices and due to extended winter rainfall in South India and some Eastern states.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty recommendation on PVC suspension grade resin sent to Finance Ministry in November, decision awaited
items.quote: However, there was a move from local producers to impose Anti-Dumping duty on import of PVC suspension grade resin. The decisi on from the Finance Ministry is awaited

items.statement: Supplies against new LOI for 10 Kg composite cylinders from IOCL ongoing, to be completed by February 2025
items.quote: Supplies against new LOI received for 10 Kg. cylinders from Indian Oil corporation Limited (IOCL) are taking place regularl y and shall be completed by February 2025

items.statement: Cross Laminated Film division expects 20% volume growth for the year with improved profitability
items.quote: Resultantly the division expects about 20% volume growth in this business segment for the year with improved profitability.

items.statement: Value-added products turnover grew 13% to Rs 961 crore in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The overall turnover of value -added products increased to Rs. 961 crores during the 3 rd quarter of the current year against Rs. 853 crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year achieving growth of about 13%.

items.statement: Furniture showrooms increased from 308 to 337 by December 2024
items.quote: Total No . of showrooms has reached 337 by end of December'24 from 308 as on 31st March'24.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with cash surplus of Rs 290 crore as of Dec 2024
items.quote: The Company Continues to be Debt free and having a Cash Surplus of Rs. 290 crores as on 31st December 2024.

items.statement: Plastic Piping volume grew 4% and value 1% in Q3 FY25; Packaging volume 9% and value 13%; Industrial volume -5% value flat; Consumer volume -7% value -5%
items.quote: Plastic Piping System business grew by 4 % in volume and 1 % in value terms. Packaging Product Segment business grew by 9 % in volume and 13 % in value terms. Industrial Products Segment business degrew by 5 % in volume and remained at flat level in value terms. Consumer Product Segment business degrew by 7 % in volume and 5 % in value terms.

items.statement: PVC resin price trend uncertain due to pending anti-dumping duty decision and crude/rupee movements
items.quote: Thus the PVC resin price trend remains in uncertain arena. Thus, Company is not in a position to give specific volume growth guidance.

items.statement: Infra demand weak as central government spent only 29% of budget in first six months, HDPE de-grew 28% in nine months
items.quote: We have seen that when the local producer who are supplying the high -density polyethylene, they did de-growth of 28 % by volume in the first nine months.

items.statement: MD & CEO says bank targets at least 13% growth in both deposits and credit for FY25
items.quote: we gave that guidance that we intend to grow by around 13% both deposit and credit. Nine months, we have turned almost around 10%, 9%, 9.5% in deposit as well as credit. items.statement: Industry cement demand expected to grow 6-7% YoY in Q4 FY25, implying full-year FY25 growth of 3-4% YoY

items.statement: Target to reach 49.5 mt cement capacity by end of FY25 and announce Phase 2 expansion to 75 mt by FY28 within next 6 months
items.quote: We are on advanced stage to reach 49.5 million tons of cement capacity by end of financial year '25. We will further announce our Phase 2 expansion to reach 75 million tons by financial year'28 within the next 6 months.

items.statement: Cost reduction target of INR 150-200 per ton through internal measures by FY27
items.quote: While we are one of the lowest cost cement producers, we are committed to further deepen our position by realizing the cost savings of INR 150 to INR200 per ton through internal measures by financial year'27.

items.statement: FY25 capex expected at INR 3,000 crores; Q4 FY25 capex ~INR 1,000 crores; FY26 capex INR 2,500-3,000 crores including land
items.quote: we expect capex for FY '25 to be about INR3,000 crores, which is largely towards Northeast and Bihar capacity expansions, lands for future projects, and some cost reduction projects, besides the maintenance capex.

items.statement: Operational RE capacity at 252 MW; target 267 MW by end FY25; RE share target 40-45% by FY25 exit
items.quote: By end of FY '25, we should have total operational RE capacity of 267 megawatts, including 57 megawatts from group captive arrangements and other smaller captive capacities. We expect to exit FY'25 with about 40% to 45% RE power share in our overall power mix on consumption basis.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA declined 34.5% YoY to INR 511 crores (INR 765/ton) due to weak cement prices
items.quote: Our EBITDA during the quarter declined by 34.5% Y -o-Y to INR511 crores, primarily due to weak cement prices. This works out to INR765 on per ton basis.

items.statement: Cement prices improved in December; expect further increases in Q4 but competitive intensity may cap gains
items.quote: We have seen some price improvements in December and expect further increases in Q4, driven by stronger demand. However, increasing competitive intensity may cap any significant gains on this front.

items.statement: Raw material cost down 2% YoY to INR 765/ton; power & fuel cost down 9% YoY to INR 1,005/ton; fuel consumption cost $96/ton vs $122/ton YoY

Power and fuel cost declined 9% Y -o-Y to INR1,005 per ton of cement production with $26 decline in the fuel consumption cost on a Y -o-Y basis.

items.statement: Logistics cost up 2.7% YoY to INR 1,120/ton due to central market supply from East plants and clinker movement; lead distance reduced to 269 km from 287 km
items.quote: During the quarter, our logistic cost increased by about 2.7% on a Y-o-Y basis to INR 1,120 per ton due to supply to central market from Eastern plants upon discontinuation of JP tolling arrangement and also high clinker movement costs due to plant shutdown amidst debottlecking activities done during the quarter.

items.statement: CC ratio improved to 1.70 in Q3 from 1.64 in Q2

And other INR300 crores was because of the capex or other cost which were not fully covered by the internal cash accruals.

items.statement: Incentive extension received for one plant for 2 years effective April 1, 2024; INR 14 crores accrued for prior 2 quarters in Q3
items.quote: Also, in the quarter, we have received an extension of incentives for one of our plants for an additional 2 years effective from 1st April '24. Consequently, an additional incentive of INR 14 crores has been accrued for the previous 2 quarters in this current quarter of Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Rajgangpur captive power plant shut after accident; may increase power cost slightly due to grid purchase; no production impact
items.quote: This accident happened in our power plant, which is a captive power plant. And that power plant is shut for now until we take all the corrective measures. It is not going to impact production in any way, but it may increase our power cost slightly because we'll have to purchase power from the grid instead of supplying it from a captive power plant.

items.quote: My operating EBITDA margin has gone up from 13.6% to 13.7% on a Y-o-Y basis. I think you may be looking at an EBITDA margin, which includes other income, the right way to look at it, is that you have to look at the operating EBITDA margin.

items.quote: So basically, capex is almost all done, maybe around INR10 crores of capex is already pending and that would be the act that most will be coming up.

items.statement: Not a capacity-constrained company; capability-based model; new plant supports up to INR2,000 crore revenue
items.quote: We are not a capacity-based company. We are a capability-based company. So, basically, capacity always we have actually, but basically we have to get new capabilities.

items.statement: HPC and Private Cloud/HCI each contribute 35-36% of revenue; AI at 14.7% and growing faster; networking switches growing slower
items.quote: Both these categories are still contributing around 32% to 35% -- 35% to 36% segment with each of them, so around 70% of revenue is still coming out of them.

items.quote: The cash conversion cycle for December '24 improved to 88 days as compared to 100 days in September '24.

items.quote: Net debt for December '24 was a negative INR737 million as compared to negative INR664 million in September '24. Kindly note that this net debt calculation excludes unutilized proceeds from IPO.

items.statement: No impact expected from US GPU export restrictions; India not on restricted list; government/enterprise use permitted
items.quote: We don't see any problem coming our way because anyway such restrictions are largely for those countries, which are expected to use such GPUs or such components for different kind of user scenarios.

items.statement: AIRAWAT POC fully booked with 6-month queue; India AI Mission RFP expected mid-2025; 10,000 GPU cloud rollout over 1-2 years
items.quote: The complete RFP should be expected sometime in 2025 mid approximately. And then the tenders we roll out, and we'll definitely bid for those tenders.

items.quote: We have customers like basically Tower Research. We have customers like Societe Generale and basically, so it's a very, very mature and a large range of customers which we have.

items.quote: I can give you some idea that within next 4 months, you should have the GB200 platforms rolling out basically from our side.

items.statement: No CTO role; organization run by engineers with technical sales/R&D/operations; interim CFO evaluation ongoing for 1-2 quarters
items.quote: We are still evaluating that and that decision we will come to maybe 1 or 2 quarters.

items.statement: No geopolitical risk seen from US administration change; business expected to grow stronger
items.quote: I personally telling you very frankly, I don't see any kind of basically on the kind of business, which we are doing or any kind of business impact primarily from Donald Trump coming in.

items.statement: Export pricing strategy same as domestic; margins similar; AI growth may push margins up slightly
items.quote: my pricing s trategy for domestic and export will remain the same. It can go a few basis points up actually because as I've been mentioning to you, as the AI business will be growing, that will push the margins a little bit on the upper side

items.quote: Basically, still the R&D team is still working on it, and we are basically making the product ready, but under development. Still, I think it will take us at least 1 or 2 quarters more to completely have a product ready a ctually there

items.quote: Notably, our aerospace business achieved 39% sequential growth in Q3, supported by a growing order book.

items.quote: I'm also delighted that in Q3, the partnership with BMW has begun operations. We now have facilities in Pune, Bangalore, and Chennai. The business began with a headcount of over 100 people.
