items.statement: Contract pricing revised every 9-12 months, gradual realization benefit
items.quote: So, because the contracts what we signed is usually for 9 months and 12 months, so where the pricing and the volumes are fixed. So, we cannot expect price realization changes in every quarter. It happens contract-to-contract basis.

items.statement: Value-added mix (stearin and CBE) at 55% of product portfolio
items.quote: But mostly, we are cons idering our stearin and CBE portion as the more value -added product mix. So, you can consider 55% of that product mix includes stearin and CBE

items.statement: New subsidiaries in West Africa (6) and UAE (1) for sourcing and MENA clients; Brazil subsidiary for Latin America market
items.quote: Manorama Industries strengthened its global operations by creating 7 new strategic subsidiaries including six in West Africa to secure Shea nuts and one in UAE to secure its sourcing and attract new clients from the MENA region.

items.statement: Brazil subsidiary enhances profitability, targeting local clients in Latin America
items.quote: It enhances our profitability.

items.statement: No competition anticipated in the space as per management knowledge
items.quote: No, we don't -- as of now, we don't see any competition from our knowledge.

items.statement: Inventory at INR580 crores including raw material and finished goods
items.quote: Inventory currently as on date total value is around INR580 crores, including raw material, what we have procured and as well as the finished goods.

items.statement: Finance cost increased due to seasonal Shea nut procurement working capital borrowings
items.quote: Sir, our current season of procurement of Shea Nut is going on. So therefore, we have taken the working capital from bank. So, this is our seasonable model of business, so we have to procure the raw materials in the quarter 3.

items.statement: Employee cost increase due to INR7.68 crore ESOP provision in Q3, INR11.50 crore for 9M
items.quote: The reason was that we have taken the provision of ESOP, employee stock option plan as per the Indian Accounting Standards. So, we have made the provision of around INR7.68 crores this quarter financial.

items.statement: Revenue, EBITDA, PAT CAGR of 25%, 14%, 15% respectively for FY20-24
items.quote: Revenue, EBITDA and PAT has registered CAGR of 25%, 14% and 15%, respectively.

items.statement: CBE business resilient with sustainable margins independent of cocoa butter price fluctuations
items.quote: Our CBE business remains resilient, ensuring sustainable margins and reven ue visibility, independent of cocoa butter price fluctuation because cocoa butter equivalent brings stability and it is a must for the big chocolate

items.statement: Planning next growth phase for 2026-31, R&D centre certified by Department of Scientific Research
items.quote: And now we believe it's an opportune time to start planning for next round of growth for 5 years starting from year 2026 to '31.

items.statement: Secured book to reach 40%+ of loan book by FY25 end with ~50% YoY growth
items.quote: Our Secured book by the year end would be 40% plus , the Y -o-Y growth on the Secured book would be around 50%

items.statement: Individual loan book expected to grow ~12% for full FY25
items.quote: the individual business growth should be around 12% for the entire year

items.statement: Overall loan book growth guided at 8-9% for FY25
items.quote: Overall growth could be hovering between 8% and 9% on the overall book

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 2.3-2.5% for FY25
items.quote: Credit cost, we continue with our guidance of 2.3% -2.5%.

items.statement: Full-year NIM guided between 8.6% and 8.8%
items.quote: The NIM for the full year should be between 8.6% and 8.8%.

items.statement: Deposit growth to maintain credit-deposit ratio around 89%
items.quote: Deposit growth will be in line with the requirements for the asset book in order to maintain a credit deposit ratio of around 89 % or so.

items.statement: Secured book grew 13% QoQ, 33% YTD, 52% YoY to 39% of loan book
items.quote: Our strategy to diversify the portfolio towards a more Secured Book has seen accelerated results, now contributing 39% to the total loan book by end of Q3, led by Affordable Housing, MSME and FIG. Our overall Secured book grew by 13% Q-o-Q, 33% YTD and 52% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Affordable Housing & micro mortgages book at Rs 6,393 cr, targeting Rs 7,000 cr by Mar-25
items.quote: Affordable Housing and micro mortgages comprising 21% of loan book demonstrates sustained growth. In December, disbursement exceeded Rs. 300 crores, marking a significant milestone. This book has reached Rs. 6,393 crores as of December '24, exhibiting a strong 11% Q-o-Q and 45% Y-o-Y growth expecting to close at Rs. 7,000 crores as of March 31, 2025.

items.statement: FIG book grew 11% QoQ, 57% YoY to Rs 2,257 cr (7% of loan book)
items.quote: FIG books continue to scale and reach Rs. 2,257 crores as of December '24, contributing 7% to the total loan book . This book grew by 11% Q-o-Q and 57% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Vehicle Finance book grew 43% QoQ, 155% YoY to Rs 375 cr
items.quote: The Vehicle Finance business witnessed impressive growth, reaching a book size of Rs. 375 crores and now contributes over 1% of our asset book growing by 43% Q-o-Q and 155% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Gold Loan book at Rs 115 cr across 198 branches (up from 63 in Mar-24)
items.quote: The Gold Loan business has experienced significant expansion with its availability increasing from 63 branches in March 24 to 198 branches in December ‘24. This book stands at Rs. 115 crores i n December ‘24

items.statement: Secured Agri book grew 27% QoQ to Rs 459 cr
items.quote: Secured-Agri, which includes Livestock and KPC, has shown significant Q-o-Q growth of 27%, reaching a book of Rs. 459 crores.

items.statement: 46% of Q3 disbursements from Secured products vs 30% YoY
items.quote: In Q3, 46% of disbursement resulted from Secured products compared to 30% in the same quarter last financial year.

items.statement: Microfinance disbursements in first 3 weeks of Jan higher than any month since Jul-24
items.quote: We expect a better performance in Q4 with higher disbursements seen in the first three weeks of January compared to similar period in any month since July 2024.

items.statement: January disbursements better than any month this fiscal; demand bounce-back seen in last 4 weeks
items.quote: Our January disbursement numbers that we have seen so far are better than what we have seen during this year so far. That is what you should note what I said.

items.statement: Cut group loan rates ~115 bps and individual loan rates ~75 bps from 1-Jan-25
items.quote: Bank took a call to reduce interest rates in group loans and individual loans by approximately 115 bps and 75 bps respectively, with effect from 1st January 2025.

items.statement: Q3 NIM 8.6%; yield down to 18.2% from 18.9% QoQ due to Secured mix; cost of funds up 6 bps to 7.57%
items.quote: On financials and margins, the NIM for the quarter is 8.6%. The compression and yields on the overall portfolio is down to 18.2% in Q3 versus 18.9% in Q2 due to growing contribution from Secured assets. The cost of funds moved up marginally by 6 basis points to 7.57% in Q3 versus 7.51% in Q2 largely attributed to the retirement of IBPC book.

items.statement: NIM expected to stay steady at current levels going forward
items.quote: It will be going steady at whatever rate it is now, it will be consistent going forward.

items.statement: Slippages Rs 298 cr in Q3 vs Rs 197 cr in Q2; ARC sale Rs 270 cr (Rs 207 cr NPA + Rs 63 cr written-off)
items.quote: Slippages from GL and IL book came in at Rs. 298 crores in Q3 versus Rs. 197 crores in Q2. Additionally, the Bank affected an ARC Ujjivan Small Finance Ban January 23, 2025 transaction of Rs. 270 crores in Q3, Rs. 207 crores from NPA book and Rs. 63 crores from a written-off portfolio

items.statement: SMA resolution improved: SMA-0 ~30%, SMA-1 25-35%, SMA-2 21-25%
items.quote: Yes, our SMA 0 resolution is in the range of about 30%. It has improved from about 25%, SMA-1 and 2, which were at 25% and 21% . SMA-1 has improved from 25 %-35% and SMA-2 has improved from 21%-25%.

items.statement: Total deposits Rs 34,494 cr (+16% YoY); CASA Rs 8,662 cr (+15% YoY, 25% of deposits); Retail deposits Rs 25,274 cr (+24% YoY, 73% of total)
items.quote: Bank's total deposits reached Rs. 34,494 crores, marking a 16% Y-o-Y growth. Notably, CASA deposit saw 15% Y-o-Y increase reaching Rs. 8,662 crores which is 25% of overall book. Retail deposits stood at Rs. 25,274 crores accounting for 73% of total deposits and demonstrating a 24% growth over December 23.

items.statement: Board approved application for voluntary transition to universal banking; will submit to RBI shortly
items.quote: I am also delighted to announce that the Board has accorded approval to move the application for voluntary transition to universal banking in its meeting held today . We will be submitting the application to RBI shortly.

items.statement: Following 4-lender guardrail; implemented 3-lender guardrail for new-to-bank customers from Jan-25; 3-lender rule effective industry-wide from 1-Apr-25
items.quote: So, we are following 4 lender guardrails. The 3 lender guardrails would come into effect on 1st of April. However, the other guardrails of 2,00,000 indebtedness and funding to SMA customers, these were already following. What we have additionally done is for the new-to-Bank customers, we have implemented the 3 lender guardrails.

items.statement: Micro-mortgage PAR 0.4-0.6%; 40-45% customers graduated from IL, 55-60% open market; IL customers have 4-5 yr relationship
items.quote: So, the micro-mortgage PAR is actually a very low number. 0.4 , 0.5, 0.6 are actually very low numbers. We see that the qualit y of the book has been exceptionally good. So, these kind of numbers are quite competitive and very reasonable. In terms of overlap, we have about 40 %- 45% of our customers who get graduated from individual loans to micro -mortgages and about 55%-60% are open market custo

items.statement: Blinkit store expansion accelerated; reached 1,000 stores ahead of March-25 guidance
items.quote: It just happens that we were able to add a lot more new stores than what we envisaged maybe a year ago when we gave the guidance of getting to 1,000 stores by March-25.

items.statement: Blinkit absolute losses expected to increase in next one or two quarters due to growth investments
items.quote: we do expect the investments in Blinkit to go up. And as a result, the losses on an absolute basis are expected go up in the next one or two quarters.

items.statement: Majority of new Blinkit stores are densification in existing cities; ~20% expansion in new cities
items.quote: half of the stores we are expanding are in the top 8 cities, out of all the expansion that you've seen. About 20% of the expansion has come from new cities, and the rest is essentially in non-serviceable areas in or around the top cities

items.statement: Store breakeven timeline unchanged at 2-3 months for new store additions
items.quote: we're still operating within the same ballpark, seeing store breakeven in around two to three months.

items.statement: Top 5% mature Blinkit stores at 6.4% contribution margin; room for improvement over 2-3 years
items.quote: There's a fair bit of room for the contribution margins to go up from where you see the top 5% stores are today to where they could be, let's say, 2 to 3 years down the line.

items.statement: Quick commerce seeing healthy traction in smaller cities; 80% of business still in top 8 cities
items.quote: 80% of our business is still in the top 8 cities. However, we are seeing fairly healthy traction in the smaller cities wherever we have entered.

items.statement: Take rate variation due to product mix shift toward electronics/general merchandise with lower percentage take rates
items.quote: the take difference that you see every quarter-on-quarter is usually just a mix of the product mix itself. OND is typically a quarter where we also see more sales of electronics products, general merchandise and some of the other categories, where percentage wise take rates are lower.

items.statement: No material impact from 10-minute food delivery competitors; initiatives still nascent
items.quote: All these initiatives (any form of 10-minute delivery in India today), are still at a very early stage and are not likely to move the needle at all, even if you aggregate and put them together.

items.statement: Zomato launched <15-minute delivery with curated menu in December quarter; scaling Bistro and restaurant delivery speed
items.quote: we've also launched the same feature that our competitor has introduced - less than 15-minute delivery with a curated menu and a dedicated fleet. This is something that we launched in the December quarter itself.

items.statement: Maintained/increased quick commerce market share despite competition; focus on service levels over discounts
items.quote: Despite the increasing level of competition over the last six quarters, we have maintained or even increased our market share. So, that is a strategy that is working for us, and we will stick to it.

items.statement: Core customer retention (2+ years) increased 1pp to ~40% despite intense competition; paying INR 20 delivery fee
items.quote: Their retention has actually increased by 1 percentage point through the quarter, despite this quarter perhaps being the most competitive we've seen in the last 2-3 years. These customers are also paying a healthy delivery fee of INR 20 per order.

items.statement: No specific customer retention subsidies; invest in service quality instead
items.quote: We are not doing any specific customer retention initiatives, by which I assume you mean offering subsidies to customers to retain them. We don't do any of that. We invest in our service to maintain customers.

items.statement: Rentals and picker salaries saw unusual run-up in some areas; expected to normalize near term
items.quote: We also believe that in some areas, there has been an unusual run-up, which we expect to normalize in the near term.

items.statement: Profitability improvement depends on store addition pace slowing to 10-12% of network per quarter
items.quote: if we reach a point where we are adding only 10-12% of the network every quarter, then we can confidently say that profitability will be there.

items.statement: Merchant transactions reached 1,000 crore in December 2024 out of 1,232 crore total transactions
items.quote: in December 2024, we had 1,000 crore merchant transactions and we had 1,232 crore total transactions.

items.statement: Merchant side business grew year-on-year while consumer side was flat or slightly de-grown even adjusted for discontinued businesses
items.quote: if you take a year on year view, then the merchant side of the business has grown, whereas the consumer side of the business, even adjusted for discontinued businesses, has been flat or slightly de-grown.

items.statement: RuPay on UPI generates MDR unlike bank-linked UPI and is growing fast though still a small percentage of merchant transactions
items.quote: we do make MDR, unlike bank linked UPI, but it is still a very small percentage growing fast, but it's still a very small percentage of the merchant transactions right now.

items.statement: RuPay credit card on QR gives disproportionately more revenue on acquiring side versus consumer side
items.quote: credit card running on QR gives us, as an acquiring side, much larger revenue than on the consumer side, because consumer side, you don't get larger revenue, even though there is some bps that is paid to the consumer app also.

items.statement: QR code presence on ground was the number two trigger for new customer sign-ups after wanting to try Paytm again
items.quote: our QR being present, our brand being present on ground was one of the big, actually, number two trigger. First was literally that they wanted to try out Paytm once again before they got to know in the press and then second was that I saw the QR code.

items.statement: Plan to aggressively expand merchant acquiring as it drives consumer acquisition through a flywheel effect
items.quote: we will aggressively expand on our merchant acquiring, because that gives us an edge in consumer also. So, there is a little bit of flywheel that we are seeing here, and that is probably one of the reasons that we didn't see a large number of exodus on either side.

items.statement: DLG model accounts for approximately 80% of merchant loan disbursements in the quarter
items.quote: That number is in the ballpark, Sachin. And, give or take a few percent, I think that's probably right.

items.statement: No target mix for DLG vs non-DLG; indifferent between models and open to partner preference
items.quote: we think DLG is a good model, non-DLG is also a good model, so relative to each other, we are quite indifferent. If a partner thinks that it is easier for them to do business, of lending to merchants, in a DLG model, or if they can do more business as a result, then we are quite open to doing DLG based business with them.

items.statement: Seeing more interest from lending partners across merchant cash and personal loans, particularly for DLG models
items.quote: we're seeing more interest from lending partners in general across MC as well as personal loans. MC in particular has been a product that has done consistently very, very well for us and for our partners, so we are seeing more interest in that.

items.statement: International expansion will focus first on merchant side payments and SME credit in Middle East and Southeast Asia
items.quote: the intent here is to first go on the merchant side, because merchant side business model is a very long term business model and every economy and geography that I'm meeting different, different senior executives in either the central bank or government, love it because SME credit is missing everywhere.

items.statement: Up to ₹20 crores investment per market for international subsidiaries, largely B2B with low upfront spend
items.quote: we are saying up to ₹20 crores of investment in each of these markets, which is also a bit of a placeholder number, we don't really think that we need large amounts of money in these countries.

items.statement: International expansion will take time due to entity formation, license applications, and operations setup
items.quote: it is very, very far ahead. So, don't misunderstand it to be shown up in a quarter or two for sure because these are entity formation, license application, operating. So, let's just please understand that it will take some time.

items.statement: ECL for DLG portfolio improved to 4.5%-5.0% from 4.75%-5.25% based on collection data
items.quote: These numbers are based on our collection data, so there's a couple of things, right. So one is, when the lenders put a program in place, they have, in their program, an expected credit loss and in our conversations with lenders, we ensure one of the questions that we obviously touch base on is whether the program is within the bounds of their expected credit loss.

items.statement: DLG book performing at least as well as rest of portfolio, slightly better; improvement driven by collection efficiencies and tighter underwriting
items.quote: The DLG book is doing at least as well, in fact, slightly better than the rest of our book and that's just sometimes some books do better, sometimes some books do, slightly worse. So, there is a, I wouldn't necessarily draw a pattern there, and, the reason for improvement is generally collection efficiencies, obviously with a lag, it is also indicative that your underwriting is getting tighter.

items.statement: Blended DLG cost significantly lower than 5% and broadly stable quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: On a blended basis, our DLG cost is significantly lower than the 5%, and it has broadly remained the same as last quarter.

items.statement: DLG provisions booked immediately in other direct expenses; unused provisions would reverse in cost
items.quote: yes, so far, all the DLGs that we have given, we provisioned them immediately in that quarter. And that is in other direct expenses, even though the DLG invocation by the partner is obviously with a lag, as and when GCL is hit. And the third is that if we do have a situation where we have provisions which are not getting used, then it would be a reversal in that cost.

items.statement: DLG also used for personal loans with select lenders in collection model only, not distribution-only model
items.quote: There is a small amount of DLG that we have given personal loans as well with select lenders only in the collection model, obviously not in the distribution only model.

items.statement: 5-6 lakh merchants have loans outstanding, representing 4-5% of device base
items.quote: It is broadly, five to six lakh merchants who have a loan outstanding. So, it is roughly 4-5% of our device base.

items.statement: Target to increase merchant loan penetration to 10-15% of device base over 2-3 years from current 4-5%
items.quote: over the next two, three years, we have an opportunity of taking this to north of 10%. And I think the long term opportunity is probably even higher than that.

items.statement: Three drivers of merchant loan growth: penetration increase, ticket size growth (₹1.1L to ₹2L in 3 years), and repeat loans with higher partner confidence
items.quote: One of the things that I should point out is that that is one, only one of the three drivers of the overall growth in, merchant loan volumes and revenues. The other two drivers are that over time, the ticket sizes have increased and they continue to increase. So, I remember three years ago this number was about 1,10,000. Currently the number is about 2 lakhs.

items.statement: Tenure decisions independent of ticket size; based on merchant stability and daily collection capacity; tenure not grown much due to conservative approach
items.quote: The tenure decision is independent of whether you're increasing the ticket size, so, if you have more confidence in the stability of the merchant, then the partner may increase the tenure as well, right? So, yes, it is the case that for select merchants for a repeat loan, the tenure might have gone up, but you don't increase the tenure just to increase the loan size.

items.statement: Payment processing margins comfortably above guided 3 bps; rental income assumption in analyst model slightly higher than actual
items.quote: your rental assumption is slightly higher than what our actual is. But it still doesn't quite get me to two and a half bps, so I can, I can, Anuj or I can look at.

items.statement: Rationalizing subsidiaries in Middle East, Southeast Asia, South Asia, Africa; many set up for old One97 telecom marketing services business
items.quote: We are in the process of rationalizing these number of subsidiaries because some of these were set up many, many, many years ago, and we may have little or no business in some of these countries. So, over the next 3 to 6 months, we'll look to see if we can reduce the number of subsidiaries.

items.statement: Personal loan disbursements FY26 expected better than FY25 unless macro worsens; driven by additional partners and rebound from lows
items.quote: unless there are big changes in and unless the FY26 macro looks worse than FY25, we do expect that FY26 will be better than FY25. And especially given that we are going to have additional partners, going into FY26, we do expect an increase in this business and a rebound from the lows that we saw earlier this year.

items.statement: Home loans and mortgages not pursued due to low margins, high line expenditure, and unfavorable opportunity cost vs other products
items.quote: No, they're very low margin. They increase the line expenditure on us and we have not been able to find a commercially logical reason. The CAC was, I mean, the opportunity cost of executing that versus other things, I'm not yet a big fan, to be honest about it, of those loans, but we did try them out, but we sort of receded from that.

items.statement: Device merchants get rent refunds based on high volumes, not activity-based waivers; high-volume merchants valuable for lending and UPI incentives
items.quote: We don't give waivers basis an activity. We give waivers basis, if you're doing a large amount of volume with us then we give that, which is what Vijay is referring to as a refund. So there are programs that we would run that if you do very large volumes with us, then you don't have to pay the subscription and the logic is that those merchants are great merchants in lending eventually and also, we

items.statement: Capex not expected to return to FY24 levels; refurbishment savings to continue for 2-3 quarters; depreciation to reduce as FY24 high capex rolls off
items.quote: we don't expect the capex to go back to FY24 levels, and, we think that the refurbishment, sort of savings on capex due to refurbishment, should generally be the case over the next two, three quarters, that this number is not something that we actively manage on a month on month basis or quarter on quarter basis. So, that might go up and down a bit. But refurbishment supply is there for the next s

items.statement: Depreciation reduction expected to accelerate in FY26 as FY24 soundbox capex (2-year depreciation) rolls off
items.quote: as the high capex of FY24 relative to FY25, as that starts to, sort of, roll off, because these are two years depreciation for soundbox, then we should see a reduction in capex, sorry, reduction in depreciation. And we're already starting to see some of that, but we should see that just sort of, accelerate a bit next year.

items.statement: Lenders choose DLG or non-DLG based on their comfort; some prefer non-DLG with sourcing fee and collection incentive model
items.quote: Some lenders say, I don't really need DLG because it doesn't really help me. I'm comfortable doing it in a non DLG model. I really quite liked the model earlier of you keep the sourcing fee or I pay you a sourcing fee and then eventually you get a collection incentive in the end, versus some lenders say that, hey, it's kind of important for us, it will help us scale the business, right.

items.statement: Capex expected to return to FY24 levels
items.quote: we don't expect the capex to go back to FY24 levels

items.statement: Depreciation to reduce as high FY24 capex rolls off two-year soundbox depreciation schedule
items.quote: as the high capex of FY24 relative to FY25, as that starts to, sort of, roll off, because these are two years depreciation for soundbox, then we should see a reduction in capex, sorry, reduction in depreciation.

items.statement: Contribution margin without UPI incentives at 50-55%, with UPI incentives at 55-60%
items.quote: we've talked about the contribution margin without UPI incentives is at 50 to 55%. So 50 to 55% and including UPI incentive for this to be 55 to 60%.

items.statement: DLG costs impacted contribution margin this quarter due to full quarter ramp-up with largest partner
items.quote: the contribution margin last quarter, in this quarter, particularly this quarter, has been impacted by DLG costs, which comes in other direct expenses.

items.statement: Contribution margin expected to uptick as DLG costs plateau relative to overall disbursals
items.quote: as that number sort of plateaus a bit, relative to our overall disbursal, we should see an uptick in contribution margin, just based on that factor alone.

items.statement: Gross take rate on DLG MCA book over loan lifetime: sourcing 3-4%, collections 1-2%, plus FLDG amount (e.g., 3.5-4%)
items.quote: The gross take rate over the lifetime of a loan in the DLG business, so if you remember earlier, we used to talk about 3 to 4% on sourcing and 1 to 2% on collections, right. So, to that you can add the FLDG amount.

items.statement: Non-lending revenue consistently 10-20% of financial services revenue over last 8-9 quarters
items.quote: broadly it has been 10 to 20% of our financial services revenue almost consistently over the last 8 or 9 quarters.

items.statement: Very close to EBITDA before ESOP profitability; would be profitable if this quarter's UPI incentive received
items.quote: we're very close to EBITDA before ESOP profitability. This is without UPI incentive just to point out. So, for example, if we got this quarter's share of UPI incentive in this quarter, then we would already be profitable.

items.statement: Gap between EBITDA before ESOP and PAT to become basically zero in 2-3 quarters as depreciation and ESOP costs decline and interest income rises
items.quote: our depreciation is going down, as we discussed earlier, and our ESOP costs are going down, as we have disclosed in the back of the earnings release. So as a result, the gap between EBITDA before ESOP and PAT is going down very meaningfully, I think in 2 or 3 quarters that gap will be basically zero.

items.statement: Expect PAT profitability once EBITDA before ESOP turns profitable, possibly in next 1-2 quarters sequentially
items.quote: just mathematically, we're going to get very close to, we're going to get to PAT profitability, once EBITDA before ESOP is, is profitable either in, you know, maybe in the next 1 or 2 quarters, sequentially.

items.statement: Goal is double-digit EBITDA margin relatively soon, translating into substantial PAT
items.quote: The goal is to have, double digit EBITDA margin relatively soon and then have that translate into a substantial amount of PAT.

items.statement: Payment volumes in India growing 20-25% year-on-year relatively safely
items.quote: payment volumes in India are growing very meaningfully. So, maybe 20 - 25% year on year, relatively safely.

items.statement: Take rates seeing tailwinds from RuPay on UPI, merchant willingness to pay for devices/hardware/software
items.quote: the take rates are starting to have some levers of tailwinds. So, somebody asked earlier about RuPay on UPI. Just like that, there are several other things which are inching take rates, you know, which are putting a bottom at the take rates, but also increasing take rates.

items.statement: DLG book (5 months) performing noticeably better than non-DLG book AUM; no concern on unit economics or expected credit losses
items.quote: our DLG book that we have done in the last five months has done, I would say, noticeably better than the non DLG book AUM that exists. Right. So it is very much on track. If anything, it is doing slightly better and we have really no cause of concern on the unit economics or the expected credit losses of that book.

items.statement: Incremental DLG disbursals have <50% contribution margin in month of disbursal due to FLDG cost > sourcing fee, but trail revenue makes overall business significantly higher margin
items.quote: in the month of disbursal, the merchant loan is less than 50% margin, right. Because, we get a sourcing fee, like we've always mentioned, it's 3 to 4% and then we have an FLDG cost meaningfully greater.

items.statement: Expect merchant loan revenue to grow faster than incremental FLDG, reducing drag on contribution margin going forward
items.quote: we expect our revenue from merchant loans to grow faster than incremental FLDG, than effectively FLDG growth, because we are starting to get collection revenue from not only the old book, but also from the FLDG book.

items.statement: Cash from PayPay stake sale sitting overseas in Singapore entity; no immediate need to repatriate as ₹10,000+ crores cash in India
items.quote: The cash is sitting overseas. And, obviously cash is fungible. If we needed cash in India, then we would have brought it back, but we don't need this cash in India. We have over ₹10,000 crores of cash in India.

items.statement: Will decide over next couple of quarters whether to use overseas cash abroad or repatriate to India; most likely eventually bring back in some form
items.quote: we will work this out over the next couple of quarters, whether there is an overseas use of funds of this money or whether we should bring that back to India. Most likely, eventually we'll bring it back to India in some form.

items.statement: Tax implications of repatriating PayPay stake sale cash still being worked through
items.quote: We're still working through the tax implications of this.

items.statement: Consumer growth gear shifted to product-led growth without marketing spend enhancement; organic flywheel seen
items.quote: internally we have now switched our gear towards the growth where the merchant growth and consumer growth, both are something that are very imminent and seeable. If you notice the number of consumer growth without marketing spend enhancement is very, very, very encouraging.

items.statement: Insurance broking focused on embedded insurance with health and auto as good bottom-line contributors
items.quote: insurance wise it is an embedded insurance along with our health and auto insurance, which are very good bottom line contributors.

items.statement: UPI incentive eligible GMV growing 15-20%; ballpark this year's incentive similar to last year's number
items.quote: we do have about 15 to 20% growth in eligible GMV. And so, if you look at our last year number and going forward, and had to sort of take a ballpark guess at this number, this year's number, then it should be in that range.

items.statement: Microfinance slippages flat QoQ at Rs 230 cr in Q3
items.quote: Ajay Kanwal: 230. Chintan Shah: So, that is flat on Q-o-Q basis, right? Abhilash Sandur: Yes

items.statement: Collection efficiency for unsecured portfolio at 98.5-98.6% consistently across Oct-Dec, targeting 99%+
items.quote: collection efficiency, unsecured at 98.6, 98.5, consistent across October, November, December.

items.statement: SMA reduced in Q3 over Q2, recoveries better in Q3 vs Q2 and Q1
items.quote: Our SMA has reduced in Q3 over Q2. So, I don't see a challenge. Also, recoveries are much better than in Q3 versus Q2 and Q1.

items.statement: Secured PCR increased to 48.3% in Q3 from 29% in Q2 to keep net NPA below 1%, may rise to 58-68%
items.quote: But now we have no other room. We have to make it 48. I worry that when we put the next money in this quarter to keep net NPA below 1, this may become 58 or 68 also.

items.statement: Accelerated provisions of ~Rs 300 cr (Rs 208 cr YTD + Rs 60-70 cr in Q4) to unwind over next year starting Q1/Q2 FY26
items.quote: So, the Q3 provisioning will probably unwind around Q2, Q3 next year. What we provisioned about, I think around Rs. 60 crores in Q1, that is probably what will be available in Q1 next year.

items.statement: Interest reversals in MFI: Rs 18 cr for Q3, Rs 50 cr YTD
items.quote: Rs. 50 crores of interest reversals which has happened year -to-date actually, For the quarter, it's around Rs. 18 crores, for the quarter

items.statement: BC book FLDG deposits of ~Rs 110 cr applied against NPAs during the year, reducing credit cost
items.quote: Roughly we would have taken about Rs. 110 odd crores out of the various deposits available with us during the year.

items.statement: MFI growth constrained by stringent underwriting: rejecting customers in non-metro with >Rs 50k exposure to other MFIs
items.quote: my existing customer, if he's not in a metro city, and has more than Rs. 50,000 outstanding balance with any MFI, I am not giving him money.

items.statement: Management sees peak stress behind in MFI, expects sequential disbursement uptick in Q4 and book to flatten out
items.quote: do think that we are very, very attentive on microfinance still. But only good news for us is given the shape of our book, we have not had the damage that one would have anticipated

items.statement: CASA pricing capped at upper end (7.8% rate) to avoid wholesale deposits; retail CASA growing via segmental offers
items.quote: What we felt was at the top end, when you are offering a 7.8 or some other extreme CASA rate, you tend to get very large tickets. And fundamentally, we looked at it and said, listen, this does help us grow our CASA. But is it the kind of CASA that we want to build ourselves for?

items.statement: LCR very high; bulk deposits being made non-callable (70% >1 year); retail deposit products launched to reduce bulk reliance
items.quote: We have launched a few products which would increase our retail deposit and reduce bulk in general. Once that happens, the LCR will also come down.

items.statement: Credit guarantee programs (CGTMSE, CGFMU) being extended to entire unsecured book including BC to mitigate event risk
items.quote: next few quarters we will keep adding to our CGTMSE and CGFMU guarantee programs so that any event risk on unsecured will not disturb us too much.

items.statement: 3,000 dedicated feet-on-street for affordable housing and micro LAP, separate from MFI salesforce and underwriting
items.quote: We have 3,000 feet on street to do affordable housing micro LAP. These 3,000 people are reporting to a business manager who runs affordable housing micro LAP business.

items.statement: Only one unsecured product in bank (JLG/individual loans); no other unsecured offerings
items.quote: So, we only have one in the bank only. We have no other unsecured business only. Our entire bank only does microfinance.

items.statement: Cost-income ratio target ~53% in steady state (currently elevated due to unsecured book below Rs 10k cr)
items.quote: cost-income would be about 53%.

items.statement: CASA target 30% in steady state; current decline due to pricing cap on wholesale deposits, retail CASA recovering
items.quote: CASA had become 30%. So, there were three variables, 80% secured, CASA at 30%.

items.statement: Plan to apply for Universal Bank license in May 2025
items.quote: we would certainly like to apply for a Universal Bank in May.

items.statement: Micro LAP slippages in 2-3 geographies only; LTV 33%, SARFAESI applicable; MSME and two-wheeler stable
items.quote: I specify that it is entirely SARFAESI applicable property business with a 33% LTV. With an LTV which we have given, as you can see on page 9 last column, is 32.8%, which is 33%.

items.statement: Gross Written Premium INR 7,706 crores for 9M FY25; total customers 6.2 crores; AUM INR 19,000 crores
items.quote: Gross Written Premium INR 7,706 crores, total number of customers now 6.2 crores. Assets under management is about INR19,000 crores

items.statement: Q3 FY25 GWP INR 2,677 crores; on like-to-like basis adjusting for 1/n implementation, GWP would be INR 2,738 crores
items.quote: in Q3 if you look at we are giving -- we're showing a premium of INR2,677 crores. And as you know from 1st of October 1/n has been implemented. So, when we compare to last year's quarter, Q3 '24 on a like -to-like basis, then our premium would be INR2,738 crores instead of INR2,677 crores

items.statement: 9M FY25 industry GWP growth 8% vs Digit 15%; on like-to-like basis Digit 9M growth ~16% and Q3 growth ~13%
items.quote: if you look at 9 months growth rate overall has been in 9 months for industry is 8% against that Digit is at 15%. And if we -- again, if you see without 1/n the growth rate in quarter 3 where the growth rate would be about 13%. And for 9 months, it will be about 16% on one-to-one basis

items.statement: Q3 FY25 loss ratio 72.9% vs 74.5% previous quarter; combined ratio 108.1% vs 110.3% previous quarter; on like-to-like basis combined ratio improved ~3% to 107.2%
items.quote: Loss ratios compared to last quarter 74.5% to 72 .9%. And when we look at combined ratio, combined ratio has improved to 108.1% compared to 110.3%.

items.statement: Profit after tax Q3 FY25 INR 119 crores vs INR 43 crores YoY; 9M FY25 PAT INR 309 crores vs INR 129 crores YoY; Q3 ROE non-annualized 3.1%, 9M ROE 9.6%
items.quote: Our profit a fter tax has increased from INR43 crores to INR 119 crores. And ROE non -annualized for the quarter is about 3.1%. For 9 months non-annualized ROE is about 9.6%.

items.statement: Net worth (IGAAP) crossed INR 3,900 crores; solvency ratio 2.22x
items.quote: Our net worth in IGAAP has now crossed INR3,900 crores. Solvency ratio is strong at 2.22%.

items.statement: Third-party reserve release 9M FY25 INR 336 crores vs INR 499 crores in 9M FY24; full year FY24 release INR 577 crores; FY25 expected in +/-5% range of FY24
items.quote: This year in 9 months, we have reserved -- released -- TP reserve release of about INR336 crores. And if we look at quarter 4, I'm not giving any guidance. We don't really know because we -- our actuarial colleagues will do this as of 31st of March. But my personal best guess is that if last year was INR577 crores we would be in a plus minus 5% range in this.

items.statement: Investment yield (ex-capital gains) Q3 FY25 1.83% vs 1.76% YoY; 9M FY25 capital gains loss INR 2 crores; Q3 capital gains INR 7 crores
items.quote: our investment yield is1.83 without capital gains in Q3 compared to 1.76 in the previous year. So, our investment yield on fixed income is good.

items.statement: AUM grew INR 3,200 crores; high-commission TP business reduced proportion while lower-commission TP business increased, supporting AUM growth despite lower TP GWP growth
items.quote: In case of Q3, growth in AUM despite a lower growth in TP is good because high commission business has reduced in proportion while lower commission business has increased.

items.statement: Asset allocation stable: equity up 0.5%, AT1 bonds up ~80 bps; comfortable increasing equity allocation up to 10% of AUM
items.quote: No major real change, a very small increase in equity of 0.5% some increase of roughly about 80 basis points in AT1 bonds. Otherwise, I think asset allocation is more or less stable in our AUM.

items.statement: Health loss ratio improved substantially in 9M and Q3 YoY; employer-employee (corporate health) business degrowing for 9M but pricing discipline maintained
items.quote: And especially in Q3, our loss ratio has improved compared to previous year Q3. And this again I think just to reemphasize, and this is the point I've made in the last two calls also that we have seen some intense price competition in employer -employee. This business is even on a 9 -month basis is still degrowing for Digit.

items.statement: Fire business seeing market pricing discipline from Jan 1; Digit 9M fire growth better than industry; rate discipline positive for growth and profitability
items.quote: In case of fire business I think we are seeing some market discipline in pricing from 1st of January. So, I think this is good from industry perspective, also from Digit's perspective because overall in 9 months in fire, our growth rate has been better than the industry.

items.statement: Motor OD premium share 39% (industry 41%), TP 61% (industry 59%); OD loss ratio expected to rise slightly as renewal mix increases and commissions decline
items.quote: If you look at 9 months, OD premium is 39% for Digit and TP is 61% while for the industry, OD is 41% and TP is 59%. So, what we have been doing purely from a Digit perspective is that one OD proportion is increasing and TP is reducing.

items.statement: Motor TP portfolio mix actively managed across geographies, vehicle types, fuel, age, CC to maintain loss ratios; TP market share 9M FY25 6.4% vs 6.5% FY24 full year
items.quote: The portfolio, Supratim, when you think about you can think in terms of geographies. You can think in terms of vehicle mix, commercial vehicles, two-wheeler, private cars. Within commercial vehicles, within private cars, again it could be more granular, could be based on say fuel, for example, new, old, for example, it could also be type of vehicle like everyone knows, a bus is a bus, but school b

items.statement: IRDAI granted forbearance on AUM for FY24; asked for AUM guidance for FY26 and quarterly updates to Board and regulator; 1/n accounting impact on AUM targets unclear pending circular
items.quote: we actually on December 27, '24, we have rece ived a letter from the regulator granting us forbearance for AUM for year '23 -'24. So last year, they have already given us a forbearance. For '24 -'25, obviously, once the year is complete and we update the regulator, we will know.

items.statement: Inward reinsurance (facultative) across property, fire, engineering, liability, marine, health, crop; accept ~40% of slips reviewed
items.quote: In inward business, we basically write facultative inward. And facultative means every risk is seen on a stand alone basis. So , you might even get some repeat business of a risk, but every slip is to be seen from a fresh eyes perspective because this is not a business where you are saying, I'll write this now in future. So, every slip has to be seen and then you write this business.

items.statement: Employer-employee (group health) competition remains intense; no significant improvement in pricing discipline as of December; expects correction when players incur losses
items.quote: On the group side till December we have actually not seen any significant improvement in the reduction of competition intensity. It continues to be strong as of now. But as I said earlier this is like if I have to use in Hindi the goat's mother won't stay safe forever, the Eid will come. So, the Eid of this. I think people will lose money and then the correction will happen.

items.statement: Motor TP: ~50% of industry book needs price increase due to 4 years without tariff hike and TP inflation; regulator's 'no TP obligation' signals industry not writing TP freely
items.quote: What I understand is that about -- maybe about 40% of the TP book of the industry is rightly priced. Mayb e 10% book might actually can even see some small reduction in premium. But there is about half -- roughly half book of TP of the industry which needs price increase because there is TP inflation and for the last 4 years, there has not been any increase in TP business

items.statement: Motor TP market share 9M FY25 6.4% vs FY24 full year 6.5%; Q4 FY24 share 5.7%; Q1 FY25 share low, Q3 FY25 6.2%; corrective actions taken in H2 FY24 reduced share from 7.1% (H1) to 6% (H2)
items.quote: last year for full year our TP market share was 6.5%. On 9 months, our market share in TP is 6.4%. In quarter 4 of last year our market share was only 5.7%. Now, again no guidance or anything in quarter 1 where our market share was quite low in motor and quarter 3 is only 6.2%.

items.statement: All retail claims serviced in-house via large in-house TPA network; group health uses both in-house and external TPAs; two TPAs collaborating on process/tech improvements
items.quote: All retail business is anywhere serviced today in-house. We have a very large network of in-house TPA. On the group side, we also continue to work with the TP A and also do business in -house. So, I think at the end of the day, we have to -- there is a customer, there is obviously an insurance company. So, we have to find what works for both under circumstances.

items.statement: 1/n accounting: ~INR 60 crores premium deferred to next period; ~INR 19 crores commission on deferred premium already accrued in Q3; combined ratio appears 1% worse but no P&L impact
items.quote: In our case, though we have shown the premium of about INR60 crores which has moved to next year, the commission on that which is roughly about INR 19 crores or so, we have actually provided that in Q3 already. So, on a like -to-like basis, our combined ratio has improved by 3%. Premium recognition will happen in future years, but the commission of that is already accrued in quarter 3.

items.statement: No guidance given on Q4 TP reserve release, Motor TP growth, or AUM targets; will publish IFRS results and internal profitability benchmark in April with full-year results
items.quote: I'm not giving any guidance. We don't really know because we -- our actuarial colleagues will do this as of 31st of March. But my personal best guess is that if last year was INR577 crores we would be in a plus minus 5% range in this.

items.statement: Will continue publishing unaudited IFRS results; aims to define consistent profitability benchmark for seamless IGAAP to IFRS transition
items.quote: we will continue to publish our IFRS results. So, you can see the 9 months unaudited results on IFRS. And just to repeat what I said when we publish our full results in April, we'll actually cover this in more detail as to how we internally look at profitability, having the same benchmark so that you are not changing the goal post every time.

items.statement: Board target of Rs 15,000 crore revenue by 2030 reiterated
items.quote: I am very happy to note that the board has again reiterated its target of Rs. 15,000 crore for 2030, sir.

items.statement: Management confident of achieving Rs 15,000 crore target based on 18% CAGR from 9M FY22 to 9M FY25
items.quote: We have also put out in our presentation that if you see from FY22 to FY25, the CAGR of growth because in between we were hit by COVID and it took a couple of years to come back, so 9M FY22 to 9M FY25, that is the last few years, we have had a healthy CAGR of 18%. And this kind of helps us believe that we will be good to achieve the ambitious target that the Board has set out for us as management.

items.statement: FY25 capex for GCL and Excel approximately Rs 100 crore
items.quote: Overall, in this year, between GCL and Excel, we will have roughly Rs. 100 crore approximately of capex being spent out.

items.statement: Excel expanding capacity proactively with de-bottlenecking projects and upstream component expansions
items.quote: We are proactively expanding certain parts, certain upstream components which feed into the end-product as well as have a market of their own such as rubber. So, there will be piecemeal kind of expansions going on, but as of now there really isn't any constraint to fulfill any orders that we get.

items.statement: Non-automotive revenue grew over 30% YoY in Q3 FY25
items.quote: In Q3 FY25, on a year-on-year basis, revenues from non-automotive applications registered an over 30% increase.

items.statement: Genset market share increased from less than 3% to nearly 4% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Our market share has inched up from less than 3% to nearly 4% in this quarter.

items.statement: Excel Controlinkage revenue down 7% YoY but up 15% QoQ in Q3 FY25
items.value: 7% lower year-on-year, quarter-on-quarter it was 15% higher
items.quote: While Q3 FY25 revenue in Excel Controlinkage was 7% lower year-on-year, quarter-on-quarter it was 15% higher.

items.statement: GCL plus Excel delivered EBITDA margins at healthy 15% plus in Q3 FY25
items.quote: GCL plus Excel, we have delivered margins at a healthy 15% plus.

items.statement: Standalone profitability at Rs 67 crore in Q3 FY25 and Rs 176 crore for 9M FY25
items.quote: Our profitability in Q3 stood at Rs. 67 crore at a standalone level and for 9M FY25 at Rs. 176 crore.

items.statement: Less than a third of Engineering revenue now from automotive diesel engines vs nearly 100% few years ago
items.quote: As a result, currently less than a third of our revenue is generated from automotive diesel engines from a nearly 100% share a few years ago.

items.statement: 64% of consolidated business now from B2C segments
items.quote: Notably, 64% of our business now comes from B2C segments reflecting our strategic pivot towards customer centric growth and market alignment.

items.statement: Ampere added 24 new dealerships, ELE brand 16, Greaves three-wheeler 17 in Q3 FY25
items.value: 24 new dealerships for Ampere, 16 for our ELE brand and 17 for our Greaves three-wheeler brand
items.quote: In the 3rd Quarter, we added 24 new dealerships for Ampere, 16 for our ELE brand and 17 for our Greaves three-wheeler brand.

items.statement: Retail exports growing strongly with new markets opened in Philippines and East Africa
items.quote: Exports is growing strongly. We have opened several new markets, including Philippines and East Africa.

items.statement: Engineering exports collaboration with Alliance partners across EU, USA, Africa and Middle East with teams in UAE and USA
items.quote: We have established collaboration with Alliance partners across EU, USA, key economies in Africa and the Middle East with team members based in UAE and USA.

items.statement: E-two-wheeler market share reached 3.4% in Q3 FY25, reclaiming fifth position in Vahan ranking for December 2024
items.quote: In the E-two-wheeler segments, we have achieved a market share of 3.4% in Q3 FY25, allowing us to reclaim the fifth position in the Vahan ranking for the month of December 2024.

items.statement: E-two-wheeler market share 10%+ in Tamil Nadu and Bihar as per Vahan data
items.quote: states like Tamil Nadu and Bihar where we are currently at 10% plus market share as per the Vahan data

items.statement: L5 diesel three-wheeler market share increased from 1.2% in FY24 to 3.7% in Q3 FY25, reaching fourth rank in Vahan
items.quote: We have successfully increased our market share in the L5 diesel segment from 1.2% in FY24 to 3.7% in Q3 FY25, driven by the growing demand from the southern market, propelling us to fourth ranking as per the Vahan for the L5 diesel segment.

items.statement: Greaves Electric Mobility filed DRHP with SEBI on Dec 23, 2024 for proposed IPO
items.quote: Greaves Electric Mobility, well known for the Ampere brand, has filed a DRHP with SEBI on December 23, 2024, for a proposed IPO.

items.statement: IPO proceeds to fund technology development, battery assembly, manufacturing expansion, subsidiary stake increase, digitization, inorganic growth and general corporate purposes
items.quote: We propose to utilize the proceeds for investments in technology development, enhancing capabilities at our technology center, development of in -house battery assembly, funding expansion of manufacturing capacities of our subsidiarie s, increasing the stake in one of the subsidiaries, increasing digitization and deployment of information technology infrastructure, funding inorganic growth opportu

items.statement: Path to 100% ownership of Excel Controlinkage per SPA and SHA signed with promoters
items.quote: So, as far as Excel goes, there is a path to 100% ownership and this is as per the share purchase agreement (SPA), shareholders' agreement (SHA) signed with the promoters, and we will be working along the same lines.

items.statement: Shendra plant received AS9100D certification for aerospace component machining
items.quote: In addition, the Shendra plant received AS9100D certification required for machining components for the aerospace industry.

items.statement: Euro 5 Plus compliant single cylinder engine ready as norms applicable from Jan 1, 2025
items.quote: The 'Euro 5 Plus' compliant engine is actually up and running because the norms were applicable from 1st January of 2025. So, they are probably the world's first single cylinder 'Euro 5 Plus' compliant engines for that category.

items.statement: Near zero debt with consolidated cash reserves of Rs 503 crore as of end December 2024
items.quote: With near zero debt and strong cash reserves of Rs. 503 crore, we are well positioned for a future growth.

items.statement: Overall demand recovery for diesel, CNG and EV parts with monsoon retreat and quick commerce pickup
items.quote: We are seeing an overall demand recovery for our diesel, CNG and EV parts with the retreat of monsoon and the pickup of the last mile economic activity driven by quick commerce.

items.statement: Hydrogen engine commercialization depends on hydrogen availability, total cost of ownership and other factors
items.quote: For example, availability of hydrogen, the total cost of ownership, etc., which will determine which ones take off or which one s take what time

items.statement: Expect cost-to-income ratio around 28% for FY25 and to moderate further going forward
items.quote: we will be able t o maintain at around 28% because always have given a forward guidance between 27% to 28

items.statement: Expect AUM growth at mid-teens level for next financial year if GDP grows above 6.5%
items.quote: If that is the case, definitely, we'll be growing at mid-teen levels.

items.statement: Expect NIM to improve in Q4 FY25 as excess liquidity gets utilized
items.quote: the higher liquidity, which is built up will get utilized. So NIM will improve.

items.statement: Target 2-wheeler disbursement growth at double the market growth plus 2% minimum
items.quote: Typically, what we target is double the market growth plus 2% minimum. So if it's growing at 5%, we look at 12% growth.

items.statement: Rural credit demand improving due to good monsoon and crop output
items.quote: The good rainfall monsoon and the Kharif and Rabi crop is giving some positive indicator for the rural market. And we do see good credit demand coming from the rural and also overall economy improving in the rural market for us.

items.statement: M&HCV demand expected to recover in Q4 FY25 as government infra spend picks up
items.quote: There are new projects have been activated. And I believe the last quarter now is going to be a bigger quarter, and there will be demand coming back.

items.statement: Passenger vehicle growth to continue for next 3-4 years driven by private demand for public transport
items.quote: I feel the passenger vehicle growth will continue to be there for next maybe 3 years to 4 years because of the same.

items.statement: Used commercial vehicle transactions to increase significantly over next 3-5 years as post-COVID sales feed into secondary market
items.quote: I believe next 3 years to 5 years will be really good for us in used vehicle financing because number of transactions will go up significantly.

items.statement: NIM fell to 8.48% in Q3 FY25 from 8.74% in Q2 FY25, ~20 bps due to negative carry from excess liquidity
items.quote: Our NIMs was 8.48% as against 8.99% in Q3 FY '24 and 8.74% in Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: Incremental cost of borrowing at 8.9%, overall cost of liabilities at 8.95% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The cost of liability is at 8.95% which is marginally down from the previous quarter which was 8.97%.

items.statement: Disbursements grew 15.82% YoY to INR 43,766.27 crore in Q3 FY25
items.quote: We have registered disbursement growth of 15.82% year -on-year. Our disbursements in Q3 FY '25 this year aggregated to INR43,766 .27 crores versus INR37,787.84 crores in Q3 FY '24.

items.statement: AUM grew 18.78% YoY and 4.70% QoQ to INR 2,54,469.69 crore as of Dec 2024
items.quote: Our AUM as on 31st December 2024 registered a growth of 18.78% over Q3 FY '24 and a 4.70% sequentially. Our AUM stood at INR2,54,469.69 crores as against INR2,14,233.47 crores a year-ago and INR2,43,042.55 crores in Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM declined sequentially for two quarters but expected to resume growth from Q4 FY25
items.quote: we should see an uptake in the next -- this quarter, I mean the fou rth quarter and also going -forward the next financial year

items.statement: Gross Stage 3 at 5.38%, Net Stage 3 at 2.68% in Q3 FY25; credit cost at 1.85%
items.quote: On our asset quality, gross Stage 3 in Q3 FY '25 stood at 5.38% and net Stage 3 at 2.68% as against 5.66% gross and 2.72% net in Q3 FY '24 and 5.32% gross and 2.64% in Q2 FY '25. Our credit cost for Q3 FY '25 stood at 1.85% as against 2.15% for Q3 FY '24 and 1.84% for Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: MSME Stage 2/3 increase attributed to seasonal cash-flow mismatches, expected to correct in Q4
items.quote: I feel it is temporary, mainly because of seasonal and cash-flow mismatches.

items.statement: Gold loan Stage 3 amount flat at INR 112 crore vs INR 118 crore; percentage up due to lower denominator
items.quote: The stage 3 has been more or less flat, I would say in terms of amount which is the Q2 number it was INR118 crores and now in fact it has come down to INR112 crores.

items.statement: Stage 1 PD 9.05%, Stage 2 PD 20.74%, LGD 38.75% in Q3 FY25; PD/LGD reset annually in March quarter
items.quote: Stage 1 PD was 9.05 as against 9.06 in the previous quarter. Stage-2 PD was 20.74 as against 20.98 and the LGD was 38.75 as against 38.59%

items.statement: Added 1,641 employees in Q3 FY25; staff cost up INR 64 crore, other overheads up INR 62 crore
items.quote: we had added around 1,641 employees in the current quarter and the staff cost has increased by around INR64 crores and there were other overheads which has gone up by INR62 crores

items.statement: Hiring freeze planned; focus on productivity and digital adoption to slow future headcount growth
items.quote: We are trying to have some freeze on this. We'll be reworking the productivity levels and trying to focus on productivity.

items.statement: LTV maintained at 70% on used vehicles despite ~30% price increase over 3 years
items.quote: The LTV has remained same, but price has gone up. The average increase in the price of vehicle is around 30% over the last 3 years. So that has gone up, but LTV has not gone up. LTV remains 70% on used vehicle.

items.statement: Liquidity increased to INR 27,000 crore (6 months of liabilities) from INR 17,000 crore; will moderate to 3 months over next two quarters
items.quote: Because of the last transaction of ECB, the liquidity has shot up from INR17,000 crores to INR27,000 crores which is almost equivalent to our next 6 months liability. This excess liquidity will be moderated over next two quarters and we'll go back to our earlier policy of 3 months of liability to be in liquid assets.

items.statement: Offshore borrowing increased due to USD 1.22 billion ECB loan in Q3; ECB done once or twice a year
items.quote: the offshore borrowing both loan and bond at around 19%. This has increased substantially because of the large loan transaction what we have done in the current quarter, which was 1.22 billion.

items.statement: Launched EV/green financing vertical on Dec 20, 2024; gradual growth planned with separate credit policy
items.quote: we have announced a EV lending vertical, that is green financing. So focus is trying to build a separate vertical and focus on building the business there so that there is a focus and also there is separate what supervision and credit policy for that.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of 125% (INR 2.5 per share); record date Jan 31, 2025
items.quote: With the continuing good results, the Board has declared interim dividend of 125% that is 2.5 per share. The record date for the entitlement thereof has been fixed as January 31, 2025.

items.statement: No structural asset quality decline seen; credit cost consistently below 2% for two quarters
items.quote: credit cost has been all -time best, Kunal. We are less than 2% consistently for two quarters.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio 28.59% in Q3 FY25 vs 27.04% YoY; guided to ~28% for FY25
items.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio was 28.59% in the Q3 FY '25 as against 27.04% recorded in Q3 FY '24.

items.statement: Surpassed FY25 presales growth guidance of 30%-35% with 40% growth in Q3
items.quote: We registered a strong presales growth of 40% in our third quarter surpass ing our growth guidance of 30% - 35

items.statement: Targets 25-30% presales growth in FY26
items.quote: Yes, very easily and very confident about it.

items.statement: 9M FY25 presales at INR1,661 crores, highest ever
items.quote: We now stand at INR1,661 crores presales for the 9-month FY '25, our highest ever so far.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 presales at INR635 crores, 40% YoY growth
items.quote: We sold INR635 crores worth of area in quarter 3 FY '25, which is a 40% growth over quarter 3 of FY '24.

items.statement: Uber Luxury segment contributed INR422 crores in Q3
items.quote: The total contribution from Uber Luxury segment was close to INR422 crores.

items.statement: Total GDV stands at INR40,225 crores, more than doubled in 2 years
items.quote: The total GDV of Sunteck as of 9 months FY '25 stands at INR40,225 crores, which has more than doubled in last 2 years.
