items.statement: VNB grew 8.5% YoY to Rs 15.75 billion in 9M-FY2025 with margin at 22.8%
items.quote: VNB grew by 8.5% year-on-year to ` 15.75 billion in 9M-FY2025. With an APE of Rs.69.05 billion, the margin stood at 22.8%.

items.statement: Linked business grew 49.8% YoY with contribution increasing from 43.1% to 50.8% of APE in 9M-FY2025
items.quote: Linked business grew by 49.8% year -on-year and its contribution to overall APE increased from 43.1% in 9M-FY2024 to 50.8% in 9M-FY2025 on account of customer preference shifting towards ULIP products given the market buoyancy.

items.statement: Non-linked savings excluding annuity declined 17.4% YoY with contribution declining from 26.8% to 17.5% in 9M-FY2025
items.quote: Non-linked savings business excluding annuity declined 17.4% year -on-year and its contribution also declined from 26.8% to 17.5% in the corresponding nine months this year.

items.statement: Group Funds business grew 102.5% YoY with contribution increasing from 3.7% to 6.0% in 9M-FY2025
items.quote: Group Funds business grew by 102.5% year -on-year in 9M-FY2025. Contribution from Group Funds business increased from 3.7% last year to 6 .0% in 9M-FY2025.

items.statement: Protection APE grew 6.9% YoY contributing 16.9% to APE; Retail Protection grew 40.0% in Q3 and 24.2% in 9M-FY2025
items.quote: Protection APE grew by 6.9% year-on-year and contributed 16.9% to APE in nine months period. Retail Protection business grew by 40 .0% in Q3 -FY2025 and 24.2% in 9M-FY2025 on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Credit Life business witnessed slowdown due to MFI industry challenges; Non-MFI business continues to do well
items.quote: In Credit Life business, we have witnessed some slowdown due to ongoing challenges in MFI industry. Non-MFI business continues to do well.

items.statement: Group Term business impacted by increased competition but increased depth in market coverage with growth in deals, lives covered and sum assured
items.quote: Group Term business, as we highlighted previously as well, continues to be impacted due to increased competition. However, we have been able to increase our depth of market coverage as seen in the growth in number of deals, lives covered, and sum assured during the quarter.

items.statement: Annuity business grew 50.0% in Q3 and 81% in 9M-FY2025 YoY with contribution increasing from 6.2% to 8.9% of APE
items.quote: Annuity business grew by 50 .0% in Q3-FY2025 and 81% in 9M-FY2025 on a year-on-year basis. Its contribution increased from 6.2% in nine months last year to 8.9% of APE in nine months this year.

items.statement: Agency APE grew 41.3% YoY contributing 30.2% to overall APE and 36.2% to retail APE in 9M-FY2025
items.quote: Agency business APE grew by 41.3% year-on-year and contributed 30.2% to overall APE and 36.2% to retail APE in 9M-FY2025.

items.statement: Direct APE grew 31.6% YoY contributing 15.3% to overall APE and 18.4% to retail APE in 9M-FY2025
items.quote: Direct business APE grew by 31.6% year-on-year and contributed 15.3% to overall APE and 18.4% to retail APE in 9M-FY2025.

items.statement: Bancassurance APE grew 26.3% YoY contributing 27.7% to APE mix in 9M-FY2025
items.quote: Bancassurance business APE grew by 26.3% year -on-year and contributed 27.7% to APE mix in 9M-FY2025.

items.statement: Partnership Distribution grew 2.0% contributing 10.1% and Group business grew 20.9% contributing 16.7% to APE mix in 9M-FY2025
items.quote: Partnership Distribution business grew by 2 .0% and contributed 10.1%, while Group business grew by 20.9% and contributed 16.7% to APE mix in 9M-FY2025.

items.statement: Cost/premium at 19.8% and cost/TWRP at 27.8% in 9M-FY2025; cost/TWRP on savings line at 16.8%
items.quote: Our cost/premium stood at 19.8% and cost/TWRP stood at 27.8% in 9M-FY2025. Our cost/TWRP on the savings line of business stood at 16.8% in 9M-FY2025.

items.statement: PAT for Q3-FY2025 grew 43.6% YoY to Rs 3.26 billion; PAT for 9M-FY2025 grew 18.3% to Rs 8.03 billion
items.quote: The Company's PAT for Q3 -FY2025 grew by 43.6% year -on-year to ` 3.26 billion and PAT for 9M-FY2025 grew by 18.3% to ` 8.03 billion.

items.statement: Assets under management stood at Rs 3.1 trillion and solvency strong at 211.8% at December 31, 2024 aided by Rs 14 billion sub debt fund raise
items.quote: Our assets under management stood at ` 3.1 trillion and our solvency continue d to be strong at 211.8% at December 31, 2024 aided by the ` 14 billion sub debt fund raise that we had done.

items.statement: Par and non-par split roughly 60:40 ranging between 60:40 to 66:33
items.quote: Yes, we discussed what the split between par and non-par numbers are; they're roughly in the range of about 60:40. We discussed this last time as well. It ranges somewhere between 60:40 to 6 6:33 in that range.

items.statement: No assumption changes taken; expense forecasts updated for full year; assumption review typically at year end
items.quote: No, we haven't taken any assumption changes. Typically, we'll do that at the end of the year. We will review all assumptions at one shot. Of course, we have updated some of the expense forecasts that we see for the full year.

items.statement: Repriced non-par plans in line with yields at October; last changes were in April; non-par share in overall mix is quite small
items.quote: We have repriced our non-par plans in line with the yields at October. The last time that we had made these changes was at April. So, in the intervening quarter we did not have the chance to do that because we had to update it for surrender value regulations as well. But in October, we did update the IRRs in line with the yields. But in any case, the share of non-par for us is quite small in our o

items.statement: Annuity and non-par products linked to G-Sec yields corrected effective October 1st
items.quote: Yes, the pricing of non-par, annuity, all those products linked to G-Sec yields were all corrected effective 1st October, something that we could not do in Q2, it was corrected as we got into this quarter.

items.statement: VNB growth target medium-term is mid-teens; currently at 8.5% for 9M-FY2025 up from 4% at H1
items.quote: The view that we want to take from a medium -term perspective is to work towards mid -teens. No doubt about that. And we are working at it for quarter -to-quarter. As you can see from H1 to nine months, there has been a positive improvement.

items.statement: Credit life business grew 8% contributing 38% of protection; 45% of credit life is MFI and remaining non-MFI
items.quote: So, credit life business for us actually has grown by 8% and this contributes close to 38% of our overall protection business. You know our protection is close to 16.5% 7 of our overall APE and 38% of that is credit life. And within credit life, 45% of our business is MFI and remaining is non-MFI

items.statement: Group protection down due to MFI stress from lower disbursements impacting credit life in Q3; non-MFI business doing well
items.quote: So, group protection being down like is quite well known for the stress that we see on MFI business. And largely it is because of disbursements getting lower, which has impacted credit life side of the business taking a hit in Q3.

items.statement: Zero surrender value annuity product launched three weeks ago; no adverse surrender trends seen; surrender expectations miniscule and in line with other products
items.quote: So, let me go one-by-one. With regard to our annuity products, yes, it's a little about three weeks over a year since we launched and frankly we have not seen any adverse trends at this point, because again, our belief is that this product has been bought from the perspective that the customer wants to take an annuity.

items.statement: New product variants priced to be margin-neutral; not looking at margin drop
items.quote: Sanketh, in short, we are not looking at a margin drop. We are pricing them to be margin-neutral.

items.statement: ROP Protection APE for nine months roughly in range of 15% to 20%
items.quote: It's small. I think for the nine months it's roughly in the range of 15% to 20%. It's broadly been there.

items.statement: Commission structures aligned with surrender value guidelines; over 95% of partners closed revised arrangements with deferral, claw-back or reduced commissions
items.quote: More than 95% of our partners, we have closed the arrangement, the revised structures and whatever is pending is something very small, I think also will get over in the next couple of weeks' time. So, from that perspective the commission structures have been completely aligned with the change in surrender guidelines.

items.statement: ULIP momentum holding in early days of current quarter
items.quote: Yes, that's right. At least the early days of this quarter.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 order book at INR2,681 crores
items.quote: The Q3 PAT was INR166 crores and the order book at the end of the Q3 was INR2,681 crores.

items.statement: Completed RAN supplies for 27,000+ sites in Q3, total 86,000+ sites delivered for BSNL 4G/5G network
items.quote: For the wireless business, we have completed RAN supplies for 27,000 plus sites in this quarter, leading to a total of 86,000 plus sites delivered till date in BSNL's 4G /5G network.

items.statement: Signed 3-year contract with Vodafone Idea for pan-India 4G/5G mobile backhaul equipment supply
items.quote: For the wireline business, one of the highlights has been signing a 3 -year contract with Vodafone Idea for supplying equipment for their pan-India 4G and 5G mobile backhaul network.

items.statement: Selected as broadband equipment supplier for BharatNet Last Mile Connectivity in Tamil Nadu using GPON technology
items.quote: We have b een selected as a broadband equipment supplier for state -led BharatNet Last Mile Connectivity in Tamil Nadu.

items.statement: Completed POC and received initial purchase orders for US network modernization deal
items.quote: We also successfully completed the POC and received the initial purchase orders for a network modernization win in the US.

items.statement: Received major orders from existing Asia customer for mobile backhaul network expansion
items.quote: From our existing c ustomer in Asia, we received, again, major orders for the expansion of the mobile backhaul network.

items.statement: Sanjay Malik, former Nokia India Country Head, joined as EVP, Chief Strategy and Business Officer
items.quote: Sanjay Malik, who was former India Country Head of Nokia has joined the management team as EVP, Chief Strategy and Business Officer.

items.statement: Doubled floor space capacity in Bangalore for R&D and manufacturing, set up wireless center of excellence
items.quote: We have significantly expanded our office and manufacturing facilities in Bangalore, in line with our business and headcount expansion and we have almost doubled our floor space capacity, both for our R&D as well as for manufacturing.

items.statement: Expect large tender-driven opportunities (BSNL expansion, 5G, BharatNet) to convert in Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26, contributing to FY26 business
items.quote: Some of the large tender -driven opportunities such as the BSNL expansion network, 5G, Power, BharatNet etc., are all live opportunities, which are maturing as we speak, and we expect them to convert in Q4 of FY'25 and Q1 of FY '26.

items.statement: Q3 margins lower due to product mix change, old inventory provisions, higher R&D depreciation; expect improvement as international business picks up
items.quote: The margins or profitability are a bit lower than the previous quarter, and that's mainly on account of change in product mix. And also, there are certain provisions for old inventory and higher depreciation for certain R&D equipment that we've taken in this quarter.

items.statement: Collected INR2,000 crores in Q3; inventory at INR3,127 crores, receivables at INR4,730 crores
items.quote: We've collected about INR2,000 crores during this quarter.

items.statement: Closing borrowing position INR3,157 crores, cash INR643 crores; borrowings mainly for working capital
items.quote: Closing borrowing posi tion was around INR3,157 crores and cash of INR643 crores. Borrowings are mainly for working capital purposes.

items.statement: Expect significant order book refill in FY26 if BSNL 4G expansion, 5G, Kavach, BharatNet opportunities convert in Q4/Q1
items.quote: So if we are successful in most of the se opportunities, it could lead to a significant bump or refilling of our order book.

items.statement: Initial 1 lakh site BSNL 4G order to be executed this financial year; 4G expansion, 5G upgrade and n78 band build-out to follow
items.quote: That's correct. I think this initial 1 lakh site order should get executed in this financial year.

items.statement: Headcount upwards of 2,350 people, over 60% in R&D
items.quote: So as of today, we are upwards of 23 50 people, and more than 60% of them are in R&D, that is part of our engineering team.

items.statement: R&D investments to continue at absolute level despite revenue outlook; focus on optimizing overall spend
items.quote: While we would always look at optimizing and controlling the overall spend in general, but at an absolute level the investments in R&D will continue.

items.statement: Import content for active electronics 40-65%; enclosures, cables, connectors, mechanical items localized; PCB assembly and system testing done in India
items.quote: The amount of it can vary between 40% to 65%, in terms of the active electronics that gets imported especially for the semiconductor chips.

items.statement: Cost advantage from integrated architecture (radio+transport+broadband) giving 20-25% COGS advantage plus opex savings vs separate equipment
items.quote: So you may get a cost of goods advantage of maybe 20% -25% to that extent, but you get a larger benefit in terms of the opex also in terms of running a converged or integrated equipment.

items.statement: Ongoing POCs with domestic operators for 4G/5G; expect success in Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26; international engagements in advanced technical discussions with band customization
items.quote: Yes. So as I mentioned that live POCs are going on for operators in India, and we think probably in this quarter or in Q1FY'26, we should be able to see some success in that in terms of additional orders and additional deployment.

items.statement: Sales teams in North America and LatAm grown >50% YoY, added 6-7 people; added 1-2 partners per region in Europe, Asia, ANZ
items.quote: Well, with respect to l ast financial year, we have grown our teams by more than 50% in those regions. In the US and LatAm, we've added at least 6-7 people.

items.statement: No regulatory issues in North America/LatAm; equipment certified to global standards (TUV, UL) tested in India; tariff impact unknown and speculative
items.quote: Now as far as tariffs and all are concerned, it's still an open question. We really do not know. I mean nothing has been announced, so nothing has come up. So until that time it comes up, it's all pure speculation on this front.

items.statement: Targeting BEAD program, Rip and Replace, and network modernization (circuit emulation) opportunities in North America with local partners
items.quote: Yes, both of those programs we are trying to addres s with our local partners . BEAD is about the expansion of broadband rollout in the rural areas of US where there is a significant amount of investment.

items.statement: Wireless: 5G RAN across diverse bands, massive MIMO, FWA, ORAN/3GPP support, non-terrestrial comms from Saankhya tech. Wireline: evolving to 1.2Tbps/channel, 10G/50G PON, converged broadband with LTE/5G FWA, XGS-PON
items.quote: For wireless, of course, developing state -of-the-art 5G RAN equipment, supporting diverse bands, which are the spectrum, which is available across the world, including massive MIMO radios, fixed wireless access solutions for the N78 /3.5 gigahertz as well as the millimeter wave bands.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 revenue INR2,642 crores (4.7x YoY); EBIT INR260 crores, PBT INR211 crores, PAT INR166 crores
items.quote: For Q3FY '25 we did a revenue of INR2,497 crores and other operating revenue, which is mainly the PLI incentive of about INR145 crores. So total revenue from operations is INR2,642 crores, which is roughly about 4.7x of the previous year.

items.statement: PLI incentive for FY23 received in FY24; FY24 incentive process ongoing, expected soon; FY25 incentive expected next fiscal
items.quote: We received the PLI incentives for FY '23 in FY '24. And typically, the payment happens in the subsequent year. So what you would see in recognized as revenue in FY '24 is what we would expect to receive this year.

items.statement: Revenue crossed Rs 500 crore quarterly milestone; aim to build on this for stronger future performance
items.quote: This quarter, we are proud to have crossed the Rs. 500 crore milestone in quarterly revenues and we aim to build on this achievement to deliver an even stronger performance in the future.

items.statement: International business grew 21% YoY in Q3 and 28% over nine months
items.quote: Our international business registered YoY growth of 21% during the quarter and 28% over the nine months, providing strong support to overall performance.

items.statement: Ethoxylation capacity expansion at Unitop Dahej and HPPC Dahej on track for phased commissioning in coming months and Q1 FY26
items.quote: On our CAPEX project, including the ethoxylation capacity expansion at Unitop's Dahej facility and the Dahej expansion of HPPC, both are progressing well and are on track for commissioning in a phased manner in the coming months and some of them in Q1 of FY26.

items.statement: Adding 30,000 tons ethoxylation capacity; full utilization expected in about 3 years
items.quote: We are adding about 30,000 tons of ethoxylation capacity. As I said, it will take us about 3 years or so for these capacities to get fully utilized.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 137 bps YoY; EBITDA margin 12.6% vs 13.7% last year due to growth initiative expenses
items.quote: Our gross margin improved by 137 bps YoY during the quarter, supported by a favorable product mix and operational efficiencies. However, higher expenses related to ongoing growth initiatives, capacity expansion, and certain businesses in their growth phases, such as our institutional cleaning vertical impacted the EBITDA margins, which stood at 12.6% compared to 13.7% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Expect similar EBITDA margin levels of 13% plus/minus in first year of new capacities
items.quote: Currently, I think we would still be okay to, at least for the first year, to come up with similar kind of margin levels of 13% plus minus.

items.statement: HPPC demand strong; Textile showing early export recovery; AHN improving as demand strengthens
items.quote: The HPPC segment continues to benefit from strong demand fundamentals and innovation-led offerings while the Textile business is showing early signs of recovery, presenting emerging export opportunities. In the AHN division, we anticipate further improvements as demand conditions strengthen.

items.statement: Gross margin expansion driven by favorable product mix and operational efficiencies
items.quote: Our gross margin improved by 137 bps YoY during the quarter, supported by a favorable product mix and operational efficiencies.

items.statement: Export focus on America, Europe, Turkey, Gulf; adding new customers and segments in existing geographies
items.quote: Our major exports are to America, which includes Latin and South America, to Europe and also to Turkey. But now we are opening up geographies also in the Gulf area. Basically, I think geographies remain the same, but we are trying to add new customers and new segments in the businesses.

items.statement: Nine-month revenue growth of ~11% driven entirely by volumes (9-10% volume, 1-2% pricing) across all three verticals
items.quote: I think it would be fair to say that the YTD nine months growth that we are seeing about 11% kind of growth, the entire growth has come out of volumes. Prices have not really played a key role in terms of the growth. I would say the volume would have grown about 9%-10% and a couple of percent increase would have come from pricing. And this has been across the three verticals.

items.statement: Buzil Rossari target Rs 450-500 crore revenue in 2 years; expect positive EBITDA contribution at that scale
items.quote: In 2 years, we want this business to be double of what it is today. Our two-year target, if you see, we should be closer to Rs. 450 – Rs. 500 crore kind of a revenue. And we expect that once it reaches that number, it will start contributing to the EBITDA.

items.statement: Ethylene oxide supply constrained; reliant on Reliance for additional allocation; no import/transport option
items.quote: We do not have any option because Reliance is the only supplier of EO and we cannot import or transport the EO. We are already discussing with Reliance and we are asking them for a higher share in terms of the EO that they have given us this year.

items.statement: Debtor days improved by 4-5 days; inventory high due to opportunistic raw material buying; aim to streamline by year-end
items.quote: has been slightly better for us. Debtor days has come down by about 4-5 days it has come down. Inventories are still high. We have maintained some high inventory because we were getting some raw material at good pricing

items.statement: Current ethoxylation utilization: Unitop 80-85%, Tristar 90-95%, core ethoxylation fully utilized
items.quote: Currently if you see in our ethoxylation business, our capacity utilization is almost close to 80% plus. If I break it down in terms of the companies in Unitop, we are almost at 80%-85% capacity utilization. In Tristar, we are at about close to 90%-95% capacity utilization. In the core ethoxylation, we are almost fully utilized in terms of capacity.

items.statement: New capacity revenue contribution expected from Q2 FY26
items.quote: Yes, the revenue should start showing up from Q2 of next year.

items.statement: Export revenue Rs 156 crore in Q3, Rs 405 crore in 9M FY25
items.quote: Rohit, this quarter we have done about Rs. 156 crore of exports. And for the nine months, we are at about Rs. 405 crore.

items.statement: Textile exports grew 14% YoY driven by Egypt, Turkey, North Africa, Bangladesh; domestic textile growing 5-6%
items.quote: In Textile if you see YoY, we have grown about 14% and most of this growth has actually come up out of exports. The export market is something we are now tracking very, very diligently for the Textile because the domestic market is growing at a very low single-digit kind of a number for us.

items.statement: Bangladesh target Rs 6-7 crore monthly sales intact but timeline extended due to local issues
items.quote: Our goal of Rs. 6 – Rs. 7 crore of monthly sales to Bangladesh is still there. I think it will take a little more time now given the current situation there.

items.statement: Reliance EO expansion delayed; clarity expected by end of Q4 or early Q1 FY26; could delay revenue/margin ramp-up
items.quote: We will get a better hang of this probably by the end of this quarter or early Q1 as to what Reliance is planning to do with their new expansion. We have timed our CAPEX closer to what we got an understanding from them that their expansion is going to come.

items.statement: New office and two warehouses leased; IND-AS lease accounting added Rs 1.5-1.6 crore one-time depreciation in Q3; ongoing quarterly depreciation ~Rs 1.4 crore
items.quote: There is a onetime charge in depreciation of about Rs. 1.5 - Rs. 1.6 crore kind of a number which has come in this quarter. Going forward, the charge that will come in the depreciation will be about Rs. 1.4 crore kind of a number.

items.statement: Institutional cleaning business expanding into equipment, tools, tissues to match competitors' full-service model
items.quote: We have to match what the competitors are doing. We will have to give this entire basket as a service. And that's where finally, as a consumer business, this will bring in value to Rossari.

items.statement: Textile expansion into spin finish for synthetic fibers, regenerated cellulose; silicon-based raw materials now produced in-house
items.quote: Besides this, the company has also planned to enter the spin finish business for synthetic fibers as well as regenerated cellulose. And we are well on track with this product range and in this quarter, these products are going to be launched, whereas another initiative which the company has done is to produce all the silicon-based raw materials in-house.

items.statement: Export growth traction expected from H2 FY26 as new offices and capacities ramp up
items.quote: Yes, you are right, it will probably start seeing some good traction H2 onwards.

items.statement: Target debt-to-equity ratio of 8-9x going forward, down from previous 10x limit
items.quote: And going forward, since we are looking forward to business outside Railways also, so we would like to be hovering around somewhere 8 to 9, this is the target right now.

items.statement: PAT to grow steeply quarter by quarter as higher-margin non-Railway business increases
items.quote: Rest assured, going ahead we are working very actively on ensuring that our bottom-line growth is bigger than what we have right now quarter by quarter.

items.statement: Non-Railway business of Rs 10,000 crore equivalent to Rs 30,000-40,000 crore Railway business in PAT impact
items.quote: Suppose if I do Rs. 10,000 crores business outside Railway, it is akin to Rs. 30,000 crores to Rs. 40,000 crores of business that we do for the Railways.

items.statement: FY25-26 expected to be very exciting with visible product mix shift toward non-Railway business
items.quote: And we believe that FY '25-'26 will be very, very exciting for the Company.

items.statement: Non-Railway margins 3x-5x higher than Railway margins of 35-40 paise
items.quote: Once we go out, the margins are quite higher. I am not quoting a number, but it hovers around somewhere between 3x to 5x of what I am getting in the Railways.

items.statement: NIM will definitely improve as non-Railway business mix increases
items.quote: Definitely, as our CMD has already told you, the mix of the business would definitely get changed and the non-Railway business will yield me a higher return, so definitely my NIM will improve.

items.statement: Won coal mining development project bid of over Rs 3,000 crore and Rs 700 crore deal with NTPC
items.quote: We have already been selected a lowest bidder in one project of more than Rs. 3,000 crores, one Rs. 7 00 crores ticket we have already done with NTPC, and many more are in pipelines.

items.statement: Multiple refinancing opportunities identified for allied Railway projects currently funded at higher rates
items.quote: there are many alli ed projects which are already running, and they are being funded at a very high rate. So, now positioning ourselves as the main financing arm of the Railway ecosystem, we want to look at every business which is there on the platter

items.statement: Actively shifting product mix toward higher-margin non-Railway Railway ecosystem projects
items.quote: What we plan is we plan to maintain the asset under management, but within that the mix has to be towards lucrative assets where I earn, say 150 bps, 200 bps, and still be cheaper than any of my peers.

items.statement: Non-Railway business currently less than 1% of AUM but growing rapidly
items.quote: Yes, right now yes, you are very right. It is just the beginning, for the first time in the history of the Company we are doing business outside Railway as a client.

items.statement: Gati Shakti program and dedicated freight corridors represent huge long-term CAPEX opportunity for next decade
items.quote: This dedicated freight corridor of eastern and western, they have covered only two lines. This country has got a golden quadrilateral, so four next lines of Gati Shakti are still on the pipeline and CAPEX should be huge.

items.statement: Aggressively mobilizing cheapest funds via 54EC bonds, zero coupon bonds, domestic bonds and ECB market
items.quote: We are extremely aggressive in tapping the cheapest fund resources which are our raw materials. we are actively mobilizing more and more funds under 54EC bond market and exploring zero coupon bond market, and domestic bond market, apart from keeping an eye on any opportunity from various currencies in ECB market.

items.statement: Moratorium on project assets extends to FY28; AUM stable till then due to offsetting capital recovery and interest servicing
items.quote: During this current financial year, I will be getting around Rs. 20,000 crores as capital recovery, and same quantum of the money being the debt servicing for these project asset, and these two items will offset each other that is why there will not be any major impact on my AUM.

items.statement: 46% of total AUM currently under moratorium period
items.quote: Currently, it is around 46% of my total AUM.

items.statement: No tax liability expected for next 4-5 years due to Rs 6,000+ crore unabsorbed depreciation cushion
items.quote: As of now, I have a cushion of more than Rs. 6,000 crores in my balance sheet as unabsorbed depreciation. I think going forward for next four, five years, I do not foresee any tax liability on my balance sheet.

items.statement: Maintains zero NPA record and CRAR above 700%
items.quote: We proudly maintain an extraordinarily high CRAR of more than 700%, as you know, and also a clean zero NPA record in the history of the Company.

items.statement: Leasing model adds 25% extra to PAT
items.quote: Our leasing model continues to benefit Indian Railway Finance Corporation January 21, 2025 us adding 25% extra to our PAT

items.statement: AUM could decline post-FY28 if no new EBR allocation and no non-Railway business replacement
items.quote: And just to answer your one more concern, as you mentioned that AUM after '28 will be coming down drastically.

items.statement: Expanding beyond Indian Railways to full Railway ecosystem including backward-forward linkages, PPP projects, ports, coal blocks
items.quote: We are actually now looking for the whole Railway ecosystem where we want to finance everything, like PPP or any other thing which comes through the Railway system at a better margin.

items.statement: Won open bid against all major banks and NBFCs by offering cheapest funding for Railway infra projects
items.quote: Your Company for the first time participated in an open bid for a coal mining development project having forward linkage with Indian Railway and emerged as the lowest bidder, outsmarting almost all the banks and NBFCs in the fray.

items.statement: Completed most domestic market bond tapping in last two months
items.quote: In fact in the last two months we have done most of the domestic market bond tapping, which earlier was not that frequent.

items.statement: Fluoro-intermediate project targets 10% of peak revenue in Q4 FY25 and 40-60% in FY26
items.quote: And at our Fluoro-Intermediate site at Lote, thrilled to share that in quarter 4, as we have been really working very diligently towards it, is where we are seeking about 10% of the peak revenues. And in the course of the next financial year, that is FY '26, we target to have 40% to 60% of the peak revenues.

items.statement: Fluoro-intermediate peak revenue is INR 200 crores
items.quote: The second one is the peak revenues that we are achieving from that asset base is a peak revenue of INR 200 crores.

items.statement: Company targets doubling sales from INR 2,800 crores in FY24 to FY28
items.quote: So, we are going to double our sales, correct, from INR 2,800 crores last year to FY '28.

items.statement: Essentials business targets 3x-5x asset turns and 8-12% EBITDA per dollar invested; Specialty targets 1x-2x asset turns and 20-25% EBITDA
items.value: Essentials: 3x-5x asset turns, 8-12% EBITDA; Specialty: 1x-2x asset turns, 20-25% EBITDA
items.quote: The margin profile, I think, is also something we have called out in our investor deck is for our Essentials business for every dollar that we invest, we are looking at specific asset turns. So, asset turns for Essentials 3x to 5x for every dollar invested, EBITDA of 8% to 12%. And for Specialty is 1x to 2x asset turns; EBITDA 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Dahej project on track for pending regulatory approvals, timelines and budget
items.quote: When we look at the projects that we are executing at our Dahej site, we continue to remain on track to receive the pending regulatory approvals and the project remains in schedule on timelines and in budget.

items.statement: Fluoro-intermediate project at Lote: key products commercialized, on track for revenue ramp
items.quote: In fact, all the key products that will contribute into FY '26, we have successfully commercialized at our asset base in Lote. So that is also positioning us well moving ahead.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 gross margin improved ~240 bps YoY due to better product mix and operational excellence
items.quote: This has enabled in improving our gross margin by nearly 240 bps.

items.statement: Sequential gross margin drop of 3% in Q3 FY25: 1.5% from input costs (acetic acid, alcohol), offset by 1.2% freight savings; net 1.8% drop plus 0.3% FX impact and 0.4% one-time damage costs
items.quote: So sequentially, our dip is 3%, mainly on account of input cost reason. That's around contributed to 1.5%. So sequentially, if you look at a 3% drop, let me explain you that first, that is getting offsetted by a saving in the transport and freight cost of nearly 1.2%. So, real decrease is 1.8%. Around 1% of that is contributing to the raw material cost increase, mainly in acetic acid and alcohol.

items.statement: EBITDA stabilized around INR 75 crores in Q3 FY25, up from INR 53 crores YoY, driven by power and fuel cost control despite 17% volume growth
items.quote: As you can see, our EBITDA has now stabilized at around INR 75 crores, which has grown around by INR 53 crores, mainly coming out of the power and fuel, which is remaining same in spite of the volumes increasing by nearly 17%.

items.statement: Fluoro-intermediate business targets Specialty EBITDA range of 20-25%
items.quote: So, Devang, basically, in our Specialty block, that's what we have called out, the focus remains that we deliver EBITDA of 20% to 25%. You have seen that also with our Specialty performance. We've actually delivered slightly above that. So that is also true for our fluoro-intermediates business that, that will be in that ballpark.

items.statement: Pharma, Coatings, Printing & Packaging, Flavors & Fragrances demand stable QoQ; Agro segment weak but expected to improve over time

So that's nothing new that you are grappling with or navigating

items.statement: Ethyl acetate spreads suppressed in bottom quartile at USD 145-150/t; no large spikes expected
items.quote: We are also seeing now linked to our product. If you see ethyl acetate, we see that the spreads remain in the bottom quartile being a bit suppressed in that about USD 145 to USD 150 range. We are expecting some movement but nothing large as compared to what we experienced in the previous time last year.

items.statement: Specialty revenue grew 29% YoY in Q3 FY25 on improved mix; Essentials volume grew 18% YoY on operational excellence without capex
items.quote: In quarter 3, our sales grew at 13% year-on-year, with a strong business volume growth in Essential business of 18%. That's driven by the operational excellence, mainly without any capex. Our Specialty business, which is a high profitable business, has grown 29% due on account of improved mix.

items.statement: Strategy to reduce ethyl acetate share from 60% of FY24 revenue to 40% by broadening offerings
items.quote: With the strategy that we are envisaging, this number will come down to 40%.

items.statement: Specialty exports driven by CASE industry (coatings, additives, sealants, elastomers) serving large MNCs in Americas, Europe, China; Pharma and Pigments split domestic/export
items.quote: The CASE industry, that is coating, additive, sealants and elastomer industry, primarily, we are serving the needs of large MNCs and catering to demand not domestically, but in the Americas, Europe and even China. items.statement: China revenue share increased consciously via targeted applications; adjacencies being explored
items.quote: So, China has been really a conscious bias, not an unconscious bias. And again, this is the strength of the portfolio. We have been able to target a specific application base, which has enabled us to tap into that. And there are, I would say, adjacencies that we would be working towards.

items.statement: Dr. Milind Vaidya now leads both R&D and Marketing to turbocharge Specialty innovation pipeline; Mr. Prateek Singh joining as CHRO end of January

We have had Dr. Milind Vaidya, whom I've introduced to you, managing now both the R&D and Marketing roles, which is then enabling end-to-end steering from market to in-house and which will turbocharge, we believe, our innovation pipeline for growth for Specialty. items.statement: No HF plant investment planned; sufficient HF capacity available competitively
items.quote: Simple answer to that, no, Devang we will not be doing it. We are not a large consumer of HF, and we believe there is enough capacity out there to meet our demands competitively.

So that should, I would say, buffer any untoward element. Secondly, as I've called out in the past, also for the feedstocks, when you look at supply-demand dynamics, a lot of the key products tend to be long. So, for example, acetic acid. So I am not anticipating at

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded to AA/stable/A1+ by India Ratings and rated by CRISIL
items.quote: Also, I'm glad to share that in quarter 3, Laxmi Organic received a credit rating upgrade from India Rating and got rated by CRISIL. The company is now rated AA/stable/A1 positive.

items.statement: Agro chemical segment <10% of Q3 revenue; innovators face USD 0.5bn launch costs; recovery timing uncertain, Europe/US may recover faster than South America
items.quote: If you see really the slide deck again, agro chem segment is only about 10% to 13%, or in fact, if you look at quarter 3, it is less than 10% of our overall exposure. I think one thing, while there's a lot of talk about agro, if you take a step back, the big reflection is now if you want to launch a product from lab to scale and if you want to globally launch it, If you speak to the large innovato

items.statement: Sustainability rating improved to 87% from 67% on Together for Sustainability; National Safety Council appreciation for third consecutive year
items.quote: We also received Together for Sustainability. From a sustainability lens, we had a big step up in the ratings. We've achieved a rating of 87%. Our last rating was 67%. So that is, again, committing ourselves to our customers, to our stakeholders and for future growth.

items.statement: Target net debt below Rs. 4,000 crores by end of FY25 to support future investment
items.quote: The Company stays on course, with its objective to bring net debt below Rs. 4,000 crores to support our future investment.

items.statement: Target 10% year-on-year volume growth for next 3-4 years reaching 21-27 million tonnes
items.quote: I am looking at a 10% growth year-on-year. From next year we should have all the way to 21 million tonnes, 23 million tonnes, 25 million tonnes, 27 million tonnes.

items.statement: Vadraj Cement production targeted to start Q3 FY27 with 1 million tonnes in FY27, 2 million in FY28, 3-4 million in FY29
items.value: 1 million tonnes in FY27, 2 million in FY28, 3-4 million in FY29
items.quote: Q3 FY '27 is when we are going to be ready with the plant. So, I will get one quarter of FY '27 and then '28 and '29. I am looking at a very optimistic 1 million coming out of Vadraj in FY '27, and then it goes to 2 million in '28, and 3 to 4 million in '29.

items.statement: Vadraj acquisition: Rs. 1,800 crores bid payment post NCLT approval plus Rs. 900-1,200 crores over 18-24 months for plant restart
items.quote: So, we are looking at Rs. 1,800 crores of payment post the court approval, and then on another Rs. 900 crores to Rs. 1,200 crores over a period of the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: FY25 YTD capex Rs. 299 crores, Q4 FY25 additional Rs. 50-60 crores for Jajpur siding and sustaining capex
items.value: Rs. 299 crores YTD + Rs. 50-60 crores Q4
items.quote: YTD CAPEX this year has been Rs. 299 crores, and I guess in Q4 we are looking at this Jajpur and a little bit of sustaining CAPEX which should be close to the tune of another Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60 crores.

items.statement: Routine annual sustaining capex ~Rs. 300 crores; Vadraj capex ~Rs. 1,200 crores over 2-2.5 years funded by internal accruals
items.quote: I had mentioned, Rs. 300-odd crores will be the kind of routine CAPEX for the Company. And hence, with this kind of CAPEX to run the operation and also do Rs. 1,500-odd crores or Rs. 1,700-odd crores to set up the brownfield we would be able to fund the CAPEX with the internal cash flows and the profitability improvement in the next two years.

items.statement: Vadraj adds 3.5 mtpa clinker (Kutch) and 6 mtpa grinding (Surat); total capacity to reach 31 mtpa by Q3 FY27
items.quote: By acquiring Vadraj Cement, the Company is poised to reach 31 million tonnes per annum cement capacity by Q3 F Y ‘27, with 19 million tonnes per annum in East, and 6 million tonnes per annum each in North and West

items.statement: Sonadih railway siding completed, moving from 3 to 4 rakes/day, target 5 rakes to eliminate road clinker movement
items.quote: Sonadih railway siding is completed, so we used to do about 3 rakes per day movement of clicker. Recently we have moved from three to four rakes, and our target is to move five rakes, which would mean that no more of road movement of clinker from Sonadih, everything will be by rake movement

items.statement: Jajpur siding advanced stage, last 100 meters track to be laid, expected ready in 6-8 weeks for Q1 FY26
items.quote: Jajpur siding is an advanced stage of completion, so I think the last 100 meters of track needs to be laid, so it should be ready in the next six to eight weeks. Come Q1 FY '26, Jajpur should be on.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA Rs. 258 crores on revenue Rs. 2,409 crores; unit EBITDA expanded QoQ despite 4% price decline due to cost reductions
items.quote: In Q3 FY '25, the Company recorded revenue and EBITDA of Rs. 2,409 crores and Rs. 258 crores, respectively.

items.statement: Project Bridge 2.0 delivered Rs. 50+/tonne YTD cost reduction; Q3 at Rs. 54/tonne, targeting Rs. 75/tonne in Q4
items.quote: On cost efficiency program Project Bridge 2.0 is on track, delivering a reduction upwards of Rs. 50 per tonne YTD.

items.statement: Cement prices plummeted in Oct-Nov, improved mid-Dec; Q3 cement realization down 3.6% QoQ but Dec exit up 6% over quarter average
items.quote: Cement realizations dropped Q-on-Q by 3.6%. But as I mentioned, we ended the quarter with December exit realization of 6% over the quarter average.

items.statement: Power & fuel cost per tonne reduced 6% QoQ to lowest in 13 quarters at Rs. 1.45/million cal; fuel mix: coal 42%, petcoke 48%, AFR 10%
items.quote: Power and fuel cost per tonne were reduced by 6% quarter-on-quarter. The Company has reached the lowest blended fuel cost in the last 13 quarters at Rs. 1.45 per million cal.

items.statement: Cement demand recovery in Q3 FY25 after challenging H1; 16% YoY volume growth to 4.7 mt; broad-based across East and North, trade and non-trade
items.quote: Firstly, let me touch upon the volume growth of 16% Y-O-Y to 4.7 million tonnes in Q3 F Y ‘25. Following the challenging conditions in H1 FY ‘25, demand conditions showed improvement in Q3 FY ‘25

items.statement: Key demand drivers: Centre Rs. 5.97 lakh crore and States Rs. 5.34 lakh crore pending capex as of Nov 2024; Eastern states avg 65% unspent; rural housing boost from good monsoon
items.value: Centre Rs. 5.97L cr, States Rs. 5.34L cr pending capex
items.quote: As of November 2024, the Center has Rs. 5.97 lakh crore in pending CAPEX, while States have Rs. 5.34 lakh crore CAPEX spending to be executed. Region wise, in Eastern states, including states of West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Orissa, pending states' CAPEX on an average is upwards of 65%.

items.statement: Premium product share maintained at 39% despite 16% volume growth; launched Concreto UNO in RMC, ZERO M tile adhesives/chemicals in MBM
items.quote: We had a broad based growth both in trade and non-trade, and certainly we maintained our value strategy, our premium product percentage continue d to be at 39

items.statement: Trade share stable at 71% in Q2 and Q3; expanded in Chhattisgarh (Vijay Chhattisgarh program), Bihar, Bengal, Jharkhand with premium products
items.quote: An additional data point, Jashandeep, to answer your question, our trade percentage share remained at 71% for Q2 and Q3.

items.statement: Net debt reduced Rs. 151 crores QoQ mainly driven by working capital release
items.quote: On a quarter-on-quarter basis net debt further declined by Rs. 151 crores , m ainly driven by release of working

items.statement: Net debt Dec 31, 2024 at Rs. 4,350 crores, down Rs. 183 crores YoY; trajectory from Rs. 5,495 crores (Dec 21) to Rs. 4,350 crores (Dec 24)
items.quote: Net debt as of December 31st, 2024 stood at Rs. 4,350 crores, reflecting a year-on-year reduction of Rs. 183 crores.

items.statement: Comfortable debt range Rs. 3,500-4,000 crores; Vadraj financing modalities being worked out, mindful of covenants
items.quote: In all of our calls in the last few years we have maintained that we would be comfortable having a debt level of Rs. 3,500 crores to Rs. 4,000 crores.

items.statement: Successful resolution applicant for Vadraj Cement (3.5 mtpa clinker Kutch, 6 mtpa grinding Surat); LoI issued, NCLT filing done, approval expected 8-9 months
items.quote: Friends, we became a successful resolution applicant for Vadraj Cement Limited, which is undergoing a corporate insolvency resolution process. And accordingly, Letter of Intent has been issued. Filing with NCLT has been done and approval to the Company's resolution plan is expected within eight to nine months.

items.statement: Vadraj deal subject to NCLT approval (6-9 months); business risk of deal reversal exists but confident; fair-weather port at Kutch requires clinker stocking for 3 months
items.quote: Possible, because recent issues which happened in others, I guess there are various reasons. Technically, I guess, if somebody wants to put a spanner on reverse, it is possible. But I do not think in terms of the reasons which hampered others' issue may not be the reason which will come for us.

items.statement: Audited FY24 emission rate 457 kg CO2/tonne cementitious, among lowest in industry
items.quote: The audited emission rate for FY '24 stands at 457 kg CO2 per tonne of cementitious material, which is amongst the lowest in the industry.

items.statement: Long-term slag supply agreement provides raw material advantage; exploring slag procurement from ArcelorMittal near Surat for blended cement
items.quote: On the raw material side, Nuvoco continues to be better placed due to its long-term slag supply agreement.

items.statement: Vadraj acquisition under IBC process; NCLT approval required within 8-9 months
items.quote: Filing with NCLT has been done and approval to the Company's resolution plan is expected within eight to nine months.

items.statement: Three new redevelopment projects added in Andheri East, Malad West, Borivali West spanning ~5 acres with 5.85 lakh sq ft saleable carpet area and expected turnover of Rs 2,150 cr
items.quote: To su pport this and to strengthen our presence in Western Mumbai, we added three redevelopment projects in Andheri East, Malad West and Borivali West. Cumulatively, we span an area of approx 5 acres and offer 5.85 lacs square feet of saleable carpet area. Together, these projects are expected to generate a turnover of Rs. 2,150 crores

items.statement: Eight upcoming projects with potential revenue of Rs 5,000 cr; another Rs 5,000 cr in final acquisition stages to be shared this quarter
items.quote: So, we have shared the upcoming project, list of eight projects which is having a potential revenue of Rs. 5,000 crores, approx imately. And another Rs. 5,000 crores worth of projects are in the final stages of acquisition, which will be shared very soon in this quarter, maybe by this quarter end

items.statement: IPO proceeds of Rs 410 cr: Rs 176 cr utilized (Rs 26 cr construction, Rs 82 cr approvals, Rs 43 cr general corporate, Rs 25 cr IPO expenses); Rs 234 cr balance
items.quote: we raised Rs. 410 crores from IPO, out of which we have already utilized Rs. 176 crores, and the balance funds are Rs. 234 crores from the IPO. items.quote: Currently there is a fund of around Rs. 300 crores out of the IPO, half of which should be deployed by March this year, and remaining half by this year end, which is towards the construction of the ongoing project, and half of which towards land acquisition should be deployed by March.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 sales bookings of 74,000 sq ft worth Rs 220 cr, up 93% YoY; nine-month bookings 179,000 sq ft worth Rs 556 cr, up 24% YoY
items.quote: this quarter we achieved sales booking of 74,000 square feet of area, which amounts to Rs. 220 crores, wh ich is up by 93% on a Y -o-Y basis. The collections for Q3 FY ’25 stood at Rs. 178

items.quote: So, those debtors, basically the demands what we raised during last 15 days of September '24 and we realized those money in the next 15 days, October 15, first 15 days of October we realized that money. So, that was not that high.

items.statement: Six ongoing projects expected to complete next financial year; launching 3-4 projects annually; current pipeline completion over 4 years
items.quote: The six ongoing projects we are expecting to complete in the next financial year and we will be launching three, four projects every year. So, the current pipeline of existing projects should be completed in four years of the existing as well upcoming, both combined.

items.statement: Mid-segment 2 BHK is the fastest moving; greenfield commands higher rates than redevelopment but similar sales velocity
items.quote: So, sales is kind of uniform. The mid segment as in the 2 BHK y ou can say is the ever moving item. Then bigger the ticket size, maybe slower the velocity. B ut there is no differentiation as such between redevelopment for a greenfield project, the velocity is similar. Rates in greenfield are more than redevelopment, but the velocity is similar

items.quote: Our consolidated revenue for nine months FY ‘25 was Rs. 560 crores vis-à-vis Rs. 513 crores in nine months FY ‘24, registering a growth of 9.3%. items.statement: Q3 FY25 revenue Rs 231 cr (+13.8% QoQ), EBITDA Rs 68 cr (+12.3% QoQ, margin 29.3%), PAT Rs 50 cr (+15.4% QoQ, margin 21.7%)

items.quote: By the time our projects get occupation OC, we are managing to sell 90% of our inventory. Aditya Shah: 90% of inventory? Amit Jain: By the time of OC, and the balance in three to six months, historically that's how it has been. To give you an idea, currently we may be 40% of the project completed and we store 30%, 35% of goods

items.statement: New Western suburb projects (Malad, Andheri) in approval stage; launch expected in 6-9 months (next financial year)
items.quote: These new project you are talking, they will take some time. Th e Malad and Andheri projects, maybe they will be launched in the next financial year. They will take time for approval and all, so minimum six to nine months

items.statement: Management team young (Chairman <50); succession planning not imminent; professional team in place
items.quote: Succession planning, I am too young. I am not even 50 currently and we have very you ng Directors in the company who are themselves very young. So, you can say we have a young team, it is a little bit too early for succession planning. And it’s driven in a professional way by a very equipped team

items.statement: Redevelopment margins under pressure due to increased competition; greenfield margins more resilient
items.quote: In the past we made good margin in redevelopment also, but now the competition has increased a lot in redevelopm ent, so the margins have squeezed. So, going forward, the margins in redevelopment proje ct can go down to as low as 15% and land buy the greenfield projects will continue to make better margins, 25% per say

items.statement: Management does not provide predictive revenue or CAPEX guidance; they react to demand and deploy just-in-time.
items.quote: We are kind of like very agile in terms of like how we deploy the CAPEX. So, we are anticipating that like majorly based on the pipeline we will evaluate and based on that like we will kind of like do just-in-time deployment as much as possible over next several quarters.

items.statement: Capex deployed till December 2024 is Rs 2,017 million (Rs 201 crores).
items.quote: So, we have deployed 2,017 million till December. That is Rs. 201 crores.

items.statement: No orders placed yet for Blackwell GPUs; reactive capex on Hopper range possible depending on sales outlook.
items.quote: Currently, we have not placed the orders for Blackwell GPUs, although we have a lot of conversations going on for acquiring the Blackwell GPUs. And as we plan the initial capacity, it will obviously keep all the stakeholders informed about that.

items.statement: Data center capacity expanding from 4.2 MW to nearly 10.2 MW supported by recent fundraise.
items.quote: In line with our growth plan, we are also expanding our data center capacity from 4.2 megawatts to nearly 10.2 megawatts, which is a move which is supported by our recent fundraise.

items.statement: Chennai data center expected to be operationalized during next quarter (Q4 FY25).
items.quote: We are trying to do it as soon as possible. I guess like during the next quarter, it would get operationalized whether we will be able to deploy all the services in the first quarter itself, like remains to be seen.

items.statement: Demand environment remains strong; sales cycles have lengthened but demand has not gone away.
items.quote: The demand environment continues to remain strong. So, the pipeline is there obviously for both H100 as well as H200. What we are potentially missing is immediate closures that we were seeing in the past. So, I think the sales cycles have grown.

items.statement: Q3 revenue declined 12.6% QoQ due to churn and downscaling of bursty training deployments concentrated in the quarter.
items.quote: We have witnessed total revenue decline of 12.6% on quarter-on-quarter basis from 476 million to 416 million in the current quarter.

items.statement: Cumulative GPU deployments: nearly 700 H100, 256 H200, and around 700 non-H100/non-H200 GPUs.
items.quote: Our cumulative deployments have now grown to nearly 700 H100 GPUs, 256 H200 GPUs, and around 700 non-H100 and non-H200 GPUs.

items.statement: Training workloads constitute majority of revenue; long-term mix expected to normalize toward 50:50 or 60:40 training:inference.
items.quote: I believe that ultimately it's going to be somewhere the ratio eventually over the medium and long term, I think it should become more like 50:50 or maybe 60:40 in favor of like training.

items.statement: Revenue concentration in a few large customers caused QoQ decline; goal is to broaden base with larger enterprise deals via L&T partnership.
items.quote: We currently have a fairly small scale and compared to that, some of our larger customers, their deployments were quite large. Now our goal obviously is kind of like build a much larger infrastructure which is spread across much larger footprint of larger customers.

items.statement: L&T partnership enables pursuit of long-cycle enterprise opportunities and larger market share.
items.quote: This collaboration will open new revenue streams, drive growth in high-demand AI services, and we will also improve our operational efficiency leading to enhanced profitability and revenue. Together, we will leverage each other's strengths to capture a larger market share and create a more powerful presence in the AI and cloud sector.

items.statement: Raised Rs 14,849 million via preferential issue in 2024; utilized Rs 1,508 million till Q3 FY25; balance Rs 13,349 million as of Dec 31.
items.quote: During 2024, we had raised a total of 14,849 billion through presidential issue of equity shares. Out of this, we have utilized INR 1,508 million till Q3'25 and we have balance of 13,349 million as on December 31st.

items.statement: US GPU export rule not expected to have immediate impact; India volumes below limits and exceptions exist for certain end-users.
items.quote: In the short term, I don't think there would be any immediate impact. So, one is, of course, there is like about like a more than a period of a quarter before these regulations come into effect. Secondly, based on what India is doing today in terms of overall volume, currently, we are not really hitting the limits that are being placed.

items.statement: ARPU declined in Q3 due to churn and downscaling of larger training customers.
items.quote: Some of the larger customers on the training side has churned or downscaled. So, that has resulted in the ARPU decline.

items.statement: Competitive intensity has increased with more players in cloud GPU infrastructure; market expanding to accommodate more participants.
items.quote: Yes. So, as AI has become very, very mainstream since 2019-20, since we have been working with AI, the competition has become far more intense today. And competition in the compute and technology world has always been intense. So, that has definitely increased.

items.statement: Bursty training workloads cause revenue volatility at current scale; impact expected to mute as customer base and infrastructure grow.
items.quote: We anticipate the effect of bursty training workloads would eventually become muted at a larger scale and then we intend to build cloud GPU computing

items.statement: No management changes or key hires discussed.
items.quote: We have with us on the call today Mr. Tarun Dua – Managing Director; Ms. Megha Raheja – the Whole Time Director and C hief Financial Officer; and Mr. Ronit Gaba – the Company Secretary

items.statement: R&D spend expected at 8.5-9% of sales for full fiscal year
items.quote: We expect the investment to be in the range of 8.5-9% for the full fiscal.
