items.statement: Gold Loans grew >30% YoY; new RBI guidelines may slightly impact near-term growth
items.quote: Gold Loans increased over 30% year-on-year, though new RBI guidelines may slightly impact growth in the near future

items.statement: LAP grew 20% YoY with marginal pricing improvements
items.quote: LAP grew 20% year-on-year, with marginal improvements in pricing

items.statement: Auto loan portfolio grew 25% YoY; transitioned to 80% fixed-rate disbursements in one quarter
items.quote: Our auto loan port folio grew 25% year -on-year, despite a slower growth last quarter due to a strategic pivot from a floating rate model to a fixed rate model

items.statement: Home loans grew 9% YoY with 80% savings account penetration for home loan customers
items.quote: Our approach to low-yield assets, such as home loans, reflects this strategy, with the segment growing 9% year-on-year and achieving 80% penetration for savings accounts with home loan customers

items.statement: Credit card business growing rapidly in organic sourcing and ENR on small base
items.quote: Our credit card business is growing rapidly, both in organic card sourcing and ENR, albeit on a small base

items.statement: Average CASA grew 2.3% QoQ (SA avg +2.5%, CA avg +1%) while EOP CASA declined due to wholesale CA drop
items.quote: SA averages grew by 2.5% quarter-on-quarter, CA averages increased by 1%, and overall, Average CASA grew by 2.3% this quarter

items.statement: Wholesale term deposits >₹3 crore dropped from ₹37,821 crore to ₹33,848 crore
items.quote: wholesale term deposits — specifically those above ₹3 crore —have decreased from ₹37,821 crore to ₹33,848 crore

items.statement: Cost of funds benefit from liability reorientation to show over medium term; not immediate
items.quote: Directionally these efforts will show results. I am sure over medium term because all these changes, some of these have played out during the quarter till the end of the month

items.statement: Gold loan regulatory changes (RBI Sept 30 letter) causing industry-wide disruption; 1-2 quarters of disruption expected
items.quote: the RBI letter of 30th September has been sent across to all banks and NBFCs, and there are quite a few changes in terms of processes and practices that were being done, which has definitely caused a little bit of a disruption in the industry as a whole

items.statement: Reorientation is a medium-term process; balancing growth and quality; short-term headwinds expected
items.quote: reorientation is never complete, I think it's a process. We cannot expect it to be over in a month, but like I said, we will balance growth and reorientation all the time

items.statement: Not pressing pedal on unsecured lending in near term; waiting for credit cost environment to stabilize
items.quote: in the short term, just now, I don't think we are going to press the pedal on these segments because it will be like wading into the storm

items.statement: Average CASA adopted as key internal metric replacing EOP CASA for quality-focused deposit growth
items.quote: One of the most significant changes has been shifting our internal focus to Average CASA as a key metric

items.statement: New MD & CEO KVS Manian completed first quarter; conducted 'Listening Tours' across 9 zones meeting 2,000+ employees
items.quote: This quarter is particularly noteworthy as it marks the full first quarter under the leadership of our new MD & CEO, Mr. KVS Manian

items.statement: FMCG volume growth slowed over last 6 months; urban growth moderating while gradual rural recovery sustained.
items.quote: At the MAT level, total FMCG volume growth has slowed down over the last 6 months, indicating subdued demand. Within this, urban growth continues to moderate while gradual rural recovery is sustained.

items.statement: Market data shows step-up in small pack growth pace across portfolio due to macroeconomic conditions and urban moderation.
items.quote: Reflective of the current macroeconomic situation, market data for the quarter shows a step-up in the pace of growth for small packs across the portfolio.

items.statement: Net material inflation turned positive last quarter signifying net cost inflation; pricing in line with NMI during the quarter.
items.quote: Net material inflation, or NMI, as you're aware, is the net absolute inflation after adjusting for buying efficiencies and savings. NMI turned positive last quarter, signifying net cost inflation for the business.

items.statement: Crude palm oil and tea saw year-on-year inflation; soda ash benign; crude oil deflated; rupee depreciated ~1% vs dollar.
items.quote: When it comes to commodity prices, we continue to see a year -on-year inflation in crude palm oil and tea, but soda ash largely remained benign. Crude oil prices continue to deflate during the quarter and rupee depreciated by around 1% against the dollar.

items.statement: Expect low single-digit price growth in near term if commodity prices remain at current levels.
items.quote: If commodity prices remain where they are, we expect a low single-digit price growth in the near term.

items.statement: Expect to maintain EBITDA at lower end of 23-24% range amidst inflationary material prices.
items.quote: Amidst inflationary material prices, we expect to maintain EBITDA at the lower end of 23 -24% range.

items.statement: Gross margin 50% for quarter; EBITDA margin 23.5% within 23-24% range.
items.quote: For the quarter, our gross margin was 50%, while EBITDA at 23.5% was within our range of 23% to 24%.

items.statement: Proactive measures restricted gross margin dilution to 70 bps year-on-year.
items.quote: Our proactive measures effectively restricted the gross margin dilution to 70 basis points year -on-year.

items.statement: Underlying sales growth 2% led by pricing; underlying volume growth flat.
items.quote: In this backdrop, HUL delivered a turnover of INR15,195 crores with an underlying sales growth of 2%, led by pricing. Underlying volume growth was flat.

items.statement: Turnover weighted market share gaining as of MAT December 2024; business winning percentage back to 60%.
items.quote: I'm happy to share that we are continuing to gain turnover weighted market shares as of MAT December '24.

items.statement: Negative mix from Home Care growing ahead of portfolio and shift to smaller packs; premiumization partially offsets.
items.quote: While absolute volume grew competitively, it was offset by a negative mix. There are a few drivers for this negative mix. One, Home Care, which has relatively low realization per ton versus HUL average, has grown ahead of the rest of the portfolio.

items.statement: Premium segments growing ahead of mass segment; secular trend of premiumization remains resilient.
items.quote: The secular trend of premiumization remains resilient with premium segments growing ahead of mass segment this quarter.

items.statement: More than 70% of business gaining penetration; share of voice higher than share of market.
items.quote: More than 70% of our business is gaining penetration, indicating that we continue to expand our consumer base, reaching more people than we did before.

items.statement: Acquired 90.5% stake in Minimalist at pre-money enterprise value of INR2,955 crores; path to acquire balance 9.5% in 2 years; expected completion Q1 FY26.
items.quote: We will acquire 90.5% stake in the company at a pre -money enterprise value of INR2,955 crores (Subject to closing adjustment as per terms set out in transaction document s) through a combination of secondary buyout and primary infusion with a path to acquire the balance 9.5% stake in 2 years

items.statement: Board approved scheme to demerge Ice Cream business into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited; 1 equity share of new entity for every 1 HUL share held.
items.quote: Our Board of Directors has approved the scheme of arrangeme nt to demerge HUL's Ice Cream business into Kwality Walls ’s (India) Limited. Pursuant to the scheme, 1 equity share of the new entity will be allotted for every 1 equity share held in HUL.

items.statement: Sale and divestment of Pureit business completed on 1st November; consideration received and profit recognized in quarter.
items.quote: The sale and divestment of Pureit business was completed on 1st November, as mentioned earlier in the presentation, consideration for this was received and profit was recognized in this quarter.

items.statement: Board approved acquisition of palm undertaking of Vishwatej Oil Industries for palm localization strategy and supply chain resilience.
items.quote: Additionally, the Board of Directors has approved the acquisition of the palm undertaking of Vishwatej Oil Industries Private Limited. This is a part of HUL's palm localization strategy to build supply chain resilience for palm derivatives through backwar d integration.

items.statement: Leveraging HUL supply chain scale and efficiency to unlock capacity and generate margin synergies for Minimalist.
items.quote: Supply chain is a core strength for HUL. We have a large supply chain network and are best-in-class when it comes to supply chain cost. Leveraging our scale and efficiency, we will be able to unlock capacity and generate margin synergies.

items.statement: Home Care growth driven by premium portfolio (Surf Excel), liquids market entry (Rin, Sun), and filling white spaces.
items.quote: We've been -- this is a category where the growth is driven by a great portfolio, especially a portfolio that's got a good presence in premium Surf Excel. And here is also the category where we entered the liquids market quite aggressively, both in fabric cleaning and in dishwash.

items.statement: Gaining value and volume share in Hair Care, Skin Care, Nutrition Drinks, Tea, Coffee, Packaged Foods.
items.quote: We continue to strengthen our market leadership with value and volume share gains.

items.statement: Significant volatility observed in crude palm oil, crude oil prices and rupee over last couple of weeks; will monitor and take proactive actions.
items.quote: However, significant volatility has been observed in crude palm oil, crude oil prices and the rupee over the last couple of weeks. As always, we will closely monitor price fluctuations and take proactive actions as appropriate.

items.statement: Effective tax rate for quarter 24.6% (lower due to LTCG on Pureit disposal); excluding LTCG, ETR 26.8%; expect full year ETR around 25.5%.
items.quote: Excluding the long-term gains, ETR for the quarter was 26.8%. We expect our full year ETR to be around 25.5% after taking into consideration prior period tax adjustments.

items.statement: Expect current moderation in demand trends to continue; watchful of real wage growth, food inflation, employment levels.
items.quote: We expect the current moderation in demand trends to continue. We remain watchful of various macroeconomic indicators that could impact the pace of recovery, such as real wage growth, food inflation and employment levels.

items.statement: Minimalist team to join HUL family; partnership to unlock next phase of growth.
items.quote: We are delighted to welcome the Minimalist team into HUL family and are excited to partner them to unlock the next phase of growth, scaling the brand to greater heights.

items.statement: Foods & Refreshment margin range seen as healthy at 19-20% for 9M FY25
items.quote: And we believe that margin range of 19% to 20% is pretty healthy for our Foods business.

items.statement: Personal Care margin band of 17-18% considered healthy for 9M FY25
items.quote: Again, at a 17%, 18% margin band, I think, is a pretty healthy margin for the Personal Care business.

items.statement: Overall HUL margin improvement to be mix-led and leverage-led
items.quote: And the totality of the margin outlook for Hindustan Unilever, the way we want to drive this improvement - mix led, and leverage led.

items.statement: Beauty & Wellbeing margins to decline from ~30% as portfolio shifts 900bps toward premium over few years
items.quote: So, you will see more innovation intensity. You will see more launches as you already have seen this quarter. And also going forward in March quarter as well, it's a busy quarter for us in Beauty & Wellbeing. So, we do believe that we will take some amount of margin basically decline in Beauty & Wellbeing compared to the healthy levels of around 30% that we have today

items.statement: Urban demand moderating; rural recovering gradually; near-term subdued FMCG growth expected to continue
items.quote: We believe that the moderate overall subdued atmosphere for growth for FMCG industry will continue near term.

items.statement: Small-pack down-trading seen in December quarter across discretionary categories; expected to self-correct in a quarter or two
items.quote: And importantly, this quarter, we've seen titration from large packs to small packs, across categories, especially the more discretionary the category is, more titration there is, less so in Home Care.

items.statement: Volume growth sustained well ahead of market for 3 quarters; competitive volume share at all-time highs
items.quote: We have sustained grow th, growing consistently over 3 quarters by volume, well ahead of the market. We've gained competitive volume share at all time frames

items.statement: Negative mix in Q3 FY25 due to Home Care outperformance and small-pack shift; premium mix contribution up 100bps YoY
items.quote: And even in this quarter, our contribution of 120 index and above segment is 100 basis points more than last year's same period.

items.statement: Small-pack negative mix impact expected to self-correct in a quarter; premiumisation drive to continue building mix
items.quote: I do believe and we do believe at this point in time that the impact of small pack negative mix should self-correct in a quarter or so, number one. Number two, our own drive to make portfolio more premium, that should continue building further mix possibility within our own performance going forward.

items.statement: Minimalist acquisition at pre-money INR 2,955 crore at 5.9x sales multiple; 90.5% acquired, balance 9.5% in 2 years
items.period: next 1 quarter for closing, 2 years for balance
items.quote: I quoted a number that on secondary buyouts that we have done pre- money at INR2,955 crores at 5.9 sales multiple. And this price, this is to acquire the brand as of now, we acquired 90.5% of that enterprise value, and we'll acquire the balance 9.5% in 2 years' time.

items.statement: Minimalist integration to preserve agility; operate as 'speed boat' for at least 2 years with HUL enabling ecosystem
items.quote: But in the next -- at least 2 years, we want them to operate like a speed boat. We will offer them whatever they need to become more successful.

items.statement: Four routes to build Beauty & Wellbeing portfolio: expand big brands, bring global brands, launch own brands, bolt-on acquisitions like Minimalist
items.quote: And the fourth route, which we had called out, we will do bolt-on acquisitions as we get the right target. And Minimalist is a classic example.

items.statement: Glow & Lovely rural penetration 60-70%; urban revamp with Glass Bright launch; core relaunch in rural in next few weeks
items.quote: As you know, it's got the highest unmissable brand superiority score we have. It's got a 60% - 70% rural penetration. And over the last few years, it's seen under rural stress, a category drop out leading to loss of penetration.

items.statement: Beauty & Wellbeing 6 big bets portfolio (~INR 2,000 cr) growing strong double digits in Q3 FY25
items.quote: So yes, the INR2,000-odd crores portfolio that we have, Percy, at the 6 big bets we've spoken about, the growth trajectory of that portion of the business continues to remain strong. And even this quarter, we have grown in good double digits that portfolio of INR2,000 crores

items.statement: Organised trade (modern trade + e-commerce) grew double digits in Q3 FY25 but slowed vs previous quarter
items.quote: Overall, organized trade, if I look at modern trade e-commerce put together, they have grown in double digit. Overall, if I look at the segment and growth like everything else put together, even that has slowed down compared to the previous quarter.

items.statement: Oral Care grew mid-single digit in Q3 FY25 driven by pricing and Closeup master brand
items.quote: Oral Care grew mid-single digit, driven by pricing and driven by Closeup, which is the master brand that we have, which has been doing pretty good business for us.

items.statement: Stratos formulation rolled out across Lifebuoy and Lux in large part of country across WIMI clusters; remaining pockets in next couple of quarters
items.quote: But let me say that a large part of the country across WIMI clusters, across both the brands, we have moved to Stratos formulation. There are some pockets of brand geography combination because of the innovation footprint, we will make the move in next couple of quarters

items.statement: Stratos formulation risk assessed as 100% confident after 6-9 months in market across multiple WIMI clusters and both brands
items.quote: Yes. So, answer is yes, and I would not say 80%, Manoj, I'll say 100. We are very confident that Stratos formulation is the right thing to do.

items.statement: Minimalist founders to be retained; HUL people embedded but operating as founders; learnings from OZiva integration applied
items.quote: There are HUL people there, but they operate in the start-up as if they were founders there, too. So, we will -- we've learned from that, and this is going to be the way we will build these speedboats.

items.statement: Near-term demand moderation expected to continue for a quarter or two; transitory not long-term; recovery pace depends on employment, real wage growth, food inflation
items.quote: And when this behavior comes, it does remain for a couple of quarters. So, we do believe that this will be there for a quarter or 2 more. And -- but it is transitory in nature. I don't think so this is a long-term conversation and it should go away in a quarter or so.

items.statement: Commodity environment supportive; Rabi crop outcome expected to boost rural consumption going forward
items.quote: We do believe that overall commodity inflation for FMCG, it will support. It will support the recovery of consumption overall. So hence, we are hopeful that we should see better times, but the pace of recovery will get determined, basis what happens with employment, real wage growth and food inflation.

items.statement: FY25 volume target similar to FY24 at around 5.5 million tonnes
items.quote: For the full -year FY '25, we believe we will be able to achieve sales volume similar to FY '24 of around 5.5 million.

items.statement: FY26 volume target of 6.4 to 6.5 million tonnes
items.quote: Going to the next year, I think we are looking at anywhere between 6.4 million to 6.5 million as a number , which we should be able to comfortably achieve

items.statement: Internal target for FY26 EBITDA per tonne around ₹500+
items.quote: Our internal pencilling also is very similar number.

items.statement: Demand picked up in second half of Q3 after slow start due to festive season and labour unavailability
items.quote: While the quarter started on a slow note owing to festive season and unavailability of labo ur, we did exp erience pickup in construction activities during the second half.

items.statement: Rural demand improved gradually aided by better agricultural output and increased construction activity
items.quote: Rural demand as well improved gradually, aided by better agricultural output and an increase in construction activity.

items.statement: Prices stable in December and early January with no increase or decrease; expect similar trend to continue
items.quote: December exit all the way up to 10th and 20th prices fortunately remain very, very stable. They have been steady. There has not been an increase, nor there has been a decrease. We expect similar trend to continue

items.statement: Current prices versus Q3 average up by ₹2-3 per bag in some South markets
items.quote: I think it is safe to assume around ₹2 to ₹3 increase, not more, because in between, it went up, but it gradually s lipped, barring ₹2 to ₹3 in some of the markets.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA per tonne at ₹273; expect improvement from operating leverage as utilisation rises
items.quote: EBITDA per ton stood at ₹273 during the quarter. Loss after tax for the quarter stood at ₹54 crore. Going ahead with the rising utilis ation rate, we expect EBITDA per tonne to improve on account of lower power and fuel expenses and savings in

items.statement: Operating leverage could add ₹200-300 EBITDA per tonne as Jajpur and Andhra plants ramp up
items.quote: I think the operating leverage itself should add another ₹200 to ₹300 EBITDA per tonne kind of a number , because as we have seen both Jajpur as well as Andhra Cements operating rates are subpar.

items.statement: ₹88 crore spent in 9M FY25; balance ₹241 crore over next 1.5 years, bulk in Andhra plant upgrade
items.quote: The amount spent so far for FY '25 is ₹88 crore is what we have spent. The balance to be spent is ₹241 crore over the next 1.5 years.

items.statement: 6 MW solar plant commissioned at Gudipadu in January 2025; approvals received for another 6 MW at Dachepalli
items.quote: the company has successfully commissioned a 6 -megawatt solar power plant at its Gudipadu unit. Further, the company also has received approvals f or implementation of another 6- megawatt solar power plant at its Dachepalli unit.

items.statement: New 6-stage pre-heater at Dachepalli progressing slightly ahead of schedule
items.quote: The new 6 stage pre -heater construction project at Dachepalli unit is progressing slightly ahead of schedule.

items.statement: Andhra plant upgrade (pre-heater) now expected by October-November 2025, 3-4 months ahead of March 2026 schedule
items.quote: we are running almost good quarter to four months ahead of schedule. We should, in all likelihood, be ready for this Dussehra which is in October, November, we should be ready to commission the Andhra plant, especially the pr e-heater.

items.statement: Plant utilisation rates: Mattampally 51%, Gudipadu 93%, Bayyavaram 68%, Jeerabad 78%, Jajpur 22%, Dachepalli 32% in Q3
items.quote: Mattampally plant operated at 51% utilisation, while Gudipadu, Bayyavaram, Jeerabad, J ajpur and Dachepalli plants operated at 93%, 68%, 78%, 22% , and 32% respectively during the quarter.

items.statement: Power and fuel cost at ₹1,456 per tonne in Q3 vs ₹1,701 in Q3 FY24; freight at ₹835 vs ₹864
items.quote: Power and fuel cost stood at ₹1,456 per tonne as against ₹1,701 per tonne reported during Q3 FY '24. Freight cost for the quarter stood at ₹835 per tonne as against ₹864 per tonne during Q3 FY '24.

items.statement: Fuel cost expected to remain flat; pet coke and coal prices seen stable with possible slight downside from oil price decline
items.quote: we expect, all in all, prices to remain more or less flat.

items.statement: Gross debt ₹1,462 crore as of Dec 2024 (₹1,123 crore long-term); net worth ₹1,866 crore; debt-equity 0.66:1; cash ₹159 crore
items.quote: the gross debt as on 31st December 2024 stood at ₹1,462 crore , out of which ₹1,123 crore as a long -term de bt and the remaining constitutes the working capital. The net worth of the company on a consolidated basis as on 31st of December 2024 stood at ₹1,866 crore . Debt equity ratio stands at 0.66:1. Cash and bank balances were at ₹159 crore

items.statement: Bank debt cost around 10.5% including provisions and other financial costs
items.quote: The bank debt is around 10.5%, that includes the provisions and the other financial costs, but the bank debt is at around 10.5%.

items.statement: Vizag land sale: two of three approvals received; cabinet approval expected end of Q4 to early Q1 FY26; monetisation over 1.5 years after approvals
items.quote: we received two approvals . I think by middle of Q1 coming year, I think we should have got all the approvals. So, we are just waiting for cabinet approval to come, which is likely probably during end of Q4 to early part of Q1.

items.statement: Andhra Cements merger planned after land monetisation; land conversion delays holding up process
items.quote: The idea is first to sell the land, monetise the land and then merge the company into Sagar. So we are in the process. So as soon as that part is done, we 'd be more than happy to merge it at the earliest.

items.statement: Andhra Cements expected to break even by end of FY26; upgrade of old asset to accelerate turnaround
items.quote: think end of next financial year, we should be in a situation to break even as far as Sagar Cements Limited (SAGCEM) Q3 FY25 Earnings Conference Call January 27, 2024 Andhra is concerned. What you have to please remember is Andhra, the asset is old. So, there is an upgrade that is happening. Once the upgrade is done, I think the turnaround for that company could be a lot quicker

items.statement: Waste heat recovery at Gudipadu to save ₹50-75 per tonne; Andhra upgrade to save ₹350-400 per tonne at Andhra level
items.quote: The waste heat recovery at Gudipadu should save anywhere between ₹50 to ₹75 per ton, primarily because of electricity. But the Andhra upgrade should help us save anywhere between ₹ 350 to ₹400 per ton in terms of cost structure at Andhra level.

items.statement: South market has 35+ players; M&A reduced actors by only 1-2; competitive intensity not significantly lower; prices cannot stay low forever as acquirers need ₹1,000-1,200 EBITDA/ton to justify deals
items.quote: All in all, number of market actors, probably it got reduced by only one or two, but you still have 35 -plus actors sitting in this region . So, the competitive intensity may not have significantly come down.

items.statement: Andhra growing strongly, followed by Tamil Nadu and Karnataka; Telangana lagged post-election but low-cost housing push may revive demand
items.quote: Andhra is growing very strongly, followed by Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, then only Telangana because unfortunately, the real estate in Hyderabad also has taken a back seat.

items.statement: Amaravati capital development in planning stage with finances tying up; expected to spearhead South demand over next couple of years
items.quote: we believe it is a long-drawn process. So, we are very hopeful that over the next couple of years, I think Amaravati demand should actually sp earhead the overall South demand in a big way.

items.statement: Industry volume focus driven by player targets; supply additions gradual but persistent; management believes industry cannot sustain volume-only focus and will shift to margins
items.quote: It's true th at there is some amount of supply that is likely to happen, and that is likely to continue. We don't see any stoppage to supply coming into the market. Fortunately, that supply is likely to be in a gradual kind of a thing, not in a single burst. But we strongly believe that industry cannot run the way it is with only volume focus.

items.statement: Employee cost increase of ₹7 crore Q-o-Q due to annual appraisal
items.quote: It's because the annual appraisal has kicked in.

items.statement: Revised FY25 revenue guidance: may miss by up to ~3%; EBITDA margin maintained at 24%
items.quote: Further, we find it necessary to revise our revenue guidance to reflect the impact of the current market uncertainties, slower growth in key sectors and geopolitical factors on our outlook for FY '25. On the consolidated level, we anticipate we may miss our revenue guidance by up to approximately 3% for FY '25. However, we remain confident in our ability to maintain EBITDA margins of 24% for the f

items.statement: Consolidated order book INR 684 cr as of Dec 31, 2024 vs INR 572 cr a year ago
items.quote: Despite the above challenges, we have a healthy order book of INR 684 crores as of December 31, 2024, as against INR 572 crores as of December 31, 2023, which will convert into revenue in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Gear division order book INR 684 cr as of Dec 31, 2024; Q3 order intake INR 469 cr (+27.4% YoY)
items.quote: The order intake for the quarter was INR 469 crores, reflecting a healthy 27.4% year -on-year increase. As of 31st December 2024, our order book stood at INR 684 crores, positioning us for sustainable growth in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: MHE division open order book INR 421 cr as of Dec 31, 2024; Q3 order inflow INR 185 cr (+17.8% YoY)
items.quote: The order inflow for the quarter stood at INR 185 crores, up by 17.8% year-on-year compared to INR 157 crores in Q3 FY '24. As of 31 December 2024, the open order book for MHE stood at INR 421 crores, reflecting strong demand and growth prospects.

items.statement: Gear division: modest 2.1% YoY growth in Q3, -3.6% YoY for 9M; slowdown in steel and sugar sectors domestically; UK/Europe macro and geopolitical headwinds
items.quote: We experienced a modest 2.1% year -on-year growth in Q3 FY '25 and a decline of 3.6% year-on-year for the first 9 months of FY '25. This performance is largely attributed to a slowdown in the steel and sugar sectors in India, where demand has been subdued specifically in domestic market . Further external macroeconomic factors slowdown in the UK, political instability in Europe and other geopoliti

items.statement: MHE division: 55.2% YoY revenue growth in 9M FY25; 75.9% YoY order inflow growth in 9M; strong demand across sectors
items.quote: Our MHE division witnessed a 55.2% year-on-year growth in revenue in the first 9 months of FY '25, with a robust 75.9% year -on-year increase in order inflows for the same period. This performance is a testament of our effectiveness of our strategic actions and the growing demand for material handling solutions across sectors.

items.statement: Consolidated Q3 EBITDA margin 27% (+150 bps YoY) driven by favourable product mix, after-sales, operational efficiencies
items.quote: Our consolidated EBITDA for the quarter was INR 143 crores, up from INR 120 crores in Q3 FY '24, representing a solid growth of 18.4%. Consequently, our EBITDA margin improved to 27% compared to 25.4% in Q3 FY '24. We have a 150 basis points improvement. This margin improvement was mainly driven by a favo urable product mix, improvements in after sales service and operational efficiencies.

items.statement: 9M FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin stable at 24.3%
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the 9 months was INR 347 crores compared to INR 339 crores in 9 months FY '24. The EBITDA margin for the period stands at 24.3%, which is stable despite the challenges faced in certain sectors and markets.

items.statement: Gear division Q3 EBIT margin 27.9% (+50 bps YoY) driven by product mix changes
items.quote: The EBIT margin improved to 27.9% in Q3 FY '25 compared to 27.4% in the same period last year, driven by changes in the product mix.

items.statement: MHE division Q3 EBIT margin surged to 31.6% from 18.6% YoY (+1,300 bps) due to favourable product mix and higher aftermarket contribution
items.quote: The EBIT for MHE stood at INR 35 crores compared to INR 12 crores in Q3 FY '24, reflecting a significant turnaround. EBIT margin surged to 31.6% in Q3 FY '25, up from 18.6% in Q3 FY '24, an increase of 1,300 basis points. This was primarily due to a favourable product mix and a higher contribution from the aftermarket business.

items.statement: MHE sustainable EBIT margin guided at 20-22%
items.quote: MHE margins will go through fluctuations, okay? Positive as well as negative. So, it is difficult to ascertain because they will depend on the type of product mix that we are able to market and sell depending upon the demand. However, we are reasonably confident that we should be able to maintain anywhere between 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Consolidated sustainable EBITDA margin guided at 23%
items.quote: In terms of the sustainable margin, I said, considered at the consol e level, we see 23% is my sustainable margin. 20%-22% margins is specifically for the MHE division.

items.statement: Gear division 9M product mix: standard (CP) 51%, engineered (EP) 49%; shift toward 50-50
items.quote: So for the 9 months now considering in this quarter, we had a better revenue from EP that is engineer product. So with this for 9 months, we are now CPs at 51% and EP that is engineered customers product it is 49%.

items.statement: Q3 overseas revenue INR 126 cr (-1.2% YoY); slowdown in UK/Europe due to macro and geopolitics
items.quote: Our overseas revenue in Q3 FY '25 stood at INR 126 crores, a slight decline of 1.2% year-on-year compared to INR 128 crores in Q3 FY '24. This was primarily due to a slowdown in the UK and European markets, geopolitical scenario and global economic volatility, which adversely impacted business sentiment and project investments in these regions affecting our export performance.

items.statement: Loan book target of INR 1.5 lakh crores by FY26 and INR 3 lakh crores by 2030 at 15-16% CAGR
items.quote: So we are looking at the figures in the next fiscal of around INR 150,000 crores and by 2030, around INR 300,000 crores. So average CAGR will be around 15%.

items.statement: Near-term growth of 30-40% for next 1-2 years before settling at 15-16% CAGR
items.quote: So in 1 to 2 years at the time, our growth rate may be around high as good as maybe 40% or 30%. But finally, we will be settling in the CAGR of 15% -16% only because we will not be aggressive after 2 years.

items.statement: Committed liabilities/order book exceeds INR 1.2 lakh crores
items.quote: And we will not be stopping at this pace because we have a very robust pipeline, so committed liabilities of the loan, the loan book or, you can say, order book of the Company is more than INR 1.2 lakh Crores presently.

items.statement: Sanction-to-disbursement conversion ratio over 80% with 3-4 year conversion timeline
items.quote: So the conversion ratio presently is more than 80%, and we are definitely sure that whatever we are promising and committing to our borrowers because of our terms and conditions, including the interest rate, we will be the most preferred lender.

items.statement: NIM around 3.2% overall; 3.85% excluding EBR portion; spread 2.41%
items.quote: NIMs will be around 3.2%. If you exclude the EBR portion of INR 20,000 crores, which has been taken by the Government of India, our NIMs are around 3.85% and our spread is around 2.41%.

items.statement: ROA at 2.45%, ROE improved from 11% to over 14%
items.quote: And the return on assets also, if you can see, we had improved a lot. We are at 2.45%, and the return on equity, we had improved from around 11% to more than 14% now.

items.statement: Incremental cost of borrowing reduced to 6.8% in 9M FY25 from 7.2% a year ago
items.quote: As you have seen in the last 9 months ended during the current financial year, our incremental cost of borrowing has reduced from 7.2% to around 6.8%.

items.statement: Target to increase external commercial borrowings/FCNR share to 20% of borrowing mix from current 17%
items.quote: And we look forward to take this percentage of external commercial borrowings and FCNRs to around 20% of our total borrowing mix, so as to have -- so as to further reduce our cost of borrowing.

items.statement: Net NPA 0.18%, gross NPA reducing; total NPA INR 2,200 crores with INR 1,200 crores under NCLT
items.quote: And you can see that our NPA levels are coming down very, very heavily and now our net NPA is only 0.18% and gross NPA is also reducing. So you can say that we are not only working towards growing business, we are also resolving our assets.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 recovery target: INR 150 crores principal and INR 50 crores interest

items.statement: PMAY 2.0 expected to drive INR 1 lakh crores disbursement over 4-5 years for HUDCO

items.statement: Housing portfolio ~40%; urban infra ~60%; targeting 40% housing / 60% urban infra mix going forward
items.quote: It will be around 40-60 only because housing is not so capital-intensive. We are into the affordable housing category only. So you can take 40% towards the housing and 60% towards the urban infrastructure.

items.statement: Over 75% of loans backed by government guarantees; expanding into cash flow based and PPP projects
items.quote: Of course, presently, our more than 75% of the loans are backed by the government guarantees, but we had off late started doing the cash flow based projects also. So we have a very diverse kind of loan portfolio.

items.statement: Government guarantee share may reduce going forward due to FRBM constraints; focusing on bankable/PPP projects
items.quote: So I don't see any high -- this is the highest that government guarantee we had. So going forward, the number may reduce. But at the same time, we will not compromise on the quality of the asset and the quality of the entities to which this lending will be done.

If you see, last year, by 31st of December, quarter 3,

items.statement: Sanctions up 5x YoY from INR 18,000 crores to INR 92,000 crores
items.quote: And you can see our sanctions has raised around 5 times on quarter to quarter on a yearly basis, from INR 18,000 crores, we have raised up to INR 92,000 crores.

items.statement: Average loan tenure 6-7 years; longest 20 years, shortest 1 year
items.quote: Longest loan will be around 20 years, the shortest is around 1 year. So average, we'll be maintaining between 6 to 7 years of the time.

items.statement: Raised INR 39,000-40,000 crores in 9M FY25 at 6.8% weighted average cost; borrowing mix diversified with 17% foreign currency, 40% bonds
items.quote: Our borrowing, if you see that we had continually worked to cut down our cost of funds, irrespective of our growth, we had been successfully able to cut down our cost of fund and during last 9 months, we had raised around INR 39,000 crores - INR40,000 crores and the weighted average cost of the borrowing is 6.8%.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 disbursement slightly above INR 10,000 crores; H2 quarterly run rate ~INR 10,000 crores
items.quote: I think everything is going as per plan, in H2, every quarter, we are disbursing around INR 10,000 crores and I think in quarter 4, it will be slightly more than that.

items.statement: New delinquency addition rate slowing since mid-November 2024; expect normalisation by Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26
items.quote: Overall, we believe that the new delinquency addition should normalise by Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26.

items.value: INR 229 Crore accelerated write-off, INR 376 Crore total Q3 write-off, INR 606 Crore 9M write-off
items.quote: Accordingly, we took an accelerated write-off on loan accounts with 180+ DPD on paying amounting to INR 229 Crore this quarter resulting in an additional credit cost of INR 73 Crore. The total write-off for Q3 FY25 stood at INR 376 Crore and for 9M FY25 at INR 606 Crore.

items.statement: NII grew 7.4% YoY to INR 862 Crore; portfolio yield 20.2%, interest spread 10.4%, average cost of borrowing 9.8% for last 6 quarters
items.value: NII INR 862 Crore, yield 20.2%, spread 10.4%, cost of borrowing 9.8%
items.quote: The net interest income grew by 7.4% year-on-year to INR 862 Crore with a portfolio yield of 20.2% and an interest spread of 10.4%. We have been able to maintain our average cost of borrowing at 9.8% for the last 6 quarters, despite the prevailing scenario.

items.statement: NIM 12.5% in Q3 FY25 due to INR 75 Crore interest reversal; 9M FY25 NIM 30%
items.quote: NIM slightly declined to 12.5% for Q3 FY25 due to an interest reversal of Rs. 75 crores, while 9 months FY25 NIM stood firm at 30%.

Based on our internal evaluation, we are confident that we can retain more than 80% of borrowers in the 4/5 lenders cohort.

items.quote: The EBIT margins for the Wires and Cables segment improved by ~120 bps on a sequential basis to stand at 13.5%.

items.statement: Solar cables, inverters, panels seeing strong traction from Surya Ghar Yojana, driving FMEG growth

items.statement: International business grew 62% YoY, 29% QoQ; contribution 8.3% of revenue in Q3 FY25; expanded to 81 countries
items.quote: The international business registered a robust growth of 62% year-on-year and 29% quarter-on-quarter, resulting into improvement in its contribution to the Company's top-line to 8.3% in Q3 FY25 and 6.6% for nine months FY25.

items.statement: Have almost all approvals for targeted SKUs in US market; addressable market size not quantified
items.quote: As far as the SKUs, which are the ones we are targeting, and if we are specifically talking about U.S., we have almost all the approvals for all the type of SKUs that we want to export over there.

items.statement: Industry demand expected to exceed capacity additions; top 4-5 players hold 60-70% share and will add capacity; no overcapacity risk seen
items.quote: As of now, the thought process is that the demand will exceed the capacity. And probably we'll have to wait out and see what the other players or the industry does going ahead as far as the capacity additions are concerned.

items.statement: Potential US tariffs on Mexico (25%) could create pricing advantage for Indian cable exports; monitoring if similar duties applied to India
items.quote: As per what the American President is saying, and if he actually goes on implementing 25% import duty on Mexico, then the pricing differential between the cables that we are able to supply versus what Mexicans can supply, obviously, the pricing goes in favour of India.

items.statement: Net cash position ₹17.1bn; working capital cycle 51 days within 50-60 day comfort range
items.quote: Further, our net cash position stood at ₹ 17.1 billion. In addition, our working capital cycle stood at 51 days, within our comfort range of 50 to 60 days.

items.statement: Finance cost ₹498mn in Q3 FY25; other income ₹250mn

items.quote: So, Shreepal, yes, Shreepal, the 1 to 30 number last quarter was about INR527 crores. This quarter, the closing number was about INR348 crores. So that number has been coming down.

items.statement: Added ~105-106 split branches in FY25; no greenfield branches

items.quote: Yes, yes it has produced 5 tons of the equivalent of the silver in the last 6-7 months. So, it is not like that it is not producing, it is producing at the run rate of course 30% of the design capacity, but we are hopeful that the Q4 should be almost 60%-70% of the design capacity.

items.statement: Hindustan Zinc Alloy subsidiary: Q3 EBITDA Rs. 43 crore, PAT Rs. 31 crore; annual run rate Rs. 150 crore EBITDA, peak Rs. 200 crore
items.quote: The EBITDA generated by Hindustan Zinc Alloy Private Limited is Rs. 43 crore during the Quarter 3 and profit after tax of Rs. 31 crore.

items.statement: Fertilizer plant (5.1 lakh ton) commissioning Q4 FY26; EBITDA potential Rs. 400-450 crore, revenue Rs. 2,000-2,500 crore annually
items.quote: On a full scale basis for this 5.1 lakh tonne of the fertilizer plant, we are having the EBITDA potential of Rs. 400 to Rs. 450 crore annually.

items.statement: 10M ton tailings recycling plant under design; testing samples in Australia; technology finalization in 1-1.5 months
items.quote: We are sending samples to Australia for testing so that the technology can be frozen. Once, I guess, another 1-1.5 month, that will be done. And once that is done, then we can come back and share with you how much will be the yield of it, how much will be the CAPEX of it.

items.statement: Provisioned Rs. 83 crore for mining cess (Supreme Court ruling); no new demands received; may reverse in subsequent quarters
items.quote: So, Shreyans, I think we have been very, very ultra conservative and we provided Rs. 83 crore as a provision in the last quarter. And there has not been any demand on account of it. We will actually see whether to reverse in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Management reiterates forecast of minor sales volume growth for full FY25
items.quote: We are confident and hold on to our forecast of achieving minor sales volume growth in this financial year.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY26 provided at INR1,100-1,200 crores
items.quote: Roughly about between INR1,100 crores and INR1,200 crores for next year.

items.statement: First phase of 35,000 MTPA OTR tire capex on track for H1 FY26 completion
items.quote: The first phase of this capex is progressing as per schedule, and we expect to complete it in the first half of financial year '26.

items.statement: 9M FY25 capex at INR968 crores
items.quote: Our capex for 9 months of this financial year were at approximately INR968 crores.

items.statement: Advanced carbon black plant of 30,000 MTPA completed in September, undergoing customer testing
items.quote: Post the completion of capex of 30,000 metric tons per annum of high-value advanced carbon material plant in September last year, we are undergoing testing with end customers.

items.statement: Market scenario remains challenging; Europe weak, Americas and India growing
items.quote: Market scenario continues to be challenging. However, our strong product profile, backed by brand investments, has led us to achieve minor sales growth on a year-on-year basis in Q3.

items.statement: Q3 standalone EBITDA margin at 24.8%, 9M at 25.4%
items.quote: The standalone EBITDA for the quarter was at INR639 crores, registering a growth of 9% year-on-year. The margin came at 24.8%.

items.statement: Raw material costs up 100-200 bps, major impact expected in Q4 due to shipping lag
items.quote: So on raw material, we indicated that the price is going up for 100to 200 basis points, it should impact the margins. But the major impact of that cost will be coming in the coming quarter because of the lag of the shipping time, material comes in this quarter.

items.statement: Freight costs have stabilized after previous reduction
items.quote: Freight cost, whatever has been reduced that we have indicated in last time, now it is on thestable.

items.statement: Euro-INR rate averaged Rs 91 in Q3, expected at Rs 92-93 for balance period
items.quote: So it was Rs 91 for the last quarter and the whole of the year. And for the balance period, we expect Rs 92 to Rs 93.

items.statement: Q3 volumes at 76,343 MT (+5% YoY), 9M volumes at 233,211 MT (+11% YoY)
items.quote: For the quarter, our volumes stood at 76,343 metric tons, a growth of 5% year-on-year. For nine months, volume stood at 233,211 metric tons, a growth of 11% year-on-year.

items.statement: 9M sales mix: Europe 43%, India 29%, Americas 16%, ROW balance; Channel: Replacement 73%, OEM 25%
items.quote: For the nine months of financial year '25, approximately 43% of the sales came from Europe, 29% from India and 16% from Americasand the balance comes from rest of the world. In terms of channel contribution, roughly 73% was contributed from replacement segment, while OEM contributed to about 25% and the balance came from offtake.

items.statement: Gross debt INR3,045 crores, cash INR2,942 crores, net debt ~INR103 crores as of Dec 31, 2024
items.quote: Our gross debt stood at INR3,045 crores at the end of 31st December '24. Our cash and cash equivalents were at INR2,942 crores. Accordingly, we have a net debt of approximately INR103 crores.

items.statement: Third interim dividend of INR4 per share declared, total FY25 dividend INR12 per share
items.quote: The Board of Directors has declared a third interim dividend of INR4 per equity share. This brings the total dividend for this financial year to INR12 per share, including the earlier 2 interim dividends.

items.statement: Satish Sharma hired as Senior President for Strategy and Business Development
items.quote: I'm happy to welcome Mr. Satish Sharma to our team as Senior President for Strategy and Business Development. He brings with him a rich experience of over 3 decades in the tire industry.

items.statement: EU deforestation regulation deferred to Jan 1 next year, no further updates
items.quote: It is not in Q3. It is deferred to 1st Jan of next year. But apart from that, there is no further update on that.

items.statement: India off-highway market share ~6-7% overall, agri ~10%, industrial/construction/mining 3-4%
items.quote: So overall in both the off-highway would be similar to international levels of 6% to 7%. Agri would be closer to 10%, and the others are growing up. So approximately 6% to 7%, I would say, for the whole off-highway business.

items.statement: Too early to comment on US tariff impact under new administration
items.quote: So too early to comment. We'll have to wait and watch what comes, then only we can comment. Otherwise, at the moment, we can't comment what he will do.

items.statement: Channel inventory at normal levels, wait-and-watch mode due to geopolitical and shipping uncertainties
items.quote: It is at same levels. So I think everybody is waiting and watching what happens on the geopolitical scenarios, what happens on the shipping times and price cost, both. So I think there is a lot of wait-and-watch scenario for us to comment on that.

items.statement: 9M category mix: Agriculture 59%, OTR/industrial/construction 38%
items.quote: In terms of category, agriculture contributed to 59%. OTR, industrial, construction contributed to 38%, and the balance came from other segments.

items.statement: Carbon black revenue ~9% of 9M revenue
items.quote: Approximately 9%. Less than 10%.

items.statement: Advanced carbon black plant ramp-up will take time, profitability expected at par or slightly better than industry
items.quote: is very less, 30,000 tons, and it is initially there -sSamples are being given and tested. So it will take time to ramp up. Pramod Amthe: Okay. And anything on the profitability side? Madhusudan Bajaj: Probably it will be at par with the industry, maybe slightly

items.statement: No buyback planned; cash to be used for capex, promotion, product mix, new capacities
items.quote: We are constantly investing in the capex and the growth of the company, whether it is in terms of promotion, in terms of product mix, in terms of setting up new capacities, so which will continue. So we will use the money for those purposes.

items.statement: Americas growth driven by long-term product and infrastructure focus, expected to stabilize and grow
items.quote: So the top two drivers has been the focus that we've been doing over the years in terms of product for Americas, in terms of infrastructure for Americas. So that is now kicking in. Going forward, we are quite hopeful that this should stabilize and continue to grow over there.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin of 18-20% by end of FY26
items.quote: we had recommended to the Board at the beginning of this financial year itself that by FY ‘26 we will be targeting to get to 18% to 20% margin. And the Board had approved that.

items.statement: EBITDA margin up 590 bps YoY and 10 bps QoQ in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Effective cost management in a soft advertising environment, has helped us maintain our momentum on profitability with our EBITDA margins up 10 bps QoQ, and up 590 bps YoY.

items.statement: Ad revenue down 8% YoY, up 4% QoQ; urban and Hindi heartland weakness, South holding better
items.quote: Q3 FY’25 was a soft quarter for advertising growth, wherein broad consumption slowdown outweighed festive season pickup. While we did see some pick up in October closer to Diwali, the momentum quickly cooled down in November, December.

items.statement: Subscription revenue up 8.2% YoY for nine months FY25
items.quote: We have been able to drive healthy YoY growth in subscription revenues and our nine -months FY ’25 subscription revenues are up 8.2%.

items.statement: TV viewership up 1.4% industry-wide; network share gained 40 bps to 16.9% YoY
items.quote: the overall industry wide TV viewership has increased by 1.4%. Further, we continue to be a strong #2 entertainment network in India, and we have gained 40 bps share to 16.9% compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: ZEE5 EBITDA loss narrowed by Rs 22.6 Cr QoQ and Rs 107.8 Cr YoY; subscribers and watch time grew YoY
items.quote: ZEE5 has further narrowed its operating losses in this quarter. It’s EBITDA loss is lower by Rs 22 .6 Cr QoQ & Rs 107.8 Cr YoY basis. While cost structure and profitability has been a key focus area for us in this business, we also continues to make steady progress on usage and engagement KPIs. Both the total number of subscribers and average watch time during this quarter has grown on a YoY basis

items.statement: Movie business lean in Q3 with 5 distribution deals; key releases lined up for Q4
items.quote: During this quarter, we released 5 movies, 2 Hindi and 3 regional . which were all distribution deals. And therefore, “Other Sales and Services” revenues have shown a declined 43% YoY due to lower syndication and leaner movie lineup.

items.statement: Zee Music Company remains #2 with 160M YouTube subscribers and 43B video views; profitability healthy but selective on growth
items.quote: Zee Music Company (ZMC) remains #2 music channel with around 160 mn subscribers of YouTube and over 43 bn total video views during the quarter driven by the new-age music catalogue and rich library. Within the music business, our profitability remains fairly healthy.

items.statement: New RIO published per TRAI tariff regulations; competitive pricing approach adopted
items.quote: In line with the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India’s (TRAI) tariff regulations, we have published the new Reference Interconnect Offer (RIO) that reflects the competitive pricing approach adopted by the Company.

items.statement: Content inventory, advances and deposits at Rs 69.9 bn, down Rs 4.3 bn YTD
items.quote: Dec’24 Content inventory, advances and deposits were at Rs 69.9 bn, lower by Rs 4.3 bn on YTD basis.

items.statement: ICC arbitration proceedings with Star initiated; initial filings done, long-drawn process expected
items.quote: On the ICC arbitration, the proceedings have begun. Both the sides have made their filings with the court and the arbitrator. But it's still initial days, it's a relatively long drawn process.

items.statement: Depreciation reduced organically; expected to remain at similar levels going forward
items.quote: it's an organic reduction. I mean, there is no major shift in our asset profile or the depreciation rate. So, it would be around the same levels.

items.statement: Music rights getting aggressive from domestic players; international players not yet aggressive
items.quote: On the music part, yes, as we stated that the music rights are getting a bit aggressive in the market, but from what I see, it's largely from the domestic players itself. I do not see that much aggression yet from the international players.

items.statement: Employee expenses increased QoQ due to wage increments rolled out from September
items.quote: Our employee expenses have increased on a QoQ basis as we have rolled out wage increments from September.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 EBITDA margin expected to be similar to FY24 (9-11% range); FY26 margin guidance 13-15% driven by premium product sales
items.quote: This year, our margins we are expecting on a year-on-year -- for the full year basis should be on a similar line. Since we have recently launched the new products in the premium segment, this will contribute additional margin for the next year onwards maybe. This year, we expect the margin remains in a similar range.

items.statement: Revenue guidance FY26 expected to exceed INR1,200 crores assuming flat ethanol revenue
items.quote: Yes, we should. So considering ethanol and all if we will be flat, we should be crossing that number. It should be higher than that.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 gross margin 38%, EBITDA margin 12%, PAT margin 8% despite high grain prices (rice INR28,000/MT, maize INR24,000/MT)
items.quote: Even the rice price reaching 28,000 per metric ton and the maize at 24,000, our focus on operational efficiency and disciplined cost management help us sustain a healthy gross margin of 38%.

items.statement: Ethanol margin sustainable at 7-9% range depending on raw material pricing
items.quote: So margin in ethanol should be within the range of 7% to 9%. It depend on the pricing of the raw-material. But Yes, if the price of raw-material sustained to level what it is, so we should be able to deliver those sort of numbers.

items.statement: Festive season and winter onset drove strong Q3 demand; proprietary IMFL volume grew 23% YoY to 4.69 lakh cases
items.quote: The festive season in the advent of winter provided us a significant boost to demand, resulting in a robust performance. Net revenue increased by 71% to INR327 crores compared to INR191 crores in the same period last year.

items.statement: Secured OMC ethanol tenders for 29,724 KL for supply year 2024-25; ethanol plant running at optimum capacity
items.quote: Our ethanol plant is currently running at optimum capacity and we have successfully secured tenders from OMC with an allocation of 29,724 kiloliters of ethanol for the estimate supply year of '24-'25.

items.statement: FY25 and FY26 capex ~INR100 crores each year funded by internal accruals and preferential issue; INR50 crores spent on new bottling hall with 10 lines for contract manufacturing
items.quote: So for '25 and '26, we know around INR100 crores each year will be our capexand that will be mainly through our internal accruals and the preferential money which we have raised.

items.statement: Total bottling lines increased to 41 after adding 10 new automated lines for contract manufacturing; malt plant capacity 6,000 L/day expected to start production April 2025
items.quote: To support our growth initiative, we have installed additional bottling lines, bringing our total to 41 lines. This advanced facility enhanced our ability to meet the growing demand of both proprietary and licensed IMFL products.

items.statement: Launched Nicobar Gin (EBB INR8,100) and Hillfort Whiskey (EBB INR3,100) in prestige+ category; combined 3,000 cases sold in 9M FY25; RTD launch Q4 FY25, Tequila and single malt in pipeline
items.quote: Over the past year, we have introduced two new products in the prestige and above category, Nicobar gin and Hillfort whiskey. The launch of these brands has not only strengthened up our premium product portfolio, but also refined our commitment to deliver quality at affordable price.

items.statement: MP FY25-26 excise policy: 47/3,300 shops closed (minor impact), 20% license renewal duty hike, mandatory e-BG, new bar license for beer/wine/RTD (positive for RTD launch), new 60-proof country liquor segment
items.quote: The proposed policy includes a restriction in sale of liquor in regional sites across 17 town and villages, resulting in closure of 47 retail shops across Madhya Pradesh. From this perspective, the closure represents just 47 shops out of 3,300 shops statewide. This constitutes a minor fraction of the retail network and we do not foresee any material impact on sales.

items.statement: Rice INR28,000/MT, maize INR24,000/MT in Q3; FCI broken rice at INR22,500/MT expected to soften raw material prices; rice-to-ethanol yield ~450 L/MT
items.quote: Even the rice price reaching 28,000 per metric ton and the maize at 24,000, our focus on operational efficiency and disciplined cost management help us sustain a healthy gross margin of 38%. Encouragingly, raw material costs have begun to stabilize, which would provide further relief in coming quarters.

items.statement: IMIL realization similar or slightly higher; proprietary IMFL realization expected to rise with premium brand sales; Nicobar EBB INR8,100, Hillfort EBB INR3,100
items.quote: So in terms of the IMIL, the realization would be on the similar lines or slightly higher. But we are expecting that in coming years that the realization in our IMFL brands, proprietary brands should increase as the sale of our premium brands would increase.

items.statement: Gin market: ~100 launches in 2 years, only 20-25 performing; Tequila: 30-40% market growth, AABL to be 3rd Indian player with 100% agave imported from Mexico; RTD market expected 17-20% growth
items.quote: Like we've seen 100 gins which has been launched in India over the last couple of years. But out of which I think only 30 to 20- 25 are performing well. So one is that you have to be consistent. Second is that you have to assure the quality is really good of the liquid and the packaging is good.

items.statement: Proprietary IMFL revenue INR37 crores (+31% YoY), Licensed IMFL INR77 crores (+13%), IMIL INR62 crores (+23%), Merchant ENA INR39 crores, Ethanol INR72 crores (10M L volume) in Q3 FY25
items.quote: In terms of segment-wise performance, proprietary IMFL brand contributes to INR37 crores, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 31%. License brand revenue grew at 13%, reaching to INR77 crores. IMIL sales stood at INR62 crores, grew at 23%.

items.statement: Excise duty varies by state: borne by manufacturer in Delhi/Chhattisgarh, by retailer in MP/Kerala; impacts reported revenue differently across states
items.quote: So see, so excise duty, you have to look statewide. So like in MP and Kerala, there is no excise duty on the part of manufacturer that is being borneby the retailers. So that doesn't come in our books. And okay and the duty right now we are seeing is basically because of our increase in sales in Delhi and Chattisgarh, where the excise duty is on the part of the manufacturer.

items.statement: Recruiting senior sales and marketing personnel in new states (UP, Maharashtra, Goa) as part of market entry strategy
items.quote: And that's why the company is also taking aggressive actions and recruiting senior sales and marketing people in various states. That's our strategy has been that we take certain senior well experienced players in different markets wherever we enter.

items.statement: Order book to be executed over remaining tenure is around Rs. 700 crores
items.quote: So, the order book that we have to be executed in the remaining part of the tenure is around Rs. 700 crores.

items.statement: Order book executable over 3 to 5 years on average
items.quote: I think over 5 years. Tapan Jayaswal Yeah. I mean, different phases are there for different customers. But on an average, you can assume around 3 to 5 years

items.statement: Over 90% of order book is product revenue, balance services
items.quote: So, most of it is in product, almost like more than 90% would be in the product territory. The balance is for the services.

items.statement: Employee count reduced from 1,938 in Sep 2024 to 1,903 in Dec 2024
items.quote: And in terms of the employee size, by end of September 2024, it was around 1,938, which was reduced to 1,903 by December end.

items.statement: Southeast Asia and ANZ leadership roles were replacements after being vacant
items.quote: Yes. Clearly, both these were replacements. We did not have these positions filled for some time and that's what we've done.

items.statement: Company has a couple more senior positions in process of filling
items.quote: And we have a couple of more senior positions that we are in the process of filling it.

items.statement: Strong traction from banks and NBFCs for digital transformation across India, Southeast Asia, Middle East, Australia
items.quote: A lot of traction when it comes to upcoming banks and NBFC in terms of digital transformation. We are getting a lot of traction not just in India, but in different countries, including Southeast Asia, Middle East, Australia.

items.statement: Sales cycles have lengthened from 6 months to 1-2 years with Board involvement
items.quote: See, typically, the sense we get is that our customers want to be very cautious about the solutions that they are choosing. And hence, their selection cycles have moved from typical 6 months to a year, sometimes 2 years and so on.

items.statement: Price increase on existing platform accepted by customers; new solutions being implemented
items.quote: Our customers have been understanding enough to realize this point. And they continue to look forward to implementing our new solutions as well. Some of them are getting implemented already, and the others, we are confident, would like to implement and derive benefits out of the new product.

items.statement: Management does not provide revenue or earnings guidance per policy
items.quote: As you all are aware, Nucleus Software does not provide any specific revenue earning guidance.

items.statement: EBITDA margin around 15% for 9 months; long-term benchmark is much higher
items.quote: We will want to move to profitability much better than this number. How soon that happens is that remains to be seen. But clearly, this is not our benchmark. Benchmark would be much higher.

items.statement: May allow margins to dip below current level for a quarter or two to fund long-term investments
items.quote: though we do not expect anything of that sort to happen, but if required for a quarter or two, maybe if it goes below this, we would allow that to happen, but continue to focus on the investments that we make for the long-term value

items.statement: Gross fixed asset addition of Rs. 2.45 crores in Q3 FY25 (computers, software, furniture, office equipment)
items.quote: During the quarter, there is a gross addition of fixed assets of Rs. 2.45 crores, consisting primarily of Rs. 1.17 crores on computers and servers, Rs. 0.69 crores on software, Rs. 0.56 crores on furniture and pictures and Rs. 0.3 crores on office equipment.

items.statement: Receivables increased to Rs. 109.6 crores from Rs. 99.7 crores previous quarter
items.quote: With regard to receivables, we are at Rs. 109.6 crores against Rs. 99.7 crores previous quarter.

items.statement: USD 4.25 million forward contracts at avg rate Rs. 84.95; mark-to-market loss of Rs. 0.6 crores
items.quote: In terms of foreign currency hedges on December 31st, 2024 we had USD 4.25 million of forward contract at an average rate of Rs. 84.95. There is a mark to market loss of Rs. 0.6 crores, which is hedging reserve in the balance sheet.

items.statement: FinnAxia handles $15+ trillion transactions annually across 20 countries; re-architected with API-first strategy
items.quote: So, we are handling more than $15 trillion worth of transactions a year through this platform, which also talk about a size of the kind of volume this platform is handling today. And we are operating with this platform in 20 countries as of now.

items.statement: AI enabled in products for 3-4 years; FinnAxia has AI fraud detection, lending product has AI across origination, servicing, collections
items.quote: Our product offering has this. So, we have AI enabled in our product from almost more than 3, 4 years now. So as Abhishek mentioned, so our transaction management product. FinnAxia, is already enabled with an AI fraud detection module

items.statement: Top 5 clients contribute 28.1% of revenue vs 28.2% previous quarter
items.quote: Revenue contribution from the top five clients for the quarter is 28.1% against 28.2% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Federal Bank went live on FinnAxia on time; pursuing more large bank deals for transaction banking
items.quote: We replaced one of the solutions, which was not giving them value enough for their corporate customers. So, they have grown live absolutely on time, and I think that's what jointly both Federal Bank and Nucleus done a press release about that win

items.statement: Cash and equivalents Rs. 877.9 crores (mutual funds Rs. 613.8 crores, FDs Rs. 196.4 crores, tax-free bonds Rs. 34.1 crores, current accounts Rs. 33.6 crores)
items.quote: Total cash and cash equivalent as on December 31 st, 2024 are Rs. 877.9 crores against Rs. 895.1 crores as on September 30 th, 2024. This includes balances in current accounts of Rs. 33.6 crores, various schemes of mutual funds Rs. 613.8 crores, fixed deposit of Rs. 196.4 crores, investments in tax free bonds of Rs. 34.1 crores.

items.statement: Hoshin Kanri lean initiative showing early productivity benefits; financial impact expected in 3 years but not quantified
items.quote: It will be difficult to, say it in land terms, but I'm sure, yes, 3 years is a reasonable time, but how much we can't quantify right now. But we are all very excited about the results that we are seeing on some of our engineering and process improvements.

items.statement: Non-domestic geographies have volatile profitability due to implementation vs AMC revenue mix; expect steady profitability going forward
items.quote: we've been having implementations in certain geographies and at the end of the time, the revenue may go up, profitability may come down. And then there's other geographies at some other point of time where AMC revenue will be there and that's where the profitability is higher.

items.statement: Marketing spend increasing to tell company story; believe investments will generate returns when customers start deciding
items.quote: We strongly believe that our story has not been told at all. To use a phrase, we have not gone to rooftop and shouted about our achievements. So, we will need to continue to talk about our achievements.

items.statement: Substantial AI investment planned; existing human capital to be deployed in AI in coming quarters
items.quote: However, areas like AI are something where substantial part of our existing human capital would start getting deployed in the months and quarters to come.

items.statement: Expect 25% revenue CAGR over next 2-3 years and 25% ROCE in 2 years
items.quote: we are confident of achieving 25% of ROCE in next 2 years as we increase our sales volume 25% CAGR with margin improvement

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA per ton to improve by INR 1,000-1,500 in FY26
items.quote: we are confident that improvement of INR1,000 per ton to INR1,500 per ton is definitely on the cards

items.statement: Kisan EBITDA per ton target INR 6,000-7,000 over next 2.5 years
items.quote: The business plan what we have made for Kisan is that we shall ramp this up to INR6,000 ton to INR7,000 a ton over the next 2.5 years

items.statement: Incurred INR 130 crore capex in 9M FY25; plan INR 350-400 crore over next 2-3 years including South India greenfield
items.quote: in 9 months, we have so far spent around INR130 crores which includes like addition in gross block plus capital advances what we have paid. And for next 2 years to 3 years including the Greenfield South India plant, we may be investing another INR350 crores to INR400 crores

items.statement: Target total capacity 360,000-370,000 tons in 2-3 years from current ~286,000 tons
items.quote: now from 2,86,000 tons we want capacity of 360,000, 370,000 tons in 2 years, 3 years

items.statement: OPVC: 2 lines operational, 3rd line commissioning in 1-2 months; currently 4-5% of revenue, targeting 7-9% in 1-2 years
items.quote: OPVC has already started contributing just about like 4%, 5% of our revenue at APL Apollo level and it shall increase to 7%, 8%, 9% over the next 1 year to 2 years

items.statement: Window profiles to start revenue contribution in 3-4 months; target top 3-4 position in 2-3 years
items.quote: window profile segment which we will start in next 3 months, 4 months that will start contributing to my revenue

items.statement: Q3 blended EBITDA ~INR 8,500/ton (8%); standalone ~INR 10,000/ton; Kisan ~INR 3,000-4,000/ton
items.quote: So that's why the margins I would say are more nominal now at around INR10,000 per ton at APL Apollo level. And Kisan anyways is ramping up. So Kisan is at INR4,000 per ton. So blended we are at INR8,500 per ton, which is like 8% at percentage level

items.statement: Expect margins to reach low teens as capacities ramp up with better mix and operating leverage
items.quote: we are of a very strong view that once we ramp up our capacities, the margin shall reach low teens on a back of better product mix and operating leverage gains

items.statement: Q4 seasonally strong; channel destocked due to falling PVC prices; green shoots visible in construction; expect govt water/housing push post state elections
items.quote: We expect good demand from Agri and housing segments for the last quarter. The entire channel has de-stocked seeing the continuous fall in PVC prices. As the prices have reached low level, we expect demand recovery in Q4

items.statement: OPVC order book building up; currently 4-5% of revenue, targeting 7-9% in 1-2 years
items.quote: OPVC has already started contributing just about like 4%, 5% of our revenue at APL Apollo level and it shall increase to 7%, 8%, 9% over the next 1 year to 2 years as the order book builds up

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on PVC resin may add INR 6-8/kg max; no steep resin price hikes expected; pass-through manageable
items.quote: Maximum to the tune of INR6 to INR8 per kg will be impacted as per the initial guidelines issued by the DGTR for anti-dumping. So we don't see very steep hikes. So because of that, we don't see any major margin effect because of the resin prices

items.statement: OPVC: only 4-5 serious players with European tech; Chinese machines not yet up to mark; 10-15 manufacturers may emerge but quality gap remains
items.quote: right now, if you compare Apple-to-Apple only four to five players are there who are working aggressively in this product. Apart from that, some more three to four more Chinese machinery manufacturers, they have entered the market, but they are still to establish their product

items.statement: Kitara Capital (Oman) investing INR 110 crore at ~30% premium via preferential issue; company to remain debt-free
items.quote: we got commitment from an Oman based fund Kitara Capital which is investing INR110 crores at almost 30% premium to today's market price

items.statement: Receivables cycle 30-35 days with dealers; 90% sales through dealers; channel financing 10-15% of dealers vs 5-10% prior year
items.quote: If you look at our receivable cycle, that's around 30 days 35 days which we have with our dealers. So ye s it doesn't matter to us whether my dealer is selling in agri or he's selling in housing. We don't offer more than 30 days, 40 days of credit period to our distributors

items.statement: OPVC and window profiles to drive mix improvement; OPVC payback 2-3 years; window profiles target INR 100-200 crore in 2-3 years
