items.statement: Lead demand strong domestically (auto, telecom, data centers, EV, railways) and internationally; both double-digit CAGR; expansion rationale based on order book and demand visibility
items.quote: both are in double -digit numbers. If you see the international market, that also shows a CAGR of -- a good amount of CAGRs. And likewise, in the domestic side also, we see a good amount of growth.

items.statement: Target to reduce lead revenue share from 95%+ to 90% by end FY25, 80% by FY26, 70% by FY27 (10% reduction per year) via plastics, copper, aluminium growth
items.quote: The target is to reduce from the 95% plus to 90% before the end of this financial year. Next year, probably, we bring down to 80%, '25/'26. Then thereafter brin g down to 70%, every year, 10% reduction

items.statement: Aluminium segment paused due to hedging challenges; evaluating alternative product portfolio; expect some aluminium revenue contribution in FY26
items.quote: Looking forward for this year, we're not kind of completely moving out from aluminium. We're looking at it from a very different approach where there is a very strong possibility of kind of hedging both the supply and demand side of it.

items.statement: EPR, BWMR, PWMR, RCM, GST seen as positive for organized recyclers; EPR to level domestic vs import pricing in 3-6 months; RCM notification expected shortly
items.quote: Everything kind of also positive for us. I mean, all the government initiatives that have been undertaken, be it the BWMR in terms of stringent guidelines. So better the compliances, the stringent the compliance, the better for us.

items.statement: Domestic procurement transition creates 3-6 month volatility in raw material pricing; managed via weighted average procurement and EPR credits
items.quote: There will be a transition of close to six months where you will see a volatility, but that this volatility is not kind of more concerning to us because they're looking at procuring larger number of batteries

items.statement: Harsha Exito acquired via NCLT last year; board to decide on merger at appropriate time; merger is on the cards
items.quote: The board will take it at the appropriate time. That we cannot give you anything on that now. Board has to take a call. And definitely, Board will take a call. Definitely, it is on the card.

items.statement: Revenue 9M FY25: INR1,533 cr (+30% YoY); EBITDA INR80 cr (+47%); PAT INR41 cr (+108%); Q3 FY25 revenue INR509 cr (+11%), EBITDA INR26 cr (+11%), PAT INR13 cr (+31%)
items.quote: Consolidated revenue increased by 30% to INR1,533 crores. That is we achieved in the 9 month's last year's full year's revenue in the current year. Consolidated EBITDA increased to INR80 crores, up by 47%. EBITDA margin increased to 5.2% compared to 4.6% in 9 months in FY '24. Pondy Oxides and Consolidated PAT more than doubled to INR41 crores, up 108

items.statement: Domestic procurement improves cash conversion cycle vs imports; logistics better for domestic sourcing
items.quote: the cash conversion cycle will improve given that the domestic procurement logistic is far more better than the inputs.

items.statement: R&D facilities being set up for value-added products; lithium-ion feasibility study ongoing; mechanical process ready, chemical leaching phase 2 targeted for FY27 procurement cycle
items.quote: we are in talks for implementing an R&D strategy, because if you look at the overall lithium -ion manufacturing structure, majority of it is leaching, which is part of the second phase, which is a bit of a questionable process, which has not been kind of implemented by anyone as such in India or if you see globally.

items.statement: Dahlias Q3 presales INR 11,800+ crore, 173 apartments sold at average INR 65,000/sq ft
items.quote: I mean, Dahlias obviously was the prime highlight of the last quarter and I think we did a sales of almost INR11,800-plus crores.

items.statement: Dahlias free margin INR 8,000+ crore booked; construction cost 25-30% of sale price vs Privana 40%
items.quote: I think the metric that should truly excite us is not the INR 11,800 crores of the presales, but the fact that INR 8,000-plus crores of free margin has been booked on account of the Dahlias sales

items.statement: Total construction underway approaching 40 msf; comfortable bandwidth 40-50 msf simultaneously
items.quote: I think including the 2 downtowns that Sriram spoke about, I think our total square footage under construction is now approaching 40 million square feet. We believe that with the current bandwidth that we have, I think a number of between 40 to 50 is what I think we should be efficient at.

items.statement: Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 (4.5-4.6 msf office, 2 msf retail) construction commenced; Downtown 4 Phase 1 OC expected this quarter
items.quote: We have commenced construction on downtown Gurgaon Phase 2, where we have 4.5 million - 4.6 million on offices and 2 million of retail. The construction has commenced there.

items.statement: Gurgaon demand maturing, global investor interest, end-user driven; Dahlias buyer mix: 50% Golf Links community, 12% NRI, rest NCR/other metros
items.quote: So it's the Golf Links community, first, in that order I'm going. Then NCR, then NRIs and then rest of the country. NRIs have contributed to about 12% of our sales in Dahlias. About 50% has been the community, friends and family and people who live there

items.statement: Dahlias pricing: first 173 units avg INR 65,000/sq ft, exited at mid-70s, remaining inventory priced at mid-80s; community offer to be withdrawn
items.quote: INR 65,000 is the average price that we have obtained in the first 173 apartments. We have exited more at a mid-70s price point right now. So really, the delta is from mid-70s to mid-80s

items.statement: DCCDL debt/EBITDA down to 3-3.5x; ICRA upgraded to AA positive; CRISIL review by Feb-end; Kolkata IT park sold for INR 675 crore (INR 637 crore net cash)
items.quote: ICRA has improved our rating from AA+ stable to AA positive a few weeks back. CRISIL is in the process of reassessing our rating, and their report should come out by probably February end.

items.statement: Mumbai launch (1,100-1,500 units, premium plus) approval expected in weeks; Goa super-luxury approval ongoing; Privana Phase 3 under approval
items.quote: Our current reading of it is that it looks that the Mumbai approval should come hopefully in the next few weeks, and we should be able to launch it. And the other 2 could overflow into the next quarter.

items.statement: Dahlias 41% inventory sold vs planned 10%; taking short breather for recalibration before next phase; experience center launch mid-year
items.quote: initially we thought there will be -- we plan to bring only a 10% stock in. But as you see, it's about 41% So right now, without compromising on the valuation and the price points, I think the focus will be that.

items.statement: Gurgaon price points compared to Dubai/London by CRE; DLF product preferred for liquidity and appreciation
items.quote: In fact, today, price points, the CRE, which is a data analysis company, has started to compare price points of Gurgaon to Dubai and London and all.

items.statement: Office vacancy down to 7.2% (non-SEZ 2%, SEZ 12-12.5%); target 6-6.2% by Q4; retail vacancy ~2%
items.quote: Our vacancies now have come down to 7.2%, which in offices, which at the beginning of the year were at 9% and the 7.2%, the vacancies in our non-SEZ portfolio are down to about 2% now whereas the vacancy in the SEZ portfolio hovers around 12% - 12.5%.

items.statement: No immediate monetization plans for DCCDL or Cyber City; committed to 4-5 year capex build-out cycle; GIC not in hurry
items.quote: No. So , we remain, frankly, equally committed to both the businesses, the DevCo and the RentCo. And frankly, neither us nor our partners, GIC, are in any hurry of any form, frankly, for the monetization exercise.

items.statement: New CFO Badal Bagri joined December from GE, GE Capital, Airtel, Reliance
items.quote: I'd also take this opportunity to introduce our new CFO, Badal Bagri, who has joined us in December. Badal comes from an extremely checkered career with GE, GE Capital, Airtel, Reliance

items.statement: Construction contracting ecosystem key constraint beyond 50 msf; approval cycles for Mumbai/Goa/Privana Phase 3 may cause delays
items.quote: But I think, really, if you were to ask us, they won serious constraint to growth beyond this number would be the contracting ecosystem.

items.statement: SEZ de-notification: 2.2 msf applied, 1.9 msf approved, 1 msf already leased
items.quote: Our SEZ, the total stock that we had, which was vacant was 2.3 million square feet, out of which we have applied for 2.2 million square feet for de -notification. 1.9 million of that has been approved by the Board of Approvals and out of this 1.9 million, 1 million has already been leased.

items.statement: No fund raise discussed; strong cash balance INR 4,500 crore; Q3 operating cash flow INR 1,800 crore
items.quote: You must have seen the cash flows for the quarter are also extremely healthy at INR 1,800 crores. In fact, we are now sitting on a total cash balance of almost INR 4,500 crores.

items.statement: No dividend/buyback discussed; focus on debt reduction and growth capex
items.quote: We realized that just reducing debt for the sake of reducing debt is not a good idea, especially for an annuity company, and we are sort of focusing on it.

items.statement: Construction cost: Privana ~INR 8,000-8,500/sq ft (40% of sale price); Dahlias 25-30% of sale price including infrastructure; Downtown Gurgaon office INR 6,200-6,300/sq ft GLA, next phases INR 8,000-8,200; retail INR 10,000-10,200/sq ft
items.quote: if you check out our filings on the Privana piece, I think our construction cost is ballpark in the range of INR 8,000-odd a square foot, INR 8,500 on a sale price of about INR 20,000, which broadly is a 40% ratio. In Dahlias, frankly, we are expecting a construction cost to be in the range of ballpark 25% to 28% to 30% of our total sale price

items.statement: Sustainability: LEED Platinum for all operating buildings; LEED Zero water discharge achieved; 60% portfolio LEED Zero waste, target 100% by June 30; carbon neutrality announcement coming quarters
items.quote: We, as you know, have achieved LEED Platinum for all our operating buildings. We have got LEED Platinum Zero for water discharge for all our buildings, both are sort of leaders globally. And now we are working on LEED Zero for waste, where about 60% of the portfolio has got LEED Zero waste. And by 30th June, we plan to convert the entire portfolio to LEED Zero waste.

items.statement: Order book remains strong on towers and co-locations from all customers; growth expected to remain robust in foreseeable future
items.quote: I think our order book remains quite strong both on towers and co-locations from all the customers. So we expect the growth to remain robu st in the foreseeable

items.statement: Visibility of pipeline for next three to four quarters
items.quote: If you are looking at a timeframe, I think we are looking at a timeframe of visibility of the next three to f our quarters, that is what we have

items.statement: Capex muted due to earlier procurement timing and Rs 6.6 billion capitalization reversal from Supreme Court CENVAT credit ruling
items.quote: Obviously the procurement for th e rollouts that we have done were much earlier and then there is also the adjustment on account of the Supreme Court ruling wherein we are now able to avail the CENVAT credit on towers and to that extent we have also reversed some capitalization to the extent of 6.6 billion that we have explained in the notes

items.statement: No technical limit on co-location deployment; field force can meet all customer co-location orders
items.quote: from a technical limit point of view I think there will be no limit from our side in terms of co-location deployment. Our turnaround time and our spread of the field force is enough that we can meet all the requirement s of co-location orders that come from the customer

items.statement: Debt reduced to Rs 1,000 Crores excluding lease liabilities; balance sheet optimization expected over next couple of months and quarters as uncertainty reduces
items.period: next couple of months and quarters
items.quote: I do not see this first of all as a very long-term situation this is basically just part of our normal cash management. Coming to the long-term view on how the balance sheet can be optimized, clearly we know that there is a lot of headroom.

items.statement: Board to evaluate dividend at year end given strong cash flow; buyback done in Q2
items.quote: We are fully aware that no dividend has been paid in the last two years although we did a buyback in Q2 and distributed some cash, but clearly by year end if we are still in a very strong cash flow situation, I am sure the Board will evaluate all this.

items.statement: Energy margins improved to -3.4% in Q3 from -4.8% in Q2; initiatives include diesel reduction and renewable energy
items.quote: Our energy margins were at -3.4% in Q3 compared to -4.8% in Q2. We are taking many initiatives to improve our energy margins, which includes reducing our diesel consumption and increasing the share of renewable energy to benefit from the lower cost.

items.statement: Diesel consumption reduced 8% year-on-year; solar sites grew to over 28,000; signed PPA for 130 MW solar plant under captive mode with 26% equity for Rs 38 Crores
items.quote: Our ongoing initiatives including electrification of non-electrified sites and deployment of energy storage solutions have yielded an 8% year-on-year reduction in diesel consumption in Q3. We also continue to focus on increasing the share of renewable sources of energy with our solar sites growing to over 28,000.

items.statement: Right of Way Rules 2024 implemented from Jan 1, 2025; Green Energy Open Access policy notified in 24 states; composite billing in 11 states; Supreme Court allowed CENVAT credits on towers reducing contingent liability by Rs 37 billion; Delh
items.quote: During the quarter, the honourable Supreme Court in a landmark ruling allowed CENVAT credits on towers and shelters resulting in a reduction of Rs.37 billion in our contingent liability. Following the Honourable Supreme Court ruling, the Delhi High Court quashed the show cause notice issued by the DGGI on the issue of disallowance of input tax credit availed by the Company on passive infrastructur

items.statement: 5G BTS deployed industry-wide at 465,000; 5G loading contributes meaningfully to revenue; expect new site demand after penetration for network decongestion
items.quote: The industry-wide total number of 5G BTS deployed stands at almost 465,000 with over 50,000 BTS being deployed in the last calendar year. Though the pace of deployment has slowed down, 5G loading contributes meaningfully to the overall loading revenue.

items.statement: Highest quarterly IBS deployment in history; lean tower co-locations at 132 in Q3, total base 11,492; micro cell solutions customized per customer needs
items.quote: Our In-Building Solutions (IBS) portfolio continued to witness good traction, and we are pleased to have recorded the highest quarterly IBS deployment in our history.

items.statement: Dominant market share maintained in major customers' rollouts; incremental market share also dominant; BSNL existing customer with MSA, actively upgrading to 4G
items.quote: I think we are currently the dominant market share for all our customers that are rolling out and I think we will continue to do so.

items.statement: Trade receivables increased Rs 16.9 billion QoQ to Rs 73 billion due to provision write-back timing; collections received subsequently in January
items.quote: Trade receivables increased by Rs.16.9 billion primarily due to the significant provision reversal against which the amount was collected subsequently in this month.

items.statement: Provision for doubtful debt reduced to Rs 5 billion after Rs 30.2 billion write-back; collected Rs 19.1 billion from Vodafone Plc share pledge monetization and additional overdue recovery
items.quote: Please note that during the quarter , we collected Rs.19.1 billion for monetization of the secondary pledge on the shares held by Vodafone Plc in Indus Towers. We also recovered an add itional amount against the overdues from a major customer. This resulted in an overall write-back of provisions for doubtful debt of Rs.30.2 billion reducing our provision for doubtful debt to about Rs.5 billion

items.statement: Gender diversity improved to 14.2% in Q3 FY25 from 11.3% year ago; launched 'Her Success' programme
items.quote: In our workfor ce our gender diversity stood at 14.2% in Q3 FY25 compared to 11.3% in the corresponding period last year. We continue to make efforts towards improving gender diversity across the value chain and to this end we launched “Her Success” programme during the quarter

items.statement: EV charging business at very early stage; separate business unit and team; hurdle rates aspirational mid to high double digits; no timeline for scale
items.quote: From an EV business point of view , it is too early to say on the investment. It is a very early-stage discussion tha t we are currently looking at. We are planning to look at or capitalize on our core strengths of managing space , power, and as we expand our discussions with th e potential customers on a case-to-case basis, we will make the decisions accordingly

items.statement: Tenancy ratio stable at 1.65x; macro towers up 10.8% YoY to 234,643; co-locations up 7.2% YoY to 386,819; net co-location additions 7,715 in Q3 vs 4,490 in Q2
items.quote: A significant number of tenancy additions during the quarter helped our industry-leading tenancy ratio remain stable at 1.65x, which has been declining for many years.

items.statement: Rental revenue grew 7.5% YoY to Rs 48.2 billion; ARPT up 0.7% QoQ due to seasonality benefits (better uptime, lower diesel cost)
items.quote: core revenues from rental grew by 7.5% year-on-year to Rs.48.2 billion driven by strong tower and co-location additions

items.statement: Acquired 26% equity in strategic partner for 130 MW solar plant under captive mode for Rs 38 Crores
items.quote: In order to expand our renewable energy portfolio, we have entered into a power purchase agreement with a strategic partner for procurement of renewable energy of 130 MW solar plant under captive mode. As part of the agreement, we would acquire 26% of the equity shares of the said entity for a consideration of around 38 Crores.

items.statement: Network uptime 99.98% in Q3 FY25 vs 99.96% in Q2 despite severe natural calamities (Dana cyclone, heavy rains)
items.quote: we continue to maintain a very high uptime and delivere d an uptime of 99.98% in Q3 FY25, compared to 99.96% in Q2. Please note that the quarter was marked by severe natural calamities such as Dana cyclone in Odisha and heavy rains and thunderstorms in areas of Rajasthan and Punjab amongst others

items.statement: MFI credit cost expected to peak in Q4 and decline each quarter next year; ex-MFI credit cost seen range-bound at 1.8-1.9%
items.quote: And just to add, even into the next year, so as Vaidya said, that on MFI, we expect the peak to sort of come in, in Q4, and the credit cost should keep coming down into the next year, every quarter. And for the rest of the book, we feel the provisions could be very range bound or more or less around the current levels, right.

items.statement: Targeting 2%+ ROA over the long term driven by operating leverage and liability business breakeven
items.quote: So we feel that any which way we look at it, this bank is feeling the heading there, whether you can reach there in 2030, or FY31 or FY32, I mean, it would be very hard to really pick a number. But this bank will have zero doubt in my mind that this 1.7%, 1.8% kind of ROA.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target of 65% by FY27 reaffirmed
items.quote: Sir, I was talking about cost-to-income trajectory that you have given that by FY 27, we should be hitting 65% mark.

items.statement: Credit card business expected to break even next year and generate INR500-600 crore PAT by FY29-FY30
items.quote: And by that time, like I said FY24, FY29, FY30, it should be making like INR500 crores, INR600 crores of PAT. So therefore, if you take this 4.3%, which is today and get some operating leverage on it take it to maybe 4.7%, 4.8% by that time, probably more.

items.statement: Liability business cost-to-income expected to reach 100% (breakeven) over time
items.quote: the liability business has said that you must expect us to take it to 0%, which is cost income to come down to 100%, which means that the loss will come to 0.

items.statement: MFI collection efficiency at 98.6%; cumulative provision coverage on MFI NPA + SMA-1/2 at ~70%
items.quote: In fact, if you sum up the NPA book on MFI and the SMA-1 and SMA-2 book, the cumulative provision which is in hand is about 70%.

items.statement: Credit card SMA-1/2 improved to 1.32% from 1.69% QoQ; GNPA improved to 1.91% from 1.95%
items.quote: Our SMA 1 and 2 credit cards has come down last quarter. It come down from 1.69% to 1.32%, in fact, last 3 quarters come down to 1.88%, 1.69%, 1.32%. So even on the NPA number... Sudhanshu Jain: Yes. The GNPA has come off to 1.91% vis-a-vis 1.95% in the previous

items.statement: Ex-MFI credit cost stable at 1.8% for Q2 and Q3; expected to remain in 1.8-1.9% range
items.quote: In Q2, it was 1.8% and Q3 has also come in at 1.8%. We feel that this could broadly remain in this range, maybe it could be or maybe 180 to 190 that kind of range.

items.statement: 2-wheeler portfolio (70% of vehicle book) holding up well; SMA and NPA numbers disclosed and stable
items.quote: 2-wheeler is the bulk of the book in the vehicle segment. That's roughly at about 70% of the vehicles book. If you see the presentation, we have also given SMA 1, SMA 2 numbers and NP A, right, at the vehicle level. So it has been holding up quite well, 2-wheeler has been growing quite nicely for us

items.statement: CGFMU insurance covers up to 70% of losses on insured MFI book; claims expected from FY27
items.quote: particularly on the CGFMU insured book, right, we would start getting claims starting from FY 27, right? And the recoup of credit losses could be as high as about 70%, right, of the losses, which we incur on the CGFMU linked NPA.

items.statement: Plan to add 75-100 branches next year (~10% increase on base of ~1,000) while growing loan book 20%+
items.quote: We may add about 75 to 100 branches into next year, which is 10% over the current stock. So clearly, some leverage sort of comes in there, right. Then our tech costs and so on, we have already done a lot of front loading in last few years, right.

items.statement: Lending business operating profit at 4.3% of loan book (down from 4.7% pre-MFI crisis); expected to rise to 4.7-4.9% with operating leverage
items.quote: Now on that front, we are having 4.3% of the loan book as an operating profit. This includes MFI, by the way. So before the MFI crisis stuck, it was 4.7%. We actually expect it to go to 4.8% or 4.9% because of operating leverage.

items.statement: Credit cost ex-MFI assumed at 1.7% of loans (1.2% of assets) for long-term ROA math
items.quote: So let me say this 4.6% or 4.7%, you subtract from that about 1.7% as the credit cost by that time. So you'll be looking like about 3% or so.

items.statement: Consumer loan growth at 10% YoY; management not concerned about market share given low base vs industry leaders
items.quote: See, frankly, for us to grow any of these businesses is not difficult at all because like we always say, they are coming on a low base as compared to, let me say, industry leaders who have a very large share of the market. We are like nothing or nobody.

items.statement: Deposit franchise still heavily new-to-bank (NTB) given young bank status; asset-to-liability cross-sell works best with affluent customers (home loan, LAP, credit card)
items.quote: A bank like us, which is starting up right now since you start with zero base, today, we're no longer zero base, we're still two lakhs but in the context in what we want to build in life, maybe INR10 lakh crores, INR15 lakh crores, INR20 lakh crores over the next many years, we're still zero based. So a large part of our business is still very heavily NTB.

items.statement: Will follow all industry norms on MFI (lender limits, exposure caps); have added extra internal controls and scorecard-based underwriting beyond regulatory requirements
items.quote: We are going to follow all the norms of the industry. And we have a little more controls over and above that at our own end. So basically, once you follow all the norms of industry, number of lenders, amount of exposure, etc, we'll broadly be in line with the industry to say.

items.statement: Karnataka MFI situation (9% of portfolio) is a very recent development (last 3 days); impact uncertain but being closely monitored
items.quote: Yes. And with respect to Karnataka, again, this is a very latest development. This has come in the last 3 days. So we will closely watch the situation. It's difficult to sort of give out what could be the impact on that front, but we are quite watchful any way on the overall MFI portfolio.

items.statement: Opex growth to moderate from 18-19% to ~13% driven by employee cost taper, branch leverage (10% branch growth vs 20% loan growth), and tech front-loading benefits
items.quote: So we feel that because a lot of expenses have sort of already come in, there is clearly an operating leverage or the proportion increase could definitely come down from the current levels.

items.statement: Lending business pre-provision operating profit (PPOP) at 4.3% of loan book; liability business loss at 1.7% of deposits; credit card loss narrowing
items.quote: if you take the P&L of the asset book, which includes retail as well as wholesale. So these numbers capture both the businesses. Then we have a liability business, then we have put out a credit card business separately, right?

items.statement: Bank PPOP to total assets at ~2.29% for 9 months; reconciles with segmental PPOP of 4.4% on assets (70% of balance sheet) and -1.7% on liabilities (70% of balance sheet)
items.quote: If you apply these proportions, you will get a number of about 2.3% on PPOP, which is the disclosed number for us for the 9 months, right? PPOP to total assets is about 2.29%, and this is the broad reconciliation.

items.statement: MFI is unique risk due to group repayment model (no auto-debit); no spillover seen to urban consumer, credit card, MSME, corporate or other rural books
items.quote: Microfinance is when the group of borrowers are coming together and repaying when our people have to go to the customers to a common venue and customers to come and pay, meaning we have no right to debit the customer's bank accounts for an EMI. Every other product we sell, we have a right to debit the customer's bank account.

items.statement: Long-term ROA trajectory dependent on credit cost staying at assumed levels; MFI crisis is only near-term headwind
items.quote: the only catch here can be credit cost. There's no other catch here. Now in the credit cost front, well, like this long period of 14, 15 years running a good credit cost company, except the MFI mishap that has happened now, you should believe th at we should be able to run the credit cost on the lines we're talking about

items.statement: Employee cost growth pace has considerably come off; headcount additions to slow relative to business expansion
items.quote: If you see, we have given some level of details, like if you see employee cost, right, that was growing at a much higher pace and the pace has considerably come off. So even into the next year, we expect that employee cost percentage increase could come down, right.

items.statement: No fund raise discussed; focus on internal capital generation via ROA improvement
items.quote: We are not planning to slow down the growth. I mean like 20% of the loan and about 22%, 23%, 24% of the deposits because, frankly, as you have seen for the last many years, we are good at deposits.

items.statement: MFI product is standalone; no significant cross-sell of 2-wheeler, auto or personal loans to MFI customers
items.quote: No, we don't sell many other products along with it. It's a regular MFI, the short answer.

items.statement: FY25 capacity growth guidance confirmed at early double digits
items.quote: we confirm basically our guidance for FY25. For FY26, that is part of the discussion we have actually right now.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 capacity growth expected around 20% YoY
items.quote: for the fourth quarter of this financial year we are expecting to add capacity of around 20 percent as compared to the same period last year

items.statement: Q4 FY25 unit passenger revenue expected to moderate early single digit YoY
items.quote: we are estimating an early single digit moderation in unit passenger revenue as compared to the h igher base of last year

items.statement: Q3 FY25 passengers grew 13% YoY to 31 million, highest quarterly ever
items.quote: We welcomed around 31 million passengers in the December quarter, achieving the highest IndiGo January 24, 2025 number of passengers served during any quarter in the history of IndiGo. This reflects a growth of around 13 percent on a year over year

items.statement: Industry domestic load factors above 90% in Nov-Dec 2024
items.quote: industry load factors in domestic markets to remain above 90 percent for the most parts of November and December

items.statement: Q3 FY25 reported PAT Rs 24.5bn after Rs 14bn forex loss; margin 11%
items.quote: Including the impact of currency movement, we reported a profit after tax of 24.5 billion rupees or 2,450 crore rupees.

items.statement: Inducted 33 aircraft in Q3 FY25 (23 from order book, 8 damp leases, 2 secondary leases); redelivered 6; fleet 437
items.quote: during the quarter, we inducted 33 aircraft of which 23 are from original order book. This includes 15 aircraft which have been inducted through our entity in GIFT city. We also inducted 8 aircraft in the form of damp leases and 2 aircra ft in the form of secondary leases, to cater to the robust demand in the market. We also redelivered 6 aircraft during the quarter resulting in a total fleet of 4

items.statement: AOG count in 60s at Q3 end; expected in 40s at start of FY26 and declining further
items.quote: Based IndiGo January 24, 2025 on the latest guidance from OEMs, we will begin the next financial year with the groundings in the range of 40s and expect the number to further go down as the year progresses

items.statement: Q3 FY25 fuel CASK down 16% YoY; global fuel prices down >20%
items.quote: On the cost side, as the global fuel prices went down by more than 20 percent on a year over year basis, our fuel CASK has also reduced by 16 percent.

items.statement: CASK ex-fuel ex-forex stable QoQ at INR 2.90; up 10% YoY due to grounding costs and contractual escalations
items.quote: sequentially, the CASK ex fuel ex forex remained stable at INR 2.90. On a year over year basis it has increased by around 10 percent, compared to the same period last year primarily driven by: Grounding related costs And contractual escalations across expense line items and annual increments

items.statement: Q3 FY25 rupee depreciated ~2% QoQ causing Rs 14bn mark-to-market forex loss; net USD exposure ~$8bn
items.quote: Third quarter saw continued weakness in rupee primarily due to strengthening of the US economy and at the end of the quarter it depreciated around 2 percent as compared to the September quarter end resulting in mark -to-market foreign exchanges losses of ar ound 14 billion rupees

items.statement: Hedging policy: cover next 12 months cash outflows; currently hedging 60-70% of positions including natural hedge
items.quote: we are hedging for the next 12 months up to 60%-70% of our positions. Going forward, we will also keep testing whether we want to extend this out from a 12-month window

items.statement: International point-of-sale revenue 10% of total; provides natural hedge
items.quote: 10% of our revenue comes from international (point of sales). items.statement: Order book >900 aircraft to be delivered over next decade
items.quote: the fact that IndiGo has the largest order book in the world and we still have a little over 900 planes to be delivered in the decade to come is providing IndiGo a very solid strategic position

items.statement: Launched IndiGo Stretch business class on Delhi-Mumbai (mid-Nov), Delhi-Bengaluru (Jan 10); 10 more metro routes in 2025 with 45 aircraft
items.quote: In the year 2025, we will launch Stretch on 10 more metro-to-metro routes across the country with a total of 45 aircraft.

items.statement: Loyalty program launched Oct 2024; hotel platform at startup phase
items.quote: the introduction of our loyalty program. Basically, which started also to run in this quarter, it was announced in August, it, started to register in October. We actually see a very positive response. So, these are all parts of, I would, say the pieces of the very same puzzle and so we have the infrastructure for the hotels in place, yet numbers today are still at the startup phase.

items.statement: New aviation bill approved by cabinet; awaits Parliament ratification; positive for lessor confidence
items.quote: it is a positive thing like that has been at least approved by the cabinet. Let us wait for it to get ratified in Parliament. It is long overdue. Given the growth that we are seeing in aviation, obviously all airlines need a lot of capital and such kind of an acknowledgement that will come from the government, related to a convention which is a global convention will obviously boost a lot of confi

items.statement: Dec 2024 capitalized operating lease liability Rs 496bn; total debt including lease liability Rs 651bn; right-of-use assets Rs 468bn
items.quote: we ended the December quarter with a capitalized operating lease liability of 496 billion rupees and a total debt, including the capitalized operating lease liability of around 651 billion rupees. Our right to use assets at quart er end were around 468 billion rupees

items.statement: Dec 2024 free cash Rs 289bn; restricted cash Rs 149bn; purchased 3 ATR and 10 finance lease aircraft
items.quote: we ended the December quarter with a free cash of 289 billion rupees and a restricted cash of 149 billion rupees. We have also purchased 3 ATR aircraft and acquired 10 aircraft on finance leases, as part of cash utilization initiatives.

items.statement: Forex volatility remains; rupee further depreciated in January; hedging covers only 12-month window
items.quote: While the currency remains volatile and has further depreciated in January, we have been actively taking steps to reduce this volatility in the financial statements by hedging part of our foreign currency outflows.

items.statement: International yield moderation higher due to capacity additions and foreign carrier competition
items.quote: on the international side, the intensity of competition went a little higher. So, there was a higher degree of moderation that happened on that front, but nonetheless the demand is very strong.

items.statement: Targets 15-20% volume growth for IEX; expects gas exchange volumes to jump if gas prices fall to $8-9 by 2026-27
items.quote: I think a number of 15%, 20% growth is definitely achievable.

items.statement: Targets 20% growth for IEX over next 4-5 years
items.quote: Vision I told. I mean, a growth of 20% is something which we are targeting.

items.statement: Electricity demand grew 3% YoY in Q3 FY25 to 393 BUs; 5% growth in first 9 months FY25
items.quote: Electricity demand at 393 BUs during the third quarter was higher by 3% Y-o-Y, better than the previous quarter's muted 0.5% growth.

items.statement: Power demand growth of 6-7% expected if Indian economy grows at 7-8%
items.quote: If the Indian economy has to grow at a rate of 7%, 8%, then power demand in the country has to definitely grow at a rate of 6%, 7%.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue grew 13.7% YoY to INR160.5 crore; PAT grew 16.9% to INR107.3 crore in Q3 FY25
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, revenue for the company grew 13.7% on a year-on-year basis in Q3 FY '25, increasing to INR160.5 crores from INR141.2 crores in Q3 FY '24.

items.statement: Electricity volumes up 16% YoY to 30.5 BUs in Q3 FY25; 19% YoY to 89 BUs in 9M FY25
items.quote: At 30.5 billion units, electricity volumes for the quarter were 16% higher on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: REC trading volumes up 31% YoY to 26.5 lakh in Q3 FY25; 158% YoY to 110.6 lakh in 9M FY25
items.quote: In Q3, a total of 26.5 lakh renewable energy certificates were traded, a jump of 31% over the same quarter last fiscal.

items.statement: RTM volumes up 30% YoY to 9.3 BUs in Q3 FY25; 29% YoY to 29.3 BUs in 9M FY25
items.quote: For Q3 FY '25, RTM volumes were higher by 30% Y-o-Y at nearly 9.3 billion units.

items.statement: Green Market volumes rose over 300% YoY to nearly 2.5 BUs in Q3 FY25
items.quote: With regards the Green Market, in Q3 FY '25, volume rose over 300% to nearly 2.5 billion units, compared with Q3 FY '24.

items.statement: IGX traded volumes up 93% YoY to 162 lakh MMBtu in Q3 FY25; 24% YoY to 398 lakh MMBtu in 9M FY25
items.quote: IGX traded volume of 162 lakh MMBtu for Q3 FY '25 compared with 84 lakh MMBtu traded in Q3 last fiscal.

items.statement: LDC volumes (TAM+GTAM) at 18 BUs for market; IEX share 38% (7.1 BUs) in 9M FY25
items.quote: For IEX alone, this number is 7.1 billion.

items.statement: DAM clearing prices averaged INR3.71/unit in Q3 FY25, down 26% YoY due to 62% YoY increase in sell quantum
items.quote: For Q3 FY '25, prices in the Day Ahead market averaged at INR3.71 per unit, a decline of nearly 26% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Coal available at 10-20% premium under Shakti B8 auction; imported coal at $50/ton; gas at $14/MMBtu
items.quote: Imported coal prices in Q3 have also been competitive at $50 per ton.

items.statement: LPSC amendments now mandate state-owned generators to offer un-requisitioned power on exchanges
items.quote: Recent amendments in the LPSC procedures has now also brought the State government-owned generating stations under its ambit, mandating them to offer URS power on the exchange platform.

items.statement: CERC issued draft procedure for trading Carbon Credit Certificates on power exchanges
items.quote: CERC issued draft procedure for trading of Carbon Credit Certificates for both obligated as well as non-obligated entities through power exchanges.

items.statement: 11-month contract hearings complete, order reserved; Green RTM petition admitted, public comments sought, decision in 3-4 months
items.quote: 11-month contract hearings were complete, order is reserved. So it depends on CERC, but then the hearings were complete a couple of months back.

items.statement: Market coupling simulation report awaited from Grid India; was due July 2024, now January 2025
items.quote: This was to be submitted in the month of July, and we are now in the month of January of next year. So already 6 months are over.

items.statement: Open access consumers 13% of volumes, DISCOMs 87% in 9M FY25; open access share increased due to lower prices
items.quote: Open access percentage was about 13%. And distribution company purchase was about 87%.

items.statement: VPPA capacity ~300-400 MW on platform; expect up to 2 GW renewable sell potential by FY25 end including merchant and disputed PPA plants
items.quote: By end of this fiscal, we are expecting up to 2 gigawatts of total renewable sell potential, which will be there and which has potential to participate in our spot markets.

items.statement: Electricity market share maintained at ~84.5%; REC market share ~60-65%; RTM/DAM share ~100%; other products ~35%
items.quote: In the electricity segment, we are maintaining a market share of around 84%.

items.statement: Incentives offered in TAM and REC segments to match competition and retain market share
items.quote: In the Term-Ahead-Market and REC market segments because of the competition between the exchanges, if they are giving incentives, we have to also match that.

items.statement: Government plans to set up coal exchange in CY2025; draft cabinet note circulated for inter-ministerial consultations
items.quote: The government recently reiterated its plan for setting up India's first coal exchange in the calendar year 2025.

items.statement: CEA forecasts peak power demand of 458 GW by 2032, driving exchange volume growth
items.quote: With the CEA forecast of peak power demand of 458 gigawatt by 2032, power consumption growth will continue to drive exchange volume growth.

items.statement: Board announced interim dividend of INR1.50 per share (150% of face value) for FY25
items.quote: For fiscal year 2025, the Board of Directors of the company announced an interim dividend of INR1.50, equivalent to 150% of the face value of equity shares.

items.statement: Market coupling implementation would require market-grade software, physical/financial settlement processes; could take 2-3 years for RTM-SCED coupling
items.quote: It could be even 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Revised Electronics division revenue growth guidance to 55%+ for FY25 from earlier 45%
items.quote: Looking into current order book, we are pleased to revise our revenue growth guidance for Electronics division from 45% earlier to 55% for FY' 25, propelled by both PCBA and bare board verticals.

items.statement: Expect Railway Sub-system & Defense division to return to normalized EBITDA margin range of 18-22% by H2 FY26
items.quote: We expect to get back to normalized range of 18% to 22% by H2 of FY '26, to emphasize delays in offtake are momentary with no cancellations of orders.

items.statement: Maintain guidance of doubling Railway Sub-system & Defense revenue in next three years backed by Rs 2,000+ crore order book visibility
items.quote: We continue to remain confident on the long-term potential of division and maintain our guidance of doubling the revenue in the next three years, backed by a strong order book visibility of Rs. 2,000 crores plus and increase in wallet share.

items.statement: Expect consolidated ROCE to cross 15% by end of FY25
items.quote: On the return on capital employed, with a strong underlying business performance, we expect improvement in ROCE and expect to cross the 15% mark by the year end.

items.statement: Expect Electronics division EBITDA margins to reach 8% in FY25 and potentially double digits in FY26
items.quote: And we expect our margins to be in the range of 8% EBITDA. And I think there's a possibility of increasing it to double digit number in the next financial year itself.

items.quote: On the Electronics side, we think that we have already announced Rs. 650 crores Capex in Hosur, out of which land parcel has come this year, then major portion will come next year, close to about Rs. 400 crores to Rs. 450 crores will be next year for the Ascent Circuits and the PCBs. And then our Railways division has already been announced, last year we announced Rs. 350 crores Capex for the two

items.statement: Korea Circuit JV investment likely Rs 1,000+ crore pending government incentive scheme finalization
items.quote: So, I think it should be in the range of Rs. 1,000 crores plus.

items.statement: Room AC facilities currently at 65% capacity utilization
items.quote: But as Amber is concerned, we are at a capacity utilization of 65% at the moment in our room air conditioner facilities.

items.statement: New Hosur facility for Electronics division expected to start commercial production by Q4 FY26
items.quote: the construction is progressing well for the new facility at Hosur and we expect to start commercial production by Q4 of FY '26.

items.statement: Sidwal greenfield facility for HVAC, Pantry, Doors and Gangways expected to commence operations by Q2 FY26
items.quote: the construction is progressing well for Sidwal's greenfield facility for HVAC, Pantry, Doors and Gangways and is expected to commence operations by Quarter 2 of FY '26.

items.quote: And we expect to commence the mass production from the new plant by H1 of the next financial year.

items.quote: backed by a strong order book visibility of Rs. 2,000 crores plus and increase in wallet share.

items.quote: This year industry ends up at about 25% growth, next year industry is expecting good summers, and in that anticipation they are ramping up the inventory right now.

items.quote: But now we are giving solutions in the space of telecom, in smart meter space , we are giving solutions in auto space, both four-wheeler and two wheeler. In fact, recently we have just started the commercial vehicles business also. And we have onboarded defense.

items.quote: The strong performance is driven by the underlying growth in the RAC industry, coupled with conversion of new customers from gas charging to ODM, and deepening of customer relationships.

items.statement: Electronics division EBITDA grew 193% YoY to Rs 34 cr in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for the quarter increased by 193% year-on-year and stood at Rs. 34 crores compared to Rs. 12 crores in Quarter 3 Financial Year '24.

items.statement: Pass on commodity/currency changes to customers at quarterly lag via price variation clauses; refrigerant gas impact Rs 100-120 per AC

items.quote: Well, there's a little uptake on the gas refrigerant prices which has impacted in the range of Rs. 100 to Rs. 120 per air conditioner. Other than that, it's a pass -on strategy from our side. So, whenever any kind of currency or commodity is hit, we have demonstrated in past that we pass on to our customers at a quarterly lag basis.

items.statement: Converted large multinational customers from gas charging to ODM; two customers grew >45% vs expected 25-30%
items.quote: We thought that they will grow in range of 25%, 30% but two of our customers, they have grown by more than 45%. So, we got benefited be cause of that.

items.statement: Added one new commercial AC customer and strengthened commercial AC order book
items.quote: I am pleased to report addition of one new customer and strengthening of the commercial AC order book.

items.quote: And we have onboarded five new customers recently.

items.quote: On the way forward, we are waiting for the finalization of the electronic component scheme by the Ministry of Electronics & IT. Which, as per the recent media articles, has got the nod from the Finance Ministry.

items.quote: So, on the first question, the asset turns normally in the PCBs are similar to OSAT businesses. It is in the range of 1x to 1.25x. items.statement: Compressor supply may face delays in April due to shipment issues from China, but alternative geographies being explored
items.quote: But yes, April sounds a little tricky because the shipments, there is a delay in shipments. And the companies who large order book was given to them but they are supplying in a little miser way, I would say. So, April may get infected in case compressor issue does not get resolved.

items.statement: Railway division margins to remain impacted for next two quarters before recovery from H2 FY26
items.quote: We feel that the margins will come back again. We will continue to get hit for the next quarter and next to next quarter. After that we will see this margins coming up because the Railways have already given us indication of resuming the supplies from H2 onwards.

items.statement: Targets ~5 GW new capacity in FY25, with ~4.3 GW incremental in Q4 FY25 and remaining ~1 GW in early Q1 FY26
items.quote: we feel very strongly that we should be able to deliver approximately 5 gigawatt of new capacity this year. So this will mean that we will have an incremental capacity of 4.3 gigawatt, which should come out this quarter, by end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Maintains 6-8 GW commissioning guidance range for FY26
items.quote: No, we'll keep it the same. I think the range is still the same and we are looking to ramp up our existing run rate and not reduce it here.

items.statement: Added 3.1 GW greenfield capacity YoY, total operational portfolio now 11.6 GW
items.quote: On a year-on-year basis, we've added 3.1 gigawatt of greenfield capacity, marking a massive 37% growth and bringing our total operational portfolio to 11.6 gigawatt, the largest footprint in the country.

items.statement: Solar capex ~INR4.5 cr/MW (bifacial with trackers); Wind capex ~INR6.5 cr/MW (5.2 MW turbine)
items.quote: Solar with a bifacial modules and trackers, it is around INR4.5 crores per megawatt. Wind is around INR6.5 crores per megawatt for a 5.2 megawatt wind turbine.

items.statement: BESS capex expected at INR1.3-1.4 cr/MWh with 8,000-10,000 cycles, 16+ year life, 1.5-3% annual degradation
items.quote: we should look at capex of INR1.3 to INR1.4 crores per megawatt hour and cycles remain between 8,000 to 10,000 cycles, which means that you can expect the battery to last for 16 plus years and degradation can be factored between 1.5% to 3%.

items.statement: EBITDA from power supply up 18% YoY to INR6,366 cr; cash profit up 23% YoY to INR3,630 cr for 9M FY25
items.quote: our EBITDA from power supply has increased by 18% year-on-year to INR6,366 crores, while our cash profit has surged by a substantial 23% year-on-year to INR3,630 crores.

items.statement: ALCM/ALMM compliance may raise solar module costs by 2-3 cents/W initially, then stabilize as domestic capacity scales
items.quote: we expect that in the beginning there will be a small increase in the cost of these by 2-3 cents from a purchase point of view. But it will then again come down and stabilize as the country manufacturing capacity picks up and so on.

items.statement: Extending supplier relationships internationally and domestically for ALMM/ALCM compliance; workforce in Khavda expanded to 12,000+
items.quote: we are extending our relationships with suppliers, not only internationally for solar modules, but also domestically as ALMM compliance and ALCM compliance comes into play. And thirdly, we are extending our workforce footprint in Khavda to north of 12,000 people.

items.statement: FY25 capacity addition split: 85% solar (75% PPA, 25% merchant), 15% wind (100% merchant)
items.quote: when it comes to solar and wind split, I think we're targeting 85% of capacity on solar and 15% on wind. items.quote: We aim to have 85% of our contracts to be long-term fixed-term PPAs, which will provide stability of cash flows, while we will have approximately 15% of our capacity around C&I and merchant, which is expected to enhance our portfolio returns. items.statement: Avoiding aggressive standalone battery tenders; focusing on integrated solutions with de-risked technology and supply chain
items.quote: We're not interested in, first of all, in these vanilla projects. And secondly, we're not interested in taking these kind of funds in the market. items.statement: RPO enforcement by MNRE/BEE expected to drive DISCOM PPA signings by end of FY25
items.quote: We believe that some of these things will get tied up as RPO obligation comes into force by end of this year. MNRE is driving and Burau of Energy Efficiency is driving that very well. items.statement: No new equity needed; AGEL fully funded for 50 GW target; TotalEnergies JV projects progressing, no new equity expected from them
items.quote: AGEL is fully funded to deliver on its ambition and there is no new project in which we are anticipating or expecting to have TotalEnergies on board. So, there is really no financial implication or any other implication, which we should be thinking of from the point of view of AGEL.

items.statement: Ashish Khanna to take over as CEO effective April 2025; current CEO Amit Singh to transition
items.quote: We also have with us Mr. Ashish Khanna, who will be taking charge as the CEO of the company effective April this year. He will primarily be a listener for this call.

items.statement: Energy sales up 23% YoY to 20 BU for 9M FY25; revenue from power supply up 18% YoY to INR6,829 cr
items.quote: Our energy sales has also increased by 23% year-on-year to 20 billion units for the first nine months ending December 31st. And our revenue from power supply has seen a robust increase of 18% year-on-year, reaching INR6,829 crores.

items.statement: AGEL contributed 15% of India's new solar capacity and 12% of new wind installations in CY2024
items.quote: AGEL contributed to 15% of nationwide new solar capacity and 12% of new wind installations in the year 2024, a remarkable achievement which truly underscores our leadership in the renewable energy sector.

items.quote: this year, we had extended monsoon. items.quote: The reason is that distribution because of which the overall NCI working was changed and because of NCD conversion to CCD, there is a control change which has happened.

items.statement: Confident of delivering revised guidance in current quarter
items.quote: We are confident of delivering our revised guidance in the current quarter.

items.statement: Deposit franchise grew 50% YoY and 10% QoQ; digital channels sourcing INR 2.5 Cr per day
items.quote: Our deposit franchise continued to grow at the expected pace with year -on-year growth of about 50% and QoQ growth of about 10%. This is primarily on account of sourcing of deposits through digital channel, which is now garnering approximately INR 2.5 Cr of deposits per day.

items.statement: Retail deposits at 81.2% of total; CASA ratio improved to 19.5% from 17.9% QoQ
items.quote: Our CASA ratio as of December has improved from 17.9% in the previous quarter to 19.5% as of December end.

items.statement: Gross advances INR 9,563 Cr, up 25.8% YoY; disbursements INR 4,888 Cr, up 6.7% YoY
items.quote: Our gross advances stood at INR 9,563 Cr, which is a YoY increase of 25.8% compared to INR7,600 Cr. The disbursements were at INR 4,888 Cr, up 6.7% from INR 4,580 Cr in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Wheels business grew 80% YoY and 14% QoQ with <1% GNPA; mortgage grew 43% YoY and 8% QoQ

items.statement: Current bucket collection efficiency at 97.9% (one EMI capped); targeting 98.5% for Q4
items.quote: Our current bucket collection efficiency with one EMI capped stood at 97.9%.

items.quote: So out of the total INR 270 Cr that we have had for the bank as a whole, around INR 240 Cr will be for microfinance in this particular quarter.

items.quote: our pre-approved list contains around 6 lakh customers. The focus for Q4 is m ore in terms of existing pre-approved customers and that around 80% of that qualifies

items.quote: We continue to focus on widening our reach by adding new branches each year. Our Smart Banking Outlets are present in certain micro markets. These SBOs are customer touch points, which offer all banking services but have a focused target segment within 2-kilometer areas.

items.quote: We have launched Dhanashree, our MSME product, which is completely digital, primarily to cater to our inclusive finance customer segment and other small business segments. items.statement: FY26 guidance to be shared at Q4 results; too early to provide numbers now

However, it is not as per our expectation, but we still expect to recover from the slow first half and have some single-digit growth.

items.statement: Marketing spend doubled to INR33 crores in Q3 FY25 vs same period last year
items.quote: In Q3 FY25, we spent around INR33 crores towards advertising and marketing, which is almost double the expenditure during the same period last year.

items.statement: Franchising model open for future but not actively pursued; 30 signed stores are company-owned
items.quote: For the moment, we wanted to open a few stores and get a grasp of the business and get the operations to some extent, before we open this out for franchisees. However, we are not actively looking for franchises, but we are getting a lot of contracts and we are in discussion. So, we will see how it goes. At the moment, these 30 stores are what we have signed for running ourselves.

items.statement: AUM reached INR 11,067 Crores, up 32% YoY
items.quote: We are proud to share that UGRO Capital's Asset under management reached a record INR 11,067 Crores, reflecting a robust 32% YoY growth.

items.statement: Net disbursement hit all-time high of INR 2,098 Crores
items.quote: Our net disbursement hit an all-time high of INR 2,098 Crores, showcasing our operational strength and strategic focus.

items.statement: Emerging Market channel disbursement grew to INR 543 Crores from INR 180 Crores YoY
items.quote: This channel's disbursement grew to INR 543 Crores compared to INR 180 Crores in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Added 74 new branches in Emerging Market channel, total 224 branches across 11 states
items.quote: This exceptional growth has been supported by additions of 74 new branches, taking our total to 224 branches across 11 states.

items.statement: 4% ROA target delayed by 2-3 quarters due to slower liquidity environment
items.quote: I think we are seeing around two to three quarters of delay versus what AUM we should have been versus what we are. It is showcasing at least a 2 to 3 quarter delay.

items.statement: Target cost-to-income ratio ~55% for FY25, to decline in FY26 depending on distribution
items.quote: This year we should end closer to 55%, 1% here and there. And next year, it should go down depending upon how next three months pan out as far as distribution is concerned.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing flat at 10.68%, higher than peers; expect gradual reduction with scale
items.quote: While we are navigating a slow liability environment, our costs of borrowing remain flat at 10.68%. We continue to believe that our rate of borrowing is higher than our p eers set of markets

items.statement: Gross yield 18.2%, net yield ~16.7% flat; divergence due to embedded finance partner share
items.quote: If you look at the yield, it is, yield remains flattish to 16.7%. And this quarter, there is some uptick on the gross yield, which is 18.2%.

items.statement: Secured-unsecured mix target 70-30 at AUM level; unsecured 41% covered under CGTMSE
items.quote: So, our broad intent is to keep secured-unsecured mix as around 30-70. And within the unsecured loans also now, 41% of our portfolio is covered under the Central Guarantee Scheme.

items.statement: Secured loans average LTV ~55%; unsecured loans without collateral ~30% of book
items.quote: And on average, on LTVs for secured loans, we are at around 55%.

items.statement: GNPA stable at 2.1%, NNPA at 1.5%; disciplined underwriting and proactive risk management
items.quote: Despite these headwinds, UGRO Capital has maintained a stable GNPA ratio of 2.1% and net NPA of 1.5%, reflecting our disciplined underwriting practices and proactive risk management.

items.statement: CGTMSE guarantees 75% of principal on covered unsecured loans; claims typically 2x premium paid
items.quote: What CGTMSE policy does is, it guarantees 75% of the principal outstanding. So, for example, if INR 100 of loan is covered and it is covered under the guarantee scheme, then at the end of the, after it becomes NPA and the documentation and the normal operational paperwork is completed, then INR 75 of that government reimburses as part of the plan.

items.statement: Plan to expand to 400 locations; all branches expected positive-accretive in 3 quarters
items.quote: Over a period of being established at 400 odd locations, I think in three quarters from now, all of our locations would be positive-accretive.

items.statement: MyShubhLife AUM INR 302 Crores; served 28,000+ customers via PhonePe, FINO, Meesho, Airtel, Mobikwik
items.quote: MyShubhLife's AUM stands at INR 302 Crores as of December 2024, and it has served over 28,000 customers since we announced the acquisition, through partnership with platforms like PhonePe, FINO, Meesho, Airtel, Mobikwik, and we expect more partners to be onboarded in this quarter.

items.statement: Co-lending volume dropped to INR 372 Crores from INR 615 Crores QoQ as banks cautious on unsecured business loans
items.quote: Hence, the volume in this quarter dropped to INR 372 Crores from INR 615 Crores in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Machinery finance avg INR 75 Cr/month; target INR 150-175 Cr/month; tenure ~3.5 yrs, ticket ~INR 35 lakh, yield ~14%
items.quote: We are doing average of around INR 75 Crore a month. Our target was to take it to INR 150-odd Crores. What we are seeing is that we have worked with roughly around 75 plus OEMs in India.

items.statement: RBI tightening on unsecured loans created perception challenge; banks cautious on co-lending; expect restart in current/ensuing quarter
items.quote: At the same time, the regulatory tightening around unsecured loans has created a perception challenge for NBFC, while co-lending volumes have temporarily declined as banks have become cautious on business loan segments.

items.statement: Liquidity environment slower; cost of funds higher than peers; capacity built out but constrained by expensive borrowing

items.statement: If share price doesn't reflect performance, will grow at lower pace to avoid dilution; cannot grow 30% without capital
items.quote: If we continue to perform the way we are performing, which means on all metrics we deliver, but it does not get reflected into the share price, then which is something which is beyond our control, we would no choice but to go at a lower pace because we cannot grow at 30% because we would need more capital.

items.statement: Emerging Market branches: 11-member team (branch manager, 6 sales, credit manager, ops manager, collections manager); 250 collection staff for 210 branches
items.quote: So, your question, every branch today has a branch manager, about 6 sales officers, a credit manager, an operations manager, and a collections manager. So, it's a typically 11-member branch, and the collections guy comes in month, too.

items.statement: Focus on MSME turnover INR 15 lakh to 15 crore; loan size INR 5 lakh to 5 crore; diversified collateral types
items.quote: We are the only player in the country which has a diversified asset channel and a focus on one customer segment which is INR 15 lakh to INR 15 crore turnover where we have the ability to do a loan of INR 5 lakhs to up to INR 5 crores.

items.statement: Only pan-India small-ticket LAP player; peers south or north focused; strong in Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Karnataka, Andhra, Rajasthan, Gujarat, UP, MP, Maharashtra
items.quote: We are the only small-ticket LAP business or Emerging Market business which is pan-India. Most of our peer set either are south focused or north focused. We are very prominently present in Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Karnataka, Andhra in South. And now we are very strongly present originally in Rajasthan, Gujarat. And now we have expanded into UP, MP and Maharashtra.
