items.statement: Fair and Handsome rebranded to Smart and Handsome; transition completed for base cream and face wash; new advertising started January 15; full male grooming range rollout in next 3-4 months.
items.quote: The transition has happened for the base cream and face wash. So it started about a month back. And now the product that you will see in the market is all Smart and Handsome. In fact, the new advertising has also started from 15th of January for Smart and Handsome. And as far as the extensions or the entire male grooming range is concerned, that we will start rolling out in the next 3 months to 4

items.statement: No price changes for Smart and Handsome rebrand; pricing maintained similar structure.
items.quote: We haven't changed the prices.

items.statement: Gross margins expanded 150 bps to 70.3%; EBITDA grew 8% to INR339 crores with margins up 70 bps; PAT up 8% to INR279 crores in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: Our gross margins expanded by 150 basis points to 70.3%. EBITDA grew by 8% to INR339 crores, with margins expanding by 70 basis points. And profit after tax also increased by 8% to INR279 crores.

items.statement: For 9M FY25, gross margins expanded 140 bps to 69.6%; EBITDA grew 9% to INR806 crores; PAT increased 12% to INR644 crores.
items.quote: In 9 months ended December '24, gross margins expanded by 140 basis points to 69.6%. EBITDA grew by 9% to INR806 crores, and PAT increased by 12% to INR644 crores.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by price hikes (1.5-2.5% on larger packs), lower packaging material costs, and cost reduction initiatives.
items.quote: We have seen some on the packaging material mostly, and also, the pricing is mostly across. So not on the LUPs, but on the larger pack, some bit of pricing and on average 1.5% to 2.5% kind of pricing benefited there.

items.statement: Weighted average price increase expected in range of 1.5% to 2% for coming quarter.
items.quote: It would be in the range of 1.5% to 2%.

items.statement: Board approved second interim dividend of 400% (INR4 per share) for FY25; cumulative dividend 800% (INR8 per share) for FY25.
items.quote: I'm pleased to inform that the Board of Directors have approved a second interim dividend of 400%, translating to INR4 per equity share for FY '24. This follows the first interim dividend of 400%, also amounting to INR4 per share declared in Q2. Cumulatively, we have distributed dividends of 800% equivalent to INR8 per share during FY '24.

items.statement: Organized channels (modern trade, e-commerce, institutional) now contribute 28.6% of domestic business, up 160 bps; growing at nearly double the pace of overall domestic business.
items.quote: Our organized channels continue to strengthen with modern trade, e -commerce and institutional sales, now contributing to 28.6% of domestic business, an increase of 160 basis points in Q3. These channels grew at nearly double the pace compared to overall domestic business.

items.statement: Rural contribution remains ~53-54% of domestic business; CSD contributes ~4%.
items.quote: So rural would still be -- if you exclude that, if you take the overall business, it should still be about 53%, 54% of the domestic business.

items.statement: Receivables cycle at 16-17 days as of December, slightly improved from last year; credit cycles consistent since COVID.
items.quote: So, Rahul, our receivables would be roughly around 16 days, 17 days which is slightly improved from the last year period or March quarter, but still that's what Mohan ji said is continuing for quite some time now post COVID.

items.statement: Operating cash flow for 9M FY25 estimated around INR500-550 crores; no significant capex till December.
items.quote: So if you look at our 9 months profit is almost -- EBITDA is almost INR800 crores plus and profit after tax would be INR640 crores. So there is not significant c apex till December. So I think around INR500 crores, INR550 crores, kind of would be the operating cash flows.

items.statement: Effective tax rate projected at 8-9% for FY25 and around 10% for FY26.
items.quote: So, Ajay, for FY '25, I think the current trajectory should be there around 8%, 9% kind of tax rate. And going ahead for next year also, it should be within the range of 10% kind of.

items.statement: International business declined 3% in Q3 due to sharp decline in Russia (high inflation, credit constraints); Russia still delivered double-digit growth for 9M; Bangladesh stable with political instability; expansion in Africa (East Africa)
items.quote: International business, we couldn't do much in Russia with a very high inflation environment over there. And that is the prime reason. When we look at the quarter, we had a massive decline in that particular geography. But cumulatively, for the 9 months, still Russia has delivered double-digit growth.

items.statement: Expect good revival in international business in Q4 FY25; Russia underperformance seen as aberration.
items.quote: We have been -- not been able to deliver the growth. But when we look at 20 quarters, we would have decent, and we'll see a good rival in quarter 4, again. We should have good revival in quarter 4. That's more an aberration which is happening.

items.statement: Insurance coverage for ayurvedic medicines may gradually benefit ethical and generics portfolio in ayurvedic hospitals; no dramatic short-term impact expected.
items.quote: And we've not seen much of a direct impact by way of change in the policy in terms of our business volumes. And it's a bit difficult to quantify that also. But as we gradually move forward as the industry accepts it and consumers and patients accept it, we definitely see some upsurge in patients getting admitted to ayurvedic hospitals.

items.statement: Pancharishta facing category-wide pressure (Arishtha/Asava format) due to changing consumer preferences; modernizing packaging and campaigns to address decline.
items.quote: From what I've understood of the industry per se, and I'm not just talking Pancharishta, this format which is called as Arishtha or Asava as checked across companies. So this whole format is seeing a bit of a pressure in terms of volume growth across organizations, across categories.

items.statement: No impact seen from Dabur's acquisition of Sesa on Kesh King; hair oil category slowdown is category-wide, not brand-specific.
items.quote: No, we don't -- we haven't seen any impact of that as yet. The Kesh King category was not going for some quarters. It is to do with the category itself, not just Kesh King category, but the entire oil categories.

items.statement: Goodwill amortization expected at roughly INR90 crores for FY26 and FY27.
items.quote: So for next year also roughly INR90 crores kind of amortization would be there, Kunal.

items.statement: Urban trade liquidity constraints persist since COVID; credit cycles extended; no visibility on improvement timeline.
items.quote: No, it's a -- as I said, Rahul, this is a problem which has been going on since many, many, many quarters. It's not a new problem. Maybe we've just highlighted it in our con call, okay? So that's why the credit cycles and everything has been consistent since the COVID.

items.statement: Targets INR30,000 crores AUM by FY27 and mid-teen ROE by then
items.quote: We remain confident of achieving our earlier guidance of INR30,000 crores AUM by FY '27 and delivering mid-teen ROE by then.

items.statement: AUM reached INR20,663 crores in Q3 FY25, up 54.6% YoY
items.quote: We maintained a strong growth momentum in 3Q FY '25, with our AUM reaching INR20,663 crores, an increase of 54.6% year -on-year.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM grew 196% YoY to INR7,092 crores
items.quote: Our gold loan AUM increased by 196% year -on-year to cross INR7,092 crores supported by our extensive gold loan branch network of 776 branches across nine states and union territories.

items.statement: Housing loan AUM grew 31% YoY to INR4,586 crores
items.quote: And housing loan segment AUM reached INR4,586 crores, up by 31% year-on-year.

items.statement: Construction finance AUM grew 65% YoY to INR3,742 crores
items.quote: Our Construction Finance AUM increased by 65% year -on-year to cross INR3,742 crores, driven by strong demand in real estate sector and pipeline of new affordable housing projects.

items.statement: Co-lending AUM surged to INR3,681 crores, 17.8% of total AUM
items.quote: Our co-lending AUM continued to surge during 3Q FY '25 and stood at INR3,681 crores, comprising 17.8% of AUM, compared to 8.9% in Q3 FY '24.

items.statement: Yields and spreads expanded to 16.7% and 7.3% respectively in Q3 FY25
items.quote: yields and spreads expanded further in the quarter to 16.7% and 7.3%, respectively, primarily Capri Global Capital Limited Q3 FY25 Concall Transcript | January 27, 2025 on account of increase in yields for housing finance to 12.9% and Gold Loan to 20.6

items.statement: Cost-income ratio improved to 58.3% in Q3 FY25 from 64.3% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: We opened 70 new branches exclusively for our Micro LAP segment. Following our significant investment in branch expansion over the past 3 years, we are now focusing on bringing more efficiency and productivity, effect of which has already started to reflect in our cost-income ratio, which improved to 58.3% in third quarter FY '25, down from 64.3% in second quarter FY '25 and down from the peak of

items.statement: Gross Stage 3 at 1.7%, Net Stage 3 at 1%, PCR 39.4% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Gross Stage 3 ratio stood at 1.7%, and Net Stage 3 ratio stood at 1% in third quarter FY '25, an improvement of 40 basis year-on-year in both. We continue to maintain a healthy PCR on Stage 3 loans of 39.4% in third quarter FY '25.

items.statement: Credit cost at INR18 crores in Q3 FY25, 0.7% of loan book for 9M FY25
items.quote: As regards asset quality, our credit cost for third quarter FY '25 was at INR18 crore, a modest increase of 4.8% quarter-on-quarter, whereas for 9-month FY '25, it declined by 6.5% year-on-year and was INR82 crores, which translates to 0.7% of loan book.

items.statement: Intends to keep net NPA not more than 1%
items.quote: Asset quality, we intend to keep net NPA not more than 1%, and that's the philosophy we will continue to do.

items.statement: Plans to open 100-200 branches next year, exact number to be finalized by March
items.quote: So next year, yes. Next year, we are going to open anything between 100 to, 200, but we make our budget in the month of February and till mid-March we finalize, when we keep our meeting with all the business heads internally and go to the Board for that.

items.statement: Branch network expanded to 1,066 branches; 70 new Micro LAP branches opened
items.quote: Our branch network expanded to 1,066 branches in third quarter FY '25, and employee base increased to 11,022, up by 13% year-on-year. We opened 70 new branches exclusively for our Micro LAP segment.

items.statement: Launched Micro LAP (INR157 crores AUM in 2 quarters) and Rooftop Solar loans
items.quote: In the last quarter, under our MSME loan segment, we launched Micro LAP, a small ticket secured loan product for self-employed customer, and launched Rooftop Solar loans.

items.statement: Car loan origination at INR2,972 crores in Q3 FY25, up 16% QoQ and 5% YoY
items.quote: Our car loan origination in third quarter FY '25 was INR2,972 crores, up by 16% quarter-on-quarter and 5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Insurance distribution tied up with 18 companies, expects >INR60 crores net fee income for FY25
items.quote: On the insurance distribution front, we have tied up with 18 insurance companies and expected to generate more than INR60 crores of net fee income for FY '25.

items.statement: Borrowings predominantly floating rate (<5% fixed); new credit lines of INR1,025 crores sanctioned in Q3 FY25
items.quote: During third quarter FY '25, we got new credit lines of INR1,025 crores sanctioned for CGCL and CGHFL.

items.statement: Expects interest rate cycle to remain stable or fall, not rise
items.quote: We expect now interest rate cycle should remain here and not go up. In the best, it might remain here for some time before it starts falling down again, but we don't expect the interest rate to go up.

items.statement: Net interest income grew 41% YoY to INR347 crores in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Our net interest income for third quarter FY '25 reached INR347 crores, marking a 41% year-on-year increase and, for 9 months FY '25, reached at the INR953 crores, marking a 30% year-on-year increase driven by margin expansion and robust growth in our loan book.

items.statement: Pre-provisioning operating profit rose 46% YoY to INR189 crores in Q3 FY25
items.quote: As a result, our pre -provisioning operating profit increased significantly to INR189 for third quarter FY '25 and INR480 crores for 9 months FY '25, up by 46% year-on-year and 39% year-on-year, respectively.

items.statement: Consolidated net profit up 88% YoY to INR128 crores in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Our consolidated net profit saw strong increase and stood at INR128 crores for third quarter FY '25, up by 88% year -on-year and 32% quarter -on-quarter, whereas our profit for 9 months FY '25 stood at INR301 crores, up by 53% year-on-year.

items.statement: Annualized ROA 2.8% and ROE 12.6% in Q3 FY25, up QoQ
items.quote: We reported an annualized return on average asset of 2.8% and annualized return on average equity of 12.6% on third quarter FY '25, up by 0.5% and 2.8% q uarter-on-quarter, respectively

items.statement: Collection team attrition less than 20%
items.quote: So, your question is related to the attrition in the team member of the collection team. So , our collection team is quite stable in the sense on the ground because we had a good collection efficiency, good technology and also the incentive plan. So, it is less than 20%.

items.statement: No regulatory mandate for EMI-based gold loan products; product design is at company discretion
items.quote: Regulator never say what should be a product. Regulator always say, your compliance requirement are A, B, C, D, you can do it. How you design your product, they don't guide us, but there's no instruction or circular on that as such.

items.statement: Gold loan LTV at 71-72% considered healthy and in line with industry; full recovery via auctions
items.quote: So, gold loan portfolio, if you see, the maximum permissible LTV is around 75%, and the competition alsohave LTV in the range to 71% to 75% only. Gold being very liquid, I think these are very healthy levels of the LTV levels. And even with the auctions and the NPA cases, we are able to recover fully.

items.statement: Rooftop Solar target INR1,000 crores AUM over next 4 years, dependent on government subsidy scheme
items.quote: So INR1,000 crores AUM is not the target for 1 year. INR1,000 crores target will be in the period of next 4 years or so, and it will be governed by the government subsidy scheme.

items.statement: Marketing budget INR15 crores for FY25; INR10 crores spent in 9M FY25
items.value: INR15 crores budget, INR10 crores spent
items.quote: So we have a budget of about INR15 crores for marketing, which comprises of radio, which comprises of hoarding, which comprises of newspaper, which comprises of the media. So combination of this INR15 crores is our budget. And till 9 months, we have already spent about close to INR10 crores.

items.statement: Technology center in Gurgaon with 125+ engineers and 25 data scientists across Bangalore, Pune, Mumbai, Delhi
items.quote: We have set up a tech center, which is in Gurgaon. We have 125 -plus engineers and 25 data scientists. Our data scientists are across Bangalore, Pune, Mumbai and Delhi.

items.statement: FY25 domestic credit growth guided at 14-15% and domestic deposit growth at 13-14%
items.quote: Considering the positive outlook as stated earlier, domestic credit growth will be around 14-15% and domestic deposit growth is projected at around 13-14% for FY25.

items.statement: FY25 credit cost guidance maintained at 0.70%
items.quote: As regards the guidance for the full year is concerned, we are giving a guidance of 0.70% for FY25 on the credit cost, which remains to be the same guidance which we had given in the last quarter.

items.statement: FY25 Cost to Income ratio guidance at around 51%
items.quote: As regards Cost to Income ratio is concerned, there also we are expecting that our guidance is at around 51%. So we would be able to maintain a Cost to Income ratio of around 51

items.statement: FY25 global NIM guidance at around 2.90%
items.quote: So, as far as the guidance is concerned on the global NIM, it should be at around 2.90% for March '25. That is the number we are giving.

items.statement: Recovery from written-off accounts expected at Rs.300-500 crore per quarter
items.quote: This quarter also we expect that the recovery from written off account will be somewhere around Rs.300 to Rs.500 crores.

items.statement: Credit pipeline of Rs.70,000+ crore, with Rs.60,000 crore corporate and Rs.10,000 crore RAM
items.quote: As on date, if I give you the credit pipeline which we have, we have nearly Rs.70,000 crores of credit pipeline, out of which nearly Rs.60,000 crores is in the corporate book, both domestic and international, and another Rs.10,000 crores of the pipeline is in the RAM book.

items.statement: Global NIM 2.80% in Q3 FY25, domestic NIM 2.98%, nine-month global NIM 2.90%
items.quote: Global NIM stood at 2.80% for Q3FY25 and 2.90% for 9M Dec'24.

items.statement: Yield on advances improved 10 bps to 8.55%, cost of deposits up 1 bp to 4.96%, spread 3.59%
items.quote: our yield on advances, they have improved from 8.45 % in the month of September 24 to 8.55% in the month of December 24. And our cost of deposit has gone up by only one basis point from 4.95% to 4.96%. The gap between the two now is 3.59

items.statement: Gross NPA 3.69% (down 166 bps YoY), Net NPA 0.85% (down 56 bps YoY)
items.quote: Gross NPA ratio is at 3.69% and has improved by 166 bps YoY. Net NPA ratio at 0.85% only and has improved by 56 bps on a YoY basis.

items.statement: Slippage ratio 0.19%, credit cost 0.39% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: There is significant im provement in Slippage Ratio at 0.19% and as regards Credit Cost, it is at 0.39

items.statement: Fresh slippages Rs.1,105 crore in Q3 vs Rs.2,546 crore in Q2; one large PSU account caused Q2 spike
items.quote: This quarter, our fresh slippages are only Rs.1,105 crore as against Rs.2,546 in September and further as against Rs.1,313 in December 23.

items.statement: SMA reduced to Rs.7,200 crore (1.16% of standard book) from Rs.7,600 crore; SMA-2 increase due to State Govt PSU accounts
items.quote: Overall SMA has come down if you see from our presentation. However, there has been an increase in SMA-2 number because of few accounts which are of State government, one State Government PSU account because of which it is at increase. However, overall SMA number has come down from Rs.7,600 crores to Rs.7,200 crores.

items.statement: RAM advances grew 18.96% YoY to Rs.3.12 lakh crore (57% of domestic advances); corporate book Rs.2.34 lakh crore (10% YoY)
items.quote: RAM advances have increased by 18.96% on YoY basis from Rs.2,62,000 Cr in Dec'23 to Rs.3,12,000 Cr in Dec'24 with incremental growth of more than Rs.49,000 Cr and with RAM advances contributing 57% of total domestic advances.

items.statement: Retail book Rs.1.27 lakh crore: housing 51%, vehicle 15%, education 3%, mortgage 8%, personal 9%, others 14%
items.quote: our t otal outstanding is Rs.1,27,000 crores as on December 24 which comprises of housing loan which is nearly 51% of our total retail book. Vehicle loans are nearly 15% of that retail book. Education loan is 3%, mortgage loans are 8%, personal loan are 9% and others which is predominantly staff loan, loans against FDs and others are 14

items.statement: MCLR increased 65 bps since Jan 2023; one-year MCLR now 9.05%
items.quote: When the last time the Repo increase was made by RBI was in month of January 2023, when they had increased the Repo from 6.25% to 6.50%. That time our MCLR was 8.40%. And today as we speak, our MCLR has gone up by 65 basis points.

items.statement: Project NexTech: 24x7 Resiliency Operating Centre opened; cyber solutions procured; API gateway enhanced; QR feedback implemented
items.quote: As part of project NexTech, Bank has opened a 24x7 Resiliency Operating Centre (ROC) for quick response and recovery from disruptions of Bank's applications including CBS, E-platform, Mobile Banking App. etc. due to natural disaster, system outages, cyber-attacks etc.

items.statement: Wage settlement implemented; employee expenses streamlined after Q2 provision
items.quote: Now, the wage settlement has been implemented. And now it is well settled within the system. So, for all our officer staff and also clerical staff, the new salary package is there. So, now it has got streamlined and moderated.

items.statement: LCR average around 117%, above RBI threshold of 100%
items.quote: Our average LCR is around 117 something. That is the number at which our LCR is and it is above the threshold level of 100 fixed by RBI.

items.statement: Operating profit Rs.3,703 crore (23% YoY); net profit Rs.2,517 crore (35% YoY); 9M net profit Rs.6,593 crore (35% YoY)
items.value: Rs.3,703 crore op profit, Rs.2,517 crore net profit
items.quote: Operating Profit for Q3FY25 stands at Rs.3,703 Cr witnessing a YoY growth of 23%. Net Profit for Q3FY25 stands at Rs.2,517 Cr witnessing a YoY growth of 35% and for 9M DEC'24 stands at Rs.6,593 Cr with YoY growth of 35%.

items.statement: Non-interest income Rs.1,746 crore (46% YoY) in Q3; 9M Rs.5,566 crore (28% YoY); Q3 dip due to lower treasury gains
items.quote: Non-Interest Income for Q3FY25 stands at Rs.1,746 Cr witnessing a YoY growth of 46% and for 9M Dec'24 stands at Rs.5,566 Cr with YoY growth of 28%.

items.statement: Treasury income expected to improve in Q4 as yields ease; 10-year at 6.71%, rate action and liquidity easing expected
items.quote: In Q4, looking at the markets, we feel that yields are going to come down from here. You see, 10-year is trading around 6.71. We expect a rate action as well as the regulator to ease liquidity in the markets. So, that will bring yields down and we hope to make money both on the investment side as well as on the FX side.

items.statement: Net interest margin was 4.25% in Q3-2025, down from 4.27% in Q2-2025 and 4.43% in Q3-2024
items.quote: Net interest margin was 4.25% in Q3-2025 compared to 4.27% in Q2-2025 and 4.43% in Q3-2024

items.statement: Management expects margins to remain broadly stable until the rate cycle starts, after which rate cuts would impact margins due to lead-lag effect
items.quote: We do expect the margins to be broadly stable until the rate cycle starts. Of course, after the rate cuts happen, margins would be impacted due to lead lag effect as floating loans will get repriced much faster than fixed deposits.

items.statement: Domestic loan portfolio grew 15.1% year-on-year and 3.2% sequentially to December 31, 2024
items.quote: The domestic loan portfolio grew by 15.1% year -on-year and 3.2% sequentially at December 31, 2024

items.statement: Domestic corporate portfolio grew 13.2% year-on-year and 4.3% sequentially at December 31, 2024
items.quote: Growth in the domestic corporate portfolio was 13.2% year-on-year and 4.3% sequentially at December 31, 2024

items.statement: Net NPA ratio stable at 0.42% at December 31, 2024, same as September 30, 2024, down from 0.44% a year ago
items.quote: Net NPA ratio was 0.42% at December 31, 2024 compared to 0.42% at September 30, 2024 and 0.44% at December 31, 2023

items.statement: Loan and non-fund based outstanding to performing corporate borrowers rated BB and below reduced to ₹2,193 crore at December 31, 2024 from ₹3,386 crore at September 30, 2024
items.quote: Loan and non-fund based outstanding to performing corporate borrowers rated BB and below reduced to ₹2,193 crore at December 31, 2024 from ₹3,386 crore at September 30, 2024

items.statement: Total deposits grew 14.1% year-on-year to ₹15,20,309 crore at December 31, 2024; average deposits grew 13.7% YoY
items.quote: Total period-end deposits increased by 14.1% year -on-year to ₹15,20,309 crore at December 31, 2024 2. Average deposits increased by 13.7% year -on-year to ₹14,58,489 crore during Q3-2025

items.statement: Average current account deposits grew 13.1% YoY; average savings account deposits grew 12.3% YoY in Q3-2025
items.quote: Average current account deposits increased by 13.1% year-on-year 4. Average savings account deposits increased by 12.3% year-on-year

items.statement: Liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) was 123% for the quarter; management is very comfortable with liquidity position
items.quote: Our LCR is 123%, and we are very comfortable with our liquidity.

items.statement: CET-1 ratio was 15.93% and total capital adequacy ratio was 16.60% at December 31, 2024, including profits for 9M-2025
items.quote: Including profits for 9M-2025, CET-1 ratio was 15.93% and total capital adequacy ratio was 16.60%

items.statement: No immediate plans to raise equity; capital position is very comfortable
items.quote: This is a very comfortable position. We have got no immediate plans of raising equity. I just want to correct it. There are no plans to raise it.

items.statement: Infrastructure bond issuance is one of the funding sources; no specific plan for Q4 but will evaluate based on rates and balance sheet strategy
items.quote: So, it's one of the sources of funding. So, depending upon what are the rates and what is our overall strategy on the balance sheet, we can look at it from time to time. I mean, there is no specific plan as of now.

items.statement: Personal loan growth slowed to 8.8% YoY (from mid-30s a year ago) as a conscious decision to calibrate growth after RBI call-out; credit card portfolio grew 17.9% YoY
items.quote: I think you rightly pointed out there has been a slowdown in personal loan growth. It has grown by about 8.8% year-on-year for this quarter. It was growing in the mid-30s about a year back. I think this has been a conscious decision.

items.statement: Business banking growth of ~32% YoY driven by formalisation from GST, increasing compliance, and granular, well-secured portfolio across the country
items.quote: We have been having this, the Business Banking group, that's what I presume when you say mid-market, has been growing in this range of about 32% year-on-year, and this has broadly been the range that we have been growing for the last couple of years. With this secto r getting more and more formalis ed, we continue to see healthy opportunities over here

items.statement: Core operating profit grew 13.1% YoY to ₹16,516 crore in Q3-2025; excluding subsidiary dividends, grew 14.7% YoY
items.quote: Core operating profit grew by 13.1% year-on-year to ₹16,516 crore in Q3-2025. Excluding dividend income from subsidiaries, core operating profit grew by 14.7% year-on-year in Q3-2025

items.statement: Profit before tax excluding treasury grew 12.8% YoY to ₹15,289 crore; profit after tax grew 14.8% YoY to ₹11,792 crore in Q3-2025
items.quote: Profit before tax excluding treasury, grew by 12.8% year -on-year to ₹15,289 crore in Q3-2025 7. Profit after tax grew by 14.8% year-on-year to ₹11,792 crore in Q3

items.statement: Consolidated profit after tax grew 16.6% YoY to ₹12,883 crore in Q3-2025
items.quote: Consolidated profit after tax grew by 16.6% year -on-year to ₹12,883 crore in Q3-2025

items.statement: Standalone RoE was 17.6% in Q3-2025
items.quote: Standalone RoE was 17.6% in Q3-2025

items.statement: Opened 129 branches in Q3-2025, 371 branches in last 12 months; network of 6,742 branches and 16,277 ATMs/CRMs at December 31, 2024
items.quote: The Bank opened 129 branches during Q3 -2025, 371 branches in the last 12 months and had a network of 6,742 branches and 16,277 ATMs and cash recycling machines at December 31, 2024

items.statement: Stake sale in ICICI Merchant Services (held <20%) to bring merchant acquiring in-house for better synergies and 100% ownership; not exiting the business
items.quote: Since merchant acquiring is a strategic part of our overall business, we felt it is better to do it in-house. And from an overall perspective, especially given the strategy of driving 360 perspective, we are able to drive synergies much better. So, it's not that we have got out of merchant acquiring. In fact, we have invested much more in merchant acquiring which is from an in-house angle.

items.statement: Overseas loan portfolio declined 21.2% YoY in USD terms at December 31, 2024; comprises 2.4% of overall loan book, 90% Indian corporates
items.quote: The overseas loan portfolio, in US dollar terms, declined 21.2% year-on-year at December 31, 2024. The overseas loan portfolio was about 2.4% of the overall loan book at December 31, 2024. Of the overseas corporate portfolio, about 90% comprises Indian corporates.

items.statement: Total outstanding to NBFCs and HFCs was ₹89,360 crore at December 31, 2024 (6.8% of advances), up from ₹88,027 crore at September 30, 2024
items.quote: The total outstanding to NBFCs and HFCs was 893.60 billion Rupees at December 31, 2024 compared to 880.27 billion Rupees at September 30, 2024. The total outstanding loans to NBFCs and HFCs were about 6.8% of our advances at December 31, 2024.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 operating EBITDA margin reached highest ever 11.9% without PLI benefits, up 70 bps YoY and 20 bps QoQ
items.quote: Combined EV and ICE, we have achieved the highest ever operating EBITDA margin of 11.9%. Kindly note, that this is without recognizing PLI benefits.

items.statement: Management expects Q4 FY25 to do well and FY26 to be a good year for both domestic and international markets
items.quote: We are expecting Q4 to do well. The new Jupiter for TVS, we will confidently say that we will grow ahead of the industry, thanks to the new products. And the existing products are also doing extremely well in the ICE.

And with this, and that as Vasudha said, the deal will close in a couple of weeks from now, wherein we will be getting a substantial number of employees, from Central 1 to come into our fold.

items.statement: Central 1 acquisition expected to add Rs.200 crores of additional ARR to revenue pool
items.quote: So, this business will bring Rs.200 crores of additional ARR to the revenue pool of Intellect.

items.statement: Strategic investment of Rs.20 Cr in DigiVation Digital Solutions Pvt Ltd (GlobalLinker) for SME e-procurement ecosystem
items.quote: Our strategic investment of Rs.20 Cr in DigiVation Digital Solutions Pvt Ltd positions Intellect as a leader in corporate and government e-procurement, driving growth in trade and supply chain finance globally.

items.statement: eMACH.ai chosen by 11 global customers across key regions in Q3 FY25
items.quote: In Q3 FY25, eMACH.ai achieved significant milestones by being chosen by 11 global customers across key regions, showcasing its capability to address diverse and complex financial requirements.

items.statement: Year-to-date: 34 deal wins and 37 go-lives across digital transformation projects
items.quote: For the year till date, we had 34 wins and we had gone live on 37 digital transformational projects

items.statement: Management stopped giving formal guidance but expects Q4 FY25 to be much better, targeting ~Rs.700 crore quarterly revenue
items.quote: We have stopped giving guidance, but I think, we are looking for expecting better, much better next quarter. So, that's what, we would like to look at it. I mentioned to you Rs.700 Crs a quarter. I think we will be closer to that.

items.statement: R&D capitalisation target of Rs.140 crore for FY25; expensed R&D around Rs.200 crore annually
items.quote: As far as the R&D spends are concerned, we only look at the absolute numbers. So, Rs.140 crore is the target and that's the budget that we had put in the beginning of the year. And, we will be meeting that budget.

items.statement: Contract assets remain high at 100-120 days of revenue due to milestone-based accrual vs invoicing gap typical in product companies
items.quote: Generally, in a product company, it will, be quite difficult to have it between 30 days and all. It will be quite high because the accrual happens as and when we complete the deliverable milestones, whereas, the invoicing will happen only when we kick in the payment milestone, only when we meet the payment milestone. So, the gap will always be there, in many product companies. So, that's the reaso

items.statement: Pipeline growing faster than revenue; sales cycle ~12 months with 6-month delay from pipeline build to closure; confident in conversion
items.quote: We have a good pipeline. For the pipeline to closure, it says cycle time of 12 months. So, when we went to eMACH.ai marketplace, putting to Europe and Americas. So, now if you look at it, Europe and Americas, both market Americas will be Rs.600 Crs market as of now, Europe will be another Rs.600 Crs. So, we have a potential as both the market could be 1,000 Crs market in next four years.

items.statement: GeM government receivables delayed; no specific comment on resolution timeline
items.quote: No comment. Government is government. So, they are delaying the process right now. We have to look what we can do.

items.statement: Targets 20% year-on-year revenue growth trajectory; aims for Rs 4,000 Crs revenue in next four years
items.quote: We are looking for 20% growth year on year. That trajectory, we want to keep it whether its 15%, 16%, 18%. Those are the number which we look at it as a trajectory.

items.statement: Expects Q4 FY25 revenue close to Rs 700 Crs
items.quote: Next 90 day, we are saying this Q4 is definitely looking close to Rs.700 Crs.

items.statement: Mature products deliver 30%+ operating margin; portfolio target of 30% margin in four years
items.quote: So, Manoj, the mature product gives a margin of 30% plus. So, like, GTB has a business if you have a separate business that will give 30% plus margin.

items.statement: Targets Rs 1,000 Crs PAT margin in four years
items.quote: Rs.1, 000 Crs margin will be there after four years, definitely. If you want to put that in my mouth, we are also looking for 1,000 Crs margin in four years.

items.statement: Cost structure stable at Rs 475-485 Crs per quarter; margin expansion expected as revenue crosses Rs 700 Crs
items.quote: If you look at the cost structure in last four quarters, it remains around Rs.475 to Rs.480 or Rs.485 Crs. And the revenue number is Rs.607 Crs number or you take Rs.625 Crs, the number will be different. As soon as it becomes Rs.700 Crs, the margin will look very different.

items.statement: Three business portfolio: GTB (Rs 1,000+ Crs, high margin), GCB (targeting Rs 1,000 Crs next year), AI (building to Rs 1,000 Crs)
items.quote: Now business 1 GTB has been Rs.1,000 Crs plus, business 2 is now GCB will be Rs.1,000 Crs next year. Now we are building AI business into this.

items.statement: Pipeline value approximately Rs 10,000 Crs in Q3 FY25; six-month delay from pipeline to closure
items.quote: In your slide deck on, slide 30, where you have probably, you know, talked about the funnel, almost Rs.10,000 Crs of the value of the funnel in Q3 FY 25.

items.statement: Purple Fabric platform live with customers in North America and UK; ~100 prospects in various stages; adoption focus over revenue initially
items.quote: We have around 100 different people are in various stages of interest being shown. A lot of service companies are showing interest that they can use. So, this is Purple Fabric platform.

items.statement: Internal AI deployment focused on build and validation phases over next two quarters to reduce headcount growth
items.quote: Over next two quarters, we focused on the middle two legs of driving engineering using this as well as validation using AI.

items.statement: Central 1 acquisition initially margin dilutive due to higher Western cost structure; targets accretive in 18-36 months via cross-sell; purchase price much lower than Intellect's trading multiple
items.quote: So, obviously, we need to build up the accretion when we sign up a new credit core banking deal. We want to bring it to the value accretive in next 18-36 months period.

items.statement: Acquisition not core strategy; eMACH.ai focus; only inbound opportunities considered
items.quote: As of now, acquisition is not a part of our core strategy. eMACH.ai is keeping us busy. We don't want to get distracted as a core part of the strategy. It's inbound only right now.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 revenue from operations Rs 607 Crs: License Rs 118 Crs, SaaS Rs 50 Crs, AMC Rs 124 Crs, Implementation Rs 315 Crs; all segments grew QoQ
items.quote: For the quarter, I mean, the total revenue as you would have seen, the revenue from operations is Rs.607 Crs while the total revenue including other income will be higher. So, out of the Rs.607 Crs, we have about Rs.118 Crs for license revenue. SaaS revenue is about Rs.50 Crs, AMC is Rs.124 Crs and implementation is Rs.315 Crs.

items.statement: North America now 200+ customers; aims for similar scale in Europe
items.quote: Each region, now North America would have now 200 customers plus. We would like to have a Europe to also have similar kind of a number of the customers.

items.statement: Displacing global incumbents (Finastra, Temenos, Palantir) with <$40M cumulative R&D investment
items.quote: We have displaced and disrupted the existing competition each time. We disrupted Finastra, we are disrupting Temenos. We are disrupting Palantir. We are a company from India disrupting a global player with such a low investment of what you say, Rs.140 Crs plus Rs.200 Crs, Rs.350 Crs. What is this investment in terms of global terms? It less than less than 40 million dollars.

items.statement: AI efficiency targets to reduce headcount growth; not hiring more people despite revenue growth
items.quote: We have targets to reduce the headcount for the efficiency of AI efficiency, which is there.

items.statement: Government (GeM) receivables delayed; no specific timeline for resolution
items.quote: Government is government. So, they are delaying the process right now. We have to look what we can do.

items.statement: Expect net marginal decline in general staffing headcount in Q4 FY25 driven by BFSI sector
items.quote: I think there will be a net decline of a small number that we do foresee for Q4. And I called that out in my narrative. While we will have BFSI contributing to a larger element of the decline. Some of the other sectors will compensate that decline, but it will be a net marginal decline.

items.statement: Expect normalization in general staffing from Q1 FY26 with positive outlook from sector and companies
items.quote: But I think post Q4 we do see normalization coming back and there are dialogues and feedbacks from companies about looking to add headcount thereafter and so on. So I think at this point, while we've seen it subdued for Q3 and Q4, I think Q1 onwards, it is the initial outlook from the sector and companies is quite positive.

items.statement: Expect HR Services to turn positive in Q4 FY25 and full year FY25
items.quote: HR Services, I think with the seasonality element of EdTech getting pushed is really why the loss is there. With the catch-up, we should turn positive back in Q4. Bhargav: No. So for the full year

items.statement: Expect meaningful EBITDA contribution from Ikigai from FY26 onwards, none in Q4 FY25
items.quote: We are not projecting any EBITDA contribution from Ikigai in Q4 FY '25. However, FY '26 and thereon will have a meaningful contribution from this entity.

items.statement: Target 6-7% EBITDA margin in EdTech for full year FY25
items.quote: On a full year basis, EdTech can maintain 6% to 7% EBITDA this year.

items.statement: Expect inorganic contribution of INR1.1 crores EBITDA from TSR Darashaw and Crystal HR in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Inorganic contribution by these two entities would be about INR1.1 crore s in Q4 FY '25 EBITDA of the TeamLease

items.statement: Target 6-7% EBITDA margin in HCM vertical after 12-month integration period
items.quote: With this contribution, we should be able to get to an EBITDA margins of 6% to 7% after a 12-month period in this vertical.

items.statement: BFSI sector remains stable with flat headcount due to tighter RBI norms on lending
items.quote: As we had called out last quarter, the BFSI sector remains stable due to tighter norms around lending in micro finance, credit cards, personal loans and similar areas, resulting in a flat headcount by quarter end.

items.statement: Consumer, retail and e-commerce sectors saw moderated surge with earlier-than-usual scale back in Q3
items.quote: Growth in the consumer, retail and e-commerce sectors generally peaks in Q2 and the first month of Q3, driven by technical factors. This quarter, that surge was moderated by an earlier-than-usual scale back.

items.statement: Manufacturing and Telecom saw low single-digit growth in Q3
items.quote: Manufacturing and Telecom saw low single-digit growth, which while positive had limited impact on overall numbers.

items.statement: Quick commerce signalling positiveness for Q4 hiring
items.quote: I think in Q3, we are seeing some different segments kind of signalling, like, for example, quick commerce signalling positiveness to us. So I'm hoping some of those will kind of pick up going into Q4.

items.statement: Retail and FMCG hiring expected to pick up end of Q4 for summer season
items.quote: Yes, retail as well as FMCG because typically, companies start hiring sales folks, service folks, etcetera and all that, for the upcoming summer season, which typically starts around April onwards. Riya

items.statement: Added 34 new logo sign-ups in general staffing in Q3, 80% on variable markup model
items.quote: On a positive note, our sales effort brought in 34 new logo sign-ups, primarily in the consumer, retail and manufacturing segments, out of which 80% of the variable mark up.

items.statement: Signed 8 key clients in specialized staffing in Q3, including 3 very large strategic accounts
items.quote: On the sales front, we signed 8 key clients in the last quarter, including 3 very large strategic accounts.

items.statement: Year-to-date net incremental associate growth of 32,600+ in general staffing, 12% net associate growth on opening base
items.quote: This quarter, we achieved a net addition of 1,300 plus associates taking our year-to-date net incremental associate growth to a little more than 32,600 and an overall net associate growth of 12% on our opening base.

items.statement: General staffing EBITDA grew 5% Q-o-Q despite BFSI headcount impact
items.quote: Our staffin g EBITDA has grown 5% Q-o-Q, even though headcount addition got impacted by BFSI this quarter

items.statement: PBT margin improved 5 basis points Q2 to Q3, PAT margin improved 8 basis points
items.quote: Even in terms of margin, PBT, we have marginally improved it by 5 basis points between Q2 to Q3, and PAT has improved by about 8 basis points.

items.statement: Focus on absolute profit improvement rather than margin percentage due to salary revisions impacting net margin
items.quote: Also, internally, we are focusing more on absolute profit improvement quarter-on-quarter because for the reasons which Ashok and Kartik explained, the salary revisions of associates are impacting our net margin. So absolute profits, we have improved both at EBITDA level and PBT level.

items.statement: Specialized staffing average salaries increased from INR40,000 to INR70,000-75,000 per month over 2 years due to GCC mix
items.quote: Like 2 years back, our average salaries in specialized staffing business were at 40,000. And now with more contribution from GCCs and we catering to a higher experience profile. Average salaries are currently at INR70,000, INR75,000 per month.

items.statement: Manufacturing PAPM in general staffing around INR800
items.quote: And I think if we look at the PAPM specific to manufacturing would be around INR800.

items.statement: Integrated learning apprenticeship realization INR700-800 vs INR300 for pure apprenticeship
items.quote: So typically, if the realization is about INR300 for a pure apprenticeship, the element of integrated learning apprentice is anywhere between 700 to 800.

items.statement: Acquired 90% stake in TSR Darashaw and 30% stake in Crystal HR for HR Tech vertical
items.quote: Last quarter, we announced the acquisition of 90% stake in TSR Darashaw HR services and 30% stake in Crystal HR.

items.statement: Invested in Ikigai partnership for specialized staffing expansion in Singapore and Middle East
items.quote: Another investment that we are doing is in Ikigai, which is effectively a partnership for the specialized staffing business. This gives us a legal entity presence in Singapore and in the Middle East, small business at this point in time, breakeven business, but we believe that the partnership could effectively focus on building larger volumes as we go forward.

items.statement: General staffing FTE productivity improved 1% to 386 from 382
items.quote: Continued productivity improvements in FTE by 1% has moved the needle from to 386 from 382.

items.statement: Specialized staffing recruiter productivity improved from 2.5 to 3.3 hires per month
items.quote: Operationally, our efforts to build a stronger and more resilient hiring teams are yielding results with recruiter productivity improving from 2.5 to almost about 3.3 higher per month as of the end of quarter 3.

items.statement: DA business increased learning coverage from 12% to 30% of apprentices/trainees
items.quote: From the start of the year when we were at about 12% of the associates and trainees being on learning alongside the apprenticeship. We've now moved it to about 30% being there.

items.statement: GCCs contribute 55-60% of specialized staffing net revenue with 30% of headcount
items.quote: Currently, about one-third of our associate headcount is deployed with these GCCs, contributing to about 55% to 60% of our net revenue as of the last quarter.

items.statement: Let go of 2 large specialized staffing mandates due to negative margins and changed service expectations
items.quote: We also, at point, explore t he possibility if it's becoming lower margin, whether the same mandate should be handled by this general staffing business. So there have been instances where we have shifted one or two customers in the past from specialized staffing to general staffing, depending on the margin profile. But, however, these 2 specific mandates had turned negative from a margin perspecti

items.statement: RBI KYC guidelines enforcement impacting BFSI hiring in Q3 and Q4
items.quote: Of course, on an ongoing basis, including for Q4, enforcement of some of the RBI guidelines around KYC will continue to impact us not just in Q3 but including in Q4 as well.

items.statement: Labour code implementation timeline uncertain despite government intent
items.quote: There's a lot of talk, but the element of timing around when it will get done is still out in the -- from a perspective of predictability. It's a lot of talk, but we don't have firm views on that.

items.statement: Free cash stands at INR310 crores as of December 31, 2024
items.quote: All balance sheet metrics are stable and steady. Free cash stands at INR310 crores as of December 31, 2024.

items.statement: Specialized staffing achieved positive net headcount growth for first time in several quarters
items.quote: Despite these headwinds, we achieved a small but positive net headcount growth for the first time in several quarters, along with increase in quarter-on-quarter revenue and a marginal improvement in year-on-year profitability.

items.statement: Asset growth guidance lowered to ~20% for FY25 from 25% earlier
items.quote: So, that remain intact and all put together is around 20% because it's still 20% is 2x of the industry average.

items.statement: Deposit growth guidance for FY25 is 23-24%
items.quote: FY25 we are saying 23%- 24% deposit growth, 20% asset growth.

items.statement: Cost of funds guidance revised to 7.07-7.08% for FY25
items.quote: We are expecting that our cost of money should be in the range of 7.7-7.8 (Corrected: 7.07 - 7.08%), not really 7.11-7.12.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target of 55% in next 2-3 years
items.quote: the hope is this that we might be, it should be lesser than the cost of income what we'll do this year, so that we remain on the path to become a 55% cost of income in next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: MFI credit cost problem largely behind by Q2 FY26
items.quote: I think by Q2, we should largely be behind over-leveraged credit cost problem.

items.statement: ROA of 2% achievable when cost of funds drops ~50 bps
items.quote: one of the things which need to come down to make us 2% ROA Bank has to be the cost of money, has to be lesser than maybe 50 bps from here what we are actually doing it.

items.statement: MFI non-overdue collection efficiency improved to 98.7% in December
items.quote: The December number inched up to 98.7% (collection efficiency) and that was the second best number in the calendar year H2.

items.statement: MFI recovery headcount increased from 600 to ~1500 since June
items.quote: we have increased our headcount from 600 that we had on the recovery vertical as of June, we have reached a number of about 1500 and higher trained and stabilized team.

items.statement: PCR at 61% but ~80% excluding technical write-offs; target ~70%
items.quote: If you write back the technical write off in our PCR calculation, we are north of 80%. But we have very prudent write off policy also that so that we don't hang on the bad assets on the balance sheet.

items.statement: Secured retail assets growing 20-24%, commercial banking growing ~30%
items.quote: Other than that, secure retail asset is growing in the range of 20% to 24%. Commercial banking is growing in the range of 30%.

items.statement: Unsecured lending cap at 15% overall, currently ~11%; MFI at 7% vs 10% cap
items.quote: Overall, the cap of unsecured lending is 15%, is around ~11%. We want to stick to that. Of course, for some time, it may go below that the whole guided number.

items.statement: RBI gold loan circular mandates branch-only model, stops renewals, standardizes LTV at 75%
items.quote: One was your BC model have to be revamped as per the new RBI guidelines. Like they said the business has to be done only through branches. BC have to come your branch and customer have to come your branch and storing and everything valuation everything have to be done in branch.

items.statement: 50% of gold loans were previously rolled over; now must be repaid fully
items.quote: 50% loan of Gold loan was getting rollover by the existing lender.

items.statement: Fincare integration largely complete; branch banking and lending units integrated except MFI
items.quote: the Fincare was running their own head office based out of Bangalore, they had their own IT system, they had their own control functions, all has been integrated, largely in this year.

items.statement: Targeting 90% CGFMU guarantee cover on MFI portfolio; cost beneficial vs provisioning
items.quote: maybe around 90% portfolio of microfinance will be covered in this guarantee program. Yes, cost is there, but if we see the overall benefit of coverage versus the cost, right, it is much, much beneficial.

items.statement: CGFMU cover applies to both agri and non-agri SMF lending
items.quote: It's covered, SMF is also covered. We have taken the clarification.

items.statement: MFI industry asset base reduced ~10% due to irrational lending stoppage
items.quote: That is why the 10% reduction is there in the overall asset base in this market.

items.statement: AU MFI: 55% customers zero exposure, 27% second lender at disbursement
items.quote: Like for example in our case ~55% customer have the zero exposure. We were the only lender in that segment with that customer at the time of disbursement, in the new one. And then 27% customer, we are the second lenders.

items.statement: MFI book ROA dropped from expected 4% to 1-1.5% this year due to cyclic stress
items.quote: If you take my number, right, you would have expected that this book should have given us a 4% ROA this year. They might be giving us a 1% or 1.5% ROA this year instead of that.

items.statement: MFI industry typical stress cycle lasts ~6 months operating; provisions lag 4-6 months
items.quote: the AU Small Finance Bank January 24, 2025 harder part of the problem last for six months on operating basis although the provisions will come in with a 4 to 6 month lag

items.statement: MFI collection efficiency was 99.4% in FY24 vs 98.7% now
items.quote: So, FY24, we were about 99.4% on that metric.

items.statement: Digital labor/AI initiatives started to improve cost efficiency
items.quote: We're really working on our digital labor, right? We want to introduce the digital labor internally so that you know we don't depend on a human effort, other than depend more digital effort, right?

items.statement: CD ratio target maintained at 80-85%; deposit growth calibrated to asset needs
items.quote: And we want to keep our CD ratio around 85 or maybe in the range of 80, right? So, that is why we also want to really manage the cost of money by not growing that kind of deposit.

items.statement: Gold loan regulatory changes create level playing field; AU has cost, brand, storage advantages
items.quote: So, I think nobody will take the chance. We have two advantages of the Bank. One, we have the cost of money. Second, we have a storage facility. And customers generally have more belief in banks.

items.statement: March 2027 strategy remains but adjusted for economic slowdown; update due in March
items.quote: March 27 strategy is something which is out there, which we had presented in 18th of March last year. And we continue to be guided by that. I think what we are given in September is the progress around that. And we'll keep updating you every half year on how we are progressing.

name: The New India Assurance Company Limited

items.statement: Expect robust recovery in growth momentum during Q4 FY25 supported by premium strengthening in property insurance and profitable underwriting
items.quote: We anticipate a robust recovery in growth momentum during Q4 for the financial year '25, supported by encouraging signs of premium strengthening in the property insurance segment and a strategic focus on profitable underwriting practices.

items.statement: Confident of achieving solvency ratio of 2x in near future
items.quote: Our solvency ratio remains strong at 1.90x, well above the regulatory requirement of 1.50x. We are confident of achieving a solvency ratio of 2x in the near future.

items.statement: Combined ratio improved to 119.08% for 9M FY25 from 120.34% in 9M FY24
items.quote: Our key operational metrics also show a positive trajectory. The incurred claim ratio improved to 97.37% from 98.07% and the combined ratio reduced to 119.08% from 120.34%.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 combined ratio at 116.33% reflecting steady progress in managing claims and controlling expenses
items.quote: In Q3 FY '25, we achieved a combined ratio of 116.33, reflecting a steady progress in managing claims and controlling expenses.

items.statement: Motor TP incurred claim ratio on earned premium rose to 88.94% in 9M FY25 from 83.05% in FY24 due to non-revision of premium by Ministry of Road Transport
items.quote: Regarding the increasing ICRs in TP, if you see from the year '21-'22, the ICR on earned premium was 67.55%; '22-'23, it rose to 75.07%; '23-24, 83.05% and up to quarter 3 in financial year '25, which is 88.94% on earned premium.

items.statement: Health segment incurred claim ratio improved substantially to 103.25% overall with retail at 88%, group health at 103%, government at 114%
items.quote: And if we talk about ICR, we have substantially improved our ICR over last year. We are at 103.25% in toto. And in retail, the ICR is 88%, group health is 103% and government was 114%, sir.

items.statement: Indian general insurance sector grew 7.83% in 9M FY25 with gross direct premium of INR2,30,201 crores, poised to surpass INR3 lakh crores by year-end
items.quote: On the industry front, the Indian general insurance sector recorded 7.83% growth during the 9 months ended December 31, 2024, with a gross direct premium of INR2,30,201 crores compared to INR2,13,477 crores in the same period last year. This figure is poised to surpass INR3 lakh crores by the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Gross written premium reached INR32,186 crores with net earned premium of INR26,061 crores as of December 31, 2024
items.quote: As of December 31, 2024, our gross written premium reached INR32,186 crores with a net earned premium of INR26,061 crores.

items.statement: Fire segment premium declined 9.08% while all other segments showed positive growth
items.quote: So in all segments, we are showing positive growth except Fire, where we are negative by 9.08%.

items.statement: Product mix: Health & PA 46%, Fire 15%, Motor TP 15%, Motor OD 12%, Marine 2%, Others 10%
items.quote: Our business is, Fire segment it is 15%; Marine, it is 2%; Motor OD, it is 12%; Motor TP, 15%; Health & PA is the maximum, which is 46%; and Others 10%.

items.statement: Distribution mix: Brokers 33%, Direct platform agent 26%, Direct 31%, Bancassurance 1%, Dealer 9%
items.quote: Our product mix is from brokers, we have generated a business of 33%. Direct side, we -- direct platform agent, which is 26%, directly is 31%, bancassurance is I% and dealer is 9%.

items.statement: Renewed Rajasthan Government Health Scheme with 20% increase in per family premium effective February 2025
items.quote: I'm delighted to share that we recently renewed the prestigious Rajasthan Government Health Scheme, which will provide coverage to 1.3 crores families starting February 2025. This renewal also reflects our disciplined pricing strategy with a 20% increase in per family premium.

items.statement: Retail health growth of 11% mainly due to price hike implemented in October after 5.5 years
items.quote: So as I said that the retail growth is around 11%, and mainly, it is due to the price hike, which we have done in October this year. It has been done mostly after about 5.5 years this increase in pricing.

items.statement: Fire pricing holding at sustainable levels in January renewals after market dip to unsustainable levels
items.quote: Yes. So the market -- there is -- I mean there is an expectations from the market that the pricing is going up for Fire and the few renewals that have happened from Jan, yes, the price is holding to a large extent.

items.statement: Strictly implementing 1/365 accounting for long-term premium; minimal impact as long-term book not significant
items.quote: Yes. So on the one by end accounting, we are strictly implementing that part of regulation. And we are -- I mean that is being implemented. But we don't see a very big impact for New India because we don't have a very big book of long-term business.

items.statement: No plans to enter life insurance even if composite licensing introduced; non-life diversification sufficient
items.quote: On the composite license, as of right now, we do not have any plans to foray into life insurance. Life insurance is a very different business. It requires a lot of planning and it requires a lot of capital also. And I think the -- it takes -- it's a very long journey before you break even in life insurance business.

items.statement: Rationalizing operating offices, increasing digital penetration, leveraging technology for customer satisfaction and profitability
items.quote: We are rationalizing the offices, operating offices. We are increasing the digital penetration. We are maintaining healthy solvency margins. We are leveraging on technology to drive our customer satisfaction, profitability and growth.

items.statement: PhonePe partnership Q3 sales growth 50%; WhatsApp sales focused on service currently, expanding product sales
items.quote: And as a strategy, The New India has partnered with the super-app players like PhonePe and Q3 growth in the sale is 50% with PhonePe. And as far as the WhatsApp is concerned, we have started with the initial sale of the existing products, and we would like to expand further with -- on sale of the product, but however, as on date, it is more concentrated on the service for the quarter.

items.statement: Renewed Rajasthan Government Health Scheme covering 1.3 crore families from February 2025
items.quote: I'm delighted to share that we recently renewed the prestigious Rajasthan Government Health Scheme, which will provide coverage to 1.3 crores families starting February 2025.

items.statement: Investment yield impacted by equity market churn; waiting for RBI guidance to lock in higher-yielding securities
items.quote: And about the outlook, it is still quite a volatile market that we are having, and we are waiting for tomorrow's RBI guidance. So we will be seeing some change in the interest yield in the market. And we will be taking action accordingly to lock in whatever we can at the higher-yielding securities.

items.statement: Motor TP reserve releases only evaluated at year-end; quarterly reserves based on expected claim inflation with stable approach
items.quote: On the TP reserves, I'll like to answer that we have not had any prior year releases, at least for the first 9 months. In the March quarter, we will again retook for the full year's exact development patterns and decide whether there is need for any strengthening or needs for any releases.

items.statement: Underwriting losses persist across lines; price sensitivity high; competition intense with some players offering products almost free
items.quote: We have to draw a very fine balance between maintaining,the volume and the quality. And that is a very, very thin line and the tight walk that we do every day and trying to see that at the end of the day, our books show some profit for the investor.

items.statement: Revenue guidance revised downwards; FY25 revenue now expected at Rs 1,300-1,400 crore vs prior Rs 1,400-1,500 crore
items.quote: we will not get to the Rs. 1,400 crores, Rs. 1,500 crores range, we will be more in the Rs. 1,300 crores, Rs. 1,400 crores range, which means that there is a drop in approximately Rs. 100 crores of revenue.

items.statement: EBITDA guidance for full year maintained at Rs 230-260 crore; Q4 EBITDA guidance reduced by Rs 10 crore

items.statement: Pilot scale-up of electrolyte formulation for hybrid car batteries expected by April; enables unique competitive advantage.
items.quote: With encouraging results of our electrolyte formulation from lab scale the customer has now requested to scale up the formulation to pilot scale, we expect to run the scale up at pilot level by the month of April.

items.statement: Two large agro intermediates under approval; final clearance expected this quarter, commercialization to begin immediately; new Dahej plant ready by Q4 FY26.
items.quote: We expect to get final clearance within the current quarter. Post approval the commercialisation should begin immediately.

items.statement: All four agro intermediates under approval will commercialize in current year; three pharma intermediates approved, gradual commercialization from end of 2025 or early 2026.
items.quote: Finally, all the four agro intermediates which were under approval basis will see commercialisation happening during the current year.

items.statement: Monoglyme trials at 100kg catalyst level starting; 1000kg equipment delivery expected by end of FY25, installation and commercialization by June 2025.
items.quote: We are also expecting the final equipment, capable of handling 1000kg, to be delivered by the end of this financial year. Installation and commercialization are projected to be completed by June 2025.

items.statement: First commercial supply of flame retardants to begin in current quarter; full commercialization only when pricing conditions are right.
items.quote: We are set to begin the first commercial supply to the customer in the current quarter.

items.statement: Distillation plant started in January; expected to free up 12-15% reactor capacity for major products and new agro product distillation.
items.quote: I would not have the exact number, but I think it should give us at least 12% to 15% of free space in the plant.

items.statement: Semiconductor-grade chemical development progressing; achieved 38-60 PPB trace metals vs 1 PPB target; expects breakthrough in 4-6 months.
items.quote: So as of today, if you ask me, honestly, we are still in the range of about 38 to 60 PPB when it comes to the final product. So probably it is still 4 months, 6 months away.

items.statement: New plant at Dahej site for agro products expected operational by January 2026; existing plant near full occupancy by June-July 2025.
items.quote: We expect our plant to be almost fully occupied by somewhere around June or July of this year, the existing plant. And then we'll definitely need this new plant for future growth.

items.statement: Combined existing and new capacity potential to cross INR 900 crores revenue; currently at historic pricing bottom over last decade.
items.quote: So as soon as this occupancy is fulfilled, then we definitely have the chances to cross our revenue of more than INR900 crores with the existing and upcoming capacities.

items.statement: Gross profit margin expected to stabilize around 45% as new agro products with higher raw material consumption replace higher-margin PTC/SDA mix.
items.quote: Roughly in the range of 45%.

items.statement: Goods in transit stable at ~INR 11 crores due to long transit times (8-9 weeks to US, 7-8 weeks to Europe); Red Sea route reopening may reduce inventory on water.
items.quote: Even in this quarter, the transit amount is roughly the same, about INR11 crores. Basically, the transit amount has kept at this level, potentially because of the very long transit times that we are seeing.

items.statement: No price wars in SDA segment; business distribution is strategic. New applications in desulfurization and plastic recycling may hedge auto cyclicality.
items.quote: So there is no internal competition between us and competitors. Our business distribution is strategic and based on the volume of business we each handle.

items.statement: Electrolyte salt sales to smoothen from April as customer production lines stabilized; consistent regular demand expected.
items.quote: It will smoothen out from April. So dispatch is beginning from April, it will definitely smoothen out in terms of consistent sales that is happening.

items.statement: US policy shift away from EVs may indirectly benefit SDA business (hybrid vehicles) rather than harm electrolyte salts.
items.quote: It might indirectly benefit us in some way but still time will tell what will happen. So it's not going to be a negative impact for the business.

items.statement: Photochlorination product approvals complete; customer visit end of February for contract starting April; commercial shipments from April 2025.
items.quote: So that also we are through. So now we will see consistent shipments rolling out again from April or May of this year.

items.statement: Polymer product plant trial successful; first shipment by mid-February; commercial rollout after customer approval within few weeks.
items.quote: Plant trial has went well. So it's just getting into final quality checks and packaging. So we'll make the first shipment probably by mid of February.

items.statement: Process excellence team formed to optimize bottlenecks and reaction times as plant approaches 100% utilization; continuous optimization activity.
items.quote: So basically, we have created a team, which we call it as process excellence. And this team identifies which could be the potential bottlenecks, which is removed.

items.statement: SDA demand cyclicality acknowledged (3 downturn cycles since 1999); new applications in desulfurization and plastic recycling may provide natural hedge.
items.quote: So yes, it's a cyclical thing. As of today, one is the petrochemical application, which is large in terms of volume.

items.statement: EBITDA margin for PASC segment to improve as volumes hit from May; raw material consumption factor already very good.
items.quote: EBITDA margins if you cover the plant as a fully occupational plant, the EBITDA margins are already healthy.

items.statement: High-purity water plant commercially set up for semiconductor-grade production; obstacle took 3 years to overcome.
items.quote: So that obstacle has taken us 3 years to actually overcome this obstacle of reaching the water of required quality.

name: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Ltd

items.statement: January retail growth looks very positive across all areas

items.quote: We would also like to highlight our retail loss ratio for 9-months FY '25 which stands at 69.2% and group loss ratio is 90.4%.

items.statement: Expense ratio on like-to-like basis flat at 30.2% vs 30.3% last year; 1/N impact elevates reported ratio by 1.6%
items.quote: Yes because of the 1/N impact otherwise last year it was 30.3% expense ratio, now it is 30.2% which is flattish.

items.statement: Annualized yield target of 10-12% on product pricing to match medical inflation

items.statement: Solvency ratio 2.22x vs regulatory requirement of 1.5x as of Dec 24

items.statement: Home healthcare expanded to 100 locations with partners Apollo, Max Home Health, Portea

items.statement: Banca partners increased to 69; added Bajaj Finance and NeoGrowth in Q3
items.quote: Our number of Banca partners now stands at 69. In this quarter, we added names like Bajaj Finance and NeoGrowth to our portfolio.

items.quote: there has been a consistent increase in frequency and severity largely driven by heightened awareness in cashless availability, accessibilit y, active reach out by hospitals, and generally more higher preference for going for surgical interventions rather than going for conservative treatments

items.quote: It's introduced for one of the products which is 30% of our portfolio as of now. It is introduced for SIP product.

items.quote: Although, overall, yes, there is some erosion happening in the API prices because we have a very strong backward integrated model in place, for our set of products, we are not seeing that kind of erosion. For us, the growth is going to be very stable moving forward also.

items.statement: Working capital days improved to 124 in Q3 FY25 from 134 YoY
items.quote: On the operational efficiency front, our working capital days have improved to 124 days in Q3 FY '25 compared to 134 days in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio 0.01; conservative borrowing using only LCs and bank guarantees, no working capital limits utilized
items.quote: We have maintained a strong financial position with a debt -to-equity ratio of 0.01, adopting a conservative ap proach to borrowing by utilizing only letter of credit and bank guarantees without tapping into working capital limits.

items.statement: CMO/CDMO contracts take minimum 2-3 years to generate commercial revenue; no top-line impact in FY26
items.quote: No, we will not be able to because any contract manufacturing opportunity takes minimum 2 to 3 years to start giving commercial revenue.

items.quote: Probably January business would be higher than what we did in the month of November, December. Similar would be the case in case of fresh sales as well.

items.quote: Our net sales in first 9 months is 50% higher than what we did in last full fiscal of 2024. The redemption ratio at 44% within the last quarter is much lower than the 30-quarter historic average of 60%.

items.statement: Monthly SIP book touched INR935 crore in December; added INR280 crore in last 12 months
items.quote: During the month end, our monthly SIP book has touched INR935 crores. We have added INR280 crores to our SIP book in last 12 months

items.quote: And the December quarter, we earned INR43 lakhs only. So there was a significant drop of INR2.1 crores in the P2P segment in this quarter alone.

items.quote: On the stock broking too, sequentially, revenue has fallen by a third. Large part of this fall is attributed to a fall in transactional revenue owing to a heightened volatility and fall in the market.

items.quote: On the insurance front also -- I think the insurance revenue de-grew by 15.6% sequentially to INR28.6 crores, which was led by a fall in the life insurance fresh premium.

items.quote: So actually the opex also, if you look at the current fiscal we added almost 16 branches. Incremental cost is visible on the opex side, mainly because of rent, electricity, conveyance because this is all related to branch expansion.

items.quote: Overall, we expect that the next year growth -- looking at the current year base, then 12% to 14% should be the range for operating expenditure, which include the employee costs also.

items.quote: If you see the right-hand chart, which shows the movement in equity on a sequential basis, equity AUM has declined by 1.2% mainly due to negative mark to market of 4.7% in last quarter. However, our M2M losses were lower than the Nifty 500 downfall of 7.7% in last quarter.

items.statement: Regular plan market share gaining; direct plans growing faster but regular distributors still growing

items.statement: RBI P2P regulations from August 2024 stopped fresh inflows; existing AUM running down
items.quote: With the implementation of new regulations by RBI around August last year, there is no fresh inflow in this segment. And with no fresh inflow, existing AUM is going to run-down due to constrained maturity.

items.quote: Additionally, our treasury book has reached INR330 crores, which is also giving us a war chest to grow inorganically.

items.quote: The gross new active investors added in first 9 months of our fiscal is already equal to the number of active investors we have added in last entire financial year of 2024. Our monthly run rate of adding 20 crores SIPs is still continuing

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin of 23-24%
items.quote: The target is to stay around 23-24% EBITDA margins and any increase in revenue will immediately add to the EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Striving to cross 23-24% EBITDA margins sustainably

items.quote: I don't think it is animal spirits anywhere to be seen at this point in time. But regardless of that, the environment is better as compared to what it was six months ago.

items.quote: By business, InfoBeans Cloudtech has shown a slight dip. It used to be 18%, now it is 15% right now.

items.statement: Painfully aware of capital allocation concerns with Rs 150 crore free cash
items.quote: Yeah, we are painfully aware of that.

items.quote: It is a combination of two things, interest income as well as any foreign exchange gain or loss that we get.
