items.statement: German revenue nearly doubled YoY
items.quote: You can see the European market, which is German revenue is almost doubled from what it used to be a year ago.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to remain in the 40-45% range.
items.quote: Overall, the EBITDA margins will remain in the range of 40% to 45% that we have been maintaining.

items.statement: Mutual fund industry AUM grew ~39.4% YoY; KFintech AUM grew ~42.8% YoY, gaining ~300 bps market share.
items.quote: Our overall AUM also in terms of market share has grown as against a market expansion of 39.4 odd percent. We have grown about 42.8%. That's a good 300 basis points expansion in the overall AUM on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Alternatives: manage ~535 funds (~37% market share by count), AUM ~INR1.4T (+55% YoY); win rate >60% domestic, ~75% in GIFT City.
items.quote: Today, we manage about 535 funds, getting our market share closer to 37% in terms of the number of funds. The AUM growth has been substantive at about close to 55% year-on-year, bringing our total assets under management to over INR1.4 trillion. We have been winning more than 60% plus in domestic market and about three fourth of the funds in the GIFT City.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 44.1% in Q3 (down 10 bps QoQ due to seasonality); range 44-45% for the quarter.
items.quote: EBITDA margins, as I talked about, have seen a sequential dip of 10 bps, but that's more to do with some bit of seasonality that we have seen. Otherwise, in terms of the overall results, they are still 44.1%.

items.statement: PAT margin 31% for Q3, 30.6% for 9M FY25.
items.quote: PAT margins are in the range of 31% for the quarter and 30.6% for the year.

items.statement: Capex spend ~INR65-75 crore so far (hardware, wealth platform); expect additional INR60-70 crore in coming year.
items.quote: We have spent over INR65-odd, INR75-odd crores already in terms of infrastructure. A large portion of this, again, is in hardware and some very tangible assets such as the wealth platform that we've created. So cash flows vis-a-vis capex, we are looking to be bringing in another INR60 crores to INR70 crores in the coming year.

items.statement: International deal sizes increased: avg ~INR1 cr/yr annuity historically; last 6 deals avg ~INR3-3.5 cr/yr; pipeline deals ~$1M each.
items.quote: On an average, the deal sizes earlier used to be anywhere about INR1 crores or so per annum recurring right annuity. That deal size now, if I average out the last 6 deals that we have signed, has now expanded to over nearly about INR3 crores to INR3.5 crores, right? And the deals that we are now in the pipeline are closer to $1 million in terms of each deal that we are looking to work with.

items.statement: Alternatives pricing: pure TA deals ~1.5-2 bps; full stack (TA+FA) ~2.5-3 bps.
items.quote: Those opportunities give us spread of anywhere about 1.5 to 2 basis points. And of late, pretty much almost every opportunity we enter into is a combination of transfer agency and fund accounting, a full solution stack, and that gets anywhere between 2.5 to 3 basis points.

items.statement: Revenue mix Q3: MF fee-based 71%, Issuer Solutions 14%, International & Other Investor Solutions 11% (GFS 5%, AIF 5%, Pension & Webile 2%), Mortgage/GBS 2.7%.
items.quote: In terms of the various mix of the revenue, mutual fund revenue, fee-based revenues is 71%. The Issuer Solutions business is 14%. The International and Other Investor Solutions business is about 11%. Within that, GFS is about 5%, AIF is about 5%, Pension and Webile is about 2% and the mortgage business, GBS is about 2.7%.

items.statement: Cash & equivalents ~INR570 crore; will use for business expansion, M&A, and potential dividend per Board policy.
items.quote: We remain cash positive. We have a dry powder of almost INR570 crores sitting in cash and cash equivalents, which we will utilize as per the Board policy for business expansion, M&A and the Board policy at the year-end in terms of looking at dividend payout if the Board considers that.

items.statement: 9 international contracts signed in recent quarters in transition (2-3 quarters to go live); revenue not yet recognized.
items.quote: There are close to about nine asset management companies, which are in transition of delivery. We have announced them in Q2 and some in Q1 and of course, some of them now. As I've said, it takes roughly about 2 to 3 quarters depending upon the size and complexity of the contract for us to be able to transition it. And hence, the revenue for these 9 contracts is yet to be clocked and goes well, hop

items.statement: Headcount expansion driving expense growth; tech costs growing faster than payroll; cloud-first strategy.
items.quote: So it is a symptom of expansion of headcount and the technological investments. Of course, the headcount does not go in the same proportion as the total volumes. But the tech costs are, in many ways, can grow much faster than even the payroll component in India. And that's what we have seen in terms of our cloud costs expanding rapidly.

items.statement: Hexagram revenue INR9.5 crore for 9M FY25 vs INR6 crore 9M FY24 (+60% YoY).
items.quote: Hexagram had a revenue of about INR9.5 crores for 9 months ended December versus about INR6 crores for the same period last year. So it's a 60% plus growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Aim to sustain EBITDA margins around current level and improve gradually in subsequent quarters depending on two-wheeler industry growth
items.quote: Our aim is to sustain this level of EBITDA margins and improve gradually in the subsequent quarters depending upon the growth of the two-wheeler industry.

items.statement: Delivered highest ever EBITDA margin of 12.5% in Q3 FY25, up 180 bps YoY; 9M FY25 EBITDA margin at 12.2%, up 205 bps YoY
items.quote: I am glad that we have delivered the highest ever EBITDA margin of 12.5% in Q3 FY25, which is 180 basis points higher than Q3 FY24.

items.statement: Expect two-wheeler demand momentum to continue for remaining part of FY25 with positive market sentiments; Q4 sorted and optimistic on next financial year
items.quote: We anticipate the growth momentum in two-wheeler sector to continue for the remaining part of the year with prevailing positive market sentiments.

items.statement: Export order of Rs. 100 crore from Ford Motor under testing, expected to start beginning of next financial year; Rs. 75 crore export order book maintained
items.quote: We have got an export order of Rs. 100 crore for Ford Motor, but that is under testing. We have already given the samples and once the approvals come, and then that will start hopefully in the beginning of the next financial year.

items.statement: Invested Rs. 475 crore in Karoli plant and up to Rs. 200 crore in 18th manufacturing facility in Bangalore; Rs. 600 crore total capex to last 18 months; target debt-equity 0.3 next year
items.quote: we invested very heavily. We invested Rs. 475 crore in the Karoli plant till date and we are continuously investing up to Rs. 200 crore in the 18th manufacturing facility in Bangalore

items.statement: 18th manufacturing facility in Bengaluru commercialized on 14th January 2025; QAV expected to finish by March, full stream from next financial year
items.quote: Our 18 th manufacturing facility at Bengaluru, incidentally that is our third plant in southern India, in Bengaluru. It has commercialized on 14th January 2025

items.statement: Rajasthan plant subsidy of Rs. 6.65 crore received in Q3 FY25; similar figure of around Rs. 7 crore expected to continue in forthcoming quarters
items.quote: is about Rs. 6.65 crore subsidy from the Karoli plant in the Q3. Joseph George: Understood. Kuldip Singh Rathee: Now onwards, a similar figure of around Rs. 7 crore will continue in the forthcoming quarters also

items.statement: Aluminum lightweighting precision solutions largest segment at 43% revenue share, grew 25% YoY; advanced braking systems grew 14% YoY; safety control cables grew 10% YoY
items.quote: The aluminum lightweighting precision solutions have a largest business segment with 43% share of revenue, let the growth momentum and delivered 25% year-on-year.

items.statement: Supplying to 80% of OEMs in EV sector; EV share 5% of total two-wheeler production; ICE contribution 76%, EV contribution 5% in business
items.quote: See our percentage is similar because we are supplying to 80% of the OEMs in the EV sector. So, the EV percentage at the moment is only 5% of the total vehicle production in two-wheelers and our share of business is also that.

items.statement: EV component content 30-50% higher than ICE; company is ICE and EV agnostic, positioned to benefit from EV adoption
items.quote: The EV component because we are into very critical lightweighting and thermal management products. In EV, the component is higher, it's 30% to 50% higher in EV.

items.statement: Exports may not grow this year due to European customers consuming pipeline inventories; Q4 exports trying to be better than Q3 and Q2
items.quote: In spite of such good results, we would like to tell the investors that our exports may not grow this particular year because the customers, very prominent customers, they are first consuming the vast inventories in the pipeline.

items.statement: Debt-equity closed at 0.42 last year; expected to close at 0.38 this year despite heavy investment; target 0.3 next year
items.quote: I am happy to share that last year we closed at a debt equity of 0.42. And in spite of such a heavy investment, we will be most likely closing at a debt equity of 0.38. Further next year our target is 0.3.

items.statement: Two-wheeler industry production grew 8% in Q3 FY25 and 13.1% in 9M FY25 YoY; ASK outperformed industry growth
items.quote: Amongst all segments, two-wheeler posted production growth of 8% in Q3 FY25 and 13.1% in 9M FY25 on YoY basis.

items.statement: Honda EV plans not aggressive - yearly plan of only 18,000 units; one more model launching around Q2
items.quote: Mr. Basu, their plans are not very aggressive. The whole year plan for next year, they have taken only around 18,000. That's all, yearly plan.

items.statement: AISIN JV aftermarket launch planned for Q1 FY26; targeting breakeven in first year; huge dealer response at Bharat Mobility Expo
items.quote: We are in the process of appointing dealers all over the country and we hope to launch the operations in Q1 FY26 as we had always told before.

items.statement: Karoli plant utilization between 45% and 50%; asset turnover target 2x; new Bangalore plant has fungible lines for various products
items.quote: So, the utilization percentage is similar, between 45% and 50%. But now the capacities are further ahead, and we expect that the coming years growth shall be very much taken care of from there.

items.statement: Solar power plant of 9.9 MW in Sirsa, Haryana started trial production on 27th January 2025 for captive consumption
items.quote: Solar power plant of 9.9 megawatt in Sirsa, Haryana for captive consumption started trial production on 27th January 2025 and will start supply of power soon.

items.statement: EPS increased to Rs. 9.64 per share in 9M FY25 from Rs. 6.39 in same period last year
items.quote: With strong performance on profitability, our earning per share in 9M FY25 has increased to Rs. 9.64 per share against Rs. 6.39 per share in the same period last year.

items.statement: Medium-term guidance: 24-26% AUM growth, OpEx to net total income 14-15%, GNPA 40-60 bps, credit cost 20-25 bps, provisioning coverage 40-50%, ROA 2-2.2%, leverage 7-8x, ROE 13-15%
items.quote: We estimate in the medium term 24% to 26% AUM growth, Opex to net total income to go down to 14 % to 15% from in the current quarter it came to 19.8%, GNPA at 40 bps to 60 bps. Credit cost remaining sideways between 20 to 25 bps. Provisioning coverage at 40 % to 50%. ROA is of a 2% to 2.2% with leverage of 7 to 8 times. Thus ROE of 13% to 15% in the medium term horizon.

items.statement: AUM grew 26% YoY to Rs 1,08,314 crore; quarterly AUM addition Rs 5,745 crore
items.quote: During the quarter AUM was up by 26% and overall AUM have now stood at Rs. 1,08,314 crore.

items.statement: Segmental AUM growth: home loans 23%, LAP 19%, LRD 26%, developer finance 59%
items.quote: Within 26% under various segments, home loans grew by 23%, loan against property by 19%, lease rental discounting by 26%, and developer finance by 59%.

items.statement: Portfolio mix: home loans 57%, LAP 10%, LRD 19%, developer finance 12%
items.quote: Broadly, overall, portfolio mix remains stable with slight movement between the products. HL at 57%, LAP at 10%, LRD at 19%, and DF at 12%.

items.statement: Medium-term spread corridor 1.7-2.2% through the cycle
items.quote: Depending on the rate cycle and depending on the competitive intensity , 1.7%, 1.8% to 2.2% through the cycle, the spreads will remain at the book level.

items.statement: Cost of funds stable at 7.9% QoQ, indicating peak and full pass-through
items.quote: Cost of funds was stable at 7.9% from the last quarter indicating that the cost of funds have peaked out and the pass-through of all cost of funds has been there in the balance sheet.

items.statement: GNPA 0.29%, NNPA 0.13%, provisioning coverage 55%; Stage 1 99.34%, Stage 2 0.37%, Stage 3 0.29%
items.quote: Asset quality continued to hold well during the quarter with GNPA remaining stable at 0.29% and NNPA at 0.13%, provisioning coverage of 55%.

items.statement: Credit cost 0.15% net of overlay release (0.20% gross); no management overlay remaining
items.quote: In terms of credit cost, loan loss to average loan assets stood at 0.15% in Q3. However, net of overlay release, it was 0.20. If the same number net of overlay release during the last year same quarter was 0.15%. Now, past this, there is no other management overlay, which is there remaining in the balance sheet of the company.

items.statement: Medium-term GNPA guidance 40-60 bps, credit cost 20-25 bps, provisioning coverage 40-50%
items.quote: GNPA at 40 bps to 60 bps. Credit cost remaining sideways between 20 to 25 bps. Provisioning coverage at 40 % to 50%.

items.statement: OpEx to net total income improved to 19.8% from 23.2% YoY; OpEx grew 7% vs NIM growth 25%
items.quote: Operating efficiency has improved further during the quarter and OpEx to NIM came at 19.8% in the quarter gone by against a 23.2% in Q3 FY24. Operating expenses remain ed in control at 7% growth on YoY against a NIM growth of 25%.

items.statement: Medium-term OpEx to net total income target 14-15% driven by operating leverage as AUM scales
items.quote: We intend to keep on, if you look at even the past also, every year generally we improve this ratio by 1.5% to 2%. Because the kind of investments that are required or the income growth would always outpace the OpEx growth, given the nature of the business and as the balance sheet keeps on becoming bigger, there will be natural jaw which will keep on coming in.

items.statement: Affordable/near-prime vertical launched May-Jun 2024; targeting southern and western states (Andhra, Telangana, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan); ticket sizes Rs 16-17L affordable, Rs 35-40L near-prime; purchase transactions focus
items.quote: This SBU business has started picking up which is in line with our expectations and as we go forward we expect this vertical to become very significant in our overall scheme of things.

items.statement: Affordable vertical to remain 5-10% of home loan book (not 5% of overall book) in medium term; prime to stay ~80% of book
items.quote: 5% to 10% of the home loan book can be affordable, but not a 5% of overall book. That is first part because I think it will because Prime has a much more head start. We are already at Rs. 108,000 crore kind of a balance sheet for us to built a 10% on overall 5% to 10% on overall books that fast.

items.statement: Balance transfer out stable at ~12% annualized for home loans
items.quote: In a home loan, we generally have, you see on an annualized basis, close to 12% kind of a balance transfer out which is more or less in line with what we had seen in previous part.

items.statement: High competitive intensity in LAP led to faster LRD growth; LRD risk-adjusted returns better than LAP over last 2-3 years
items.quote: Our recent assessment of last three years had been that the lease rental discounting adjusted for risk is better return generator in last 2-3 years, given the intensity of competitive activity in loan against property market and the kind of what we say risk-adjusted returns which are coming in.

items.statement: PBC ratio 62.15% (regulatory min 60%); individual home loan 50.9% of total assets (regulatory min 50%); residential assets 62.1% of total assets (regulatory min 60%)
items.quote: PBC ratio also remained above. PBC is a principal business criteria Bajaj Housing Finance January 27, 2025 ratio which is applicable to housing finance companies which is at 60%. The ratio was at 62.15% for BHFL

items.statement: Borrowing mix: 43% banks (30% EBLR, 13% MCLR), 46% money market, 11% NHB; CAR just below 28% post capital raise
items.quote: Capital adequacy of the company remained strong with CAR tad below 28% due to the capital raise which we recently did.

items.statement: Leverage target raised to 7-8x from previous 6-7x threshold as company scaled
items.quote: We had previously been raising capital when we had been closer to 7 x, but as we have now grown in scale and reached a stage, our earlier threshold used to be 6 x to 7x leverage as a private company. Now we have moved the threshold to 7x to 8x of a leverage as we have grown bigger.

items.statement: ROA 2.4%, ROE 11.5% (down from 13% due to full impact of Sep capital raise); medium-term ROA 2-2.2%, ROE 13-15%
items.quote: In terms of profitability, as already called out, PA T grew by 25% in Q3 and RO A remained at 2.4% in line with Q3 FY24 and ROE at 11.5%. ROE is down given the full impact of capital raise, what we have done in September in Q2 F Y25.

items.statement: Disbursement growth 17% YoY
items.quote: During the quarter, we also saw disbursement growth of 17% compare d to same quarter last year.

items.statement: Residential real estate sales growth slowed in 9M FY25 vs prior year; decline led by fewer launches not demand weakness; no inventory overhang building
items.quote: the first nine months of F Y25 residential real estate has witnessed slowness in growth versus last year. So I'll say slowness in growth versus last year and there is an overall sale drop also as what has been reported by few agencies Bajaj Housing Finance January 27, 2025 but in terms of a market sizing and in terms of their the launches have been lower. So the sales are lower because of the numb

items.statement: Developer finance book Rs 13,000 cr across 738 projects; only 4 NPA cases since inception (2 recovered, 2 outstanding); only 2 DCCO extensions ever (1 during COVID); no DCCO extensions in last year
items.quote: since inception we have funded close to more than 1300 odd projects. We have so Bajaj Housing Finance January 27, 2025 far seen only four cases which have slipped into an NPA . Out of them two we managed to recover later on and close and the two which are still in NPAs which is visible from the balance sheet

items.statement: Developer finance to stay 12-15% of AUM to balance risk; not a standalone balance sheet driver due to execution/macro risk
items.quote: Developer finance remains critical for us in two parts. First, of course, as a funnel for home loan and a point of availability at the expansion of a distribution counter. But in itself also from a mortgage company point of view, it is a return enhancer. But given there is an inherent risk in construction finance, which is higher than the normal home loan business, we would like to not exceed arou

items.statement: Near-prime/affordable SBU sourcing model still evolving; using existing branches where geographies overlap, new branches for new geographies; no dedicated affordable branches
items.quote: The geographies where we are commonly present with the other segments, it will be the same branches, but where geographies, there will be geographies which we are going to cover through this segment where we are not existingly operating, we will set up the branches for those markets for this particular. But there are no dedicated branches in that sense.

items.statement: Near-prime/affordable yields 9-13% (not 13-18% higher-risk segment); still learning skill set for higher-yield segment
items.quote: We largely operate in this segment between 9% to 13%. We are not in a much higher segment because there is a 13% to 17% or 18% segment as well in the market. But for a near future, in the foreseeable future, we'll operate in the 9 % to 13% kind of a market, not 13% to 17%, 18%.

items.statement: Karnataka e-Khata caused registration delays but normalizing; no disruption in Telangana; no long-term volume impact
items.quote: There has been some delays in execution of registrations due to a change in Karnataka, if you are calling out as state of Karnataka because of e-Khata introduction which is for long term good for the industry and long term good for the customers. But situation is getting normalized as we speak because there are delay. It is not cancelling or impacting the volume in the long run.

items.statement: Targets 30% YoY revenue growth for FY26 and 34-35% overall EBITDA margin
items.quote: Going into FY26, we would definitely push to maintain our 30% year-on-year growth while the EBITDA margins, which are currently about 34% is the range that we are consistently working to remain at about 34%-35% overall EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Fleet grew to 362 machines from 307; added 30 cranes, 5 AWPs, 20 prime movers with trailers
items.quote: With this CAPEX, the Company has now added 30 crane s, 5 aerial working platforms and 20 prime movers with trailers to its fleet. The total fleet size of the Company now stands at 362 machines against 307 machines in the same period last year

items.statement: Order book of Rs 73.3 crore as of Jan 2025, executable in FY25, up 67% YoY
items.quote: We have a very healthy order book of Rs. 73.30 crores as of January 2025, which is executable in the current financial year itself, and this again reflects a 67% year-on-year growth in the order book.

items.statement: No slowdown seen; demand strong across infra, cement, steel; renewable wind cautious
items.quote: At present, we are not seeing any challenges and also with the demand that we have in the present quarter and the visibility that we are getting from our clients in the coming quarters. We haven't seen a slowdown in demand because of the nature of work that we do, the mix of equipment that we have.

items.statement: Average gross monthly rental yield rose to 3.05% for 9M FY25 from 2.75% YoY
items.quote: In the equipment rental segment, the average gross monthly rental yield rose to 3.05%, rising from 2.75% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Receivable days improved to 79 days in 9M FY25 from 101 days YoY; target 65-70 days
items.quote: On another financial control measure that we have taken which has helped us to bring down our receivable days, which have come down to 79 days for the 9-month period compared to 101 days in the previous year.

items.statement: Equipment rental capacity utilization 89% in Q3 FY25, 85% for 9M FY25
items.quote: In the quarter 3 FY25, we achieved an average capacity utilization of 89% and overall, for the 9-month period, the utilization has been at about 85%.

items.statement: RINL ramp-up to benefit Segment B warehousing; manage central dispatch stockyard plus Mumbai, Nagpur yards
items.quote: We would definitely be benefiting directly because we are managing the entire central dispatch stockyard of Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited plus we have got their stockyard in Mumbai and Nagpur.

items.statement: Renewable wind projects slow on ground due to right-of-way and funding issues; cautious on aggressive expansion
items.quote: Specifically, wind is where we did not see the kind of movement on the ground with regards to the projects that were announced or were anticipated, so wind is the area where especially a lot of our larger cranes are utilized. So, that is where we were being focusing on when I said on the slowdown.

items.statement: ~10 large organized players nationally; 2-3 listed; competition rising but differentiated by multi-solution offering and regional diversification
items.quote: It is hard to put numbers on it, but for the organized side, I do know that there are close to about at max 10 big companies in the country who can be considered big by the virtue of the number of machines or the kind of machines they have. And there again, it is difficult to kind of put them in a same basket because not everybody is doing the mix of equipment like we have got cranes, piling rigs,
